title: Avoid target-lock reentry in KillPilot and KillGarrisoned damage
description: Live registered damage applies through Weapon::deal_damage_internal -> OBJECT_REGISTRY.with_object_mut(target_id, ...) -> Object::attempt_damage_with_return while the target Object write lock is held (GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/weapon/weapon_instance_combat.rs:665; weapon/damage_application.rs:248; object/object_combat.rs:1822+). ActiveBody's special DamageType branches rediscover and blocking-lock their own owner: KillPilot owner.read()/write() at object/body/active_body.rs:1537-1548 (stationary rider path reads it again at :1588), and KillGarrisoned owner.write() at :1619-1624. For registered targets this is the same Arc already write-locked by the caller, so authored KILL_PILOT against a vehicle or KILL_GARRISONED against a building hangs before applying behavior. C++ ActiveBody.cpp:365-450 operates on its direct obj pointer and does not reacquire the target. Carry a synchronous borrowed owner/context through these branches (including contained-target scoring/kill order), without try-lock skips or ambient state. Preserve ordinary vehicle unmanned/team change, rider-change moving/stationary evacuation and scoring, neutral sniped stat, garrison immunity/count/floor/clear-stat order. Add executable actual Weapon -> registered Object regression(s) with a timeout proving completion and effects, plus ordinary zero-secondary target control; run relevant ActiveBody/weapon cohorts and Xfer gate.
notes:
Read-only investigation (2026-09-30): `Weapon::deal_damage` (GameLogic/src/weapon/weapon_instance_combat.rs:626-669) calls `OBJECT_REGISTRY.with_object_mut(target_id, ...)` before `Object::attempt_damage_with_return`; Object then locks body and sends `BodyDamageContext` (object/object_combat.rs:1843-1855), currently only owner source-preference facts (object/body/body_module.rs:312-318). ActiveBody KillPilot reacquires owner via read/write (active_body.rs:1537-1548, 1588+) and KillGarrisoned via owner.write (1621+): registered target is already exclusively write-locked, so weapon path blocks. C++ ActiveBody.cpp:365-418 mutates direct `obj`; 421-450 reads its contain inline.

Proposed smallest safe interface: transient `BodyDamageContext<'a>` borrows `&'a mut Object`, created synchronously in Object damage after cloning the body Arc; add a default owner-context trait method delegating to existing context method so non-ActiveBody implementations need not change. ActiveBody special branches use borrowed owner; garrison scorer uses owner directly when source ID equals owner and registry only for distinct source/occupant. Never call owner.kill while its body mutex is held: moving combat-bike branch queues a deferred owner-kill request; Object processes after body guard drops, scores once before direct `self.kill()`, and avoids duplicate outer scorer/onDie while keeping original damage-FX/post-damage order.

Parked-bike blocker: current `AiUpdateInterface::execute_command(EvacuateInstantly)` is also unsafe inside registered target lock: GameLogic/src/object/unit/ai_commands.rs:1078-1094 reads then write-locks `guard.base_arc()` at line1086 to mark passengers/order `order_all_passengers_to_exit`. A borrowed Object in BodyDamageContext does not release the caller's registry lock. Include an owner-aware non-railed evacuation path that takes `&mut Object` and applies the same subdued check + mark + exit order, or defer command until after target registry guard release; otherwise explicitly leave parked-bike branch unresolved.

Executable integration coverage belongs in GameLogic/src/object/object_tests.rs (has process-global test mutex and object fixture), using actual `Weapon::new(Arc<WeaponTemplate>)` + `Weapon::deal_damage` against registered target/source: KillPilot registered Vehicle asserts completion, unchanged hull, unmanned; KillGarrisoned registered Structure with registered live occupant asserts completion, unchanged hull, occupant dead and clearing order/stat. Extend a test contain fixture with occupant IDs/garrisonable flags. Existing direct ActiveBody tests (active_body.rs:3202+) do not hold owner registry write lock and miss this reentry. No code/tests executed for this investigation.

title: Optimize Main A* paths from CPP raw start position
description:

title: Preserve per-frame units in native AI locomotor execution
description: The native GameEngine/GameLogic locomotor templates correctly store C++ frame units, but the native AIUpdate live path treats them as per-second values in its no-Physics fallback. C++ INI conversion: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/INI/INI.cpp:1709-1723 converts speed by 1/30 and acceleration by 1/900; Locomotor.cpp:422-432 applies those parsers to Speed, Acceleration, and MinSpeed. C++ Locomotor movement applies a mass-scaled per-frame acceleration and PhysicsBehavior integrates `m_vel += m_accel`, `pos += vel` without dt at PhysicsUpdate.cpp:633-662. Rust Common/src/common/ini/ini_locomotor.rs:491-525 matches these frame conversions; GameLogic/src/locomotor/ini_bridge.rs:85-103 transfers speed/acceleration unchanged into the native LocomotorTemplate while parsing MinSpeed/MinTurnSpeed to frame units. However GameLogic/src/object/update/ai_update_interface.rs:1651-1661, :1684-1695, and :1707-1716 pass `delta_time = 1/30` to native movement methods but do not pass the actual PhysicsBehavior object; apply_locomotor_result writes the returned position and derives velocity by dividing displacement by that dt at :1827-1834. GameLogic/src/locomotor/core_impl/move_dispatch.rs:465-480 then treats `current_speed` as per-second in `integrate_motive` (`vel += last_motive_accel * dt`, `pos += vel * dt`), despite the live caller obtaining forward speed from native physics and native template values being per-frame. A C++-authored constant speed v therefore advances v/30 rather than v in one logic tick, and an acceleration A advances by A/900 rather than A before integration. Existing `do_locomotor_explicit_goal_moves_owner_with_locomotor_like_cpp` only asserts positive displacement, so it cannot detect scale. Fix the native live boundary by either using the object PhysicsBehavior path with C++ per-frame force integration, or normalizing inputs/outputs once to host seconds with an explicit unit contract; preserve separate turning behavior and avoid a second dt conversion. Regression plan: use a parsed native Locomotor row with fixed Speed/Acceleration, invoke actual AIUpdateInterface::do_locomotor for exactly one logic tick from rest and from known velocity, and assert displacement/velocity deltas against CPP frame values; also compare angle turn rate. No source edits or test runs in this audit.
notes: 10/30 current explicit canonical UnitAI test now executes owned AI locomotor force followed by the receiving PhysicsBehavior phase; added actual frame assertion: velocity from rest equals applied acceleration, and it passes. C++ PhysicsUpdate.cpp633-661 agrees; this does not validate magnitude from parsed INI, nonzero initial velocity, turning, nor the older Core no-Physics adapter. The source finding predates owned physics-phase migration; do not blindly change dt or close based on this partial evidence.

title: Keep Main locomotor force integration in host-second units
description: A read-only source trace found two reachable Main host locomotor seams that mix per-frame C++ physics with the host MovementComponent per-second state. C++ Locomotor INI maps Speed through parseVelocityReal (dist/sec to dist/frame) and Acceleration/Braking through parseAccelerationReal (dist/sec² to dist/frame²): GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Locomotor.cpp:422-432 and Common/INI/INI.cpp:1709-1723. C++ PhysicsBehavior then integrates acceleration and position once per logic frame without multiplying by dt: Object/Update/PhysicsUpdate.cpp:633-662. Main intentionally converts native template max speed/acceleration back to host dist/sec and dist/sec² in Main/src/game_logic/locomotor_bootstrap.rs:842-861, then writes them to Object MovementComponent at :989-997; its primary path movement applies acceleration * dt in Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/movement.rs:1664-1707, which is unit-consistent. However the live ANGLE path calls Object::loco_update_move_towards_angle from world_tick/movement.rs:850-857; with min_speed > 0, Main object/physics.rs:679-697 calls apply_forward_speed_force. That helper labels acceleration as units/sec² but multiplies by frame_dt*30 (~1) then integrates the result directly into velocity at :1786-1807, followed by a second host-second blend of acceleration*dt at :1808-1820. title: Align Main path-grid cells to CPP absolute world coordinates
description:
## Evidence
Main PathfindingGrid::new_with_origin stores origin = GameLogic.world_min; world_to_grid currently casts (world - origin) / 10 and grid_to_world reconstructs origin + index * 10 (GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/pathfinding/grid_core.rs:177-190). GameLogic initializes symmetric extents such as world_min = -world_width/2 (game_logic/construct.rs:38,530), which need not be a multiple of the 10-unit path cell size. CPP Pathfinder::worldToGrid instead truncates absolute world/10 (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Include/GameLogic/AIPathfind.h:854-858); newMap separately floors terrain extent to absolute cell bounds (AIPathfind.cpp:4530-4532). For extent min -256, Rust maps world x=0 to relative cell 25, while CPP absolute cell 0 with map origin -26 corresponds to storage index 26. The Rust cell lattice is shifted by 4 world units versus CPP.

## Regression
Use a non-cell-aligned world extent (e.g. -256), place one obstacle at the CPP absolute-world-derived storage cell, and compare Rust world-to-cell, adjusted route waypoint, and blocker avoidance against worldToGrid + m_xOrigin + adjustCoordToCell. Include negative coordinates and exact map edge. Preserve truncation toward zero and CPP separately rounded path extent.

## Limits
This is source-grounded coordinate arithmetic; a live Main route differential is still needed. It is adjacent to, but distinct from, the loaded terrain/classification ownership issue in hq-i10n6.

title: Preserve C++ player-slot order in live AI updates and target selection
description: C++ updates AI through AI::update -> PlayerList::UPDATE (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/AI/AI.cpp:333-341); PlayerList::update visits every slot in ascending index order (Source/Common/RTS/PlayerList.cpp:221-229). Rust AIManager::update currently collects `ai_players.keys()` and peer targets from HashMaps (GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/ai/manager.rs:85-101), while update_enemy_assessment scans `GameLogic.players.keys()` (Main/src/ai/player_core.rs:1198-1200). HashMap iteration is randomized; on equal enemy scores the strict `<` keeps the first candidate, so Rust can choose a different target and run stateful AI/actions in an order unlike C++, and can vary between runs/insertion orders. Reproduce by creating two equal-distance enemies and two AI players, permuting registration/insertion order, then ticking the real Main GameLogic AI path; assert C++ numeric-slot tie winner and stable per-player action/queue ordering. Fix by explicitly processing player IDs in C++ slot order at every behavior-sensitive traversal (including peers/candidates), preserving fixed-frame cadence and excluding any claim that all PlayerList::update side effects are already ported.

title: Invalidate cached terrain GPU color when a pulse expires off draw window
description: Verified read-only path after hq-li1vu: TerrainVisualImpl::update_chunk_meshes only iterates chunk_ids_for_gpu_draw. A chunk uploaded while a pulse is active remains in chunk_meshes when it leaves that set (retain removes only deleted chunks). When the pulse expires, global had_dynamic_lights forces one static upload for the CURRENT draw set then becomes false. An old chunk outside that set keeps its lit GPU buffer. On return with unchanged chunk.geometry_revision/LOD and unchanged active texture slots, needs_mesh_upload is false, so record_chunk_draws reuses stale lit colors. ChunkManager's per-chunk dynamic_lit flag restores CPU vertex colors on return, but GPU upload colors are rebaked from base_colors only when an upload occurs; CPU color changes do not increment geometry_revision. Regression: uniform-texture heightmap, keep an edge chunk at same LOD while shifting draw window past it, light it and cache its GPU mesh, expire pulse while absent, restore window and assert one static GPU upload/color reset. Preserve C++ HeightMap.cpp m_priorEnable previous-bound restoration. A bounded fix can invalidate a per-chunk lighting revision on static restore or track per-mesh light epoch; avoid forcing all quiet-frame uploads.
notes:

Prefer a private GpuChunkMesh was_uploaded_with_dynamic_lights bit and force static reupload whenever that cached mesh is lit but current enabled-light list is empty, independent of global had_dynamic_lights. Record false after static upload. This keeps upload ownership with the GPU cache.

title: Give name-key registry and cached keys explicit game-instance ownership
description: NameKeyGenerator source audit hq-mw2kh confirms existing Rust Common NAME_KEY_STATE is Lazy<Mutex<NameKeyGeneratorState>> and public static APIs use one process-wide identity catalog. No real concurrency boundary justifies global synchronization; two game instances cannot independently initialize/reset namespaces safely, and cached StaticNameKey invalidation must preserve C++ initialization/allocation order. Follow AGENTS ownership contract: owner change, ambient accesses removed, original identity/RNG/save behavior, two-instance executable test, missing proof. Collision-order fix is independent and does not earn explicit ownership/instance isolation credit.
notes:
Current OCL regression (hq-nmxcp): Common src/common/name_key_generator.rs now allocates keys per thread, while the OCL store can move/share across threads. Equal numeric keys can name different strings. OCL private dictionary is being repaired to exact authored String identity, retaining all existing NameKey allocation calls for compatibility order. This removes OCL aliasing only; no registry ownership or serialized numeric-key isolation is claimed. Broader owned registry and cached-key migration remains this issue.
2026-10-09 current containing world_save11 reproduces skirmish_sides_make_no_team_slots_enemies_and_teammates_allies (Neutral vsEnemies) in /tmp/generals-rust-rng-main-world_save.log. Main authored string relation writer appears to match CPPGameLogic1332-1368; exact causal link is not established. Concrete existing key hazard: common/name_key_generator.rs108-111 has calling-thread TLS sequential namespace, but common/well_known_keys.rs7-9 uses process-global OnceCell numeric caches. A newly started test/worker thread can reuse cached ids from another namespace; a newly initialized uncached well-known key may collide with cached Dict keys and overwrite playerName/enemies/allies fields. Even test-threads=1 creates fresh per-test threads, so serial execution alone cannot prove identity consistency. Require actual dict keys/string/type/name/enemy/allies assertions before and after add_host_players_as_sides and application; isolated child-process vs containing suite and same-thread reset/key lifetime tests. This is a hypothesis for the new failure, not confirmed causal attribution. Do not add another TLS cached key/global mutex shortcut or relax relationship expectations; coordinate exact regression follow-up with owner-namespace migration.
close_reason: ALREADY_FIXED: NameKeyNamespace lives on CommonServices (common_services.rs name_key_namespace); NameKeyGenerator::* routes through common_services(). Two-instance NameKeyNamespace tests exist in name_key_generator.rs.

title: Keyboard repeat arbitration follows randomized HashMap order instead of original scan-code order
description: Original Keyboard.cpp:checkKeyRepeat scans key=0..255 and chooses first eligible key. Rust KeyboardState::update_repeat iterates randomized HashMap key_sequences and takes first eligible key. Keyboard KeyCode enum discriminants also differ from KeyDefs.h, so sorting enum discriminants is not a valid fix. Build original/Rust trace with simultaneous held keys, explicit scan-code mapping, wrapping frame counters and release/repress. Do not trust comment claiming a two-frame interval: original sequence assignment must be executed to derive actual repeats.
close_reason: Repeat arbitration fixed; compiled C++/Rust differential11124 cases and177984 frames passes with failing old-loop negative control.20 internal keyboard tests and macOS executable check pass; rustfmt, Ruff, LOC, unsafe and clean staged-export provenance gates pass. Explicit103-key mapping preserves Rust enum layout. Scope and remaining event/locale/message gaps documented in prior comment.

title: Single-instance startup differs from original mutex and races during lock creation
description: Full WinMain audit: original CreateMutex with GENERALS_GUID atomically excludes a second process. Rust single_instance.rs checks PID text before flock, removes a supposedly stale path, truncates before locking, and writes metadata through a second open. Concurrent launches can remove/recreate a locked inode while metadata is empty; Drop also unlinks the lock path. Developer mode admits a second process with a per-PID lock, unlike original unconditional mutex check. Main retains the guard in process-global OnceLock instead of its launch scope. Implement scoped guard held by entry point, atomic exclusion independent of PID text, and concurrent-process/crash-restart tests; preserve explicit development overrides only if authorized deviation.
close_reason: Implemented in 1dc0b569f; deterministic before/after race regression, 7 full-crate lock tests including process death, macOS executable check and all applicable gates pass. Windows path not executed on this host.

title: Focus reset adapter does not reach the GameClient keyboard receiving OS keys
description: During WinMain comparison, platform/unified.rs notify_input_reset delegates to SubsystemManager::notify_focus_change(false), which only resets InputSystemSubsystem. Main host_inject_game_client_key instead writes GameClient input::keyboard::THE_KEYBOARD via with_keyboard; no focus reset reaches it. C++ WM_SETFOCUS/WM_KILLFOCUS reset the actual TheKeyboard, including modifier/capslock state. Move/route actual keyboard ownership explicitly through the driving instance and test held-key/repeat/modifier state across focus; do not introduce another global reset adapter. Separate from hq-l6arz, which addresses the Main instance pressed-key set.
close_reason: Implemented actual keyboard ownership and focus reset in 1bade23ea: GameClient owns Keyboard by value; Main injects/resets and menu/gameplay update that same device. Removed THE_KEYBOARD/with_keyboard/KeyboardHandle and unnecessary lock. 18 internal keyboard tests including two-instance isolation and no stale repeats pass; 7 Main input tests pass. Focus preserves input clock. Capslock/localization remains explicitly tracked hq-drdca, repeat arbitration hq-9nepl, raw event/lifecycle hq-g0ltr; this closure is delivery/ownership only, not whole-keyboard parity.

Resource code contains bitmap loading and GameClient InputManager handles Ime::Commit, but neither is observed on the executable route. title: Platform quit message adapter logs instead of delivering MetaInstantQuit

title: [Team] tryToRecruit ranks by 3D host distance not C++ 2D XY
description:
## C++
`Team::tryToRecruit` (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/RTS/Team.cpp:2357-2370) ranks candidates with `dx = teamHome.x - pos.x; dy = teamHome.y - pos.y; dx*dx+dy*dy` — 2D ground plane only (C++ Y is north).

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/team/team_members.rs:241-264` same 2D XY: `dx = team_home.x - pos.x; dy = team_home.y - pos.y`.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/ai.rs:4958-4969` `try_to_recruit_excluding` uses `(pos - home).length_squared()` on host `Vec3` (Y is up). `team_home_or_base` (`:4809-4818`) converts leftover `Coord3D` as `Vec3::new(loc.x, loc.z, loc.y)`, so leftover Z/up is included in the rank. Height delta can flip who is nearest or push a default-team fallback past `maxDist`.

## Evidence
- C++ Team.cpp:2357-2370
- Leftover team_members.rs:241-264
- Live ai.rs:4809-4818, 4958-4969
- No existing bead on 2D vs 3D recruit distance (hq-mp3he / hq-1g58t / hq-cyk2g are other tryToRecruit gates, closed)

## Player-visible
Skirmish/script recruit steals the wrong matching unit on hills or when home Z is 0 and units sit on terrain height.
acceptance_criteria: Recruit ordering and max-distance checks use only the C++ ground-plane XY components; host height cannot change the selected unit; focused regression test passes; no unrelated recruitment behavior changes.
close_reason: Implemented and verified. Main library tests compile; 2D recruitment regression passes; current-version AI update snapshot round-trip preserves final settle, ignored obstacle, unit pass-through and command source; v1 compatibility defaults pass.

`GameLogic/src/ai/group.rs:1625-1641` `group_attack_team` fans `ai_attack_team` with `Arc<RwLock<Team>>`. `AIAttackSquadState::choose_victim` (`GameLogic/src/ai/states/attack.rs:1463-1565`) uses `get_machine_goal_squad()` + `get_live_object_ids()` — only that named team instance.

Script `host_script_attack_team` (`world_scripts/scripts_camera.rs:4600-4623`) first-picks a named-team member, then stamps `AIGroup.AttackTeam.{USA|China|GLA}` so the persist tick expands to the whole faction.

- Leftover group.rs:1625-1641; states/attack.rs:1463-1565

title: [Audio] Upgrade complete never plays ResearchSound or UnitSpecificSound
description:
## C++
`ProductionUpdate::update` PRODUCTION_UPGRADE complete (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/ProductionUpdate.cpp:888-917`) when the producer is locally controlled and the upgrade has a display name:
1. `AudioEventRTS sound = *upgrade->getResearchCompleteSound()` (`UpgradeTemplate` INI `ResearchSound`).
2. If `TheAudio->isValidAudioEvent(&sound)` → `setObjectID(us->getID())` + `TheAudio->addAudioEvent`.
3. Else `TheEva->setShouldPlay(EVA_UpgradeComplete)`.
4. Always then `sound = *upgrade->getUnitSpecificSound()` (INI `UnitSpecificSound`) + `setObjectID` + `TheAudio->addAudioEvent`.

Retail example leftover parse test: `Upgrade_AmericaRadar` `ResearchSound = RadarUpgradeComplete`, `UnitSpecificSound = RadarVanVoiceUpgrade`.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/object/production/production_update_complete.rs` `handle_upgrade_production_complete` (`:1441-1455`) is the leftover factory `ProductionUpdate` (`module_overrides/ai.rs` / `contain_module_overrides/production.rs` construct `ProductionUpdateCompleteModule`):
- `upgrade.get_research_sound()` non-empty → leftover `TheAudio.add_audio_event` on the producer.
- `upgrade.get_unit_specific_sound()` non-empty → leftover `TheAudio.add_audio_event` on the producer.

`GameLogic/src/upgrade/template.rs` parses both INI keys (`get_research_sound` / `get_unit_specific_sound`). Leftover host objects never enter leftover `OBJECT_REGISTRY`, so this path does not run on live.

## Live (wrong)
`GameLogic::apply_host_upgrade_complete` (`Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/object_ai_combat.rs:761-771`) only uses leftover `UpgradeTemplate::get_research_sound().is_valid()` as an EVA gate (hq-eg4f5): skip `try_eva_upgrade_complete` when ResearchSound is authored. It never queues ResearchSound or UnitSpecificSound. `complete_researched_upgrade` / `world_tick/production.rs` drain into this function. Closed hq-zbm8u only removed invented `UpgradeComplete` presentation SFX; closed hq-x7nw only parsed the INI keys.

## Player-visible
Finishing radar / composite armor / nuclear tanks etc. never plays the authored ResearchSound (e.g. RadarUpgradeComplete) and never plays the upgrade UnitSpecificSound (e.g. RadarVanVoiceUpgrade). EVA_UpgradeComplete is correctly suppressed when ResearchSound exists, so those upgrades go silent.

## Evidence
- C++ `ProductionUpdate.cpp:900-917`
- Leftover `production_update_complete.rs:1441-1455`
- Live `object_ai_combat.rs:761-771` (EVA XOR only; no `queue_audio_event` / leftover TheAudio add)
acceptance_criteria: A valid authored ResearchSound is queued on the producing object and suppresses EVA; an invalid or absent ResearchSound falls back to EVA; authored UnitSpecificSound is always queued; no generic replacement sound is invented; focused tests pass.
notes: Verified/closed live production-complete audio path (no code change needed this session; implementation already present and committed). Live path: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/object_ai_combat.rs apply_host_upgrade_complete lines 754-796 — local-player + non-empty DisplayName gate mirrors ProductionUpdate.cpp:888; valid ResearchSound queued via AudioEventRequest.with_object(producer_id) suppressing EVA, invalid/absent falls back to try_eva_upgrade_complete(EVA_UpgradeComplete); UnitSpecificSound always queued afterward on producer. Tests: authored_upgrade_sounds_queue_on_producer_and_suppress_eva PASSED, absent_research_sound_uses_eva_but_keeps_authored_unit_sound PASSED (cargo test -p generals_main --lib, both filters run individually against repaired workspace).
close_reason: Upgrade complete plays ResearchSound else EVA, always UnitSpecificSound per ProductionUpdate.cpp:888-917.

title: [ScriptCond] Live UNIT_HEALTH injects current max as InitialHealth
description:
## C++
`ScriptConditions::evaluateUnitHealth` (ScriptConditions.cpp:924-934) is `(curHealth*100 + initialHealth/2)/initialHealth` where `initialHealth = BodyModule::getInitialHealth()`. ActiveBody stores `m_initialHealth` from INI `InitialHealth` (often != `MaxHealth`). `setInitialHealth(percent)` only changes current HP; `setMaxHealth` overwrites both max and initial.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/object/body/active_body.rs` keeps `initial_health` separate from `max_health` (`get_initial_health` 2079-2083). Leftover `eval_unit_health` (executor/eval_named.rs:863-868) on the empty-registry live path uses host snapshot `obj.initial_health` with the C++ formula. `HostScriptQueryObject.initial_health` is that C++ InitialHealth field.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/scripts_camera.rs:527` injects `initial_health: obj.health.maximum.max(obj.max_health).max(1.0)` — current max, not leftover/C++ InitialHealth. Live spawn (`object/construct.rs`) seeds both current and max from `template.max_health` only. Map `objectInitialHealth` (`world_save.rs:170-175`) scales current HP and never stores a separate initial.

## Evidence
A unit with INI InitialHealth 80 / MaxHealth 100 at full authored start: C++/leftover percent = 100; live inject denominator 100 with current 80 → ~80%. After map objectInitialHealth=50 with InitialHealth==MaxHealth both agree; the INI mismatch and post-upgrade/veterancy cases do not.

## Player-visible
Campaign/skirmish UNIT_HEALTH scripts fire at the wrong HP percent whenever authored InitialHealth != live current max.

Not a duplicate of closed hq-rjnou (leftover eval formula, now leftover-right).
close_reason: Live UNIT_HEALTH injects leftover/C++ InitialHealth (not current max). Object stores initial_health from leftover ActiveBody INI; setMaxHealth overwrites it; setInitialHealth/objectInitialHealth only scales current HP.

title: [Guard] HijackGuard inner scan skips canHijackVehicle aircraft/drone gates
description:
## C++
`AIGuardMachine::lookForInnerTarget` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/AI/AIGuard.cpp:221-230`) for `isHijackGuard()` installs `PartitionFilterPossibleToHijack` + `ALLOW_ENEMIES`. That filter is `ActionManager::canHijackVehicle` (`ActionManager.cpp:829-887`): live, unshrouded, Enemies, KINDOF_VEHICLE, not KINDOF_AIRCRAFT, not KINDOF_DRONE, and a HijackedVehicleCrateCollide `wouldLikeToCollideWith`. Closest legal vehicle wins.

## Leftover (right)
`scan_guard_inner_target` (`GameLogic/src/ai/guard.rs:188-197`) uses `relationship_to == Enemies` then `TheActionManager::can_hijack_vehicle` (`action_manager.rs:1350-1392`), which ports the same aircraft/drone/shroud/collide gates.

No aircraft reject, no drone reject, no shroud, no HijackedVehicleCrateCollide. CommandButtonHunt `hunt_enter_action_ok` already rejects aircraft/drone; Guard HijackGuard does not.

A Guard-ordered Hijacker therefore acquires the closest Comanche/drone (KINDOF_VEHICLE) as nemesis and walks off the legal tank. Enter-hunt is already gated; Guard scan is not.

## Evidence
Not hq-h8azg (HijackGuard unused — closed; scan now runs). Not hq-wtvdj (EnterGuard canEnterObject). Not hq-3uwdw (hijack *action* ImmuneToCapture/drone/boat — the click/collide path, not Guard inner scan).

title: [Hunt] findClosestEnemy/guard ignore undetected-defector getRelationship
description:
## C++
`Object::getRelationship` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Object.cpp:1548-1568`):
- `getIsUndetectedDefector()` → `NEUTRAL` so the defector's AI does not auto-acquire and give away position
- `that->getIsUndetectedDefector()` → `ALLIES` so teammates treat the flashing defector as their own

`AI::findClosestEnemy` (`AI.cpp:579-622`) always runs `PartitionFilterLiveMapEnemies`, which requires `getRelationship == ENEMIES`. Guard `lookForInnerTarget` (`AIGuard.cpp:209`) uses `PartitionFilterRelationship ALLOW_ENEMIES` on the same `getRelationship`. Hunt and Guard therefore skip the defector and the defector skips hunting during the undetected window (defector crate / hijack / conversion).

## Leftover (right)
`Object::relationship_to` (`GameLogic/src/object/object_queries.rs:69-82`) applies the same two overrides before `Team::get_relationship`. Leftover hunt (`ai/states/hunt.rs` → `find_closest_enemy`) and leftover guard (`ai/guard.rs:190,211` `relationship_to`) inherit them.

## Live (wrong)
`GameLogic::object_relationship` / `object_relationship_from_owners` (`Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/object_queries.rs:450-525`) never consults `Object::is_undetected_defector`. Hunt `find_closest_enemy` (`world_tick/mood.rs:190-194`) uses that when both objects have owners. Guard `scan_guard_inner_target` (`world_objects/support_states.rs:446-468`) uses `host_guard_leftover_relationship` → the same owner map.

After a team flip, live hunt/guard treat the new owner as Enemies immediately: the defector auto-hunts old teammates (gives away position) and old teammates auto-hunt the flashing defector.

## Evidence
Not hq-kb4sr (converted units keep orders / skip radar-voice-kickout). Not hq-nde4y (Neutral civilians on Guard). Not stealthed-undetected beads (hq-29qjk / hq-am2jn).
close_reason: Live object_relationship, host_guard_leftover_relationship, and find_closest_enemy apply C++ Object::getRelationship undetected-defector overrides (self Neutral, that Allies).

title: [Phys/Bounce] Live motion-step bounce overwrites leftover 0-or-PI roll
description:
C++: `PhysicsBehavior::handleBounce` (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:505-512) on `vz < 0` rights with `setAngles(yaw, 0, zvec.Z>0 ? 0 : PI)` so inverted wrecks stay inverted (roll=PI). `testStunnedUnitForDestruction` then still sees a flip.

Live motion-step then overwrites it: `tick_physics_motion_step` (`physics_motion.rs:885-894`) after applying bounce force calls `right_physics_pitch_roll`, which rebuilds yaw-only (`setAngles(yaw,0,0)`). `handle_shock_ground_bounce` (`:958`) does the same. Leftover 0-or-PI righting never survives the live Euler.

Evidence: leftover `object/behavior/physics_bounce.rs:48-58`, C++ PhysicsUpdate.cpp:505-512, live `object/physics_motion.rs:573-580, 885-894, 956-958`.

title: [Locomotor] Live FACE leftover handleBehaviorZ unused — pose-Y then double Z
description:
C++: `Locomotor::locoUpdate_moveTowardsAngle` (Locomotor.cpp:847-896). If `getMinSpeed() > 0`, it projects a point along the goal heading and calls `locoUpdate_moveTowardsPosition` once (appearance mover + one `handleBehaviorZ` with real terrain). Else rotate + one `handleBehaviorZ`. Never a second Z pass.

Leftover: `maintain.rs:53-93` `loco_update_move_towards_angle` matches that: minSpeed delegates to leftover `move_towards` (single `handle_behavior_z_for` via leftover `get_surface_ht_at_pt`).

Live: `Object::loco_update_move_towards_angle` (`object/physics.rs:623-653`) applies a homemade rotate + `apply_forward_speed_force`, then calls `handle_behavior_z(p.y)` / `handle_behavior_z(us.y)` using the object's own altitude as surface. `world_tick/movement.rs:345-349` then always calls `apply_live_handle_behavior_z(obj, surface_y, None)` again. Leftover single-pass terrain Z is unused.

Evidence: leftover `locomotor/core_impl/maintain.rs:53-93`, leftover `behavior_z.rs:121-179`, live `object/physics.rs:623-653`, live `world_tick/movement.rs:342-349`.

close_reason: Live FACE leftover-marches leftover-terrain Z once: loco_update_move_towards_angle is XY-only; movement.rs apply_live_handle_behavior_z uses leftover_surface_ht. No pose-Y then double lift.

title: [Locomotor] Live march ignores leftover CloseEnoughDist3D
description:
C++: `AIUpdateInterface::getLocomotorDistanceToGoal` (AIUpdate.cpp:2448-2456) uses 3D center-to-goal when `m_curLocomotor->isCloseEnoughDist3D()` or `KINDOF_PROJECTILE`. `LocomotorTemplate::m_isCloseEnoughDist3D` is parsed from `CloseEnoughDist3D` and stamped onto `IS_CLOSE_ENOUGH_DIST_3D` (Locomotor.cpp:473, 640). That 3D remaining-path feeds approach-brake and arrival so diving missiles keep flying until they are actually at the last node, not merely above its XY.

Leftover: `ini_bridge.rs` copies `is_close_enough_dist_3d`. `Locomotor` sets `FLAG_CLOSE_ENOUGH_3D`. `ai_loco.rs:857-858` and leftover `path_following.rs` measure 3D length when the flag or projectile is set.

Live: `HostLocomotorBinding` / `apply_host_locomotor_binding` never bind the flag. `world_tick/movement.rs` waypoint-advance and `reached_target` always use 2D `horiz()`. `raise_on_path_dist_to_goal` only special-cases projectiles to skip the 2× IS_BRAKING latch, still using 2D distance.

Evidence: leftover `GameLogic/src/object/unit/ai_loco.rs:857`, leftover `locomotor/ini_bridge.rs:162`, live `locomotor_bootstrap.rs:276-281` (no 3D field), live `world_tick/movement.rs:442-446, 923`.

Player-visible: SCUD / neutron / other CloseEnoughDist3D or projectile locos treat “over the target” as arrived while still high, so they cut throttle / plant / detonate in the air instead of diving the last vertical stretch.
close_reason: Live march leftover-uses CloseEnoughDist3D: on_path_dist seeds leftover get_locomotor_distance_to_goal 3D to last node so diving missiles keep flying until actually at the node.

title: [PlaceEvent] Sneak-attack construction drops placement facing
description:
## C++
`PlaceEventTranslator.cpp:214-232` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/MessageStream/PlaceEventTranslator.cpp`): when the builder `ProductionUpdateInterface::getSpecialPowerConstructionCommandButton()` is set (sneak-attack construct), LMB confirm appends `MSG_DO_SPECIAL_POWER_AT_LOCATION` with special-power template ID, world, **placement angle**, options, and source object. `OCLSpecialPower::doSpecialPowerAtLocation` (`OCLSpecialPower.cpp:167-185`) forwards that angle into `ObjectCreationList::create(...)`, so the spawned tunnel faces the click-drag heading.

`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/cnc_game_engine/ui_commands.rs` `place_structure_from_ui` (~1845-1869): if leftover `get_pending_special_power()` matches the builder, the host queues `CommandType::DoSpecialPower { power_type: SneakAttack, target: PowerTarget::Location(location) }` with **no facing**. `queue_sneak_attack` (`world_scripts/ambush_leaflet.rs:619`) takes only `target_position`. hq-4zy8 fixed the DozerConstruct vs DoSpecialPower branch but did not thread placement angle.

## Evidence

Leftover: `DoSpecialPowerAtLocation(..., world, angle, ...)`.
Live: `PowerTarget::Location(location)` only.
close_reason: Sneak-attack place confirm now threads TheInGameUI placement angle through PowerTarget::LocationFacing into queue_sneak_attack_facing; TunnelStart and spawned tunnel set_orientation keep the click-drag heading.

title: [Weapon] leftover RATIONALIZE getAttackRange/isContactWeapon unused — live peels raw range + #else FUDGE
description:
## C++
`Weapon.cpp:55` `#define RATIONALIZE_ATTACK_RANGE` is on.

`WeaponTemplate::getAttackRange` (`Weapon.cpp:437-445`): `m_attackRange * RANGE bonus - PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE_F*0.25` (cell=10 → −2.5).
`getMinimumAttackRange` (`Weapon.cpp:454-462`): `m_minimumAttackRange - 2.5`, clamped ≥ 0.
`isContactWeapon` (`Weapon.cpp:531-537`): `(m_attackRange - 2.5) < 10` → contact when authored range < 12.5.

The `#else` `ATTACK_RANGE_FUDGE=1.05` branch is not compiled.

## Leftover (RIGHT)
`GameLogic/src/weapon/template.rs`:
- `get_attack_range` / `get_minimum_attack_range` apply the same −¼ cell undersize.
- `is_contact_weapon` uses `(attack_range - 2.5) < 10`.

## Live (contradicts leftover)
`Main/src/game_logic/thing.rs` `weapon_from_store` copies `wt.attack_range` / `wt.minimum_attack_range` raw — never calls leftover `get_attack_range` / `get_minimum_attack_range`.

`Main/src/game_logic/weapon_bootstrap/pitch_range.rs` `is_contact_weapon_range`: `attack_range * 1.05 < 10` (C++ `#else`). `host_is_contact_weapon_name` peels raw store `attack_range` then applies that FUDGE; leftover `is_contact_weapon` is unused.

Authored range 10: leftover/C++ is contact (7.5 < 10); live is not (10.5 < 10). Live fire/getAble also keep +2.5 extra reach vs leftover `get_attack_range`.

playable_claim stays false.
close_reason: Live peels leftover RATIONALIZE getAttackRange/getMinimumAttackRange/isContactWeapon. weapon_from_store uses leftover get_attack_range/get_minimum_attack_range (−¼ cell). is_contact_weapon_range uses (authored-2.5)<10 not #else FUDGE 1.05. host_is_contact_weapon_name peels leftover is_contact_weapon. Callers that pass already-undersized weapon.range use is_contact_effective_range (effective < 10) so authored 12.5 stays non-contact.

title: [Locomotor] leftover CloseEnoughDist3D unused — live arrival is always 3D
description:

`Locomotor.cpp:640` ctor: `setFlag(IS_CLOSE_ENOUGH_DIST_3D, m_template->m_isCloseEnoughDist3D)`.
`AIUpdate.cpp:2448-2456` `getLocomotorDistanceToGoal`: if `isCloseEnoughDist3D() || KINDOF_PROJECTILE`, use `FROM_CENTER_3D`; else 2D path/flight-dist (hover/aircraft) or `distAlongPath`.
Retail SCUDStormMissileLocomotor authors `CloseEnoughDist3D = Yes`.

## Leftover (RIGHT)
`Locomotor::new` stamps `FLAG_CLOSE_ENOUGH_3D` from the template (`core_impl/locomotor.rs:115-116`).
`UnitAIUpdate::get_locomotor_distance_to_goal` (`ai_loco.rs:857-858`) uses 3D length only when the flag or projectile; otherwise 2D / aircraft flight-dist / path remaining.
`path_following.rs` / `path_follow.rs` advance waypoints with 3D length only when `is_close_enough_dist_3d()`.

## Live (unused / contradicts)
`HostLocomotorBinding` has `close_enough_dist` but no 3D flag (`locomotor_bootstrap.rs:276-277`).
`apply_host_locomotor_binding` never stamps a 3D metric (`locomotor_bootstrap.rs:993-995`).
`Object::update_movement` arrival is always `current_pos.distance(target_pos)` (host Y-up 3D) (`object/update.rs:426-427`).
`SCUD_STORM_MISSILE_CLOSE_ENOUGH_DIST_3D` is an honesty constant only — never read by march.

Ground units on slopes therefore arrive on 3D hypotenuse; missiles that author CloseEnoughDist3D have no live flag (they only look right because live is always 3D). Leftover `get_locomotor_distance_to_goal` is never called.

playable_claim: false
close_reason: Live arrival leftover-uses CloseEnoughDist3D: host_locomotor_distance_to_goal is 2D unless flag/projectile; keep_goal_y keeps last-node Y so 3D remaining is not flattened to 2D.

title: [Stealth] Live MOVING destalth ignores leftover MoveThresholdSpeed
description:
## C++
`StealthUpdate::allowedToStealth` (StealthUpdate.cpp:389-392) destalths only when `STEALTH_NOT_WHILE_MOVING` and `physics->getVelocityMagnitude() > m_stealthSpeed`. `m_stealthSpeed` is INI `MoveThresholdSpeed` (`parseVelocityReal`, StealthUpdate.cpp:79). Pathfinder retail is **3**.

## Leftover
`GameLogic/src/stealth_update.rs` parses `MoveThresholdSpeed` into `stealth_speed` and `allowed_to_stealth_runtime` refuses cloak when `physics.get_velocity().length() > stealth_speed`. Same check in `object/behavior/stealth_update.rs` and `object/update/stealth_update.rs`.

## Live
`pathfinder_stealth_desired` / `stealth_mines.rs` Pathfinder + Sentry + grant recloak use a boolean (`AIState::Moving|AttackMoving` or `status.moving`). `PATHFINDER_MOVE_THRESHOLD_SPEED = 3.0` is honesty-only — never compared to velocity. Leftover `allowed_to_stealth_runtime` is not called.

## Player-visible
Pathfinder (and other MOVING-forbidden cloak) destalths on the move order, even while speed is still below MoveThresholdSpeed. C++/leftover stay cloaked until actual velocity exceeds the threshold; a sliding stop above 3 also destalths in leftover but not live.
close_reason: Live MOVING destalth now leftover-destalths only when leftover velocity exceeds leftover MoveThresholdSpeed (allowed_to_stealth_runtime), not AIState/status.moving.

title: [SpecialPower] Object-target click skips leftover FOGGED ActionManager gate
description:
C++ path + behavior: `ActionManager::canDoSpecialPowerAtObject` (`ActionManager.cpp:1558-1590`) after module/ready always calls `isObjectShroudedForAction` (`ActionManager.cpp:76-102`): human controlling player, not `CMD_FROM_SCRIPT`, `target->getShroudedStatus >= OBJECTSHROUD_FOGGED` → FALSE. Applies to every object-target special (CashHack, Defector, Battleship, MD laser, Capture, TNT, Lotus steal/disable, Hacker disable, Disguise, charges, BoobyTrap) before the type switch.

Leftover path + behavior: `TheActionManager::can_do_special_power_at_object` (`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/action_manager.rs:680-701`) matches: `target.is_effectively_dead()` then `is_object_shrouded_for_action` (Human + not FromScript + shroud >= Fogged) before the type match. Host-facing leftover already exists for location shroud (`can_do_special_power_at_location_for_player`); the object-shroud arm was never replayed on live.

Live path + behavior: `leftover_can_do_special_power_at_object` (`Main/src/command_executor/special_power.rs:88-104`) only special-cases Battleship `!= ALLIES` and MD laser `VEHICLE && ENEMIES`; `_ => !location_target_only`. No dead/FOGGED preamble. `GameLogic::is_object_shrouded_for_action` (`world_objects/object_queries.rs:953-976`) already ports C++ `isObjectShroudedForAction` and is used by Enter; special-power object clicks never call it. Host object shroud is populated (`spawn_templates.rs` sets FOGGED on seen immobile buildings), so a fogged supply center / tank ghost still accepts CashHack / Defector / MD laser / Battleship / Capture / TNT.

Evidence: leftover + C++ share the FOGGED object-click refuse; live leftover_can_do is the host replay of those leftover gates and omits the common preamble. Not hq-xvak4 (location cell shroud / underwater) or hq-hr2ae (NEED_TARGET_POS unit-under-cursor remapped to location).
close_reason: Live leftover_can_do_special_power_at_object now applies leftover/C++ dead + FOGGED is_object_shrouded_for_action preamble before the type switch. Object-target clicks on fogged/dead targets refuse.

description:

- Save `physics->getAllowToFall()`, force `setAllowToFall(false)` around `aiFollowPath` / `adjustToPossibleDestination`, then restore. Comment (cpp:963-970): amphibious transports unload ~3ft off the ground; without the gate riders go airborne, skip pathfind, and stack on the same point.

If the hull is above terrain it only sets `allow_to_fall = true` (TransportContain::onRemoving airborne) and never clears it for the pathfind adjust. title: [Pathfind] Non-final leftover isLinePassable unused — live always A*
description:
## C++
AIUpdateInterface::computePath (AIUpdate.cpp:1691-1694): if !m_isFinalGoal && Pathfinder::isLinePassable(obj, surfaces, layer, pos, dest, false, true) then computeQuickPath. requestPath(..., false) from AIAttackPursueState (AIStates.cpp:2872), requestSafePath (isFinalGoal=false), and AIInternalMoveToState when !getAdjustsDestination().

AIUpdateInterface::computePath (AIUpdate.cpp:1663-1671): TheTerrainLogic->getMaximumPathfindExtent. If dest is off that region AND the unit start is also off it, computeQuickPath (two-node start+dest, AIUpdate.cpp:1624-1630). Off-map units cannot A* so they get a straight line onto/across the map.

title: [Cam] ROLLING_AVERAGE persists onto next path
description:
C++ W3DView::cameraModRollingAverage (W3DView.cpp:2740-2746) writes m_mcwpInfo.rollingAverageFrames, but W3DView::setupWaypointPath (W3DView.cpp:2865) hard-resets rollingAverageFrames=1 at the start of every new path (moveCameraTo, moveCameraAlongWaypointPath, resetCamera). An idle CAMERA_MOD_SET_ROLLING_AVERAGE is never observable on a later path; it only smooths a path already in flight (moveAlongWaypointPath avgFactor, W3DView.cpp:3126).

Leftover View::camera_mod_rolling_average (GameClient/src/display/view.rs:2607-2611) applies only to an existing camera_path and drops the request when idle. CameraPath::new initializes rolling_average_frames:1 (cinematic_camera.rs:426). No pending arm.

Live GameLogic::apply_script_camera_mod_rolling_average (Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/scripts_camera.rs:5793-5803) stores script_camera_pending_rolling_average_frames when no path is active, and start_camera_path_move (scripts_camera.rs:5505-5507) applies those frames to the NEXT path. Test camera_mod_rolling_average_arms_for_next_camera_path encodes the wrong behavior.

Observable: script issues CAMERA_MOD_SET_ROLLING_AVERAGE(N) while idle, then later MOVE_CAMERA_ALONG_WAYPOINT_PATH — C++/leftover path runs unsmoothed (rolling=1); live path runs with N-frame lagged focus.
close_reason: Idle CAMERA_MOD_SET_ROLLING_AVERAGE no longer arms the next path; apply only to in-flight script_camera_path (C++ setupWaypointPath reset / leftover drop).

title: [Physics] Live onCollide immobile test uses !can_move not KINDOF_IMMOBILE
description:
## C++
`PhysicsBehavior::onCollide` (`PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1221-1222`) uses `other->isKindOf(KINDOF_IMMOBILE)` only. Dead, EMP-disabled, deployed, docked, or garrisoned mobiles stay mobile: `processCollision` (usually no stiffness bounce). Immobile mass cheat is 999999; crash/stiffness path is buildings/trees/props.

## Leftover
`physics_collide.rs:144` `other_immobile = other.is_kind_of(KindOf::Immobile)`. Same KindOf gate as C++.

## Live
`GameLogic::try_physics_collide` (`world_tick/physics.rs:242-246`) and `apply_immobile_collide_bounce` (`:602-606`) classify other as immobile via:
`KindOf::Structure || KindOf::Structure /* immobile residual */ || !can_move()`.
`Object::can_move` (`object/orders.rs:5-19`) is not C++ `isMobile`: it also requires `is_alive`, `!deployed`, `!is_disabled()`, `!flailing`, and not Docked/Garrisoned.

So a tank hitting a dead wreck, EMP'd Humvee, deployed Tomahawk, or garrisoned infantry takes the building stiffness/crash path. C++/leftover keep those as mobile-mobile `processCollision`. Live has `KindOf::Immobile` (used in crash evaluate) but the pair-loop immobile test never reads it.

## Evidence
Leftover-right / live-wrong. Not a closed dup of hq-exasi (living AI bounce off real immobile), hq-yunv0 (stiffness zeros vel), hq-owowd (dead wrecks skip collide).
close_reason: Live try_physics_collide, apply_immobile_collide_bounce, and evaluate_vehicle_crash_into now classify other as immobile via KindOf::Immobile only (C++ PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1221-1222 / leftover physics_collide.rs:144). Dead, EMP, deployed, docked, or garrisoned mobiles stay processCollision. Test: collide_immobile_is_kindof_immobile_not_can_move.

title: [Locomotor] Live FACE is one-frame yaw not ANGLE-goal locoUpdate
description:
## C++
`AIFaceState` (`AIStates.cpp:7403-7455`) sets `m_canTurnInPlace = curLoco->getMinSpeed()==0`. Each update until `|relAngle| < ~2°`:
- turn-in-place → `setLocomotorGoalOrientation` (`AIUpdate.cpp:2228-2230` calls `locoUpdate_moveTowardsAngle`)
- else (Wings/Thrust minSpeed>0) → `setLocomotorGoalPositionExplicit` so the unit flies a curve toward the face point.

`locoUpdate_moveTowardsAngle` (`Locomotor.cpp:847-896`): stun return; if minSpeed>0 invent a point `2*minSpeed` along the heading and `locoUpdate_moveTowardsPosition`; else rotate + `handleBehaviorZ`.

## Leftover

`AIUpdateInterface::do_locomotor` `LocoGoalType::Angle` → `loco_update_move_towards_angle` (`maintain.rs:48-86`).

## Live
`GameLogic::private_face_position` / `private_face_object` (`world_tick/physics.rs:758-791`) call `Object::face_position` (`object/rtb.rs:740-746`) once: `rotate_towards_position` and return true.
- No persist-until-faced Face state (script FACE turns one `maxTurnRate` slice).
- No `canTurnInPlace` (jets spin in place instead of flying toward the point).
- `loco_update_move_towards_angle` exists (`object/physics.rs:623-654`) but is only called from a unit test, never from Face/script FACE.

## Evidence
Leftover-right / live-wrong. Not a closed dup of hq-rpufb (FACE leftover-only, closed when host started moving), hq-2zqa (snap-rotate, closed after `rotate_towards_position`), hq-ixce (Face xfer).

title: [Hunt] findClosestEnemy ranks by center not FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D
description:
## C++
`AI::findClosestEnemy` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/AI/AI.cpp:651-681`) ranks with `FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D`:
- no AttackPriorityInfo: `getClosestObject(..., FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D, filters)`
- with priority: `iterateObjectsInRange(..., FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D, ...)` then `getDistanceSquared(..., FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D)` for the priority-distance modifier.
Bounding-sphere 2D is center XY minus both objects' bounding-circle radii (0 if hulls overlap). Hunt (`AIHuntState::update`) and mood acquire (`getNextMoodTarget`) both call this.

## Leftover
`AI::find_closest_enemy` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/mod.rs:1787-1791`) uses `ThePartitionManager::get_distance_squared(..., FROM_BOUNDING_SPHERE_2D)`. Helper `object_queries.rs:583-591` subtracts both bounding-circle radii, matching C++.

## Live
`GameLogic::find_closest_enemy` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/mood.rs:223-226`) ranks with raw center-to-center XZ:
```
let dx = opos.x - me_pos.x;
let dz = opos.z - me_pos.z;
let dist = (dx * dx + dz * dz).sqrt();
```
No radius subtract. Hunt (`ai_authority.rs` Patrolling) and mood (`get_next_mood_target`) both use this.

## Evidence
Hunt/mood closest-first among mixed sizes picks the nearer *center*, not the nearer hull. A large building 200wu center / 50wu radius is 150wu bounding-sphere; infantry 180wu center / 5wu radius is 175wu. C++/leftover attack the building first; live attacks the infantry. Not hq-ta2g (leftover crate partition, closed), hq-cwobf (attack *range*), or hq-q7tog (guard FROM_CENTER_2D).
close_reason: Live find_closest_enemy now ranks (and applies the priority-distance modifier) with leftover FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D via Object::distance_to_object: center XZ minus both bounding-circle radii, 0 if hulls overlap. Hunt and mood acquire both call this. Mixed-size case: building 200/r50 (hull 145) beats infantry 180/r5 (hull 170).

title: [Weapon] chooseBest lock unused — live combat select falls through temp lock
description:
## C++
`WeaponSet::chooseBestWeaponForTarget` (WeaponSet.cpp:782-783): `if (isCurWeaponLocked()) return TRUE` — current slot stays locked until someone unlocks. FireCurrentWeapon then fires that slot; a reloading FireWeapon/flashbang/snipe waits, it does not auto-choose PRIMARY.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/weapon/weapon_set.rs:683-685` same early return. Leftover fire uses `current_weapon`.

## Live (wrong)
`GameLogic::choose_best_weapon_for_target` (`world_tick/physics.rs:849-850`) does honor lock.

The live combat tick does not. `update_combat` (`world_tick/combat.rs:275-276`) calls `select_combat_weapon_slot`, which (`object/weapons.rs:485-499`) returns the locked slot only when ready+in-range; `LockedTemporarily` "may fall through if clip empty / not ready" into PreferMostDamage auto-choose.

Ranger FireWeapon flashbang / Jarmen snipe / MD laser (LOCKED_TEMPORARILY) mid-reload therefore fires PRIMARY instead of waiting on the locked slot.

## Evidence
Leftover crate is RIGHT. Live should leftover-apply the lock early-return in `select_combat_weapon_slot` (the path `update_combat` actually fires) instead of re-choosing while the temp lock is held.
close_reason: select_combat_weapon_slot leftover-applies choose_best_locked_slot; update_combat FireCurrentWeapon-waits on locked unready slot instead of PreferMostDamage PRIMARY.

title: [Weapon] chooseBest ground attack never leftover-resets PRIMARY
description:
## C++
`WeaponSet::chooseBestWeaponForTarget` (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/WeaponSet.cpp:782-790) returns immediately if `isCurWeaponLocked()`. Otherwise `victim == NULL` (attack-ground / no object) sets `m_curWeapon = PRIMARY_WEAPON` and returns TRUE. Comment: lock is checked first for attack-ground powers; otherwise only Primary attacks the ground.

AIAttackState re-runs chooseBest every frame, so an unlocked unit that just auto-chose SECONDARY (Humvee TOW, Ranger flashbang vs infantry) force-attacking ground fires PRIMARY.

## Leftover (right)

title: [SpecialPower] Location-power unit click skips leftover ActionManager gates
description:
## C++
`CommandTranslator::issueSpecialPowerCommand` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/MessageStream/CommandXlat.cpp:1031-1078`):
- `COMMAND_OPTION_NEED_OBJECT_TARGET` → `MSG_DO_SPECIAL_POWER_AT_OBJECT` after `isValidObjectTarget`.
- `NEED_TARGET_POS` → always `MSG_DO_SPECIAL_POWER_AT_LOCATION` (unit under the cursor is only the optional "object in way" id; the command is still at-location).
- else → `MSG_DO_SPECIAL_POWER`.

`CommandButton::isValidToUseOn` (`ControlBar.cpp:640-648`) for `NEED_TARGET_POS` calls `ActionManager::canDoSpecialPowerAtLocation` (using the target object's position if no explicit loc). `canDoSpecialPowerAtObject` (`ActionManager.cpp:1558-1816`) returns FALSE for location-only powers (DaisyCutter / A10 / Frenzy / Paradrop / CrateDrop / PUC / Spectre / Artillery / Nuke / Ambush / Leaflet / GPS / Repair / Sneak / Cleanup / …). `canDoSpecialPowerAtLocation` (`ActionManager.cpp:1439-1523`) refuses paradrop/crate-drop underwater and ~30 damaging powers on `CELLSHROUD_SHROUDED`.

## Leftover (right)
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/action_manager.rs` `can_do_special_power_at_object` (622-772) matches C++: location-only types return false (`:721-765`). `special_power_at_location_ok` (`:117-214`) matches C++ underwater + shroud. `can_do_special_power_at_location_for_player` is the live Location helper.

## Live (wrong)
`command_system/system_impl.rs:250-256` `CommandMode::SpecialPower` converts any `context.target_object` into `PowerTarget::Object` — it never consults leftover/C++ `NEED_TARGET_POS` vs `NEED_OBJECT_TARGET`.

`command_executor/special_power.rs` `leftover_can_do_special_power_at_object` (`:88-104`) only implements Battleship (`relationship != ALLIES`) and MD/Howitzer laser (`VEHICLE && ENEMIES`). Everything else is `_ => true`.

`leftover_can_do_special_power_at_location` (`:67-83`) runs only for `PowerTarget::Location` (`:251-270`). A unit-under-cursor click therefore:
1. becomes `PowerTarget::Object`
2. skips leftover location shroud/underwater gates
3. consumes the charge and fires at the object's current position

hq-xvak4 closed the Location-only path. hq-i9iw1 / hq-gufjz / hq-4jxbc are Battleship / Baikonur / MD-laser object gates, not this remaining NEED_TARGET_POS bypass.

## Player-visible
Clicking an enemy (or any unit) in black shroud with A10 / Fuel Air Bomb / nuke / artillery / Frenzy / PUC / Spectre / leaflet / GPS / repair / sneak / ambush still spends the superweapon and fires. Clicking a unit in water with paradrop / crate-drop / tank-paradrop likewise fires. C++/leftover refuse those clicks (or treat them as location clicks that fail the shroud/underwater gate).
close_reason: Live NEED_TARGET_POS unit clicks leftover-gate as AT_LOCATION: leftover special_power_is_location_target_only (canDoSpecialPowerAtObject FALSE types with canDoSpecialPowerAtLocation underwater/shroud/on-map). CommandMode::SpecialPower emits PowerTarget::Location; execute_special_power rewrites leftover Object clicks to Location then leftover can_do_special_power_at_location_for_player. Battleship/laser/Baikonur stay object. Shrouded A10/nuke/paradrop-in-water no longer consume. playable_claim stays false.

None of them call any request_host_*; executor/mod.rs defines no HostScript*Enter/Garrison/Exit request variant at all.

## Live (wrong)
Main runs the leftover ScriptEngine (engine.update in scripts_camera.rs:4148) and dispatches these actions through the leftover executor, but leftover OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty on the player path (dual_world_registry_unavailable == OBJECT_REGISTRY.is_empty, Wave 249-445 empty-gate residuals), leftover TeamFactory/Player object lists carry no live objects, so every tracker/registry lookup fails and each action silently returns Success. Contrast: TEAM_LOAD_TRANSPORTS got request_host_script_load_transports (hq-45m90) and do_named_follow_waypoints in the same file queues request_host_script_follow_waypoints — this family was left out.

close_reason: Leftover do_named/team/player enter/garrison/exit now request_host_script_garrison_enter when OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty; live apply_host_garrison_enter_exit_script_requests drains into leaveGroup+NORMAL+aiEnter/Evacuate/Exit (nearest-building fill + player garrison/ungarrison). title: [Pathfind] findAttackPath A* never applies leftover LOS_TERRAIN
description:

For a mobile attacker with a current weapon, `!w->isClearGoalFiringLineOfSightTerrain(...)` returns blocked immediately. Immobile attackers skip terrain LOS (cannot path around). `findAttackPath` uses this per candidate firing cell, so a ridge-blocked cell is rejected and A* keeps searching for a terrain-clear shot.

`pathfind_complete/attack_path.rs` `is_attack_view_blocked_by_obstacle` (453-472) implements the same weapon `is_clear_goal_firing_line_of_sight_terrain` / `_pos` gate and Immobile skip. `find_attack_path` calls it for every in-range candidate.

No weapon terrain LOS during the search. `world_save.rs` `assign_unit_attack_path` (1950-1966) post-filters only the chosen last cell; if terrain occludes it, the whole attack path is discarded and the unit falls back to `adjustToPossibleDestination` + path-to-target.

## Evidence

title: [Save] AI BuildList object binding never persisted
description:
## C++
`BuildListInfo::xfer` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Map/SidesList.cpp:990-1023`) writes `m_objectID`, `m_objectTimestamp`, `m_underConstruction`, gatherer IDs, `m_automaticallyBuild`, and `m_priorityBuild` (v2 also `m_currentGatherers`). `Player::xfer` (`Player.cpp:4124-4176`) snapshots every pad.

`AIPlayer::processBaseBuilding` / `AISkirmishPlayer`:
- `objectID != INVALID_ID` means the pad already owns a live building or scaffold — skip starting a second one; `aiResumeConstruction` continues the same scaffold.
- `objectID == INVALID_ID && timestamp > 0` is the rebuild-delay clock (already filed as hq-05vhe).
- `m_priorityBuild` is the script `BUILD_SPECIFIC_BUILDING` stamp; automatic pads never start via `canMakeUnit(dozer, NULL)`.

After load the AI must still know which pad owns which object, whether that object is mid-construction, and whether a script stamped priority.

## Leftover (right)
`Player::xfer` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/rts/player.rs:4146-4363`) already writes the same table: `object_id`, `object_timestamp`, `under_construction`, gatherers, `automatically_build`, `priority`.

## Live (wrong)
`AIPlayerQueuePersist` AITQ v4 (`Main/src/save_load/snapshot/ai_player_queue_persist.rs`) only stores `building_rebuild_counts` (hq-49v5x) and `building_destroyed_at_times` (hq-05vhe). `AIPlayer::apply_queue_persist` (`Main/src/ai.rs:613-630`) comments explicitly: write remaining spend / rebuild-delay clock only; **do not rebind pad object_id or under-construction**.

`restore_players_from_save` rebuilds `AIPlayer` via `add_ai_player` → `initialize` → `setup_base_layout` (all pads `object_id=None`, `is_built=false`, `is_priority=false`). `retain_queue_object_ids` never touches `building_queue`. `rebind_after_world_reset` / `on_game_loaded` **clears** `object_id` and `is_built`. There is no post-load scan that rebinds pads to restored world objects by template/position.

## Player-visible
1. Mid-construction AI buildings: `resume_interrupted_construction` cannot find the scaffold (`object_id` lost). Underpowered AI then starts a **second** power plant because `power_under_construction` is only detected via `building.object_id`.
2. Already-built pads: `select_priority_or_power_build` sees `object_id=None` and `is_built=false`. Automatic pads still skip, but power pads (`automatic_build || is_under_powered`) and any `is_priority` stamp start **duplicate** construction next to the restored building.
3. Scripted `BUILD_SPECIFIC_BUILDING` stamps (`is_priority`) are not in AITQ, so after load the AI forgets the requested pad.

hq-49v5x / hq-05vhe closed only remaining rebuilds and the delay clock. hq-05vhe close reason: "restore writes that clock only (not object_id/under_construction)".
close_reason: AITQ v5 persists BuildList object_id, is_built, and is_priority; apply_queue_persist rebinds pads after layout rebuild; retain drops stale IDs

close_reason: live queueUpgrade / add_upgrade_to_queue / find_upgrade_producer leftover-walk CommandSet via object_can_produce_upgrade (ControlBar getCommandButton + INI Upgrade= + override); Barracks cannot research SupplyLines

title: [Physics] Live Y Euler applies leftover lift without leftover gravity
description:

## Leftover (right)

Two host Y-up paths break the pairing:
1. `world_tick/physics.rs:1001-1008` `apply_live_handle_behavior_z` does `vel.y += lift_a; pos.y += vel.y` and never adds leftover gravity. At preferred height leftover lift is `-gravity` (~+0.0711/frame), so hover/wings climb instead of holding.
2. `object/physics_motion.rs:776-786` `tick_physics_motion_step` skips `apply_gravitational_forces` *and* the `physics_accel.y` integrate for `flying_loco_aircraft` (airborne_target aircraft that are not falling/shocked). C++ has no aircraft exception.

Player-visible: helicopters/jets drift up while hovering or circling; aircraft that lose lift do not fall.

## Evidence
Not a rehash of closed `hq-8vhks` (no gravity at all) — gravity was added, then flying was excepted and the leftover lift integrate still omits gravity. Deduped all beads including closed; no flying-skip / lift-without-gravity issue remains open.
close_reason: apply_live_handle_behavior_z now applyGravitationalForces + integrate lift so leftover calcLiftToUseAtPt (desired-gravity) holds hover. tick_physics_motion_step applies gravity for dead/disabled/non-Z-motive aircraft (C++ has no flying skip); living Z-motive already Euler'd lift+gravity on the host march path.

title: [Locomotor] Live blockedBy drops leftover near-goal, path-priority, and reverse skip
description:
## C++
`AIUpdate.cpp:1272-1376` `blockedBy`:
- within one pathfind cell of the goal cell → not blocked
- `isMovingBackwards` → not blocked
- stacked in the same cell → `hasHigherPathPriority` (dozer > vehicle > infantry, then heading, then lower ObjectId)
- off-angle closing pair → higher-priority unit yields (`hasHigherPathPriority` → FALSE)

`hasHigherPathPriority` is `AIUpdate.cpp:1191-1228`.

## Leftover (right)
`collision_system.rs:623-698` ports those four gates (`path_destination` cell, `moving_backwards`, `has_higher_path_priority` same-cell and off-angle). `ai_update_interface.rs:2230-2296` has the near-goal + path-priority yield (reverse skip lives on the collision_system path).

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/object/physics.rs:172-232` `ai_blocked_by` is explicitly fail-closed vs the leftover/C++ matrix:
- no near-goal ignore → units jam in the last cell
- no `moving_backwards` skip → reversing trucks still block
- same-cell uses `self.id.0 > other.id.0` instead of leftover `has_higher_path_priority`
- off-angle always `return false` (`// Off-angle residual: not blocked unless head-on closing`) so leftover heading yield never runs

Player-visible: destination pile-ups, stacked dozer/vehicle/infantry yield by id not kind, crossing traffic always passes through.

## Evidence
Deduped all beads including closed. `hq-8y2zz` was crush ally, `hq-fyn6i` was moveAllies radius — not this leftover blockedBy matrix. Do not treat leftover infantry-infantry always-false as leftover-right (C++ uses `dot<=0.25`; live already matches that).
close_reason: Live ai_blocked_by leftover-honors near-goal cell ignore, moving_backwards skip, has_higher_path_priority same-cell (dozer>vehicle>infantry then heading then lower id), and off-angle higher-priority yield. Infantry-infantry keeps C++ dot<=0.25.

title: [Locomotor] Live blocked speed skips leftover formation 0.55 crowd factor

title: [Team] selectTeamToBuild arms TeamSeconds on reinforce and multiplies by difficulty
description:

title: [Dozer] Idle never resumes a parked REPAIR task
description:
## C++
`DozerPrimaryStateMachine` idleConditions (`DozerAIUpdate.cpp:1258-1281`) are `isBuildMostImportant` → BUILD, `isRepairMostImportant` → REPAIR, `isFortifyMostImportant` → FORTIFY. `isRepairMostImportant` (`:1326-1350`) is AI idle && `getMostRecentCommand()==REPAIR`. `newTask` (`:1955-1963`) cancels only a pending task of the *same* type, so a BUILD while Repairing (or REPAIR while Building) parks the other slot. When the dozer goes idle, the primary machine immediately resumes the most-recent pending task of either kind.

## Leftover (right)
`dozer_ai_update.rs:1046-1085` `update()`: when `dozer_task` is none and `current_task==Invalid`, `current_task = get_most_recent_command()` (Build/Repair/Fortify by order_frame), then `spawn_dozer_task_from_current()` resumes that slot.

## Live (wrong)
`command_executor/leftover.rs:1582-1622` `dozer_idle_resume_pending_build` tracks both slots via `dozer_most_recent_pending_task`, then `if is_repair { return false; }` — only BUILD ever resumes from idle. A parked REPAIR (BUILD interrupting Repair, or a failed approach leaving Idle) is pruned-but-never-resumed. The only re-acquire is `update_dozer_bored_repair` after 150 frames, which picks the nearest damaged same-player structure, not the parked player-ordered target.

## Evidence
C++: `isRepairMostImportant` → `DOZER_PRIMARY_REPAIR`.
Leftover: `get_most_recent_command()` includes Repair.
Live: `if is_repair { return false; }`.

Not a refile of closed hq-ylhfz (same-frame BUILD+REPAIR *tie* while both active) or hq-vmy49 (repair mid-build abandoning the scaffold).
close_reason: Idle isRepairMostImportant now resumes parked REPAIR via dozer_idle_resume_pending_build

title: [LookAt] KEY/SCREENEDGE scroll never mouse-locks
description:
## C++
`LookAtXlat.cpp` `LookAtTranslator::setScrolling` (lines 50-62) is the single entry for all three exclusive scroll types — `SCROLL_KEY` (RAW_KEY, line 187), `SCROLL_RMB` (RMB down, line 206), `SCROLL_SCREENEDGE` (RAW_MOUSE_POSITION edge band, line 290). Every call does `TheInGameUI->setScrolling(TRUE)` + `TheTacticalView->setMouseLock(TRUE)`.

`WindowXlat.cpp:147-172` (Kris Aug-15-2003): while the view is mouse-locked, KEEP every raw message except LMB down/up when `TheInGameUI->isScrolling()`. During keyboard or screen-edge panning, hover/RMB/MMB never reach the window manager and cannot issue orders through the control bar.

## Leftover (right)
`GameClient/src/message_stream/look_at_xlat.rs` `LookAtTranslator::set_scrolling()` — one shared path from Key, Rmb, and ScreenEdge arms. Every type does `TheInGameUI::set_scrolling(true)` + `view.set_mouse_lock(true)`; `stop_scrolling` reverses both (unit test `set_scrolling_locks_mouse_and_stop_restores_prev_cursor`).

title: [Locomotor] Wheeled SMALL_TURN recaps speed after approach-brake
description:
## C++
`moveTowardsPositionWheels` (`Locomotor.cpp:1316-1323`) caps `desiredSpeed` to `turnSpeed` when `|relAngle| > PI/20` **before** the approach-brake block (`:1393-1430`).
Once `IS_BRAKING` is latched, `goalSpeed` is overwritten with `actualSpeed-braking` / `-braking/2` / `actualSpeed` and is **not** re-clamped by `turnSpeed`. Treads analog `:1194-1221`. The 15° look-ahead probe (`:1340-1389`) also uses the pre-brake `goalSpeed`.

## Leftover (right)
`move_towards_position_wheels_physics` (`core_impl/move_ground.rs:176-180`) applies the SMALL_TURN cap on `desired_speed` first, then latches/unlatches/donut/curve (`:222-270`). Matches C++ order.

## Live (wrong)
`update_movement` first calls `apply_cpp_approach_brake` (`world_tick/movement.rs:717-723`), which returns the braking goal-speed when latched (`object/physics_motion.rs:1334-1350`), **then** recaps:
```
if delta.abs() > PI/20.0 && speed > turn_speed { speed = turn_speed; }
```
(`movement.rs:769-772`). A braking wheeled/motorcycle unit with >9° heading correction is forced to `maxSpeed/4` instead of `actualSpeed-braking`. The 15° look-ahead (`:793-800`) also sees that post-brake recap.

## Evidence
Truck/Humvee/motorcycle arriving at a waypoint while still turning >9° over-brakes vs C++ and tightens the donut.
close_reason: Wheeled SMALL_TURN now caps desiredSpeed before apply_cpp_approach_brake; IS_BRAKING overwrite is not recapped. 15° look-ahead sees pre-brake speed.

title: [Locomotor] Wings idle maintain Z uses own altitude not terrain
description:
## C++
`Locomotor::locoUpdate_maintainCurrentPosition` (`Locomotor.cpp:2412-2477`) runs appearance maintain then **one** `handleBehaviorZ(obj, physics, m_maintainPos)`.
`maintainCurrentPositionWings` (`:2488-2524`) is 2D circling only.
`handleBehaviorZ` `Z_SURFACE_RELATIVE_HEIGHT` (`:2288-2316`) takes `surfaceHt = getSurfaceHtAtPt(pos.x, pos.y)` (real terrain/water), damps PreferredHeight, then `calcLiftToUseAtPt`. Idle jets hold PreferredHeight above the ground.

## Leftover (right)
`maintain_current_position_wings` is 2D circle only (`core_impl/maintain.rs:216-260`).
`lift_relative_to_layer` uses `get_surface_ht_at_pt` (`behavior_z.rs:151-172`).
`move_dispatch.rs` calls `handle_behavior_z_for` once per frame with that real surface.

## Live (wrong)
Idle Wings: `update_movement` calls `apply_live_handle_behavior_z(obj, surface_y)` (correct terrain) then `loco_maintain_current_position` (`world_tick/movement.rs:970-978`).
Wings early-returns into `maintain_position_wings` (`object/physics.rs:682-685`), which then:
```
let gy = p.y;
let _ = self.handle_behavior_z(gy, Some(maintain.y));
```
(`object/physics.rs:1392-1393`). `handle_behavior_z(SurfaceRelative)` treats `gy` as the surface, so `preferred = PreferredHeight + own_y` every frame — unbounded climb bias. C++/leftover lift off real terrain.

## Evidence
Circling jet with PreferredHeight>0 holding last waypoint climbs instead of riding terrain/water.
close_reason: maintain_position_wings is 2D only. Idle/zero-delta Wings circle then apply_live_handle_behavior_z with leftover getSurfaceHtAtPt, not own altitude.

title: [Production] Live parachute land skips UseSpawnRallyPoint
description:
## C++
`ParachuteContain::onRemoving` (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Contain/ParachuteContain.cpp:493-516): after a non-skirmish rider is released, resolve `rider->getProducerID()` (the chute) then `transport->getProducerID()` (the producing building). If that building's `ExitInterface->useSpawnRallyPoint()` is true, call `exitObjectViaDoor(rider, DOOR_1)` so the rider runs DefaultProductionExitUpdate (UnitCreatePoint + 2-cell natural rally + custom rally). Otherwise `aiIdle`. Flag authored on DefaultProductionExitUpdate (`UseSpawnRallyPoint`).

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/object/contain/parachute_contain.rs:528-568` implements the same chain: skirmish → `ai_hunt`; else producer→transport→building `get_object_exit_interface()`; if `use_spawn_rally_point()` → `exit_object_via_door(rider, Primary)`; else `ai_idle`. `default_production_exit_behavior.rs` parses and exposes the INI flag.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/saboteur_car_bomb.rs:791-806` `apply_parachute_land_ai` only does skirmish → `unit_command_patrol`. Non-skirmish riders get no idle and never consult `ProductionExitMetadata.use_spawn_rally_point` (parsed in `thing.rs:652` / `spawn_templates.rs:2186` but unused on the land path). An airdropped rider from a UseSpawnRallyPoint=Yes producer idles at the LZ instead of walking the factory exit/rally.

## Evidence
C++: `if (exitInterface && exitInterface->useSpawnRallyPoint()) { exitInterface->exitObjectViaDoor(rider, DOOR_1); }`
Leftover: `if exit_guard.use_spawn_rally_point() { exit_guard.exit_object_via_door(...) }`
Live: no `use_spawn_rally_point` consumer under Main except parse + tests.

Not a refile of closed hq-14d7 (that was leftover ungated exit; leftover is now gated correctly).
close_reason: Live apply_parachute_land_ai now 2-hops rider.producer (chute) → chute.producer (building); UseSpawnRallyPoint runs DefaultProductionExit UnitCreatePoint+2-cell natural+custom rally, else aiIdle. put_hijacker_in_airborne_parachute stamps the producer chain.

description:
## C++
`CanSelectDrawable` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/MessageStream/SelectionXlat.cpp:113-116`) returns FALSE for effectively-dead objects **unless** `KINDOF_ALWAYS_SELECTABLE` (KindOf.h:86 — "never unselectable even if effectively dead; mostly for UI feedback objects").
`PickDrawableStruct` (`SelectionInfo.cpp:56-59`) also adds `KINDOF_ALWAYS_SELECTABLE` to pick kinds when not force-attacking, so those drawables enter the pick list.
Hover (`SelectionXlat.cpp:434`) posts `MSG_MOUSEOVER_DRAWABLE_HINT` when `!isEffectivelyDead() || isKindOf(KINDOF_ALWAYS_SELECTABLE)`.

## Leftover (right)
`SelectableDrawable::can_select` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/message_stream/selection_xlat.rs:121-124`) matches C++: `if self.is_dead && !self.has_kindof(KINDOF_ALWAYS_SELECTABLE) { return false; }`.
Catalog packing (`:218-219`, `:527-528`) writes AlwaysSelectable into the UI-local kind cache so dead AlwaysSelectable units stay `can_select(false)`.

## Live (wrong)
`UnitControlSystem::presentation_is_selectable` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/unit_control.rs:323-331`) requires `!o.destroyed` with no AlwaysSelectable override, plus Selectable kind / !sold / !unselectable / !masked / not contained.
`pick_object_id_at_world_from_presentation` (`unit_control.rs:373-375`) independently `return None` on `o.destroyed`.
`pick_ray.rs` uses `presentation_is_selectable`.
`CnCGameEngine::is_point_selectable_click_target` / `is_locally_selectable_click_target` (`cnc_game_engine/mouse.rs:1199-1218`) both call `presentation_is_selectable`.
`host_context_pick_profile` (`cnc_game_engine/selection.rs:31-50`) never adds ALWAYS_SELECTABLE (C++ PickDrawableStruct does when !forceAttack).
`presentation_is_squad_live` (`presentation_frame/alive.rs:225-227`) already early-returns AlwaysSelectable — control-group recall only. Click/hover/box pick do not.

Not a refile of closed hq-6kbbu: that bead added KindOf::AlwaysSelectable and fixed `Object::is_selectable`. Live click never consults `Object::is_selectable`.

## Player-visible
Dead UI-feedback / ALWAYS_SELECTABLE rubble cannot be clicked or mouseovered on the live host. Retail and leftover CanSelectDrawable keep them selectable.
close_reason: Live pick keeps ALWAYS_SELECTABLE dead objects: presentation_is_selectable + pick_ray skip + packed always_selectable bool (32-bit KindOf bank full). C++ CanSelectDrawable SelectionXlat.cpp:113 / Object.cpp:3011.

title: [Weapon] Live waypoint-follow slot ignores leftover CapableOfFollowingWaypoints
description:
## C++
WeaponSet::findWaypointFollowingCapableWeapon (WeaponSet.cpp:998-1008) walks TERTIARY..PRIMARY and returns the first weapon whose Weapon::isCapableOfFollowingWaypoint() is true. That flag is WeaponTemplate::m_capableOfFollowingWaypoint from Weapon.ini `CapableOfFollowingWaypoints`. Script NAMED_FIRE_WEAPON_FOLLOWING_WAYPOINT_PATH and attack-path fire use that slot. Name substrings are never consulted.

## Leftover (right)
GameLogic WeaponTemplate.capable_of_following_waypoint is parsed from Weapon.ini (ini_template_loader.rs:1285-1288; leftover weapon_template.rs:2525-2528). Leftover WeaponSet::find_waypoint_following_capable_weapon (weapon_set.rs:1100-1121) prefers TERTIARY..PRIMARY on leftover store.

## Live (wrong)
Object::find_waypoint_following_capable_weapon_slot (object/weapons.rs:286-297) uses host_capable_of_following_waypoint_for_weapon_name, which is seed_capable_of_following_waypoint_for (weapon_bootstrap/damage_kinds.rs:20-32): name contains scud / tomahawk / cruise / particlecannon / nuke+missile. unit_commands.rs:640-643 attack-path fire uses that seed-only slot finder. Victim `PhysicsBehavior` bounce sound wins; else INI `MeatyBounceSound` / `BigMetalBounceSound` / `SmallMetalBounceSound` (`TrainMeatyHit` / `TrainBigMetalHit` / `TrainSmallMetalHit`) by KindOf infantry / huge-vehicle+structure / vehicle.
