title: [Cam] SETUP_CAMERA does not cancel in-flight move/path
description:
## C++
`ScriptActions::doSetupCamera` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/ScriptEngine/ScriptActions.cpp:822-834`) calls `TheTacticalView->moveCameraTo(&pos, 0, 0, true, 0, 0)` then cameraModLookToward/FinalPitch/FinalZoom. `W3DView::moveCameraTo` (`W3DView.cpp:2374-2404`) rebuilds `m_mcwpInfo` and `setupWaypointPath` (`W3DView.cpp:2879-2950`) ends with `m_doingRotateCamera = false`. The 0ms move replaces any in-flight path/rotate.

## Leftover (right)
`GameClientScriptActionHandler::setup_camera` (`script_action_handler.rs:1081-1103`) goes through `move_camera` → `View::look_at` (`view.rs:929-943`). `look_at` calls `cancel_scripted_camera_from_player_look_at`, which drops leftover `camera_move` / `camera_path` / `camera_rotate` so the setup snap is not overwritten next frame.

## Live (wrong)
`drain_camera_setup_requests` (`scripts_camera.rs:4149-4178`) only `request_camera_focus` + instant zoom/pitch/look-toward and `pending_camera_rotate = None`. It never clears `script_camera_move_to` / `script_camera_path`. `request_camera_focus` (`eva_camera.rs:577-585`) only stamps `pending_camera_focus`. `update_script_camera` (`scripts_camera.rs:4936-4998`) then keeps advancing the stale move/path and overwrites `pending_camera_look_toward` with travel facing.

## Player-visible
A campaign `SETUP_CAMERA` fired while a `MOVE_CAMERA_TO` / waypoint path is still running snaps for one frame, then the leftover path steers the camera away and the authored look-toward is lost.

## Evidence
C++ `ScriptActions.cpp:822-834` + `W3DView.cpp:2374-2404,2879-2950`. Leftover `view.rs:929-943` + `script_action_handler.rs:1081-1103`. Live `scripts_camera.rs:4149-4178,4936-4998` + `eva_camera.rs:577-585`. Not hq-3etbi (LOOK_TOWARD cancel of in-flight move). SETUP leftover-wrong standalone zoom/pitch is a different, already-skipped issue.
close_reason: SETUP_CAMERA now cancels in-flight move/path/rotate so look-toward is not overwritten

title: [Cam] RESET_CAMERA leaves stale ROTATE_CAMERA in control
description:
## C++
`W3DView::resetCamera` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DView.cpp:2765-2785`) calls `moveCameraTo` (which `setupWaypointPath` ends with `m_doingRotateCamera = false`), then forces `m_mcwpInfo.cameraAngle[2] = 0.0` and starts zoom/pitch over the same duration. Any prior `rotateCamera` is replaced.

## Leftover (right)
`View::reset_camera` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/display/view.rs:2367-2411`) replaces `camera_rotate` with a new default-angle transition (or clears it when `milliseconds <= 0`). The previous rotate cannot keep ticking.

## Live (wrong)
`drain_camera_resets` (`scripts_camera.rs:4045-4067`) sets `pending_camera_zoom_reset` and `start_camera_move_to`. `start_camera_move_to` (`scripts_camera.rs:4666-4681`) clears `script_camera_path` only — not `pending_camera_rotate` or `script_camera_rotate_remaining`. `camera_drain.rs:220-273` applies the reset yaw-to-0, then `camera_drain.rs:310-319` applies `pres.camera_rotate` afterward, so a leftover ROTATE_CAMERA overrides the reset heading.

## Player-visible
`RESET_CAMERA` during or after a `ROTATE_CAMERA` eases zoom/pitch home but the heading keeps spinning on the old rotate instead of returning to default yaw.

## Evidence
C++ `W3DView.cpp:2765-2785` + `setupWaypointPath` `m_doingRotateCamera = false`. Leftover `view.rs:2367-2411`. Live `scripts_camera.rs:4045-4067,4666-4681` + `camera_drain.rs:220-319`. Not hq-9o5v4 / hq-xe79a / hq-3puei (those were missing default yaw / ease / FXPitch on the reset itself; the reset now authors yaw-to-0, then a stale rotate overwrites it).
close_reason: RESET_CAMERA and start_camera_move_to clear pending ROTATE_CAMERA (setupWaypointPath m_doingRotateCamera=false)

title: [Leaflet] Disable is one-shot; walk-in units stay active
description:
C++ `LeafletDropBehavior::update` (EMPUpdate.cpp:425-452) after `m_startFrame` calls `doDisableAttack()` every frame (`UPDATE_SLEEP_NONE`) and again from `onDie` (457-462). `doDisableAttack` (467-505) iterates enemies in a 3D bounding-sphere `AffectRadius` and `setDisabledUntil(DISABLED_EMP, now + DisabledDuration)`. Units that walk into the 110wu cloud after the 2500ms delay still get leaflet-disabled for 20s.

Leftover `object/behavior/leaflet_drop_behavior.rs` matches: `update_simple` (184-220) pulses `do_disable_attack` after `start_frame` and returns `UpdateSleepTime::None`; `on_die` (224-245) pulses again. Same infantry/vehicle + ENEMIES filter.

Live `host_leaflet_drops.plan_due_impacts` (host_leaflet_drop.rs:366-387) emits one plan at `impact_frame`, then `record_impact_complete` (389-398) marks the mission `Completed`. `update_leaflet_drops` (ambush_leaflet.rs:511-603) applies `apply_disabled_emp` once and never re-scans. Units entering the radius after that frame stay active.

Not a dup of hq-uslx3 (ViewObject), hq-e8ic5 (enemy relationship), hq-c39nv (re-disable max-extend vs overwrite), or open hq-zt1zh (LeafletFX particles).
close_reason: Live host_leaflet_drops.plan_due_impacts now pulses leftover do_disable_attack every frame after start_frame (Queued+Completed). update_leaflet_drops applies DISABLED_EMP to walk-ins; first-pulse audio/FX stay one-shot.

title: [Cam] CAMERA_MOD_FINAL_ZOOM/PITCH snap when camera is idle
description:
## C++
`W3DView::cameraModFinalZoom` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DView.cpp:2537-2558`) only runs when `m_doingRotateCamera` or `m_doingMoveCameraOnWaypointPath`. It starts `zoomCamera(finalZoom*maxZoom, remainingMs, …)` over the remaining rotate/path time. Idle (no rotate, no path) is a no-op.

`cameraModFinalPitch` (`W3DView.cpp:2751-2759`) is the same gate: rotate or path only. Idle is a no-op.

## Leftover (right)
`View::camera_mod_final_zoom` / `camera_mod_final_pitch` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/display/view.rs:2558-2598`) only apply when `camera_rotate` or `camera_move` is in flight. Idle leaves zoom/pitch untouched.

## Live (wrong)
`scripts_camera.rs:4112-4146` always writes `pending_camera_zoom` / `pending_camera_pitch` after draining MOD_FINAL_*. `script_camera_remaining_seconds` (`scripts_camera.rs:4766-4782`) returns 0 when there is no rotate/move/path. `camera_drain.rs:276-284` then treats `duration_seconds <= 0` as an instant snap (`self.camera_zoom = zoom; camera_zoom_target = None`).

## Player-visible
A lone `CAMERA_MOD_SET_FINAL_ZOOM` / `CAMERA_MOD_SET_FINAL_PITCH` (or one fired after the move already finished) instantly changes the tactical zoom/pitch on live. Retail ignores those mods unless a rotate or waypoint path is in flight.

## Evidence
C++ `W3DView.cpp:2540-2558,2751-2759`. Leftover `view.rs:2558-2598`. Live `scripts_camera.rs:4112-4146,4766-4782` + `camera_drain.rs:276-284`. Not hq-at7ct (that closed snap-*during-ROTATE*; remaining-time during rotate is already fixed). This is the idle / no-rotate-or-path case leftover still no-ops.
close_reason: CAMERA_MOD_FINAL_ZOOM/PITCH no-op when idle (remaining==0); no instant snap

title: [Cam] CAMERA_MOD_FREEZE_ANGLE ignores in-flight ROTATE_CAMERA
description:
## C++
`W3DView::cameraModFreezeAngle` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DView.cpp:2564-2579`):
- If `m_doingRotateCamera` and not tracking an object: pin `m_rcInfo.angle.startAngle = endAngle = m_angle` so remaining rotate frames hold the current yaw.
- If tracking: clear `m_rcInfo.target.targetObjectID`.
- If `m_doingMoveCameraOnWaypointPath`: set every `m_mcwpInfo.cameraAngle[i+1] = m_mcwpInfo.cameraAngle[0]` (remaining path uses the start yaw, not the current interpolated facing).

A later `rotateCamera` still replaces the animation. FREEZE_ANGLE only pins the in-flight rotate/path.

## Leftover (right)
`View::camera_mod_freeze_angle` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/display/view.rs:1930-1936`):
- In-flight `camera_rotate`: `freeze_current_angle()` sets start=end=current (`cinematic_camera.rs:772-776`).
- In-flight `camera_path`: `freeze_angles_to_start()` copies waypoint[0].angle onto the rest (`cinematic_camera.rs:681-687`).
Test `test_camera_mod_freeze_angle_stops_rotation_progress` (`view.rs:3085-3097`) holds yaw after freeze.

## Live (wrong)
`apply_script_camera_mod_freeze_angle` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/scripts_camera.rs:4831-4844`) only sets `freeze_angle` on `script_camera_move_to` / `script_camera_path` (suppresses travel look, holds current facing). It never touches `pending_camera_rotate` / `script_camera_rotate_remaining`. Path freeze therefore keeps the current interpolated yaw instead of rewriting remaining segments to `cameraAngle[0]`.

## Player-visible
`ROTATE_CAMERA` then `CAMERA_MOD_FREEZE_ANGLE` keeps spinning on live. Mid-path FREEZE_ANGLE holds the current travel facing instead of snapping remaining waypoints to the path start yaw. Campaign scripts that pin a rotate or path mid-move keep turning.

## Evidence
C++ `W3DView.cpp:2566-2578`. Leftover `view.rs:1930-1936` + `cinematic_camera.rs:681-687,772-776`. Live `scripts_camera.rs:4831-4844`. Not hq-ry060 (that was FREEZE_ANGLE swallowing a *later* rotate; live tests now allow a replacement rotate, and over-corrected by never pinning the in-flight one).
close_reason: FREEZE_ANGLE pins in-flight rotate (rotations=0) and path remaining segments to start yaw

title: [Cam] Airborne lookAt ray uses camera-to-object not look dir
description:
## C++
`W3DView::lookAt` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DView.cpp:2313-2338`): if `o->z > PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE_F + groundHeight`, take the current camera look direction via `Un_Project(0,0)` (screen-center world ray), then restart the ray at the object and cast that same look direction to the far clip. Terrain hit XY becomes the look-at so the airborne unit sits on the screen-center look vector.

## Leftover (right)
`View::look_at` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/display/view.rs:929-937`) uses the same elevation test. `look_at_pick_ray` (`view.rs:1346-1354`) starts at the object and goes along `camera_target - eye` (current look direction, equivalent to `Un_Project(0,0)`), then `intersect_terrain_ray`.

## Live (wrong)
`host_center_camera_on_impl` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/cnc_game_engine/start_game.rs:1564-1585`) calls `airborne_look_at_ground` (`mouse.rs:314-330`) with `dir = object_pos - eye` (camera-to-object), then continues that ray from the object. That is the camera-to-object line, not the current look-at axis, unless the unit is already on screen center.

## Player-visible
SELECT_NEXT / double-tap / script lookAt on aircraft (or any elevated unit) recenters on the ground along the camera-to-object line instead of keeping the unit on the screen-center look vector. The plane slides off-center as the camera yaws to the new ground point.

## Evidence
C++ `W3DView.cpp:2313-2338` (comment: "the object intersects with the look at vector in the center of the screen"). Leftover `view.rs:929-937,1346-1354`. Live `mouse.rs:314-330` + `start_game.rs:1564-1585`. Not hq-oacsw (closed as "added airborne lookAt ray" after live used XY; the ray now exists but the direction is still leftover-right / live-wrong).
close_reason: Airborne lookAt casts current look dir from the object, not camera-to-object

title: [Shroud] 3D audio ST_SHROUDED reads square partition cells not DiscreteCircle
description:
C++ `SoundManager::canPlayNow` (GameSounds.cpp:203-205) culls ST_SHROUDED positional events when `ThePartitionManager->getShroudStatusForPlayer(local, pos) != CELLSHROUD_CLEAR`. That cell status is the DiscreteCircle looker grid from `PartitionManager::doShroudReveal` (PartitionManager.cpp:3937-3956).

Leftover `GameLogicAudioShroudResolver` (`GameLogic/src/helpers/audio.rs:115-143`) and leftover `FXList::fx_pos_cell_is_clear` (`GameClient/src/fx_list.rs:615-629`) both ask leftover `ShroudManager::get_shroud_state`, which paints DiscreteCircle lookers (`shroud_manager.rs:486-509`). That is the leftover-right store (same as hq-rxwoc FOW mix).

Live `live_position_is_cellshroud_clear` (`Main/src/game_logic/audio_dispatch_impl.rs:531-541`) instead calls leftover `partition_cell_shroud_status`, which reads `PARTITION_MANAGER` cells stamped by leftover `PartitionShroudGrid::reveal_circle` (square `±ceil(r/40)` + world `r²` reject, `partition_shroud.rs:137-163`). Square corners stay CLEAR on that grid after a circular look, so world SFX leak just outside the DiscreteCircle vision disk. hq-d80a0 only added the gate; hq-rxwoc only switched object FOW mix.
close_reason: Live 3D audio ST_SHROUDED now calls leftover ThePartitionManager::get_shroud_status_for_player (ShroudManager DiscreteCircle lookers) instead of partition_cell_shroud_status square r2 cells.

title: [Locomotor] Live never binds SlideIntoPlaceTime so Chinook/Helix never slide
description:
## C++
`LocomotorTemplate::getFieldParse` (Locomotor.cpp:474) `SlideIntoPlaceTime` uses `INI::parseDurationReal` (msec → frames). `moveTowardsPositionOther` (Locomotor.cpp:2344-2361) when `ULTRA_ACCURATE` and `|dx|,|dy| <= goalSpeed * m_ultraAccurateSlideIntoPlaceFactor` does not rotate — it slides `dirToApplyForce` toward the goal (`TURN_NONE`). `moveTowardsPositionHover` (1863-1866) delegates to Other. Retail `ChinookLocomotor` / `HelixLocomotor` / `CINE_ChinookLocomotor` author `SlideIntoPlaceTime = 100` (100 msec → 3 frames). At Chinook Speed 150 (5 wu/frame) the slide window is ~15 wu. Jet/Chinook landing sets `ULTRA_ACCURATE`.

## Leftover (right)
`ini_bridge.rs:163-164` `parse_duration_real` copies Common `SlideIntoPlaceTime` onto `ultra_accurate_slide_factor`. `move_towards_position_other_physics` (`move_ground.rs:511-531`) slides when ultra-accurate and inside that threshold. Hover calls Other (`move_ground.rs:435-445`).

## Live (wrong)
`HostLocomotorBinding` has no slide field. `apply_host_locomotor_binding` (`locomotor_bootstrap.rs:941-980`) never writes `Object.ultra_accurate_slide_factor` (ctor default 0.0). `update_movement` (`movement.rs:760-766`) already has the C++ slide gate but `ultra_accurate_slide_factor > 0.0` is never true. Chinook/Helix landing still sets `ULTRA_ACCURATE` (hq-2e10h) so they rotate into the pad instead of sliding the last ~15 wu.

## Evidence
- C++ Locomotor.cpp:474, 1863-1866, 2344-2361
- Leftover `GameLogic/src/locomotor/ini_bridge.rs:163-164`, `core_impl/move_ground.rs:423-531`
- Live `Main/src/game_logic/locomotor_bootstrap.rs:239-277,778-980`
- Live `Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/movement.rs:760-766`
- Live `Main/src/game_logic/object/construct.rs` default `ultra_accurate_slide_factor: 0.0`
- Retail INI ChinookLocomotor / HelixLocomotor `SlideIntoPlaceTime = 100`

## Player-visible
Chinook/Helix (and cinematic Chinook) yaw-steer onto a parking pad / combat-drop hover instead of sliding the last body-length when ULTRA_ACCURATE.
close_reason: Host binds leftover parse_duration_real(SlideIntoPlaceTime). Chinook/Helix seed 100 msec → 3 frames; apply stamps Object.ultra_accurate_slide_factor so Hover/Other ULTRA_ACCURATE slides without yaw.

title: [Contain] Internet Center subdual never idles occupant hackers
description:
C++ path + behavior:
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Body/ActiveBody.cpp:1250-1277` `ActiveBody::onSubdualChange`.
When a non-projectile becomes `DISABLED_SUBDUED`, C++ `contain->orderAllPassengersToIdle(CMD_FROM_AI)` (`OpenContain.cpp:1381-1392` `aiIdle` every rider).
When subdual clears and the container is `KINDOF_FS_INTERNET_CENTER` (Patch 1.01), C++ `orderAllPassengersToHackInternet` so contained MONEY_HACKER units resume `aiHackInternet`.
Microwave / subdual on an Internet Center therefore stops cash until the stun wears off.

Leftover path + behavior (matches C++ idle arm):
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/body/active_body.rs:1436-1458` calls `order_all_passengers_to_idle` on subdual and `order_all_passengers_to_hack_internet` on IC un-subdual.
`modules/contain.rs:351-375` `order_all_passengers_to_idle` issues `AiCommandType::Idle` for every occupant — same as C++ `aiIdle`.

Live path + behavior (wrong):
`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/object/install.rs:188-212` `set_disabled_subdued` only idles the container itself (and skips even that for `KindOf::Structure`). It never walks occupants.
`world_objects/resources_income.rs:745-752` `update_hacker_income` auto-starts `ensure_internet_center_hacking` every tick for any living contained MONEY_HACKER whose container is a parsed InternetHackContain. It gates on `disabled_hacked` of the hacker, never on the Internet Center's `DISABLED_SUBDUED`.

Player-visible: microwave / subdue an occupied Internet Center. C++/leftover: occupants go Idle, cash stops until stun ends. Live: occupants keep depositing the whole stun.

Not a duplicate of hq-8eobz (transport residual fire), hq-8ikxi (garrison fire), hq-leia6 (evac leak), hq-ln4ol (exit while subdued).
notes: Live set_disabled_subdued now queues leftover onSubdualChange passenger idle/IC resume; flush + income gate stop cash while subdued.
close_reason: set_disabled_subdued walks occupants to Idle; IC un-subdual resumes HackInternet. update_hacker_income gates on container DISABLED_SUBDUED so microwave stops cash until stun ends.

title: [Overlord/Helix] Selecting host never flashes portable addon
description:

Matches leftover OverlordContain/HelixContain + C++ Drawable::onSelected.

title: [Pathfind] findAttackPath never binds leftover seeker
description:
## C++
`Pathfinder::findAttackPath` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/AI/AIPathfind.cpp:10530-10843`) takes the attacking `Object*`. `getRadiusAndCenter(obj)`, `checkDestination(obj, ...)`, `examineNeighboringCells(..., obj, attackDistance)`, `isKindOf(KINDOF_VEHICLE)` strip-back, and `isHuman` (`getPlayerType()==PLAYER_COMPUTER`) all come from that object. `locomotorSet.getValidSurfaces()` is the surface mask (not hardcoded Ground).

## Leftover (right)
`pathfind_complete/attack_path.rs` `find_attack_path` (`:11-407`) takes `obj_id` + `surfaces` + `is_human`. Occupancy is `check_for_movement(obj_id, ...)`. Vehicle strip-back uses `object_is_vehicle(obj_id)`. Neighbor passability uses the passed `surfaces`. Human clamp uses the passed `is_human`.

## Live (wrong)
`PathfindingSystem::find_attack_firing_position` (`Main/src/game_logic/pathfinding.rs:6290-6663`) never calls `bind_seeker_from_mover`. `attacker_id = self.seeker_id` (stale or None). Occupancy/`seeker_player`/`seeker_is_infantry`/`seeker_path_diameter` are leftover from the last `find_path_ex_surfaces`. `assign_unit_attack_path` (`world_save.rs:1860-1909`) has `unit_id` but does not pass it. `surfaces` is hardcoded `SURFACE_GROUND`. `is_human` is hardcoded `true`.

## Evidence
C++ `:10530` signature + `:10617-10620` isHuman + `:10633` locomotor surfaces + `:10759` KINDOF_VEHICLE. Leftover `find_attack_path(..., obj_id, is_human, ...)`. Live `:6310` `let is_human = true`, `:6303` `SURFACE_GROUND`, `:6313` `self.seeker_id`, no `bind_seeker_from_mover` in the function.

## Player-visible
A tank attacking after an infantry pathfind uses infantry occupancy/diameter. Two simultaneous attacks steal each other's crush/player bits. Cliff/water locomotors never search those cells. AI attackers are clamped to `m_logicalExtent` like humans.
close_reason: Already live: find_attack_firing_position binds seeker from mover, locomotor surfaces, apply_seeker_human_flag. assign_unit_attack_path passes unit_id. Test find_attack_path_binds_leftover_seeker.

title: [Pathfind] findAttackPath range-tests cell corners not leftover adjustCoordToCell
description:
## C++
`Pathfinder::findAttackPath` (`AIPathfind.cpp:10698-10724`) range-tests and near-self rejects with `adjustCoordToCell(..., centerInCell, cellCenter, layer)` — infantry/odd-diameter cell center (`+0.5`), vehicles/even `(cell+0.05)*PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE`. `snapClosestGoalPosition` (`:5114-5148`) writes the same helper (first snap `LAYER_GROUND`, neighborhood on dest layer).

## Leftover (right)
`pathfind_complete/attack_path.rs` `:144-145` `adjust_coord_to_cell(cx, cy, center_in_cell, &mut cell_center, layer)` before `in_range` / view-blocked. `pathfind_complete/snap.rs` `snap_closest_goal_position` (`:25-62`) always `adjust_coord_to_cell` (center vs `+0.05`).

## Live (wrong)
`find_attack_firing_position` (`pathfinding.rs:6457`) uses `grid_to_world(cell)` — cell min-corner, no `+0.5`/`+0.05`. Final goal `:6652` same. `snap_closest_goal_position` (`:6055-6061`) does `grid_to_world_on_layer` then adds `+0.5` only when `center_in_cell`; vehicles stay on the corner (missing C++ `+0.05`). Distinct remaining sites from closed hq-wuufk (`crate_path_to_world`).

## Evidence
C++ `:10698-10699` `adjustCoordToCell` for `isGoalPosWithinAttackRange`. Leftover `adjust_coord_to_cell` at attack `:144`. Live `:6457` `let world = self.grid.grid_to_world(cell)` and snap `:6056-6060`.

## Player-visible
Infantry attack range is measured from the cell corner (~5wu off). Units walk to a cell they cannot fire from, or reject a cell they can. Vehicle idle/plant snap is 0.5wu off the C++ inset.
close_reason: Already live: find_attack_firing_position and snap_closest_goal_position use adjust_coord_to_cell (+0.5 infantry / +0.05 vehicle). Test find_attack_path_range_tests_adjust_coord_to_cell.

title: [Weapon] Paladin PDL shoots stealthed undetected infantry
description:
## C++
`PointDefenseLaserUpdate::scanClosestTarget` (`PointDefenseLaserUpdate.cpp:263-267`) skips any candidate with `OBJECT_STATUS_STEALTHED` and not `DETECTED` and not `DISGUISED`. Paladin SecondaryTargetTypes=INFANTRY therefore never locks a cloaked Ninja/Burton/Kell.

`point_defense_laser_update.rs:273-278` `scan_closest_target` applies the same STEALTHED && !DETECTED && !DISGUISED continue.

## Live (wrong)
`host_point_defense.rs` `is_secondary_intercept_target` is `is_infantry && is_alive && !same_team && !under_construction` — no stealth bits. `update_point_defense_intercept` (`strategy_center.rs:1656-1662`) feeds that into acquire, then applies Paladin PDL damage to the infantry.

## Evidence
C++ `PointDefenseLaserUpdate.cpp:263-267`. Leftover `point_defense_laser_update.rs:273-278`. Live `host_point_defense.rs:426-433` and `strategy_center.rs:1656-1708`. Distinct from closed stealth-on-fire beads (hq-gm3ut / hq-kqj2j) and hq-47d1j persist.

A Paladin near stealthed enemy infantry lasers them. C++/leftover leave the cloaked unit alone until detected.

title: [Weapon] Avenger PDL is one 500ms stream not two independent lasers
description:
## C++
`PointDefenseLaserUpdate` is a per-module fire clock (`PointDefenseLaserUpdate.cpp:99-214`). Each instance has its own `m_nextShotAvailableInFrames` and `m_bestTargetID`. Avenger authors **two** modules (retail residual: AttackRange 100, DelayBetweenShots 500ms each, ScanRange 200, ScanRate 0 / 100ms). Two independent 500ms streams can intercept two missiles in the same 500ms window.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/object/behavior/point_defense_laser_update.rs` ports the same per-module `next_shot_available_in_frames` + `fire_when_ready`. Two installed modules fire independently.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/world_combat/strategy_center.rs` `update_point_defense_intercept` keeps **one** `point_defense_next_ready_frame` per carrier. `host_point_defense.rs` `AVENGER_PDL_DELAY_FRAMES = 15` (500ms) and comments "Residual collapses two lasers into one fire stream with Avenger delay." Avenger intercepts at half retail rate.

## Evidence
C++ `PointDefenseLaserUpdate.cpp:99-214`. Leftover `point_defense_laser_update.rs:325-396`. Live `host_point_defense.rs:13-18,74-78` and `strategy_center.rs:1621-1721`. Distinct from closed hq-47d1j (PDL cooldown persist) and hq-61y (Avenger designator residual).

## Player-visible
Two incoming missiles at an Avenger: C++/leftover can kill both within 500ms (one per laser). Live kills one, then waits another 500ms.
close_reason: Avenger PDL is two independent 500ms clocks (pdl_module_count=2, point_defense_next_ready_frame + _1). Contract test avenger_pdl_two_independent_lasers. PDLS v2 persists laser-two.

title: [Save] Weapon leech-range latch never persisted
description:
## C++
`Weapon::xfer` (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Weapon.cpp:3341-3441) v3 writes `m_leechWeaponRangeActive` after pitch-limited. Once a LeechRangeWeapon (Terrorist, Burton knife, other melee/suicide) pre-fires or fires, C++ `Weapon::preFireWeapon` / `fireWeaponTemplate` latches leech so `isWithinAttackRange` waives max range for the rest of that attack cycle (`Object::clearLeechRangeModeForAllWeapons` only on stop).

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/weapon/weapon.rs` + `weapon_instance.rs` + `object_xfer.rs` `xfer_weapon_crc_like_cpp` write `leech_weapon_range_active` in the same slot as C++. Leftover Object xfer therefore restores the latch.

## Live (wrong)
Host `Object` already has `leech_range_active_primary` / `leech_range_active_secondary` (`object/mod.rs`, `object/attack.rs` `activate_leech_range_for_slot`, `object/rtb.rs` `leech_range_active_for_slot` returns MAX range). `save_load/` never mentions those fields: `ObjectSnapshot` / `object_xfer_persist.rs` / `ObjectXferPersist` capture pre-attack + maxShotCount + turret/vision but not leech. Restore constructs a fresh Object (`new_with_logic_frame`) so both flags stay false.

## Evidence
Save mid-chase after a Terrorist / Burton knife has already fired: C++/leftover keep infinite range until the attack ends. Live load drops the latch, so the unit fails `is_within_attack_range` / `can_target_with_slot` and stops pursuing.
close_reason: Live Object leech-range latch now rides a WLCH lifecycle-tail suffix. Restore writes Object.leech_range_active_primary/secondary only; leftover Weapon::xfer slot unchanged.

title: [Save] ScoreKeeper kills and money never persisted
description:
## C++
`ScoreKeeper::xfer` (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/RTS/ScoreKeeper.cpp:465-536) v1 writes `m_totalMoneyEarned`, `m_totalMoneySpent`, `m_totalUnitsDestroyed[MAX_PLAYER_COUNT]`, `m_totalUnitsBuilt`, `m_totalUnitsLost`, `m_totalBuildingsDestroyed[]`, `m_totalBuildingsBuilt`, `m_totalBuildingsLost`, tech/faction captures, `m_currentScore`, player index, plus objectsBuilt/Destroyed/Lost/Captured maps. `Player::xfer` snapshots that ScoreKeeper. `calculateScore` uses earned money and enemy kill counts.

## Leftover (right)
`GameEngine/Common/src/common/rts/score_keeper.rs:860-913` `ScoreKeeper::xfer` matches that table (money earned/spent, per-player destroy arrays, built/lost, captures, current_score, object-count maps). Player leftover xfer includes the ScoreKeeper snapshot.

## Live (wrong)
Host `Player.statistics` already tracks `money_earned`, `units_destroyed`, `units_destroyed_self`, `structures_destroyed`, `objects_captured`, `resources_spent` (`game_logic/game_logic/crate_tick.rs` `PlayerStatistics`, `player.rs` `calculate_score`). `PlayerStatisticsSnapshot` only stores units_built/lost, buildings_built/lost, resources_gathered (`snapshot/player.rs:77-86`). `snapshot_player_statistics` (`builder.rs:1747-1757`) copies only those five and zeros damage/XP. `restore_all_players` (`restore.rs:613-619`) applies them then `..PlayerStatistics::default()`, wiping money_earned, units_destroyed, structures_destroyed, objects_captured. `CHUNK_Players` `PlayerRuntimePersist` (`player_team_persist.rs:47-66`) has no ScoreKeeper fields either. `save_load/` has zero mentions of money_earned / units_destroyed.

## Evidence
Save a skirmish after kills and supply drop-off, then load and win: leftover/C++ score screen keeps earned cash and enemy kills. Live `calculate_score` / score overlay restart from 0 kills and 0 money.
close_reason: Live Player.statistics kills and money now ride an SCKP lifecycle-tail suffix encoded with leftover ScoreKeeper::serialize. Restore writes counters only after PlayerStatisticsSnapshot wipe.

title: [FX] MissileLauncher door FX never dispatched
description:
## C++
`MissileLauncherBuildingUpdate` door state switches (`MissileLauncherBuildingUpdate.cpp:68-158`) call `FXList::doFXPos` at the building position for `m_closedFX` / `m_openingFX` / `m_openFX` / `m_waitingToCloseFX` / `m_closingFX` (INI `DoorClosedFX` / `DoorOpeningFX` / `DoorOpenFX` / `DoorWaitingToCloseFX` / `DoorClosingFX`).

Residual INI fallback also omits door FX names.

title: [FX] BattleBus undeath StartUndeath/HitGround FX never dispatched
description:
## C++
`BattleBusSlowDeathBehavior::beginSlowDeath` (`BattleBusSlowDeathBehavior.cpp:118-130`) on first-life undeath: `FXList::doFXObj(data->m_fxStartUndeath, me)` then OCL. On land (`update` :177-184): `FXList::doFXObj(data->m_fxHitGround, me)` then OCL + `MODELCONDITION_SECOND_LIFE`. Retail names `FX_BattleBusStartUndeath` / `FX_BattleBusHitGround`.

`Object::start_battle_bus_second_life` (`object/orders.rs:1345-1381`) throws, idles, and sets second-life HP — no `dispatch_fx_list_at_host_object`. `tick_battle_bus_slow_death` :1421-1427 on land only stamps `SECOND_LIFE` + `DISABLED_HELD`. `host_battle_bus.rs` keeps `BATTLE_BUS_FX_START_UNDEATH` / `BATTLE_BUS_FX_HIT_GROUND` as honesty constants.

title: [Cam] FREEZE_TIME and CAMERA_MOVEMENT_FINISHED ignore rotate/zoom/pitch
description:
C++ path + behavior: `W3DView.cpp:2802` `isCameraMovementFinished` is `!path && !rotate && !pitch && !zoom`. `cameraModFreezeTime` sets the flag; `GameLogic.cpp:3603` freezes while `isTimeFrozen() && !isCameraMovementFinished()` (rotate counts). `rotateCameraOneFrame` clears freeze at end. `ScriptConditions.cpp` `CAMERA_MOVEMENT_FINISHED` queries `TheTacticalView->isCameraMovementFinished()`.

Leftover path + behavior: `GameEngine/GameClient/src/display/view.rs` `is_camera_movement_finished` includes move/path/rotate/zoom/pitch/rotate_toward. `rotate_camera` arms `freeze_time_for_camera_movement_active`. Leftover `CameraMovementFinishedCondition` queries the handler.

Live path + behavior: `Main/src/game_logic/mission_scripts.rs` AtomicBool is only set false in `push_camera_path_move` / `push_camera_move_to`. Rotate/zoom/pitch/look-toward/reset/setup never mark unfinished. `scripts_camera.rs` `apply_script_camera_mod_freeze_time` only flags move/path (or arms the next move). `eva_camera.rs` `is_script_camera_time_frozen` reads only those flags. A `CAMERA_MOD_FREEZE_TIME` + `ROTATE_CAMERA` pair never freezes sim, and `CAMERA_MOVEMENT_FINISHED` is true during rotate/zoom/pitch.

Evidence: campaign scripts waiting on camera-finished or freezing time during a rotate/zoom/pitch fire immediately. Same root cause, two observables.
close_reason: FREEZE_TIME + CAMERA_MOVEMENT_FINISHED now include rotate/zoom/pitch remaining

title: [Cam] LOOK_TOWARD does not cancel in-flight move/path
description:
C++ path + behavior: `W3DView.cpp` `rotateCameraTowardObject` / `rotateCameraTowardPosition` set `m_doingMoveCameraOnWaypointPath = false` (2453 / 2498). Look-toward replaces the in-flight waypoint move.

Leftover path + behavior: `GameEngine/GameClient/src/display/view.rs` `rotate_camera_toward_object` / `rotate_camera_toward_position` set `camera_path = None` before arming `rotate_camera_toward`.

Live path + behavior: `Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/scripts_camera.rs` look-toward drain (4070-4093) clears only `pending_camera_rotate`. `update_script_camera` keeps advancing `script_camera_move_to` / `script_camera_path` and overwrites `pending_camera_look_toward` with travel-look every frame, swallowing the rotate.

Evidence: `CAMERA_LOOK_TOWARD_OBJECT` / `WAYPOINT` during an active `MOVE_CAMERA_TO` / path should stop the pan and yaw toward the target; live keeps panning and yaws to travel heading. Not a duplicate of hq-2iunm (`CAMERA_MOD_LOOK_TOWARD` with no move).
close_reason: LOOK_TOWARD cancels in-flight move/path before arming rotate

title: [Cam] Script shaker steps visual dt not C++ 1/30 per draw
description:
C++ path + behavior: `W3DView.cpp:390-396` `CameraShakerSystem.Timestep(1.0f/30.0f)` runs once per rendered view update (`W3DDisplay.cpp` `updateViews` per draw). Duration, `(1-elapsed/duration)` envelope, and omega sweep advance at a fixed 1/30 s per present, independent of real frame time.

Leftover path + behavior: `GameEngine/GameClient/src/display/cinematic_camera.rs` `CameraShakeSystem::timestep(dt)` and `GameEngineDevice/.../camerashakesystem.rs` port the C++ step. Leftover is correct when driven with the C++ 1/30 present step.

Live path + behavior: `Main/src/cnc_game_engine/input.rs` uses `visual_dt = dt * visual_speed`; `camera_drain.rs` ticks `update_camera(visual_dt)`; `mouse.rs` calls `update_script_camera_shake(dt)`; `start_game.rs` does `shaker.elapsed_seconds += dt` with measured visual dt. At 60 fps a 2.0 s `CAMERA_ADD_SHAKER_AT` lasts 2.0 s wall time instead of C++ ~1.0 s; envelope and omega sweep run at half rate.

Evidence: leftover shaker math matches C++ when given 1/30; live drives it with client visual dt. Not a duplicate of hq-rqv3m (waveform/amplitude), hq-dhb57 (epicenter), hq-qq2jo (translate vs rotate), or hq-vbsq1 (freeze).
close_reason: Script shaker timesteps 1/30 per present, not visual_dt

title: [Cam] CAMERA_MOD_FINAL_ZOOM/PITCH snap during ROTATE_CAMERA
description:
C++ path + behavior: `W3DView.cpp` `cameraModFinalZoom` (2537-2562) and `cameraModFinalPitch` (2751-2762). When `m_doingRotateCamera` is set, remaining time is `(numFrames+numHoldFrames-curFrame)*TheW3DFrameLengthInMsec` and zoom/pitch animate over that remaining rotate.

Leftover path + behavior: `GameEngine/GameClient/src/display/view.rs` `camera_mod_final_zoom` / `camera_mod_final_pitch` apply over `camera_rotate.remaining_frames()` first, then over an active move.

Duration 0 snaps zoom/pitch immediately.

Evidence: a scripted rotate plus same-frame `CAMERA_MOD_SET_FINAL_ZOOM`/`PITCH` should ease over the remaining rotate; live snaps. Not a duplicate of hq-kf6mx (zoom scale) or hq-2mgn1 (ease-in/out).
close_reason: CAMERA_MOD_FINAL_ZOOM/PITCH ease over remaining ROTATE_CAMERA time

title: [Cam] LOOK_TOWARD_WAYPOINT reverseRotation dropped at presentation
description:
C++ path + behavior: `GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DView.cpp` `rotateCameraTowardPosition` (2477-2483). If `reverseRotation` is true, the target yaw is shifted by ±2π so the camera takes the long way around. `ScriptActions.cpp` passes param 4 (`getInt`) into that call.

Leftover path + behavior: `GameEngine/GameLogic/src/scripting/executor/actions_camera.rs` `do_camera_look_toward_waypoint` reads param 4 and forwards `reverse_rotation`. `GameEngine/GameClient/src/core/script_action_handler.rs` `camera_look_toward_waypoint` and `GameEngine/GameClient/src/display/view.rs` `rotate_camera_toward_position` implement the same ±2π block.

Live path + behavior: `Main/src/game_logic/mission_scripts.rs` stores `CameraLookTowardWaypointRequest.reverse_rotation` and `start_game.rs` `apply_camera_look_toward_request` honors it. The presentation freeze drops the flag: `presentation_frame/frame.rs` has only position/duration/ease, `presentation_frame/build.rs` copies those three, and `cnc_game_engine/camera_drain.rs` rebuilds the request with `reverse_rotation: false`. The honoring code is unreachable with true.

Evidence: campaign `CAMERA_LOOK_TOWARD_WAYPOINT` with reverse=true always takes the short yaw on the live host. Not a duplicate of hq-rttv2 (instant snap) or hq-2iunm (mod look-toward).
close_reason: Presentation freeze copies reverse_rotation; camera_drain forwards it so LOOK_TOWARD_WAYPOINT takes the long-way ±2π yaw.

title: [LookAt] Vertical pan drops C++ display-aspect speed boost
description:
C++ path + behavior: `W3DView.cpp` `scrollBy` (1779-1823). `aspect = getWidth()/getHeight()`; `end.X = start.X + delta->x*SCROLL_RESOLUTION`; `end.Y = start.Y + delta->y*SCROLL_RESOLUTION*aspect`. Vertical screen delta is pre-multiplied by view aspect before the world conversion.

Leftover path + behavior: `GameEngine/GameClient/src/display/view.rs` `scroll_by` uses `aspect = width/height` and `start.y + (delta.y * SCROLL_RESOLUTION * aspect)`, then unprojects both points — same construction.

Live path + behavior: `Main/src/cnc_game_engine/mouse.rs` `camera_scroll_world_delta` scales `((right * screen_scroll.x) + (forward * -screen_scroll.y)) * (height/250.0)`. X and Y share the same scale; no aspect term exists on the live pan path.

Evidence: retail vertical pan is faster than horizontal by the view aspect (~2.22x on 1920x1080 with the 80% tactical frac). Live key/edge/RMB vertical panning is ~2x slower relative to horizontal. Not a duplicate of hq-88sit (zoom-independent world step).
close_reason: Live camera_scroll_world_delta multiplies vertical screen delta by tactical-view aspect (W3DView::scrollBy).

title: [LookAt] Replay hover cursor ignores hasMouseMovedRecently gate
description:
C++ path + behavior: `LookAtXlat.cpp:117-127` `hasMouseMovedRecently` (1 logic-second window) has two consumers. `InGameUI.cpp:2462` suppresses hover SELECTING/ARROW updates during `RECORDERMODETYPE_PLAYBACK` unless the mouse moved within 1s. The replayed cursor stays put until the viewer moves the mouse.

Leftover path + behavior: `GameEngine/GameClient/src/gui/ingame_ui/impl_input.rs` `mouseover_cursor_update_allowed(!playback || mouse_moved_recently)` (839-844) applied in `create_mouseover_hint(_from_presentation)`. Main never calls the leftover setters. The InGameUI gate stays at defaults (playback=false, moved=true). `sync_ingame_mouseover_hint` runs on every camera change during playback and drives hover cursor/tooltip from replayed camera motion under a stationary mouse.

Evidence: leftover implements the C++ gate; live owns both signals (`lookat` frame stamps + `host_recorder_is_playback`) and never connects them. Not a duplicate of hq-7pm7b (stamp refresh).
close_reason: Live hover feeds InGameUISubsystem playback + hasMouseMovedRecently; replay cursor/tooltip stay put until the viewer moves.

title: [Dozer] Same-frame BUILD+REPAIR tie resumes REPAIR not BUILD
description:
## C++
`DozerAIUpdate::getMostRecentCommand` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/AIUpdate/DozerAIUpdate.cpp:2244-2268`) walks tasks `i = 0..DOZER_NUM_TASKS` (BUILD, REPAIR, FORTIFY) and keeps a slot only when `m_task[i].m_taskOrderFrame > mostRecentFrame`. Equal order frames therefore keep BUILD. Idle `isBuildMostImportant` (`:1314`) then resumes the scaffold first.

## Leftover
`DozerAIUpdate::get_most_recent_command` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/update/ai_update/dozer_ai_update.rs:590-603`) iterates `[Build, Repair, Fortify]` with the same strict `order_frame > most_recent_frame`. BUILD wins ties.

## Live
`dozer_most_recent_pending_task` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/command_executor/leftover.rs:1562-1577`) uses `frame >= f` and checks REPAIR after BUILD, so a same-frame pair replaces BUILD with REPAIR. `dozer_idle_resume_pending_build` (`:1617-1621`) then `return false` when the winner is repair, so idle / Stop does not resume the parked scaffold. `dozer_new_task_build` / `dozer_new_task_repair` both stamp the current logic frame.

## Player-visible
A dozer given BUILD then REPAIR in the same tick (queued/scripted, or BUILD parked then same-frame repair) resumes the repair first in live; C++/leftover resume the scaffold first. After Stop, live idle resume can skip the parked BUILD entirely.

Distinct from closed hq-vmy49 (parked-slot machinery) and hq-msoee (player-command cancel).
notes: 2026-10-24 source-audit correction for future ownership extraction: current original DozerAIUpdate.cpp2244-2265 getMostRecentCommand iterates BUILD0->REPAIR1->FORTIFY2 and updates only on strict greater frame from initial0, retaining BUILD on equal positive BUILD/REPAIR timestamps. Current accepted Main leftover_dispatch_tests.rs596 explicitly expects BUILD/Constructing on that tie. Historical Bead title saying REPAIR is not authoritative and must not prompt changing the source-correct selector. New shared task-owner extraction must preserve original source and actual fixture; this note is source audit, not a newly executed runtime acceptance.
close_reason: Live dozer_most_recent_pending_task now uses strict order_frame > so same-frame BUILD+REPAIR keeps BUILD and idle resume takes the scaffold.

title: [Locomotor] Wings march never floors to MinSpeed on approach
description:
## C++
`locoUpdate_moveTowardsPosition` clears `IS_BRAKING` for `LOCO_WINGS` unconditionally (Locomotor.cpp:1046-1050). `moveTowardsPositionWings` (Locomotor.cpp:1821-1860) then delegates 2D to `moveTowardsPositionOther` (Locomotor.cpp:1859-1860). Other still applies the approach floor at Locomotor.cpp:2368-2374: when `!NO_SLOW_DOWN` and `onPathDistToGoal < calcSlowDownDist(actualSpeed, m_minSpeed, getBraking())`, `goalSpeed = m_minSpeed`. Jets ease from cruise to MinSpeed before the waypoint; they never latch `IS_BRAKING` / pose-cheat.

## Leftover (right)
`move_towards_position_wings_physics` (`core_impl/move_air.rs:21-90`) delegates to `move_towards_position_other_physics`, which floors to `template.min_speed` (`move_ground.rs:552-561`, comment "C++ Locomotor.cpp:2368-2374: uses minSpeed, not 0.0").

## Live (wrong)
`apply_cpp_approach_brake` (`object/physics_motion.rs:1216-1219`) early-returns `desired_speed` for `LocomotorAppearance::Wings` **before** the `_ =>` minSpeed-floor arm (`:1303-1310`). Production march (`world_tick/movement.rs:660-665`) therefore never slows jets near waypoints/destination. Test `movement.rs:1807-1809` ("wings never brake") asserts goal stays at desired 40 — locking in the divergence.

Raptor cruise Speed 175 vs MinSpeed 60: C++ eases 175→60 within `calcSlowDownDist`; live holds 175 until the 1-unit close-enough, so jets blast through turn points and hard-plant on arrival.

Not a duplicate of hq-iriyu (treads/wheels/legs brake *curves*; documented wings IS_BRAKING clear only), hq-nj3s7 (dist source), hq-7f4ct (NoSlowDown un-latch), hq-py0re (idle circle), or hq-wievi (JetAI landing MaxSpeed clamp).

## Evidence
C++ Locomotor.cpp:1046-1050, 1859-1860, 2368-2374. Leftover move_air.rs:21-90, move_ground.rs:552-561. Live physics_motion.rs:1216-1219, 1303-1310; movement.rs:660-665.
close_reason: Live apply_cpp_approach_brake no longer early-returns desiredSpeed for Wings. C++ Locomotor.cpp:1046-1050 clears IS_BRAKING then moveTowardsPositionWings delegates to Other which floors to minSpeed (2368-2374). Leftover move_air.rs:21-90 / move_ground.rs:552-561.

title: [BuildAssistant] Live moveObjects never refuses human build on unmovables

moveObjectsForConstruction returns FALSE when any footprint occupant cannot be scooted: enemy-relationship objects, or allied/neutral objects with no AIUpdateInterface. buildObjectNow then refuses the build for PLAYER_HUMAN owners (`return NULL; ai gets to cheat`), so the human is not charged and no structure is created on top of un-scootable objects.

Leftover path + behavior:
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/system/build_assistant.rs:845-886
BuildAssistant::move_objects_for_construction sets any_unmovables on backend.object_relationship_enemy or failed backend.move_object_aside and returns !any_unmovables — the C++ bool contract.

Live path + behavior:
GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/ui_production.rs:891-935 GameLogic::move_objects_for_construction returns () and silently skips enemies, disabled, and !can_move occupants; it only set_destination's movable allies.

close_reason: Live move_objects_for_construction now returns leftover/C++ bool (enemy or no-AI occupants are unmovables). Human execute_build and place_line_build_segment refuse before charge/create when that is FALSE.

title: [FX] ViewShake impulse double-ticked per live frame
description:
C++ FXList.cpp:371-374 ViewShakeFXNugget::doFXPos -> TheTacticalView->shake. W3DView.cpp:1274-1289 processes the impulse ONCE per client frame: offset = intensity*(cos,sin); intensity *= 0.75; angle sign flips. Oscillating kick dies in ~1s.

Leftover fx_list.rs:1477-1496 ViewShakeFXNugget -> with_tactical_view(view.shake). view.rs:902-915 tick_impulse_shake is the C++ port. GameClient update_effects (impl_update.rs:1447-1450) ticks it once, and update_presentation_shell:1360 calls update_effects.

Live ticks the same thread-local View twice in one InGame frame: (a) camera_drain.rs host_tick_game_client_presentation_shell -> update_presentation_shell -> update_effects -> tick_impulse_shake; (b) camera_drain.rs:2110 update_camera -> start_game.rs:1446-1453 another tick_impulse_shake under the stale comment \"Leftover GameClient::update is not on the live tick\". Intensity decays x0.5625 instead of x0.75 and the double sign-flip keeps the sampled offset on the same side, so FX_Nuke SEVERE / tank-shell STRONG kicks push one direction and vanish ~1.8x faster. Distinct from closed hq-ya5dc (never damps — that fix added the manual tick; the shell tick was wired later).
close_reason: Live update_script_camera_shake now only samples leftover View::impulse_shake_offset. Presentation-shell update_effects ticks impulse once per InGame frame (intensity *= 0.75, sign flip), matching leftover GameClient and C++ W3DView::update. Removed the second tick that decayed x0.5625 and cancelled oscillation.

title: [Particle] ParticleSysBone drops bone Z rotation

title: [Pathfind] Live zone flood merges rubble into ground and treats Impassable as zone 0
description:
## C++
`calculateZones` (`AIPathfind.cpp:2329-2340`) joins cells only when `getType()` is equal, so `CELL_RUBBLE` is its own zone (not Clear). Impassable / BridgeImpassable / Obstacle also get real zone ids. `getEffectiveZone` (`:3157-3162`) joins clear↔rubble only for `GROUND|RUBBLE` locomotors via `m_groundRubbleZones`. `clientSafeQuickDoesPathExist` then compares effective zones.

## Leftover (right)
`block_zones.rs` `flood_fill_type` (`:488-516`) floods by exact cell type (Rubble separate; Impassable gets a real zone). `build_surface_combiners` builds `ground_rubble_zones` via `pair_ground_rubble` (`:668-669, :699-700`). `ZoneManager::get_effective_zone` has a GROUND+RUBBLE branch (`:258-261`). `are_connected` returns true on zone 0 only when zones are genuinely uncalculated (`:179-181`).

## Live (wrong)
`path_zone_flood_kind` (`pathfinding.rs:1413-1421`) maps Rubble into `_ => Some(0)` — the same flood kind as Clear — so rubble fields merge into ground zones. Impassable / Obstacle / BridgeImpassable return `None` and stay zone 0. `build_surface_combiners` / `get_effective_zone` (`:1560-1658`) have water/cliff tables only — no GROUND+RUBBLE. `quick_path_exists_for` (`:1688-1692`) treats `z==0` as uninitialized → **true**.

## Evidence
hq-c88bl closed CELL_RUBBLE stamping. hq-998ki closed missing water/cliff combiners. Remaining: rubble identity + Impassable-as-0. Feeds find_path zone precheck (`:5500`), `destination_cell_ok` (`:3042-3048`), rally (`unit_commands.rs`), and placement (`ui_production.rs`).

## Player-visible
GROUND-only units get "path exists" across/into destroyed-building rubble and map-edge Impassable / under-deck BridgeImpassable cells. Rally and placement skip the no-path warning. C++/leftover refuse unless the locomotor is GROUND+RUBBLE.
close_reason: Live path_zone_flood_kind floods by exact cell type (Rubble != Clear; Impassable/Obstacle/BridgeImpassable get real zones). build_surface_combiners + get_effective_zone join Clear↔Rubble only for GROUND|RUBBLE. stamp_rubble_at_world rebuilds zones after destroy stamps.

title: [Pathfind] Hover/thrust aircraft skip leftover tall-building segment detour
description:
## C++
`Pathfinder::getAircraftPath` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/AI/AIPathfind.cpp:5781-5847`):
- `checkClips` is true only when `getAppearance() == LOCO_WINGS` and gates **only** `circleClipsTallBuilding`.
- The `segmentIntersectsTallBuilding` insertion walk (`limit=20`) runs for **every** aircraft path (hover/thrust included).
- `avoidObject = ai->getBuildingToNotPathAround()` (Chinook combat-drop goal).

## Leftover (right)
`pathfind_complete/line_passable.rs` `get_aircraft_path` (`:390-455`): `circle_clips_tall_building` only when `check_clips`; the segment loop is unconditional with `limit=20` and plumbs `avoid_object` into both helpers.

## Live (wrong)
`PathfindingSystem::find_path_ex_surfaces` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/pathfinding.rs:6941-6957`) sets `check_clips = self.seeker_wings` and gates **both** `circle_clips_tall_building` and `detour_path_around_tall_buildings` on that flag. Hover/thrust (Chinook/Helix) get a two-node straight line. `detour_path_around_tall_buildings` also hardcodes `ignore=None` (`:6750`) and uses a per-segment insert cap of 4 with no overall 20 limit.

hq-8vdsw closed over-clipping (circleClips on ALL aircraft). That fix also hid the segment walk from non-WINGS. Distinct remaining gap: C++/leftover still detour hover/thrust around `KINDOF_AIRCRAFT_PATH_AROUND` buildings.

title: [Pathfind] Live patchPath ignores occupancy so stuck units re-path through parked allies
description:
## C++
`Pathfinder::patchPath` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/AI/AIPathfind.cpp:10344-10520`) walks the original path reverse from last→first. Each node runs `checkForMovement` with `considerTransient = blocked`, then relaxes transient outside ±2 cells of the start. Breaks on `!checkForMovement` or `allyFixedCount || enemyFixed` ("Don't patch through cells that are occupied"). Tracks `goalPos` as the still-clear node closest to the unit, A*s to a matching suffix node, splices, then `path->optimize(obj, surfaces, blocked)`.

## Leftover (right)
`pathfind_complete/classify.rs` `patch_path` (`:55-228`) matches: `CheckMovementInfo` with `consider_transient=blocked`, ±2 relaxation, break on `!check_for_movement || ally_fixed_count>0 || enemy_fixed`, closest-goal tracking, suffix-node fallback, splice, `optimize_path`.

## Live (wrong)
`PathfindingSystem::patch_path` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/pathfinding.rs:7000-7046`) reverse-walks with only static `cell_passable_for_layer`. No occupancy, no `blocked`/considerTransient, no closest-goal tracking, no suffix fallback, no post-splice optimize. Called from `world_tick/movement.rs:244-253` when `is_blocked_and_stuck` or `num_frames_blocked>60`.

## Evidence
hq-hsw04 closed "never patchPath" by adding this thinner residual. Occupancy-aware suffix scan is a remaining leftover-right/live-wrong gap.

## Player-visible
A stuck unit whose remaining waypoints sit on parked allies (statically passable cells) is re-patched straight through the occupants and keeps colliding. C++/leftover splice onto nodes past the occupied stretch.
close_reason: patch_path binds the stuck mover, refreshes occupancy, skips allyFixed/enemyFixed suffix nodes with ±2 transient relaxation, closest-goal + suffix fallback, then optimize. movement.rs passes objects+id.

title: [Physics] Stun cliff/water kill has no AIUpdateInterface gate
description:
## C++
`PhysicsBehavior::testStunnedUnitForDestruction` (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1764-1793): after upside-down (`Get_Z_Vector().Z < 0`) and off-map kills, `AIUpdateInterface *aiInt = obj->getAI(); if (!aiInt) return;`. Cliff (`isCliffCell && !hasLocomotorForSurface(CLIFF)`) and water (`isUnderwater && !hasLocomotorForSurface(WATER)`) kills run only for AI-driven units. AI-less debris/props/crates keep tumbling.

## Leftover (right)
`test_stunned_unit_for_destruction` (GameLogic/src/object/behavior/physics_bounce.rs:91-108): `let Some(ai) = obj.get_ai() else { return; }` before cliff (:101-104) and water (:105-108). Matches C++.

## Live (wrong)
`Object::test_stunned_unit_for_destruction` (Main/src/game_logic/object/physics_motion.rs:968-990) has no AI gate. `ensure_locomotor_surfaces` (:953-957) stamps a template-name default (GROUND for anything not aircraft/hover/amphib/ship), then cliff (:983-985) and water (:987-989) always fire. Called on every successful bounce from `tick_physics_motion_step` and `handle_shock_ground_bounce`.

`apply_shock_wave_impulse` (object/physics.rs:96-140) stuns every eligible non-structure/non-projectile body, including AI-less OCL debris. Shockwave-stunned debris/props landing on a cliff or water cell are destroyed on first bounce; C++/leftover leave them alive (they still get upside-down/off-map kills).

Not a duplicate of hq-ugu06 (Object::kill Die pipeline) or hq-7vpd (handleBounce never called the test).

## Evidence
C++ PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1777-1793. Leftover physics_bounce.rs:91-108. Live physics_motion.rs:953-990, object/physics.rs:96-140.
close_reason: Live test_stunned_unit_for_destruction now returns after upside-down/off-map unless leftover thing-factory AIUpdate (or mobile combat fallback) exists, matching C++ getAI() gate so stunned debris/crates keep tumbling on cliff/water.

title: [Save] CHUNK_GameState header campaign side/mission never from CampaignManager
description:
## C++
`GameState::xfer` (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/System/SaveGame/GameState.cpp:1614-1640) refreshes the v2 header on save from `TheCampaignManager`: if a campaign is current, `campaignSide = campaign->m_name` and `missionNumber = getCurrentMissionNumber()` (0-based); otherwise empty string + `CampaignManager::INVALID_MISSION_NUMBER`. `populateSaveGameListbox` shows those fields as the faction/mission columns.

## Leftover (right)
`Common/src/system/SaveGame/game_state.rs:1269-1280` on Save mode calls `notify_get_campaign_snapshot()` and writes that campaign side + mission number, else clears / `INVALID_MISSION_NUMBER`. Score-screen leftover mission-save uses this path.

## Live
`cnc_game_engine/host_authority.rs:1032-1041` `build_save_info` hardcodes `campaign_side = Some(local_team_name)` for every save (including skirmish/LAN) and `mission_number = None`. `save_file.rs:205-211` `write_cpp_game_state_header` then writes that team name + `INVALID_MISSION_NUMBER`. CHUNK_Campaign itself is captured/restored separately (`write_campaign_block` / `capture_campaign_manager_runtime`) — only the list-header metadata is wrong.

## Player-visible
Save-load list (`ui/save_load_menu.rs:666-670`) shows `Faction: <team>` on non-campaign saves (C++ wrote empty) and never `Mission N` for live campaign saves.

## Evidence
C++ GameState.cpp:1614-1640; leftover game_state.rs:1269-1280; live host_authority.rs:1032-1041 and save_file.rs:205-211.
close_reason: CHUNK_GameState v2 header campaign side/mission now from CampaignManager (empty + INVALID when no campaign). Save list no longer invents a faction label on skirmish saves.

title: [Parachute] Empty chute never dies mid-air after losing rider
description:
C++ `ParachuteContain::update` (`ParachuteContain.cpp:411-413`): "If we have lost our passenger for whatever reason, die early. Otherwise we just sit around forever." `if (getContainCount() == 0) getObject()->kill();` — altitude-independent, before the water-slop check.

Leftover `ParachuteContain::update` (`parachute_contain.rs:853-855`) is the same unconditional empty-count kill.

Live `tick_eject_parachute_residual` (`saboteur_car_bomb.rs:573-622`) destroys `AmericaParachute` only in the `is_chute && landed` ground-contact branch (C++ `onCollide(null)` land dump). There is no mid-air `containCount==0` kill. A riderless chute keeps freefalling, stays alive, and remains a `KINDOF_PARACHUTE` AntiParachute target until it hits the ground.

Retail authors the object (`AmericaParachute` via `OCL_EjectPilotViaParachute`, paradrop `PutInContainer`, hijacker airborne eject). Player-visible: shoot the parachuting rider (not the chute) mid-air — C++ empty chute dies immediately; live ghost chute drifts down as a hittable decoy.

Not a duplicate of closed hq-motc / hq-hq5fm / hq-i4xch / hq-fnz14 / hq-cxdch / hq-14d7 (other parachute legs). Wave15 left this unfiled as "narrow"; leftover is right and live is still wrong.
close_reason: Live tick_eject_parachute_residual now matches C++ ParachuteContain::update / leftover parachute_contain.rs:853-855: after occupant sweep, containCount==0 kills AmericaParachute mid-air (altitude-independent, HELD skips). Land dump still releases riders; empty-count kill covers land and rider-loss.

title: [Locomotor] Live lift/SpeedLimitZ bind undoes leftover per-frame units
description:
## C++
`INI::parseAccelerationReal` (INI.cpp:1717-1724) stores Lift/LiftDamaged as dist/sec² ÷ 900 = dist/frame². `INI::parseVelocityReal` (INI.cpp:1710-1716) stores SpeedLimitZ as dist/sec ÷ 30 = dist/frame. `calcLiftToUseAtPt` (Locomotor.cpp:2022-2110) mixes those with `TheGlobalData->m_gravity` (also parseAccelerationReal, retail -64/900). `handleBehaviorZ` applyMotiveForce is per-frame Euler.

## Leftover (right)
Common `ini_locomotor.rs:527-537` stores Lift/LiftDamaged `/900`. `ini_bridge.rs:93-94` copies lift as-is (already per-frame²). `ini_bridge.rs:108-112` applies `parse_velocity_real` (÷30) to SpeedLimitZ. Leftover `calc_lift_to_use_at_pt` (`maintain.rs:552-605`) is all-per-frame², matching C++.

## Live (wrong)
`host_locomotor_binding_from_template` (`locomotor_bootstrap.rs:900-906`):
- `max_lift = t.lift * FPS * FPS` — Common already stored `/900`, so this inflates back to per-sec² and writes that into the per-frame lift channel.
- `speed_limit_z = t.speed_limit_z` — Common stores raw dist/sec; leftover bridge ÷30 is never applied.

`Object::calc_lift_to_use_at_pt` (`object/physics.rs:1019-1063`) then mixes:
- `max_lift` (per-sec², ~900× too large)
- `leftover_loco_gravity()` (`physics.rs:122, 1768-1785` = retail -64/900 per-frame²)
- `speed_limit_z` (per-sec compared as if per-frame)

`apply_surface_relative_lift` (`physics.rs:654-657`) applyMotiveForce + the Z Euler (`world_tick/physics.rs`) are dt-less per-frame. Every INI-bound hover/wings aircraft has ~900× lift vs gravity and a 30× SpeedLimitZ cap miss. Tests that set `max_lift = 5.0` by hand do not catch the bind.

Not a duplicate of hq-rqv8 (leftover Common converters; leftover GameLogic bridge is already right) or hq-ygdfb/hq-ryf26/hq-2e10h (lift *path*, not unit scale).

## Evidence
C++ INI.cpp:1710-1724, Locomotor.cpp:428-437, 2022-2110. Leftover ini_locomotor.rs:527-574, ini_bridge.rs:93-112, maintain.rs:552-605. Live locomotor_bootstrap.rs:900-906, 953-955; object/physics.rs:1019-1063, 1768-1785.
close_reason: host_locomotor_binding_from_template copies Common Lift/LiftDamaged as already-per-frame2 (/900) and applies parseVelocityReal (/30) to authored SpeedLimitZ, matching leftover ini_bridge.rs:93-112. Omitted SpeedLimitZ stays BIGNUM.

title: [Cave] Occupant death never leaves CaveSystem pool
description:
C++ `Object::onDestroy` (`Object.cpp:720-728`) calls `m_containedBy->getContain()->removeFromContain(this)`. For caves that is `CaveContain::removeFromContain` (`CaveContain.cpp:54-83`): it removes the rider from the CaveIndex `TunnelTracker` *before* `onRemoving`, so a dying occupant frees the shared slot and a last-empty team revert can fire.

Leftover `CaveContain::remove_from_contain` (`cave_contain.rs:423-456`) does the same tracker remove then `on_removing`.

Live `process_destroy_list` (`destroy_list_bounty.rs:256-275`) only `remove_occupant`s the entrance's local list and `tunnel_network.record_exit`s GLA tunnels. There is no `cave_system.record_exit` / `index_holding_unit` cleanup on occupant death. Voluntary exit already goes through `exit_cave_unit` (`special_power_flights.rs:1709-1725`) — that is hq-ppun8, already closed. Death, splash, scripts, and bunker-buster force-exit (`missile_defenders.rs:2057-2066`, tunnel-only) leave the dead id in `cave_system.networks[idx].contained`.

Retail INI authors CaveContain + CaveIndex (civilian caves). Player-visible: a killed cave occupant leaks a slot (max 10), LastEmpty never reverts the network team, and later exits still list the corpse.
close_reason: Live process_destroy_list now calls exit_cave_unit (cave_system.record_exit + LastEmpty) on occupant death, matching C++ Object::onDestroy → CaveContain::removeFromContain tracker remove then onRemoving.

title: [Weapon] Frenzy apply keeps higher level and longer expiry
description:
## C++
`TempWeaponBonusHelper::doTempWeaponBonus` (`TempWeaponBonusHelper.cpp:65-83`): if `m_currentBonus != status` it `clearTempWeaponBonus()` first (clears the old `WeaponBonusCondition` + FRENZY tint), then `setWeaponBonusCondition(status)`, `m_currentBonus = status`, `m_frameToRemove = TheGameLogic->getFrame() + duration`. Re-applying the same status only resets the timer. FRENZY_ONE / TWO / THREE are distinct `WeaponBonusConditionType` values, so a later lower-level Frenzy pulse **downgrades** the multiplier and **shortens** the expiry to now+new-duration.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/object/helper/temp_weapon_bonus_helper.rs:100-119` `do_temp_weapon_bonus`: clears a different bonus before applying; same-bonus re-apply sets `frame_to_remove = current_frame + duration`. Tests cover timer reset and fanaticism clearing frenzy.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/object/bonuses.rs:29-40` `apply_weapon_bonus_frenzy`: keeps the **higher** level (`if lvl > level` keep) and only **extends** the timer (`if until_frame > current` extend). Overlapping allied Frenzy casts (C++ `WeaponBonusUpdate` ALLOW_ALLIES, live `host_frenzy`) never downgrade 130%→110% and never shorten a longer remaining expiry.

## Evidence
C++ `TempWeaponBonusHelper.cpp:65-73`. Leftover `temp_weapon_bonus_helper.rs:100-119`. Live `bonuses.rs:29-40`. Distinct from closed hq-3ir6n (Allies filter + contained walk).

## Player-visible
Two allied Frenzy casters of different science tiers: a unit already under Frenzy 3 keeps 130% damage for the long timer after a Frenzy 1 pulse. C++/leftover drop to Frenzy 1 and restart the short timer.
close_reason: Live apply_weapon_bonus_frenzy now matches leftover do_temp_weapon_bonus: different FRENZY_* level clears then replaces (downgrade included); same-level re-apply always writes until_frame (shorten included). No keep-higher / keep-longer.

title: [Helix] Nuke bomb unpause maps to NuclearMissile
description:
## C++
Nuke Helix carries `Nuke_SpecialAbilityHelixNukeBomb` (`StartsPaused = Yes`) and `UnpauseSpecialPowerUpgrade` with `SpecialPowerTemplate = Nuke_SpecialAbilityHelixNukeBomb` / `TriggeredBy = Nuke_Upgrade_HelixNukeBomb`. `UnpauseSpecialPowerUpgrade.cpp:67-78` walks `getSpecialPower()` modules and unpauses the matching template. After unpause the ctor-started ReloadTime (10000ms) must elapse before the first drop.

## Leftover (right)
`object/upgrade/unpause_special_power_upgrade.rs:129-176` unpauses by SpecialPowerTemplate name, same as C++. `object/special_power_module.rs` initialize starts recharge then pauses `StartsPaused` modules.

## Live (wrong)
`host_upgrade_module_residuals.rs:150-153` `unpause_power_for_upgrade` maps any upgrade containing `"helixnuke"` to `SpecialPowerType::NuclearMissile`. `object_queries.rs:2573-2588` then unpauses NuclearMissile on the Helix (a power the Helix does not carry).

The power live actually fires is `SpecialPowerType::HelixNukeBomb` (`command_executor/special_power.rs:767-772` / `:1136-1148` gates on `Nuke_Upgrade_HelixNukeBomb`). `power_starts_paused` (`host_upgrade_module_residuals.rs:171-180`) omits `HelixNukeBomb`. `init_starts_paused_special_powers` candidates are only RadarScan / HelixNapalmBomb (`drones_and_garrison.rs:2346-2354`); a name containing `"helix"` also pauses HelixNapalmBomb, which a Nuke general can never unpause.

`host_helix_napalm.rs:110-115` documents the retail pair: `UPGRADE_HELIX_NUKE_BOMB = "Nuke_Upgrade_HelixNukeBomb"`, `HELIX_NUKE_BOMB_SPECIAL_POWER = "Nuke_SpecialAbilityHelixNukeBomb"`. `command_system/special_power.rs:258` already maps that template name to `HelixNukeBomb`.

## Evidence
C++ / leftover match template name. Live name-sniff sends the unpause to NuclearMissile. HelixNukeBomb is never StartsPaused, so `queue_helix_napalm_bomb` becomes legal the instant the upgrade is owned — no 10s reload.

## Player-visible
Researching Nuke Helix bomb lets the first drop fire immediately (C++ waits ReloadTime). The intended unpause never hits HelixNukeBomb.
close_reason: Live unpause_power_for_upgrade maps Nuke_Upgrade_HelixNukeBomb to HelixNukeBomb (not NuclearMissile). power_starts_paused and init_starts_paused name-sniff a Nuke Helix onto HelixNukeBomb so ctor start+pause + upgrade unpause match leftover UnpauseSpecialPowerUpgrade template-name walk.

title: [SpecialPower] StartsPaused unit init double-pauses so upgrade never arms
description:
## C++
`SpecialPowerModule::SpecialPowerModule` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/SpecialPower/SpecialPowerModule.cpp:76-101`) for a pre-built object calls `startPowerRecharge()` (non-SharedNSync) **then** `pauseCountdown(TRUE)` when `StartsPaused`. `UnpauseSpecialPowerUpgrade::upgradeImplementation` (`UnpauseSpecialPowerUpgrade.cpp:67-78`) matches `SpecialPowerTemplate` and calls `pauseCountdown(FALSE)` once. Unpause slides `availableOnFrame` by the paused duration, so the first fire still waits the authored ReloadTime (capture 15000ms, RadarVanScan 30000ms, HelixNapalm 10000ms).

Retail Object INI: Ranger/Rebel/RedGuard `SpecialAbility` + `StartsPaused = Yes` + `UnpauseSpecialPowerUpgrade TriggeredBy = Upgrade_InfantryCaptureBuilding`. Same pattern for `SpecialPowerRadarVanScan` / `Upgrade_GLARadarVanScan` and `SpecialAbilityHelixNapalmBomb` / `Upgrade_HelixNapalmBomb`.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/object/special_power_module.rs` `initialize` (`:204-216`): `start_power_recharge_at` then `pause_countdown(true)` for `starts_paused`. `object/upgrade/unpause_special_power_upgrade.rs` unpauses the matching template once.

## Live (wrong)
Two pause paths on every `create_object`:

1. `world_combat/drones_and_garrison.rs:2218` / `:2341-2359` `init_starts_paused_special_powers` pauses capture / RadarScan / HelixNapalmBomb **without** `start_power_recharge_with_frames` (only HDB at `:2324-2335` starts recharge first).
2. Then `create_destroy_die.rs:2226-2229` → `apply_create_modules_on_build_complete` → `production_eva.rs:1289-1318` `on_structure_superweapon_creation` walks parsed `special_power_modules` (includes `SpecialAbility`, `special_power.rs:274-280`) and does start-recharge **then pause again**.

`pause_special_power_countdown` is a refcount (`object/orders.rs:85-103`). Retail INI units therefore sit at pausedCount=2. `object_queries.rs:2554-2588` unpauses once on upgrade → still paused. Capture / RadarVanScan / Helix napalm never arm after research.

Name-sniff templates without `special_power_modules` only hit path 1: unpause leaves rem=0 (instant first fire). `world_tests/projectiles_air.rs:7-40` encodes that instant-ready as expected; it is not C++.

## Evidence
C++ ctor order `startPowerRecharge` then `StartsPaused`. Leftover `initialize` matches. Live comments at `drones_and_garrison.rs:2299` admit recharge-before-pause but the capture/radar/helix loop never starts recharge, and SpecialPowerCreate then pauses a second time.

## Player-visible
After researching Capture / Radar Van Scan / Helix Napalm, the button stays disabled (retail INI double-pause) or fires immediately with no ReloadTime (name-sniff path). C++ waits the authored reload after unpause.
close_reason: init_starts_paused now matches leftover SpecialPowerModule initialize: startPowerRecharge then pauseCountdown once. on_structure_superweapon_creation only re-pauses when has_special_power_create (C++ SpecialPowerCreate). Capture/Radar/Helix unpause leaves authored ReloadTime instead of pausedCount=2 or rem=0.

title: [Shroud] Object FOW mix reads square looker cells not DiscreteCircle
description:
C++ `PartitionManager::doShroudReveal` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/PartitionManager.cpp:3937-3956`) walks a `DiscreteCircle` of `worldToCellDist(radius)` (min 1) and `hLineAddLooker`s those cells. `PartitionData::getShroudedStatus` (`:1615-1674`) then mixes object FOW from those same DiscreteCircle cells.

Leftover `ShroudManager::do_shroud_reveal` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/system/shroud_manager.rs:486-509`) matches C++: `world_to_cell_dist` + `DiscreteCircle` + horizontal looker lines. Live look already stamps that grid (`spawn_templates.rs` `restamp_host_partition_look` → `shroud_mgr.do_shroud_reveal`). Radar overlay / `refresh_shroud_for_local_player` also read leftover ShroudManager.

Live object FOW mix does not. `update_main_crate_vision` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/spawn_templates.rs:4530-4552`) samples `partition_cell_shroud_status`, which prefers leftover `PARTITION_MANAGER` (`partition_data.rs:145-165`). That grid is painted by `PartitionShroudGrid::reveal_circle` (`partition_shroud.rs:137-163`): a square `±ceil(radius/40)` walk with world-space cell-center `r²` reject — not DiscreteCircle. Live also stamps that square grid via `stamp_partition_cell_lookers`.

Player-visible: object Clear/Fogged/Shrouded (drawable hide, radar blip `getShroudedStatus > PARTIAL_CLEAR`, stealth IR, FX gates) uses the square looker disk, while the minimap/terrain overlay uses leftover DiscreteCircle. Units on the rim of vision can be visible in one and fogged in the other. Same class as closed hq-rt74q (value/threat square falloff), but looker/object FOW was never filed.

Not leftovers-only: leftover ShroudManager DiscreteCircle is already on the live look path. Live mix queries the leftover-wrong square grid instead.
close_reason: Live object FOW mix now samples leftover ShroudManager DiscreteCircle looker cells instead of PARTITION_MANAGER square r2 disk.

title: [Locomotor] Wheeled MinTurnSpeed floor uses reduced speed not maxSpeed
description:
## C++
`Locomotor::moveTowardsPositionWheels` (Locomotor.cpp:1260-1286, 1316-1323):
- `maxSpeed = getMaxSpeedForCondition(bdt)` — damage-condition constant.
- `turnSpeed = m_minTurnSpeed; if (turnSpeed < maxSpeed/4) turnSpeed = maxSpeed/4;`
- Then `|relAngle| > PI/20` clamps `desiredSpeed` down to that **fixed** floor.

The floor is not lowered when `desiredSpeed` is already cut by group speed, blocked-wait `bumpSpeedLimit`, or approach braking. A truck approaching dest at 8 with maxSpeed 40 / MinTurnSpeed 0 still has floor 10; 8 < 10 so no extra clamp.

## Leftover (right)
`move_towards_position_wheels_physics` (GameLogic/src/locomotor/core_impl/move_ground.rs:126, 131, 139-142): `max_speed = get_max_speed_for_condition(condition)` then `if turn_speed < max_speed / 4.0 { turn_speed = max_speed / 4.0; }`. Matches C++.

## Live (wrong)
`update_movement` (Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/movement.rs:712-718):
```
let mut turn_speed = obj.min_turn_speed;
if turn_speed < speed / 4.0 { turn_speed = speed / 4.0; }
if delta.abs() > PI/20 && speed > turn_speed { speed = turn_speed; }
```
`speed` is already `effective_max_speed()` after `apply_do_locomotor_blocked_speed` (movement.rs:548) and `apply_cpp_approach_brake` (movement.rs:660-666). The same collapsed floor is fed into the 15° look-ahead probe (movement.rs:739-749).

Same reduced-speed floor is in test-only `Object::update_movement` (object/update.rs:~306-313). Live `wheeled_turn_factor` (object/physics.rs:433-446) correctly floors at `effective_max_speed()/4` — only the march SMALL_TURN clamp is wrong.

## Player-visible
Wheeled units with authored MinTurnSpeed < maxSpeed/4 (typical: omitted MinTurnSpeed = BIGNUM is fine; many trucks use 0 or a small value) crawl ~4× slower through every >9° turn while already slowed (approach-brake near dest, formation `group_speed_factor`, blocked bump cap). Example: max 40, MinTurnSpeed 0, braked to 8 → C++ floor 10 (no clamp) vs live floor 2 (clamps to 2).

Not a duplicate of hq-2rfrw/hq-glk4v (turnFactor on rotate) or hq-rqv8 (INI unit conversion).

## Evidence
C++ Locomotor.cpp:1260-1286, 1316-1323. Leftover move_ground.rs:126-142. Live movement.rs:548, 660-666, 712-718, 739-749.
close_reason: wheeled_turn_speed_floor uses damage-condition effective_max_speed()/4 not the already-reduced desiredSpeed, matching leftover move_ground.rs:126-142 and C++ Locomotor.cpp:1283-1323. Wired in movement.rs march and test-only update.rs.

title: [Hunt] PLAYER_HUNT never leaveGroup before aiHunt
description:
C++ Player::setUnitsShouldHunt (Player.cpp:1979-2019) sets m_unitsShouldHunt, then for every team-prototype instance member that is not KINDOF_DOZER/HARVESTER/IGNORES_SELECT_ALL: obj->leaveGroup() then aiHunt/aiIdle if AIUpdateInterface exists. leaveGroup drops the current AIGroup/selection so units hunt independently and later group orders on the old group do not cancel hunt.

Leftover Player::set_units_should_hunt (player/production.rs:172-228) matches: KindOf skip, leave_group(), then ai_hunt/ai_idle. Leftover do_player_hunt queues HostScriptHuntGuardRequest::PlayerHunt when OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty.

Live PlayerHunt drain (scripts_camera.rs:1707-1738) sets units_should_hunt and unit_command_patrol on every owned non-dozer/harvester/ignores-select-all unit. unit_command_patrol (unit_commands.rs:973-1006) stamps player command source and Patrolling/hunting but never leaveGroup / clear formation_id. Units stay in the prior AIGroup/formation, so a later group move on that group yanks them off map-wide hunt.

Evidence: C++ Player.cpp:2008 leaveGroup; leftover production.rs:218 leave_group; live unit_command_patrol has no leaveGroup/formation clear.
close_reason: Live PlayerHunt drain now leaveGroup (clear formation_id + leftover Object::leave_group) before unit_command_patrol, matching C++ Player::setUnitsShouldHunt / leftover set_units_should_hunt.

title: [Hunt] TEAM_HUNT_WITH_COMMAND_BUTTON skips command-type gate and template-falls-back
description:
C++ ScriptActions::doTeamHuntWithCommandButton (ScriptActions.cpp:2003-2147) first findCommandButton(ability); if NULL return. Then switch command type: allow SPECIAL_POWER only with COMMAND_OPTION_NEED_OBJECT_TARGET, plus SWITCH_WEAPON / FIRE_WEAPON / HIJACK / CARBOMB / SABOTAGE. HACK_INTERNET, GUARD, CONSTRUCT, and every other GUI command hit default, append the debug error, and return before any unit is armed. No template-name fallback.
