A stealthed unit revealed to the local player through detection (detector unit/structure marks it DETECTED → calcStealthedStatusForPlayer returns VISIBLE_DETECTED) keeps drawing but its shadow is turned OFF. `setShadowsEnabled` propagates to every DrawModule's shadow (Drawable.cpp:857-869).

## Live
`shadows_enabled` on the frozen drawable comes only from `presentation_shadows_enabled()` (object/death.rs:712-717) = topple_data.shadows_enabled, i.e. only ToppleUpdate clears it. `collect_blob_shadows_from_presentation` (graphics/selection_renderer.rs:677-697) draws a dark blob disc for every `unit_render_inputs` row with `shadows_enabled`. Detected enemy stealth units stay in the mesh pass (correct: `local_viewer_hides_stealthed` only hides `effectively_stealthed` = stealthed && !detected), so a detected Burton/Jarmen/mine/tunnel keeps its blob shadow in live. No live path consults camo_stealth_look/StealthLook for shadows (host residuals Wave 79/97/1044 only freeze the ordinal).

## Player-visible
When your detector reveals an enemy stealth unit, C++ shows the model without a ground shadow; live shows a dark blob disc under it. For detected stealth structures (camo tunnels under CamoNetting with StealthLook=VISIBLE_DETECTED, camo_stealth_look=3) the blob also stays. Minor but a live-path visual difference on a recurring scenario (Pathfinder/outpost detection, detected mines).
close_reason: Detected stealth (VISIBLE_DETECTED) clears presentation_shadows_enabled so blob discs drop.

title: [Drawable] Own mines render at 50% opacity for friendly viewer — C++ KINDOF_MINE forces effective opacity 0
description:
## C++
`StealthUpdate::update` (StealthUpdate.cpp:628-634) special-cases mines every update: `if (self->isKindOf(KINDOF_MINE)) draw->setEffectiveOpacity(0.0f, 0.0f)` — m_stealthOpacity=0, effective=0, so `W3DScene` (W3DScene.cpp:1595) alphaOverride=0. This runs each frame BEFORE `setStealthLook` ( StealthUpdate.cpp:809-810), and setStealthLook's body is skipped when the look is unchanged, so the VISIBLE_FRIENDLY friendlyOpacity never sticks: mines are fully invisible to EVERY viewer, including their owner (you only find them via selection/radar).

## Live
The host already freezes the right value: `apply_mine_innate_stealth` sets `camo_friendly_opacity = MINE_STEALTH_OPACITY_RESIDUAL` (0.0, stealth.rs:225; constant host_radar_stealth_vision_residual.rs:351, re-asserted in world_scripts/stealth_mines.rs:876-880). But the mesh pass never reads it: `build.rs:767`/`overlay.rs:1974` freeze `friendly_stealth_opacity = template.stealth_friendly_opacity_min` (default 0.5, thing.rs:2518; mines have no FriendlyOpacityMin INI override in spawn_templates.rs:2737-2741), and `queries.rs:349-365` sets `input.presentation_opacity = object.friendly_stealth_opacity.clamp(0,1)` for `is_mine` under `local_viewer_uses_friendly_stealth_look`. Enemy viewers correctly hide undetected mines (`local_viewer_hides_stealthed`), but the friendly viewer sees every own mine/demo trap rendered at a static 50% alpha.

## Player-visible
Placing GLA mines / demo traps (or USA remote charges with mine kindof) leaves a half-visible model sitting on the field for the owner in live; in C++ the mine vanishes completely the moment it cloaks. Owner gets a permanent 50%-alpha marker C++ players never see (and 0.5 alpha also makes mine fields trivially scannable by scrolling the camera).
close_reason: Mines freeze camo_friendly_opacity (0) instead of template 0.5; mesh uses that for owner look.

title: Interrupted worker/dozer construction auto-resumes on live host; C++ cancels the task on any player command
description: C++ WorkerAIUpdate::aiDoCommand default case (WorkerAIUpdate.cpp:942-956) and DozerAIUpdate::aiDoCommand (DozerAIUpdate.cpp:2386-2387) cancel the CURRENT dozer task (cancelTask(getCurrentTask())) for every CMD_FROM_PLAYER command that is not Repair/ResumeConstruction — including Stop (AI.h:476-479 aiIdle routes AICMD_IDLE into aiDoCommand default), Move, Attack, and Dock. So a GLA worker (or dozer) that is actively building/repairing and gets any player order abandons the task; the scaffold stays until re-ordered. / Leftover: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine GameLogic dozer_ai_update.rs / worker_ai_update.rs never model this cancel either. / Live: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/command_executor/leftover.rs dozer_new_task_build parks dozer_task_build_target and only dozer_internal_task_complete (repair/construct completion paths) clears slots; execute_move (movement.rs), execute_stop (attack.rs) and GameLogic::unit_command_stop (unit_commands.rs:235-299) never clear the slots, and update_dozer_bored_repair + dozer_idle_resume_pending_build re-launch the parked BUILD as soon as the unit goes Idle. / Player-visible: order a building GLA worker to move away (or Stop it) — live walks it back to the scaffold and keeps building after the move completes; C++/retail leaves the half-built structure and an idle worker until the player re-orders.
close_reason: Live host: exclusive AS_SUPPLY_TRUCK skip idle/bored; FireWeaponWhenDead fires all modules and stamps after fire; mine-clear keeps boxes until already attacking; player commands cancel current dozer task.

title: [Drawable] Status tint applies instantly — C++ TintEnvelope ADSR ramps (30f disabled/frenzy, 150f subdual) missing
description:
## C++
`Drawable::updateDrawable` (Drawable.cpp:1228-1285) plays a TintEnvelope on tint-status edge: DISABLED and FRENZY use `play(color, 30, 30, SUSTAIN_INDEFINITELY)` (1s attack, 1s decay), GAINING_SUBDUAL_DAMAGE uses `play(SUBDUAL_DAMAGE_COLOR, 150, 150, SUSTAIN_INDEFINITELY)` (5s attack, 5s decay). `TintEnvelope::update` steps `m_currentColor` toward peak by `peak/frames` each frame, so the tint fades in/out gradually (TintEnvelope.cpp; TintEnvelope fields in Drawable.h:158-235).

## Live
`UnitRenderInput::from_renderable` (unit_render.rs:429-435) → `drawable_status_tint_rgb` (game_logic/object/stealth.rs:617-638) returns the full peak color `[-0.5,-0.5,-0.5]` / `[-0.2,-0.2,0.8]` / frenzy color immediately when the status bit is set, and `[0,0,0]` immediately when cleared. `render_item.apply_status_tint` (graphics/render_item.rs:834) applies it per frame with no ramp state. No envelope/attack/decay exists anywhere on the live path (no TintEnvelope host).

## Player-visible
EMP/black-lotus-disabled units snap to dark gray and snap back (C++: 1s fade in/out). Frenzy (Frenzy reward / China nationalism-era buff) tints snap on/off instead of 1s ramps. Subdual damage (microwave tanks, neutron-shelled units) blue tint snaps instantly in live; C++ slowly ramps over 5 seconds and fades out over 5 seconds — the C++ subdual tint is a slow 'freezing to death' cue, live is an instant flash.
close_reason: Live status tint samples TintEnvelope ADSR (30f disabled/frenzy, 150f subdual).

title: [Drawable] Disabled-status tint gate wrong: unmanned tints, underpowered/paralyzed/subdued/freefall do not
description:
## C++
`Object::setDisabledUntil` (Object.cpp:2099-2116) sets Drawable `TINT_STATUS_DISABLED` (dark gray `DARK_GRAY_DISABLED_COLOR {-0.5,-0.5,-0.5}`) on every disable edge whose type is NOT `DISABLED_HELD`, `DISABLED_SCRIPT_DISABLED`, or `DISABLED_UNMANNED` — i.e. DEFAULT, HACKED, EMP, PARALYZED, UNDERPOWERED, FREEFALL, AWESTRUCK, BRAINWASHED, SUBDUED, SCRIPT_UNDERPOWERED all tint dark gray. `clearDisabledUntil` (Object.cpp:2283-2302) clears the tint only when no non-exception disable flag remains. Note DISABLED_SUBDUED sets the *dark gray* tint, and TINT_STATUS_DISABLED outranks TINT_STATUS_GAINING_SUBDUAL_DAMAGE in `Drawable::updateDrawable`'s ladder (Drawable.cpp:1230-1253).

## Live
`UnitRenderInput::from_renderable` (Main/src/presentation_frame/unit_render.rs:429-435) computes `status_tint` via `drawable_status_tint_rgb(disabled_emp || disabled_hacked || disabled_unmanned, gaining_subdual || disabled_subdued, weapon_bonus_frenzy, infantry)`. Only EMP/HACKED/UNMANNED feed the dark-gray branch:
- UNMANNED wrongly included (C++ 'Doh^3. Unmanned is no tint too', Object.cpp:2112) — Jarmen-sniped vehicles glow dark gray in live, untinted in C++.
- UNDERPOWERED missing (live sets `obj.status.disabled_underpowered` from `update_power_disabled_state`, crates_radar_power.rs:1098, but presentation never tints) — low-power buildings stay normal-colored in live, dark gray in C++.
- PARALYZED, FREEFALL, DEFAULT, AWESTRUCK, BRAINWASHED, SCRIPT_UNDERPOWERED also missing.
- disabled_subdued feeds the blue SUBDUAL branch; C++ DISABLED_SUBDUED = dark gray with precedence.

## Player-visible
Low-power base: every powered building should turn dark gray (classic ZH low-power look) but stays bright in live. Subdual-disabled units show blue instead of dark gray. Sniped (unmanned) vehicles show a dark tint C++ never applies.
close_reason: Dark tint is EMP/hacked/paralyzed/underpowered/freefall/subdued/default/script_underpowered; unmanned excluded.

title: Live host: night maps never set MODELCONDITION_NIGHT on drawables (TOD ignored by presentation)
description: C++ / leftover / live / player-visible. C++ applies map TimeOfDay to every drawable at map load: W3DTerrainLogic.cpp:165-167 calls TheWritableGlobalData->setTimeOfDay + TheGameClient->setTimeOfDay (W3DGameClient.cpp:148-162), GameClient::setTimeOfDay walks all drawables into Drawable::setTimeOfDay (Drawable.cpp:4344-4354) which sets MODELCONDITION_NIGHT when tod==TIME_OF_DAY_NIGHT and restarts TOD ambient sounds; every newly created object also gets the bit at drawable bind (Object.cpp:2971-2974, m_forceModelsToFollowTimeOfDay defaults true, GlobalData.cpp:676). Live Main parses map time_of_day into global data (script_loader.rs:1040-1046, used only to pick lighting rows) but the presentation NIGHT bit comes from world_env.rs:619-620 is_night = weather_state.current_weather.contains("night"/"evening") — the runtime weather string is only ever normal/snowy/clear on map load (world_save.rs apply_world_info_weather), so is_night is always false on night maps; unit_render.rs:1117-1121 then clears the NIGHT bit on every unit. The GameClient refresh_drawable_time_of_day path (meta_event_impl/player.rs:332) sets the bit per drawable but is only triggered by the DEMO_TIME_OF_DAY demo command (dispatch.rs:541-552), never at map load. Result: on night maps (C++ TIME_OF_DAY_NIGHT) the live host renders day condition states — no lit-window/night-skin NIGHT models — while scene lighting does darken, so the mismatch is obvious. Fix: derive world_env is_night (and the drawable-map refresh) from global data time_of_day == Night after map load, mirroring C++ W3DTerrainLogic.cpp:165-167 + Object.cpp:2971-2974.
close_reason: world_env is_night follows GlobalData TimeOfDay::Night, not weather string.

title: Auto-reload clip state never refreshed when ClipReloadTime elapses (ammo stays 0, status stays ReloadingClip, RELOADING anim stuck)
description: C++/leftover/live three-way mismatch on the clip auto-reload completion. C++ (source of truth): Weapon.cpp:2628-2634 privateFireWeapon empties the clip -> reloadAmmo -> reloadWithBonus (Weapon.cpp:1884-1892) immediately refills m_ammoInClip to clipSize and sets m_whenWeCanFireAgain = now + ClipReloadTime; Weapon::getStatus (Weapon.cpp:2740-2755) lazily flips to READY_TO_FIRE the frame the reload elapses; ObjectWeaponStatusHelper (Module/ObjectWeaponStatusHelper.h:55) ticks every frame calling Object::adjustModelConditionForWeaponStatus (Object.cpp:4683-4752), which clears WSF_RELOADING once ready (or when not attacking) and pushes updateDrawableClipStatus(getRemainingAmmo()=FULL, clipSize) so HUD pips show a full clip; WeaponSet.cpp:869-877 keeps a PreferredAgainst weapon selected while merely reloading (weaponIsReady = status != OUT_OF_AMMO). Leftover GameEngine port (GameLogic/src/helpers/object_helpers.rs) models this via weapon instance reload_with_bonus/status. Live host (Code/Main): consume_ammo_on_fire_named (src/game_logic/object/rtb.rs:49-97) leaves weapon.ammo == Some(0) after the clip empties; the refill only happens inside the NEXT consume call (rtb.rs:73-74) — no tick-time refill exists (only reload_all_ammo and airfield rearm refill). refresh_weapon_fire_status is only invoked after a fire event (src/game_logic/object/attack.rs:389), so weapon_fire_status stays ReloadingClip and MC_BIT_RELOADING_* stays set long after the interval elapses. Player-visible on live path for every auto-reload clip weapon without AutoReloadWhenIdle (Patriot, Comanche rocket pods, SCUD toxin secondary, Tomahawk, etc.): (1) ammo pips / host_authoritative_projectile_clip_statuses (world_objects/host_ops_writeback.rs:1470-1505) and get_ammo_pip_showing_info -> presentation_frame/build.rs:784 report 0 rounds indefinitely after the reload completes where C++ reports a full clip; (2) the unit model stays in the RELOADING animation until its next shot where C++ clears it the frame the reload ends (or on attack end); (3) ini_preferred_slot_usable (object/weapons.rs) drops PreferredAgainst auto-selection during AND after the reload where C++ keeps it.
close_reason: Live host now completes auto-reload when ClipReloadTime elapses: complete_elapsed_auto_reload_clips refills ammo (C++ reloadWithBonus) and refresh_weapon_fire_status flips READY (C++ getStatus); ObjectWeaponStatusHelper-equivalent per-frame tick in world_tick/ai.rs.

title: [Crush] Pair collide runs one direction only — crushers with higher id never crush
description:
## C++
PartitionContactList::processContactList (PartitionManager.cpp:2479-2489) calls obj->onCollide(other) AND other->onCollide(obj) for every geom-colliding pair. Each side's PhysicsBehavior::onCollide -> checkForOverlapCollision (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1424) runs from its own perspective: the crusher side applies front/back/total crush points + HUGE DAMAGE_CRUSH; infantry victims die via SquishCollide::onCollide. Dead infantry also return TRUE from AIUpdateInterface::processCollision (AIUpdate.cpp:1530-1534) when the other can TEST_SQUISH_ONLY them, so crushers shove corpses aside.

## Leftover
GameEngine physics_collide/physics_crush ports both sides; not the live path.

## Live
tick_physics_collisions_all (world_tick/shock.rs:96-127) dedups pairs by (lo,hi) and calls try_physics_collide(a_id, b_id) with a = the lower ObjectId (mobile_ids sorted ascending); the reverse direction runs only via `else if` when the first call returns false — but try_physics_collide (world_tick/physics.rs:210-377) returns true on every path when both objects exist (ignore/parachute -> true; crush 'self being crushed -> passive' -> true; ai_process_collision !allow_force -> true; immobile bounce -> true). apply_overlap_crush_check (physics.rs:463-480) is only invoked with a as crusher, and the infantry squish lives only inside the crusher-side check_for_overlap_collision (physics_motion.rs:181-345).

## Player-visible
When the crusher's id is higher than the victim's — every tank built after pre-placed map infantry/cars, the common case — the victim-side call returns early (passive overlap) and the crusher side never runs: no squish/crush kill, no front/back crush flags, no CrushDie sounds, no corpse shoving; the tank ghosts through infantry and cars. Crushes only land when the crusher happens to have the lower id (all existing tests create the tank before the infantry), so drive-over kills inconsistently work.
close_reason: tick_physics_collisions_all runs both onCollide after geom hit so higher-id crushers crush.

title: [Player] Live MaxSimultaneous cap is a hero-name table, not INI
description:
## C++
`Player::canBuildMoreOfType` (`Player.cpp:2853-2876`) reads `whatToBuild->getMaxSimultaneousOfType()` (`ThingTemplate.cpp:1440-1448`: numeric INI or `TheGameLogic->getSuperweaponRestriction()` when `DeterminedBySuperweaponRestriction`). `countExisting` (`:2825-2849`) counts living objects by `isEquivalentTo` **or** shared `MaxSimultaneousLinkKey`, plus queued units for non-structures.

## Leftover player
`GameLogic/src/player/production.rs:81-164` `can_build_more_of_type` uses `template.get_max_simultaneous_of_type()` + link key + factory queues. Leftover `ThingTemplate` parses numeric `MaxSimultaneousOfType` (`thing_template.rs:3488-3493`).

## Live leftover player
`Main/src/game_logic/thing.rs` stores only `max_simultaneous_link_key` and the SW-restriction bool — **no numeric cap field**. `spawn_templates.rs:2373` only detects the `DeterminedBySuperweaponRestriction` token.
`can_make_unit` (`world_scripts/ui_production.rs:1475-1488`) calls `unit_max_simultaneous_of_type_residual` (`host_production_buildable_command_residual.rs:719-760`): a hardcoded Burton/Lotus/Kell name table (comment admits "not full INI parse matrix" / unique buildings). Count (`:1268-1290`) is exact template-name only — no `isEquivalentTo`, no link key.
Live leftover `Player` has no `canBuildMoreOfType`.

## Player-visible
Players can queue a second copy of any INI-capped unit that is not a named hero (unique buildings the residual comment itself lists as `MaxSimultaneousOfType=1`). Rebuild-hole / reskin link keys are ignored, so a hole plus original does not consume the cap. Leftover player's INI-correct gate is unused.

Distinct from closed hq-egcq (leftover BuildAssistant canMakeUnit ignored all limits — live now has a residual table, not INI).
close_reason: Live MaxSimultaneousOfType is parsed from INI (numeric or DeterminedBySuperweaponRestriction); can_make_unit and place count equivalent/link-key instead of the hero-name table.

title: [Dock] Queued docker death or re-task never cancels its live approach reservation — dock jams forever
description:
## C++
Any exit from AI_DOCK frees the dock: AIDockState::onExit (AIStates.cpp:6108-6117) halts+deletes the sub-machine, and AIDockMachine::halt (AIDock.cpp:46-60) calls dock->cancelDock(owner), freeing the approach slot + activeDocker (DockUpdate.cpp:349-376). New player orders reset the outer machine (StateMachine::internalSetState fires onExit(EXIT_RESET), StateMachine.cpp:340-341), and owner death tears the machine down the same way — the reserved DockWaiting slot never outlives its docker.

## Live
host_supply_gather.rs tick_live_dock_approach:34 queue.evict_dead(|_| true) — the predicate says every owner is alive, so evict_dead (:115-121) evicts nothing (dead mechanism, neutered call). cancel_live_dock_approach is only reachable via release_dock_if_holder (support_states.rs:6271) on the docker's own successful state transitions. Nothing fires on destruction (create_destroy_die.rs mark_object_for_destruction / destroy_list_bounty.rs process_destroy_list have no dock cleanup) and nothing fires on new player orders (command_executor has no dock release — re-tasking a Gathering/ReturningResources/SeekingRepair truck just overwrites ai_state).

## Player-visible
A killed or re-tasked queued truck/chinook leaves a ghost owner with reached=true at the lowest slot index. promote_active (host_supply_gather.rs:243-256) then returns the ghost every time dock_active_docker is empty, so tick_live_dock_approach never returns ClearToAct for any live docker — the supply center / warehouse / repair pad is permanently jammed and income stops until map end. Fixed-size queues (warehouse 9/5, repair 5, USA center 9) additionally lose capacity until is_clear_to_approach goes false, which also makes find_nearest_harvestable_supply_within skip the warehouse (object_queries.rs:131-135). One lost queued truck bricks the whole dock for every player.
close_reason: Closed

title: [Weapon] AutoChooseSources SECONDARY NONE ignored so Jarmen auto-snipes between rifle shots
description:
## C++
`WeaponSet::chooseBestWeaponForTarget` (`WeaponSet.cpp:816-822`) skips a slot unless `AutoChooseSources` includes the command source (or `CMD_DEFAULT_SWITCH_WEAPON`). `AutoChooseSources = SECONDARY NONE` means the slot is special/button-only: Jarmen Kell `GLAJarmenKellVehiclePilotSniperRifle`, Missile Defender laser, Toxin Tractor sprayer. During PRIMARY `DelayBetweenShots` the chooser keeps the unready primary as backup and never auto-picks the NONE secondary.

## Leftover

title: [Worker] Gather never takes exclusive AS_SUPPLY_TRUCK — idle dozer resume steals ferrying workers
description:
## Why
C++ WorkerAIUpdate is a dual-brain: WorkerStateMachine is either AS_DOZER or AS_SUPPLY_TRUCK. Live gather never enters exclusive supply mode, so the dozer BUILD slot + idle resume keep running and steal a ferrying GLA worker back to the scaffold (or freeze it for everyone else).

## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/AIUpdate/WorkerAIUpdate.cpp`
- `AS_DOZER` / `AS_SUPPLY_TRUCK` (`:49-53`). `update` (`:257-288`) runs only the matching sub-machine; harvest branch also `setWeaponSetFlag(WEAPONSET_MINE_CLEARING_DETAIL)`.
- Enter supply: `supplyTruckSubMachineWantsToEnter` (`:1211-1224`) = `isForcedIntoWantingState() || masterState == AI_DOCK`.
- Leave supply: `supplyTruckSubMachineReadyToLeave` (`:1229-1245`) = not wanting-to-enter AND `isSupplyTruckBrainActiveAndBusy` (`:1091-1094`, ST_BUSY only).
- Player gather/move/stop (`aiDoCommand` `:989-998`): `cancelTask(getCurrentTask())` then issue the command. `newTask`/`construct` force `AS_DOZER` (`:382-383`, `:650-660`).
- While AS_SUPPLY_TRUCK the dozer machine is not updated — `isBuildMostImportant` / bored never run.

## Leftover
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/supply_system/worker.rs` `is_acting_as_dozer` (`:259-262`) is only “has a dozer task” — no WorkerStateMachine. Wave 298 empty dual-world makes leftover update a no-op. Player does not run leftover.

## Live
`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/command_executor/leftover.rs` `execute_gather` (`:199-244`) and `world_scripts/unit_commands.rs` `unit_command_dock_at_supply_warehouse` (`:1051-1063`) set `AIState::Gathering` / preferred dock only — they never cancel `dozer_task_build_target` or enter exclusive supply mode.
`world_scripts/rebuild_dozer.rs` `update_dozer_bored_repair` (`:1233-1257`) calls `dozer_idle_resume_pending_build` on any Idle `can_repair` unit (workers included). `support_states.rs` `begin_supply_regroup` (`:6122-6126`) sets `AIState::Idle` + Regrouping → idle resume steals the worker.
`builder_is_actively_building` (`:852-858`) is true while `dozer_task_build_target` is set, even if the worker is Gathering — other workers cannot resume.

Skip closed: hq-gkpuk (dozer BUILD slot recording), hq-ffh67 (build/repair exits supply — opposite direction), hq-j83x1 (gather mine-clear arm).

## Player-visible
A GLA worker told to gather after placing a building (or mid-build) either walks back to finish the pad as soon as the gather cycle goes idle/regroup, or keeps exclusive builder while ferrying so the 1 HP scaffold is frozen. C++ cancels BUILD and stays in supply mode until the supply brain is ST_BUSY.
close_reason: Live host: exclusive AS_SUPPLY_TRUCK skip idle/bored; FireWeaponWhenDead fires all modules and stamps after fire; mine-clear keeps boxes until already attacking; player commands cancel current dozer task.

menu_callbacks.rs:755-758 populate missing ScrollFactor from keyboard_scroll_factor*100 (post-GameData 2.0 → 200).
menu_callbacks.rs:1115 Accept does write keyboard_scroll_factor = slider/100.

## Live

global_data.rs:438 ctor 0.5 then INI overwrites; keyboard_default_scroll_factor ctor 1.0 (C++ 0.5).
Main mouse.rs:1817-1924 update_camera uses Common keyboard_scroll_factor for key/edge/RMB.

## Player-visible

title: [Chinook] Landed move-to-evac takeoff drops the pending evac dest
description:
## Symptom
A landed Chinook told to move-to-and-evacuate a distant point takes off (or taxis) and never flies to the dest / never dumps.

## C++
`aiDoCommand` (`ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:1263-1286`): if landed and dest farther than 3, `m_pendingCommand.store(*parms); m_hasPendingCommand=true; setMyState(TAKING_OFF)`. `update` (`:1073-1078`) when parent-idle reconstitutes the pending evac and issues `MOVE_TO_AND_EVAC[_AND_EXIT_INIT]`. Commands issued during takeoff/landing/combat-drop are also queued (`:1241-1248`).

## Leftover
`handle_command` (`chinook_ai_update.rs:1733-1745`) stores `pending_command` then TakingOff. Dual-world empty — not live.

## Live
Two leftover remaining holes:

1. `execute_move_to_and_evacuate` (`transport.rs:618-633`) never calls `HostChinookAI::command_evac`. Landed Chinooks path with the taxiing locomotor and dump via `pending_evacuate_on_stop` — no takeoff-first.

2. `command_evac` (`host_combat_chinook.rs:657-664`) when landed+far does `enter_state(TakingOff); return;` **without** storing dest/and_exit. `enter_takeoff_or_landing` overwrites `dest` to the vertical takeoff point. There is no `m_pendingCommand`. After takeoff `succeed()` goes Idle; passengers stay aboard.

## Player-visible
Script/AI `AICMD_MOVE_TO_POSITION_AND_EVACUATE` on a landed Chinook: either taxis on the ground or lifts off and hovers. Troops never arrive at the ordered dump point. Closed hq-5a7lk claimed command_evac; the pending-command reconstitution is still missing.
close_reason: Live host Chinook: leave DO_COMBAT_DROP, aiRappelInto roof dest, HeadOffMap spawn dest, pending evac dest on takeoff, hover geom+MinDropHeight, regular transport install, COMBATDROP_INTO gate.

## Player-visible

description:

title: [Speech] SPEECH_PLAY ignores allowOverlap and never hits TheAudio
description:
## Why
C++ `SPEECH_PLAY` queues logical speech on `TheAudio` with `setUninterruptable(!allowOverlap)` so briefing lines do not talk over each other unless the script allows it. Live host `MissionScriptActionHandler::speech_play` ignores `allow_overlap` and `push_sound`s the name as a UI SFX.

## C++
`ScriptActions.cpp:6780-6781` `doSpeechPlay(name, param1 int)`.
`doSpeechPlay` (`:2743-2764`): `AudioEventRTS` + `setIsLogicalAudio(true)` + local player index + `setUninterruptable(!allowOverlap)` + `TheAudio->addAudioEvent`. Subtitle `DIALOGEVENT:{name}Subtitle` for 8000ms when the label exists and is not `*`.

## Leftover
Leftover executor `do_speech_play` (`actions_player_display_camera.rs:482-501`) reads `allow_overlap` and calls `handler.speech_play(name, allow_overlap)`.
`GameClientScriptActionHandler::speech_play` (`GameClient/src/core/script_action_handler.rs:1229-1241`) matches C++: `TheAudio::add_audio_event`, `set_uninterruptable(!allow_overlap)`, tracks the speech wait-slot handle.

## Live
`initialize_scripts` installs `MissionScriptActionHandler`, overwriting the GameClient handler.
`mission_scripts.rs:2521-2528` `speech_play` takes `_allow_overlap` unused; `note_speech_started` + `push_sound(name)`.
`scripts_camera.rs:529-530` drains sounds via `play_ui_sound` → `translate_audio_event` + generic `AudioEventRequest` (same path as UI clicks). No `set_uninterruptable`, no AT_Streaming speech event.

## Player-visible
Campaign briefing VO overlaps or is cut by the next line regardless of World Builder Allow Overlap. Speech is not the C++ uninterruptable streaming event (music was specially forwarded to TheAudio; speech was not).
close_reason: Live SPEECH_PLAY now queues TheAudio with setIsLogicalAudio + setUninterruptable(!allowOverlap), matching C++ doSpeechPlay. Dropped the UI SFX push_sound path.

title: [ControlBar] leftover science purchase never setControlCommand — no cameos, title, points, or click bind
description:

title: [Replay] GAME_REPLAY never setLocalPlayer(ReplayObserver)
description:
## Why
C++ playback starts GAME_REPLAY by switching the local player to ReplayObserver, forcing radar on, and applying the observer control-bar scheme. Live start_new_game(Replay) never creates that observer or switches local identity, so the player stays the recorded faction.

## C++

Recorder.cpp:1126-1127 playbackFile appends MSG_NEW_GAME GAME_REPLAY.

## Leftover
game_initialization.rs:296-310 prepare_sides_for_new_game always add_replay_observer_side for Skirmish|Multiplayer|Replay. Leftover startNewGame is not the live host.

GameMode::Replay creates default players and taps the recorder, then never set_local_player(ReplayObserver), never radar forceOn, never observer control-bar scheme. load_map_with_progress:3393-3398 repeats the Skirmish-only install.

## Not a duplicate
hq-1q37a was NewGame/ClearGameData never starting the live game (closed). hq-ceylk / hq-m6u54 are apply/remirror gates assuming observer already is local.

title: [SW] Fire gate ignores SOLD and UNDER_CONSTRUCTION
description:
## Why
C++ Player shortcut/count iterators refuse a special-power source that is under construction or sold. Live `is_special_power_ready_for` (the fire gate command_executor and AI use) only checks alive/disabled/module/science/pause/cooldown. A Particle Cannon / Nuke / Scud that is still being built, or has already been sold, can still fire.

## C++
`Player.cpp:1240-1304` `doFindSpecialPowerSourceObject` / `doCountSpecialPowersReady`:
```
!obj->testStatus(OBJECT_STATUS_UNDER_CONSTRUCTION)
&& !obj->testStatus(OBJECT_STATUS_SOLD)
&& !obj->isEffectivelyDead()
```
`SpecialPowerModule` ctor leaves `m_availableOnFrame=0` while UC (no `startPowerRecharge` until complete), so `isReady()` would be true — Player iterators are what block fire/shortcut.

## Leftover
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/object_queries.rs` unused (empty dual-world). Crate SpecialPowerModule is not the live host.

## Live
`Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/object_queries.rs:1458-1524` `is_special_power_ready_for`: no `status.sold` / `status.under_construction` check.
`command_executor/special_power.rs:276-281` and `ai.rs` call that gate.
UC PUC never gets `on_structure_superweapon_creation` (`production_eva.rs:1185` requires `is_constructed()`), so per-object remaining is 0 → ready.
`start_sell_object` (`rebuild_dozer.rs:547`) sets `sold` but does not pause/clear the module; building stays `is_alive()`.

## Player-visible
Click-sell a ready PUC/Nuke/Scud (or fire from an unfinished one): live still accepts DoSpecialPower and consumes/recharges. C++ shortcut/count never pick that object; sell then destroy removes the module.
close_reason: Live is_special_power_ready_for skips SOLD and UNDER_CONSTRUCTION (C++ Player.cpp:1240-1304). Sold PUC can no longer fire/consume.

title: [Partition] Collide/iterate stamp is selection-radius AABB + 9-cell ring, not COI geometry
description:
## Why
C++ stamps every object into all overlapping PartitionCells via geometry COI (`doSmallFill` / `doCircleFill` / `doRectFill`) and builds contacts from every COI-sharing pair. Live host now has faithful `host_object_footprint` + `cells_touched_for_footprint` but the live collide/iterate grid never uses them: it stamps an axis-aligned `selection_radius` circle and only queries the object's center cell plus 8 neighbors. Large or rotated boxes (command centers, Overlords, Chinooks) miss collide and radius iterate when centers are more than one 40wu cell apart or the hull exceeds selection radius.

## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/PartitionManager.cpp`
- `PartitionData::updateCellsTouched` `:1997-2050` — small/circle/rotated-rect COI fill from authored GeometryInfo + orientation.
- `PartitionData::addPossibleCollisions` `:1890-1923` — walks **every** COI cell of the dirty object and every other module in those cells.
- `PartitionContactList::processContactList` `:2450-2508` — geom-tests then `Object::onCollide` both sides.
- `getClosestObjects` `:3172-3315` — FASTER_GCO rings over the same COI occupancy.

## Leftover
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/collide/partition_manager.rs` `register_object_oriented` uses `partition_coi::cells_touched_for_geometry`. Unused by the player host.

## Live
- `Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/shock.rs:80-116` — `register_object_footprint(id, x, z, selection_radius)` then `neighbor_object_ids` (center+8) and a `selection_radius+selection_radius` pre-filter before `host_geom_collides`.
- `Main/src/game_logic/partition_manager.rs:100-186` — `cells_for_circle` AABB and `ids_in_radius` square ring of `ceil(r/40)` from the **query center** only.
- `Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/collide_dispatch.rs:53-84` `host_object_footprint` and `partition_coi.rs:42-50` `cells_touched_for_footprint` exist but are only used for FOW object mix (`spawn_templates.rs:3881`), not collide/iterate register.

## Player-visible
Tanks/helicopters clip through large buildings; crush, crate pickup, garrison-enter, and hijack onCollide never fire when the pair shares hull cells but not the 9-cell neighborhood. AI acquire / splash `object_ids_near` can omit a structure whose hull is in range but whose selection-radius cells are not in the query ring.

Distinct from closed hq-2hqt (center-cell only — now a selection-radius circle), hq-o6c5 (sphere collide test — geom test now exists behind the pre-filter), hq-6r69/hq-i688 (onCollide dispatch).
close_reason: Live collide/iterate stamps and walks COI geometry (host_object_footprint + cells_touched_for_footprint); leftover register already COI.

title: [Particles] DisableFX BinaryShower culled next tick as ParticleSysBone
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:1381-1395` (Hacker disable / Lotus disable vehicle): `createParticleSystem(DisableFXParticleSystem)` (`DisabledEffectBinaryShower0`), `makeRandomOffsetWithinFootprint`, `attachToObject(target)`, `setPosition(&offs)` (local), `setSystemLifetime(effectDuration * interleave)`.

## Leftover
`helpers/particles.rs:311-319` `attach_particle_system_to_object` is findTemplate + create + attach only — no `setPosition`, no `setSystemLifetime`. Leftover GameClient `set_system_lifetime` exists but live never calls it.

## Live
`support_states.rs:430-493` `leftover_spawn_disable_fx` (after closed hq-79mir spawn):
- Fake circle offset `sqrt(area/π)*0.35`, not `GeometryInfo::makeRandomOffsetWithinFootprint`
- `attach_named_to_object` stores kind `ParticleSysBone` with `attach_offset = ZERO`
- Leftover attach has no local footprint `setPosition`
- Host expire is `combat_particles.deactivate` after lifetime

Then every tick `combat_fire_fx.rs:175-199` `sync_live_state_particles` → `sync_particle_sys_bones`. Wanted = the victim's INI `ParticleSysBone` templates. `DisabledEffectBinaryShower0` is not on that list → **stale → deactivate next frame**.

`attach_named_to_object` also `mirror_spawn` first, so leftover attach's system id is discarded (`client_system_id` already set). Host cull destroys the unattached mirror; leftover attached system is orphaned at object center with no lifetime.

Skip closed hq-79mir (never spawn) and hq-6graz (tracer speed).

## Player-visible
Hacker/Lotus BinaryShower flashes one frame then vanishes. If the leftover orphan is what draws, it sits at the victim center (not footprint) and never expires.
close_reason: DisableFx kind + footprint makeRandomOffsetWithinFootprint + setSystemLifetime; sync_particle_sys_bones no longer culls BinaryShower

title: [Particles] ParticleSysBone systems sit at object origin not bones
description:
## C++
`W3DModelDraw::recalcBonesForClientParticleSystems` (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:2572-2612`) for every `ParticleSysBone` on the current ModelCondition: `Get_Bone_Index` + identity×scale `Get_Bone_Transform` so the offset is **model-space live pose**, `setPosition(&pos)`, `rotateLocalTransformZ(bone Z)`, `attachToDrawable`. `AnimatedParticleSysBoneClientUpdate::clientUpdate` keeps them on live bones. Exhaust, factory stacks, RepairCloud, FrenzyCloud.

`ParticleSystem::update` (`ParticleSys.cpp:1854-1927`) then `m_transform = parentXfrm * m_localTransform`.

## Leftover
`GameClient` `particle_system.rs` `attach_to_drawable` + `resolve_attached_parent` concatenates parent 4x4. Leftover W3DModelDraw bind-pose gap was hq-eiew5 (closed leftover). Unused by live host.

## Live

Spawn/follow use the object origin: `attach_named_to_object(owner, position, …)` and `entry.position = position`. `particle_sys_bones_for_template` returns `(bone, system)` pairs that this path never applies.

Closed hq-g7vm0 was "never spawn". They now spawn, but never at the bone.

## Player-visible
Tank exhaust, building smoke stacks, RepairCloud, and FrenzyCloud sit at the object's feet/center instead of the authored ParticleSysBone.

title: [Radiation] Nuke/tank/cannon puddles deal Unresistable so tanks and aircraft cook
description:
## Why
C++ radiation fields are DAMAGE_RADIATION through Armor.ini (structures 0%, tanks 50%, aircraft 25%) and RadiusDamageAffects ALLIES ENEMIES NEUTRALS NOT_AIRBORNE. Live nuke / Nuke Cannon / Nuclear Tanks ticks call take_damage_from_immediate (DAMAGE_UNRESISTABLE) and never skip airborne, so buildings and jets take full 25/15/5 HP per tick.

## C++
Damage.h:33 DAMAGE_RADIATION. Armor.cpp:43-55 adjustDamage (UNRESISTABLE only bypasses). NukeRadiationFieldWeapon / MediumRadiationFieldWeapon / SmallRadiationFieldWeapon: DamageType RADIATION, RadiusDamageAffects ALLIES ENEMIES NEUTRALS NOT_AIRBORNE.

## Leftover
GameEngine leftover ArmorTemplate::adjust_damage skips only Unresistable/SubdualUnresistable. Unused on this live tick path.

## Live
Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/special_power_strikes.rs:1014-1015 update_nuclear_radiation_fields → take_damage_from_immediate.
world_combat/infantry_weapons.rs:1828-1829 update_nuke_cannon_radiation_zones same.
world_scripts/helix_radar.rs:190-191 update_nuclear_tanks_radiation_zones same.
object/damage.rs:29-38 take_damage_from_immediate is Unresistable.
special_power_strikes/registry_fields.rs:112-115 comments fail-closed vs airborne filter.

## Player-visible
Nuke puddle melts Command Centers and parked Raptors that C++ radiation armor / NOT_AIRBORNE would spare.
close_reason: Live nuke/cannon/tank radiation ticks use DAMAGE_RADIATION through leftover ArmorTemplate::adjust_damage (structures 0%, tanks 50%, aircraft 25%) plus C++ NOT_AIRBORNE (airborne_target / isSignificantlyAboveTerrain) and DeathType NORMAL.

title: [ClearMines] Bored dozers never arm the mine-clearing weaponset
description:
## C++
`DozerAIUpdate.cpp` DozerPrimaryIdleState (1111-1116): after BoredTime with no repair target, `setWeaponSetFlag(WEAPONSET_MINE_CLEARING_DETAIL)` then `findMine` + `aiAttackObject`. That flag swaps in DozerMineDisarmingWeapon (DAMAGE_DISARM, AttackRange 5, PreAttackDelay 1200ms). `AIUpdateInterface::isClearingMines` is IS_ATTACKING + ANTI_MINE.

Closed `hq-8aijd` gated live auto-clear on the player/AI detail flag, assuming C++ only arms via `MSG_SET_MINE_CLEARING_DETAIL`. Idle dozers also self-arm.

## Leftover
None for this idle machine. Live `command_executor/leftover.rs` `execute_clear_mines` does call `unit_command_set_mine_clearing_detail(true)` for the player button.

## Live host
`rebuild_dozer.rs` `update_dozer_bored_repair` / `process_dozer_bored_event` (1281-1298): `find_dozer_bored_mine_target` + `apply_engagement_decision_aware` + `path_approach_with_state(Attacking)` — never `set_weapon_set_mine_clearing_detail(true)`. `apply_engagement_decision_aware` requires `get_able_to_attack_specific_object`; without the detail set the dozer has no ANTI_MINE weapon so engagement fails, or they walk in as a normal attacker and trip the pad. `update_mines_and_demo_traps` also refuses to treat them as clearers unless the flag is set.

## Player-visible
Idle USA/China dozers sitting next to enemy mines never clear them after BoredTime (5s). C++ they swap to the mine detector and disarm. Live they ignore the field (or suicide if they wander in).
close_reason: Live host: regen pads keep MIN_HEALTH rubble and AutoHeal-refill virtuals; onDamage health-band trips detonateOnce; land mines DetonatedBy ENEMIES|NEUTRAL; Cluster DropVariance on bomb drop + place_cluster_mines; bored dozers arm WEAPONSET_MINE_CLEARING_DETAIL; ClearMines waits Dozer 36f / Worker 30f PreAttackDelay.

title: [Mine] Weapon fire never trips virtual mines
description:
## C++
`MinefieldBehavior.cpp` `onDamage` (429-489): each health drop that would leave fewer virtual mines than `numVirtualMines * health/maxHealth` calls `detonateOnce` at the pad (splash + decrement). Healing raises the virtual count. Empty pad goes rubble/MASKED; regen pads clamp to `MIN_HEALTH` 0.1 so they can refill.

## Leftover
`minefield_behavior.rs` ports the health↔virtual loop, but Wave 410 empty-registry gate means leftover `onDamage` never runs live.

## Live host
`object/damage.rs` `take_damage_from_typed_death_fx`: `DAMAGE_DISARM` → `disarm_mine_safe` (delete, no splash). All other types fall through normal HP. No `onDamage` virtual sync, no `detonateOnce`. Shooting a ChinaStandardMine / ChinaClusterMine just chips HP until the object pops.

## Player-visible
Tanks/artillery walking fire onto a China minefield or cluster pad do not set off remaining virtual mines. C++ each shot that lowers the health band explodes one charge; live the pad silently dies.
close_reason: Live host: regen pads keep MIN_HEALTH rubble and AutoHeal-refill virtuals; onDamage health-band trips detonateOnce; land mines DetonatedBy ENEMIES|NEUTRAL; Cluster DropVariance on bomb drop + place_cluster_mines; bored dozers arm WEAPONSET_MINE_CLEARING_DETAIL; ClearMines waits Dozer 36f / Worker 30f PreAttackDelay.

title: [Mine] Regenerating China pads never refill and disarm deletes them
description:
## C++
`MinefieldBehavior.cpp` `disarm` (507-538): if `Regenerates` (ChinaStandardMine / ChinaEMPMine), keep the pad — drain to `MIN_HEALTH` 0.1, `m_virtualMinesRemaining = 0`, `MODELCONDITION_RUBBLE` + `OBJECT_STATUS_MASKED`. AutoHeal then refills health; `onHealing` → `onDamage` restores virtual mines. `update` (210-233): `StopsRegenAfterCreatorDies` (default true) + dead producer flips `m_regenerates = false`, `m_draining = true`, `AutoHealBehavior::stopHealing`. Empty non-regen pads `destroyObject`.

## Leftover
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/behavior/minefield_behavior.rs` ports disarm/regen/drain, but Wave 410 `dual_world_registry_unavailable()` makes leftover collide/update no-ops on the live host. Closed leftover `hq-ttiy` only fixed that crate.

## Live host
`stealth_mines.rs` `clear_mine_internal` / `object/install.rs` `disarm_mine_safe`: always `detonated = true` + `mark_object_for_destruction` / `health = 0` + `destroyed`. `HostMineData::land_mine_for_template` sets `regenerates = true` for standard/EMP but there is no AutoHeal, no `onHealing` virtual restore, and no producer-death check. `consume_virtual_mine` leaves an empty rubble pad forever when `regenerates`.

## Player-visible
China structure mines never come back after a dozer/worker clear. After the building dies they also never drain/vanish. C++ pads go rubble, refill, and die with the producer.
close_reason: Live host: regen pads keep MIN_HEALTH rubble and AutoHeal-refill virtuals; onDamage health-band trips detonateOnce; land mines DetonatedBy ENEMIES|NEUTRAL; Cluster DropVariance on bomb drop + place_cluster_mines; bored dozers arm WEAPONSET_MINE_CLEARING_DETAIL; ClearMines waits Dozer 36f / Worker 30f PreAttackDelay.

title: [INI] Live catalogue never loads Default/Object.ini so DefaultThingTemplate is not copied on spawn
description:
## Why
C++ ThingFactory loads `Data/INI/Default/Object.ini` first, then every `newTemplate` copies `DefaultThingTemplate` into the new object. Live WW3D catalogue discovery skips Default/Object.ini entirely, and spawn builds from `ThingTemplate::new()` with invented host defaults instead of the retail default object.

## C++
`GameEngine.cpp:458` `initSubsystem(TheThingFactory, ..., "Data\\INI\\Default\\Object.ini", NULL, "Data\\INI\\Object")`.
`ThingFactory.cpp:113-120` `newTemplate`: `findTemplate("DefaultThingTemplate")` then `*newTemplate = *defaultT; setCopiedFromDefault()`.

## Leftover
`Main/src/cnc_game_engine/object_ini_boot.rs` and leftover `ThingFactory::new_template` (`thing_factory.rs:469-472`) copy DefaultThingTemplate. Shell leftover bootstrap loads Default/Object.ini. That path is not the live spawn catalogue.

## Live
`Main/src/assets/ww3d_asset_manager.rs:310-326` `discover_object_ini_files` only accepts `data/ini/object/*.ini` and `data/ini/crate.ini` — not `data/ini/default/object.ini`.
`spawn_templates.rs:284` `ThingTemplate::new(template_name)` then overlays authored attrs. `seed_asset_definition_templates` reads `object_definitions_snapshot()` from that catalogue.

## Player-visible
Every spawned object misses DefaultThingTemplate inheritance (occlusion delay, shadow, geometry, default modules/audio that retail objects omit because they inherit). Combined with invented XP/vision defaults, unauthored Object.ini fields do not match retail.
close_reason: Live WW3D catalogue loads Data/INI/Default/Object.ini first and copies DefaultThingTemplate into new objects (C++ ThingFactory::newTemplate).

title: [INI] Missing VisionRange still reveals 150wu; C++ default is 0
description:
## Why
C++ ThingTemplate vision defaults to 0. Live `ThingTemplate::new` sets `sight_range = 150` and spawn only overwrites when Object.ini authors `VisionRange > 0`. Objects that omit the field (props, trees, doodads, many civilians) clear 150 world units of fog.

## C++
`ThingTemplate.cpp:976` `m_visionRange = 0.0f`. `:977-978` shroud ranges default `-1` (use vision). `doShroudReveal` uses `getShroudClearingRange()` which falls back to vision when `-1`.

## Leftover

title: [Tunnel] Shared pool is per faction Team not per Player
description:
## Why

Live: host_tunnel_network.rs:140-163,252-267,312-348; object_queries.rs:870-875; support_states.rs:3175-3178; player.rs:321-326.

Distinct from closed hq-hn3 (that residual *implemented* per-team sharing) and hq-haqz0 (capture re-home now calls on_tunnel_destroyed/created, still on Team keys).
close_reason: Live HostTunnelNetworkRegistry is per Player (owner_player_id), not Team. Enter rejects different controller (ActionManager.cpp:662-670). Capture/sell/cave-in remesh by player key.

title: [Cam] Explosion ViewShake offset never damps on live host

Script `SCREEN_SHAKE` damps `screen_shake_intensity` locally; explosion ViewShake does not. Distinct from closed hq-qq2jo (script CAMERA_ADD_SHAKER rotation).

## Player-visible
Nukes, artillery, and other ViewShake FX shove the camera once and leave it offset. Retail wobbles and settles. Script SCREEN_SHAKE still decays.

title: [Pathfind] Match CPP diameter-clearance call sites
description:
## Scope
Match the retail use of diameter-based clearance without inventing a vehicle-width veto inside regular A* expansion.

## CPP evidence
`AIPathfind.cpp:6200-6260` regular `internalFindPath` expansion checks each neighbor using `validMovementPosition` and `checkForMovement`; it does not impose `clearCellForDiameter` as an unconditional stencil at each expansion. Diameter-aware checks remain in ground-path destination adjustment (`findGroundPath`, around `:7022+`) and path optimization/line passability (around `:619`).

## Regression fixture
`routing_and_occupancy.rs::internal_astar_routes_infantry_and_vehicle_through_single_cell_opening` uses a finite wall at x=8 with one opening at y=9. Both infantry and vehicle must reach the opposite side, so the test checks that regular internal A* does not add a blanket width veto. `clear_cell_for_diameter_open_and_blocked` checks the helper only; caller-level destination clearance still needs a production-path regression if not covered elsewhere.

## Remaining gate
Playback owns the production expansion change. Root owns Cargo and integration gates. Do not claim destination-clearance parity based on helper-only coverage.
notes:
2026-09-30 CPP audit correction: `AIPathfind.cpp:6200-6260` regular `internalFindPath` neighbor expansion uses `validMovementPosition` and `checkForMovement`; it does not impose `clearCellForDiameter` as a blanket expansion veto. Keep footprint clearance at ground-path destination adjustment and diameter-aware path/line gates (CPP `findGroundPath` around `:7022+` and optimization around `:619`). Replaced the invalid two-infinite-wall fixture with a finite wall at x=8 and one required opening at y=9; test both infantry and vehicle endpoint reachability through that opening. This does NOT establish full caller-level destination clearance parity: `clear_cell_for_diameter_open_and_blocked` currently checks helper behavior only. Root/playback owns the production path gate change; Cargo/CPP runtime parity gate remains pending.
Read-only production check: find_path_ex_surfaces derives vehicle diameter from selection radius and passes it into the grid; at this audit time grid_routing.rs:92 still rejects each regular A* neighbor through diameter_allows. This is the precise Main behavior the new finite single-opening regression should catch until playback removes the non-CPP expansion veto. Destination adjust (grid_routing.rs:466) and diameter-aware line passability (:1110) remain distinct caller gates.
close_reason: folded into hq-8ecpbu

title: [Pathfind] Live flattens bridge decks onto ground — no layer, ramps, or side rails
description:
## Why
C++ keeps each bridge on its own PathfindLayer: deck CLEAR, side cells BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE, only end/entry cells connect to LAYER_GROUND, and low-clearance ground under the deck is stamped BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE. Live `stamp_bridge_deck` overwrites the single ground grid with CLEAR (or all BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE if destroyed). Units walk onto/off the sides, the river under the deck becomes walkable ground, and low overpasses do not block.

Closed hq-ao9p (leftover AABB layer), hq-5s9pt (decks never reached live), hq-c23o/hq-hneu (no layers) described earlier states. Leftover now classifies cells; live now stamps decks — remaining gap is flatten vs classified connect-layer.

## C++
`PathfindLayer::classifyLayerMapCell` (`AIPathfind.cpp:3647-3724`): 4 corners on polygon → CELL_CLEAR; 1–3 → BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE unless `isCellOnEnd`/`isCellEntryPoint` (CLEAR + `setConnectLayer(LAYER_GROUND)` both ways). If `groundHeight+LAYER_Z_CLOSE_ENOUGH_F > bridgeHeight`, ground cell becomes BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE. `checkChangeLayers` (`:5942-5981`) hops A* between layers at those connect cells.

## Leftover
`pathfind_layer_classify.rs:112-151` `classify_layer_map_cell`: count==4 CLEAR; partial + entry CLEAR+connect Ground; else BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE. `pathfind_complete` still has a real layer matrix.

## Live host
`pathfinding.rs:848-887` `stamp_bridge_deck`: AABB then `point_in_bridge_quad` on cell center; every hit is CLEAR (or all BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE). `world_save.rs:625-635` seeds that onto the single-layer host grid. No connect-layer, no side rails, no clearance stamp. `grid_to_world` Y=0 (hq-ymmw).

## Player-visible
Tanks walk onto a bridge from the riverbank/side and walk off the deck into water. Ground under a low overpass is open. Destroyed decks become a solid BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE slab on the ground layer instead of a closed upper layer with water still below.
close_reason: Live stamp_bridge_deck classifies a PathfindLayer: deck CLEAR, sides BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE, end/entry connect LAYER_GROUND; river under stays Water; destroy closes the layer only. Crate A* hops via connect_layer.

title: [Garrison] Evac burst-from-center idles at the building origin instead of walking out
description:
## Why

## C++

## Leftover
`garrison_contain.rs` exit_object_via_door was fixed for hq-szbq (cliff walk / left-right / enclosing snap). Dual-world empty — player never hits it.

## Live

## Player-visible

## Not a duplicate
hq-szbq (closed) was leftover cliff-bunker terrain walk. hq-actia (closed) was script left/right dumping in a circle. Default burst walk-out is still missing on the live host.
close_reason: Live host: stealth-garrison-only civilians accept enemy Enter then onCollide kick+detect; evac burst walks out; hide uses KINDOF_STEALTH_GARRISON count; FIREPOINT sets switch on Damaged/ReallyDamaged; transport passenger fire from FIREPOINT bones; HealContain auto-exit uses ExitStart/End walk.

title: [Garrison] Enemy enter rejects stealth-garrisoned civilians so occupants never kick out
description:
## Why
C++ lets a non-owner enter a civilian building that is *only* stealth-garrisoned (`KINDOF_STEALTH_GARRISON` occupants). Arrival `onCollide` then ejects those occupants (detected) and boards the new unit. Live rejects any occupied target for a non-owner, so the kick-out never happens.

## C++
`ActionManager::canEnterObject` (`ActionManager.cpp:656-675`): if the container is a different player, reject only when `nonStealthContainCount > 0` or it is a faction structure. If `stealthContainCount > 0 && nonStealthContainCount == 0`, force `checkCapacity = FALSE` and fall through to `isValidContainerFor`.
`OpenContain::onCollide` (`OpenContain.cpp:777-814`): eject every rider whose controlling player differs (STEALTH_GARRISON `markAsDetected` then `aiExit`), then `addToContain` if valid.

## Leftover
`garrison_contain.rs` / `open_contain.rs` port collide eject. Dual-world empty — unused.

## Live
`can_unit_enter_normal_target` (`object_queries.rs:897-905`): `!same_controller && (faction_structure || !contained_units().is_empty())` → false. Any occupant, including all-stealth-garrison, blocks Enter.
Arrival (`support_states.rs:3073-3082`) repeats the same occupied/non-owner reject. No `onCollide` other-player eject.

## Player-visible
A civilian building full of stealth-garrison infantry (Ninja / STEALTH_GARRISON) cannot be entered by an enemy. Retail: the building looks empty and walking in kicks the stealthed occupants out detected. Live: Enter cursor/order is refused.

title: [Cam] Script CAMERA_PITCH never applies FXPitch on live host
description:
## C++
`W3DView::pitchCamera` (`W3DView.cpp:2520-2532`) stores `m_pcInfo.startPitch = m_FXPitch` and `endPitch = finalPitch`. `pitchCameraOneFrame` (`:3049-3068`) lerps `m_FXPitch`. `buildCameraTransform` (`:368-380`) uses `m_FXPitch` as a look-target multiplier: `<=1` shortens look-height (`target.Z = source.Z - height*FXPitch`); `>1` pulls the eye XY toward the look-at. Orbit `m_pitchAngle` is unchanged. Script `CAMERA_PITCH` / `CAMERA_MOD_SET_FINAL_PITCH` therefore flatten or steepen the view without remapping the default ~37.5° orbit.

## Leftover
`display/view.rs` stores `fx_pitch` and applies it in the leftover transform (`:1308-1326`). `pitch_camera` (`:2299-2320`) still animates `pitch_angle` via `set_pitch` (clamped ±PI/5), not `fx_pitch`. Leftover transform is not the live WGPU camera.

## Live
`start_game.rs:934-940` `script_pitch_to_radians` does `let _ = pitch; return 45°`. `apply_script_camera_pitch_request` (`:1058`) writes that constant into `camera_pitch_radians`. `apply_camera_orbit_transform` (`:967-990`) looks at `camera_target` with orbit pitch only — no FXPitch look-target multiply. Distinct from closed hq-vdxs4 (orbit remapping 0..2 → 5..85); that remap was removed but FXPitch was never applied.

## Player-visible
CAMERA_PITCH / CAMERA_MOD_SET_FINAL_PITCH / RESET_CAMERA pitch=1.0 cinematics never flatten or steepen the lens. Retail scripted pitches (look-down intros, look-flat flyovers) keep the default 45° orbit.
close_reason: Live CAMERA_PITCH lerps camera_fx_pitch; apply_camera_orbit_transform applies C++ FXPitch look-target multiply. Leftover pitch_camera/reset_camera write fx_pitch.

title: [Dozer] New construct paths to pad center and never ignoreObstacle the scaffold
description:
## Why
C++ `newTask` docks at `findGoodBuildOrRepairPosition` (half majorRadius + findPositionAround) and `PickActionPos` `ignoreObstacle(goalObject)` so the dozer can walk through its own scaffold. Live player construct A*s the click/center of the just-placed building with no ignore, so the pad is a blocking obstacle.

## C++
`DozerAIUpdate.cpp`
- `findGoodBuildOrRepairPosition` (`:1855-1894`): offset majorRadius/2 toward the dozer, `findPositionAround` maxRadius 100, MAX_Z_DELTA 10.
- `newTask` (`:1988-1998`) stores that as START/ACTION dock; END is 5 cells back.
- `DozerActionPickActionPosState::update` (`:203-211`) `ignoreObstacle(goalObject)` then `aiMoveToPosition`.
- Build only after `DOZER_DO_BUILD_AT_DOCK` (`:506-511`).

## Leftover
`dozer_ai_update.rs` `new_task` (`:636-681`) writes START/ACTION/END docks. Wave 351 empty-registry leftover is not the live path.

## Live
`command_executor/construct.rs` `execute_build` (`:131`) `path_to_goal_with_state(unit_id, location, Constructing)` — `location` is the placement click (pad center).
`unit_commands.rs` `unit_command_begin_construct` (`:444-454`) same: `assign_unit_path(id, location)` with no ignore-obstacle. AI `ai.rs` `process_building_queue` (`:1528-1530`) even overwrites `resume_construction`'s perimeter approach with a second path to `position`.
Repair/resume already use `dozer_repair_approach_position` (`rebuild_dozer.rs:939`); new construct does not.

## Player-visible
USA/China dozers drive into or around the foundation instead of docking on the facing side. Fresh pads often have no legal A* cell at the center, so the dozer stalls short of the 70-unit build range and the scaffold never progresses. Distinct from closed END-dock backoff (`hq-evalv`) and repair-dock (`hq-yfk9k`).
close_reason: Live execute_build docks at findGoodBuildOrRepairPosition (half majorRadius) and ignoreObstacle(scaffold) via assign_unit_path_ignoring so the pad is not an A* wall.

title: [Dozer] New construct never records BUILD task slot so a move-away abandons the scaffold
description:
## Why
C++ `DozerAIUpdate::construct` always `newTask(DOZER_TASK_BUILD)` so the BUILD slot + order frame survive a later player move and idle `isBuildMostImportant` resumes the scaffold. Live `execute_build` only sets order-target + Constructing; `dozer_task_build_target` is written only when a later Repair parks an in-flight build.

## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/AIUpdate/DozerAIUpdate.cpp`
- `construct` (`:1717`) calls `newTask(DOZER_TASK_BUILD, obj)`.
- `newTask` (`:1948-2008`) writes `m_task[BUILD].m_targetObjectID` + `m_taskOrderFrame`, setBuilder, START/ACTION/END docks, then `resetToDefaultState`.
- Idle primary machine `isBuildMostImportant` (`:1314`) resumes that pending BUILD after a player move.

## Leftover
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/update/ai_update/dozer_ai_update.rs` `new_task` (`:617-697`) records the BUILD slot, but Wave 351 empty-registry makes leftover update a no-op on the live path. Leftover crate has no `construct()`.

## Live
`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/command_executor/construct.rs` `execute_build` (`:117-131`) only `unit_command_set_order_target` + `path_to_goal_with_state(..., Constructing)`.
`dozer_task_build_target` is assigned only in `command_executor/leftover.rs` `dozer_new_task_repair` (`:1228-1241`) when Repair interrupts Constructing.
`dozer_idle_resume_pending_build` (`:1278`) therefore cannot resume a brand-new pad after the dozer is clicked away.

## Player-visible
Place a building, then move the dozer. C++ walks back and finishes. Live leaves a 1 HP scaffold forever unless the player explicitly resumes (or happens to Repair something else first, which is the only path that parks BUILD).
close_reason: execute_build now calls dozer_new_task_build so BUILD slot + order frame + setBuilder survive a later move; idle isBuildMostImportant resumes the scaffold.

description:

- Default `m_approachRequiresLOS = TRUE` (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.h:91`): `PartitionFilterLineOfSight` iterate in range.

title: [PowerPlant] New Cold Fusion after Control Rods never gets EnergyBonus
description:
## C++
`PowerPlantUpgrade::upgradeImplementation` (`PowerPlantUpgrade.cpp:86-104`) calls `Player::addPowerBonus` (template `EnergyBonus`) then `PowerPlantUpdate::extendRods(TRUE)`.

The module is `TriggeredBy Upgrade_AmericaAdvancedControlRods` (Type=OBJECT — researched on a plant). Completing it still sets the player's completed upgrade mask. `Object::updateUpgradeModules` (`Object.cpp:2410-2438`) walks every owned object that is **not** UNDER_CONSTRUCTION and `attemptUpgrade`s each `UpgradeModule`. Constructor (`Object.cpp:514`) and dozer construction-complete (`DozerAIUpdate.cpp:591`) both re-run that walk. A second/third Cold Fusion built after the research therefore still receives +EnergyBonus (retail 5, total 10) and rod visuals.

## Leftover

## Live

`notify_structure_construction_complete` does call `apply_researched_player_upgrades_to_object` (`world_scripts/production_eva.rs:1161-1194`) intending C++ `updateUpgradeModules`. That helper **skips** `is_object_scoped_upgrade` names, and the residual list explicitly includes `advancedcontrolrods` (`host_upgrades.rs:152-163`). Even if it did not skip, `apply_upgrade_to_object` (`object_queries.rs:2220-2438`) only stamps a tag — it never adds EnergyBonus or extendRods.

## Player-visible

Extra plants after the upgrade never double their output, so a two-plant USA base is permanently 5 power short per extra reactor.

title: [Energy] Zero-consumption grid skips low-energy build penalty
description:
## C++

title: [Object] Script Enabled/Powered never set live disable mask
description:
## Why
C++ script panel Enabled/Powered maps onto `DISABLED_SCRIPT_DISABLED` / `DISABLED_SCRIPT_UNDERPOWERED`, which make `isDisabled()` true so the object cannot move, fire, produce, or fire specials. Live host has no script-disable bits, so campaign/WB "Enabled=No" / "Powered=No" objects keep acting.

## C++
`Object.cpp:1019-1071` `setScriptStatus`:
- `OBJECT_STATUS_SCRIPT_DISABLED` → `setDisabled(DISABLED_SCRIPT_DISABLED)`
- `OBJECT_STATUS_SCRIPT_UNPOWERED` → `setDisabled(DISABLED_SCRIPT_UNDERPOWERED)`
`ScriptActions.cpp:257-270` `changeObjectPanelFlagForSingleObject` ("Enabled" / "Powered").
`isMobile` / `doSpecialPower*` / GameLogic update dispatch all key off `isDisabled()` (any mask bit).

title: [Rebuild] Name heuristic exposes holes on USA/China CC and wrong Scud hole
description:
## C++
`RebuildHoleExposeDie::onDie` (`RebuildHoleExposeDie.cpp:80-165`) only runs on objects that actually have the die module. Gate is Neutral / `isPlayerActive` / `!UNDER_CONSTRUCTION`. title: [Parking] Takeoff always frees stall; airborne jets lose hangar
description:
## C++
`JetAIUpdateModuleData` defaults `m_keepsParkingSpaceWhenAirborne = true` (`JetAIUpdate.cpp:1630`). Takeoff/landing `onExit` (`JetTakeoffOrLandingState` ~897-900, `HeliTakeoffOrLandingState` ~1120-1123) calls `pp->releaseSpace` **only** when that flag is false. Retail jets therefore keep their `ParkingPlaceInfo` stall while airborne. `reserveDoorForExit` / `hasAvailableSpaceFor` then see those stalls as occupied, so a 4-pad airfield cannot produce a 5th jet until one dies or lands elsewhere.

## Leftover
`jet_ai_update.rs` parses `KeepsParkingSpaceWhenAirborne` (default true) and only `release_space` when `!keeps_parking_space_when_airborne()` on takeoff exit. `parking_place_behavior.rs` `release_space` matches C++. Wave-310 empty dual-world gates leftover `build_info` / update so the player never hits this path.

## Live
`try_runway_takeoff_from_airfield` (`world_tick/airfield.rs:1446` helipad / `:1498` runway) **always** calls `release_jet_from_airfield_parking`, which clears `airfield_parking_spaces` + `airfield_parking_space_index`. Host has no `KeepsParkingSpaceWhenAirborne` field. After four jets launch, all four stalls read empty.

## Player-visible
Launch the airfield's four jets, then queue more: live starts building immediately. C++ holds the queue because the airborne jets still own the hangars. Returning originals then fight the extras for pads (or circle a "full" field that just spawned replacements).
close_reason: Live takeoff keeps hangar: launch_jet_from_airfield_parking / release_jet_from_airfield_parking honor KeepsParkingSpaceWhenAirborne default true (JetAIUpdate.cpp:1630); JetTakeoffOrLandingState onExit only releaseSpace when flag is false (897-900). Sortie path uses try_runway_takeoff_from_airfield instead of freeing the stall.

title: [Firestorm] DoT radius is instant FinalMajorRadius — no expand/reverse
description:
## C++
`DynamicGeometryInfoUpdate::update` (`DynamicGeometryInfoUpdate.cpp:93-161`) lerps Height / MajorRadius / MinorRadius from Initial* to Final* over `TransitionTime`. `ReverseAtTransitionTime` swaps ends and restarts so the fire shrinks. `FirestormDynamicGeometryInfoUpdate::doDamageScan` (`FirestormDynamicGeometryInfoUpdate.cpp:221-244`) uses the **current** `getBoundingCircleRadius()` every `DelayBetweenDamageFrames`. Scorch is placed once when `m_switchedDirections` becomes true (`:181-187`). Particle emission radii follow majorRadius each frame (`:152-167`).

Retail FirestormSmall: FinalMajorRadius **90**, DelayBetweenDamageFrames **500**ms, DamageAmount **100**, Lifetime **6000**ms.

## Leftover
`firestorm_dynamic_geometry_info_update.rs` `update_simple` (`:291-381`) calls `logic.update_step` (grow/reverse) and `do_damage_scan` with current bounding circle; scorch on `switched_directions`. Unused on the player path: live never instantiates FirestormSmall objects with this module.

## Live host
`HostHelixFirestormZone` (`host_helix_napalm.rs:178-194,303-313`) sets `radius: HELIX_FIRESTORM_RADIUS` (**90**) for the entire `HELIX_FIRESTORM_DURATION_FRAMES` (**180**). `plan_due_ticks` (`:329-370`) always tests against that fixed r90. Comment at `:28` / `:79`: fail-closed vs expand/reverse. Same residual is reused for HistoricBonus Inferno/MiG firestorms (`helix_radar.rs:486`).

No reverse scorch. No particle radius follow.

## Player-visible
Helix napalm / Inferno historic-bonus firestorms are a full-size 90wu burn from frame 0. Units at the rim take 100 (or Black 150) every 15 frames immediately; C++ they only enter the DoT as the circle grows, then leave it as it shrinks. Reverse-at-transition scorch never appears.
close_reason: Firestorm DoT uses current expand/reverse major radius (Initial 1 to Final 90 over 90f then shrink). Reverse-at-transition scorch once.

title: [PUC] Beam pulses skip same-team units
description:
## C++
Each damage pulse (`ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:636-648`) iterates `PartitionFilterAlive` only — no team / relationship filter. Allies, neutrals, and the owner's units in the beam take `damagePerPulse` (35). Remnant weapon INI is `RadiusDamageAffects ALLIES ENEMIES NEUTRALS`; the beam pulse itself is unfiltered alive.

## Leftover
`particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:1712-1723` damages every alive object in range (no team skip). Unused on the live host (`OBJECT_REGISTRY` empty → `update_simple` no-op).

## Live host
`HostSpecialPowerStrikeRegistry::plan_due_beam_ticks` (`special_power_strikes/registry_fields.rs:1087-1094`) skips `id == source_object` **and** `team == field.source_team` ("host strike convention"). Remnant ticks (`:1227-1244`) correctly hit all living except the launcher.

## Player-visible
A player's own (and same-team) units standing in their Particle Cannon beam take **no** pulse damage. C++ the beam is a friendly-fire superweapon — clustering under your own PUC is lethal.
close_reason: PUC plan_due_beam_ticks hits all living except launcher (PartitionFilterAlive). Same-team takes 35/pulse.

title: [ScriptCond] Live NAMED/TEAM ENTERED/EXITED area conditions never fire
description:
## C++
`Object::setTriggerAreaFlagsForChangeInPosition` (`Object.cpp:2563-2660`) walks every `PolygonTrigger` on integer XY move, sets 2-frame `entered`/`exited` flags, and marks the team `m_enteredOrExited`. `ScriptConditions::evaluateNamedEnteredArea` / `evaluateNamedExitedArea` (`ScriptConditions.cpp:1614-1650`) resolve the unit and `getQualifiedTriggerAreaByName`, skip only `KINDOF_INERT`, then `Object::didEnter` / `didExit`. Team enter/exit (`1656-1726`) call `Team::didAllEnter` / `didPartialEnter` / `didAllExit` / `didPartialExit` (`Team.cpp:1914-2075`), which already gate on `m_enteredOrExited` plus locomotor `whichToConsider`.

## Leftover
`object_triggers.rs` ports the C++ flag walk (`set_trigger_area_flags_for_change_in_position` / `did_enter`). `eval_area.rs` `evaluate_named_entered_area_condition` / `evaluate_named_exited_area_condition` return **false immediately** when `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is empty. Team enter/exit also require leftover `Team` members + `did_enter` on crate objects (`team_areas.rs` fail-closed on empty dual-world). Extra `AreaTracker::has_area` name gate is not the blocker — names are registered from `TerrainLogic::add_trigger_area`.

## Live
`mission_scripts.rs` evaluates via leftover `ScriptEvaluator`. Host comment in `world_scripts/scripts_camera.rs`: leftover `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is empty on the live path. Host objects never call leftover `Object::set_position`, so no 2-frame enter/exit flags. Snapshot injects names/positions only — no enter/exit history.

## Player-visible
Campaign/skirmish scripts that fire on "unit enters area", "team entirely enters", "one unit exits" never run. Reinforcements, speech, objectives, and area-triggered attacks stay silent when the player walks a named unit or team through a map polygon.
acceptance_criteria: Live path matches C++ Object 2-frame didEnter/didExit and Team didAll/Partial enter/exit for host units walking map polygons. Verified against ScriptConditions.cpp:1614-1726 and Object.cpp:2563-2660, not crate-only tests.
close_reason: Live NAMED/TEAM ENTERED/EXITED use C++ 2-frame didEnter/didExit on host units vs leftover PolygonTrigger. Dispatch empty-registry gate no longer swallows these conditions. pose.rs + inject snapshot walk integer XY like Object.cpp:2563-2660.

title: [ScriptCond] Live map-polygon INSIDE never matches; OUTSIDE fail-opens
description:
## C++
`evaluateNamedInsideArea` (`ScriptConditions.cpp:397-415`) looks up `getQualifiedTriggerAreaByName` and tests **current** `Object` position with `PolygonTrigger::pointInTrigger` (no dead/inert filter). `evaluateNamedOutsideArea` is `!inside` (so a missing trigger/unit is outside=true). Team inside (`evaluateTeamInsideAreaPartially` / `Entirely`, `378-392` / `634-647`) uses `Team::someInsideSomeOutside` / `allInside` (`Team.cpp:2079-2203`) against `Object::isInside` flags + locomotor `whichToConsider`. `TEAM_OUTSIDE_AREA_ENTIRELY` is `!(entirely || partially)`.

## Leftover
`polygon_trigger.rs` `point_in_trigger_int` matches C++ ray-cast (horizontal skip, AABB reject). `eval_area.rs` NAMED_INSIDE: if dual-world empty, `host_script_named_unit_in_named_area` (axis-aligned **AABB** in host XZ). `register_polygon_area` (`events.rs:1081-1092`) stores name only (`bounds=None`, `radius=None`). `trigger_area_aabb` then returns None, so `all_area_aabbs()` **omits every map polygon**. Host fallback `unwrap_or(false)` → inside=false. NAMED_OUTSIDE is `!inside` → **true**. TEAM_INSIDE calls leftover `Team::all_inside` / `some_inside_some_outside`, which fail-closed when `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is empty. TEAM_OUTSIDE is `!(all || partial)` → **true** for every leftover team with no crate members.

## Live
`mission_scripts.rs` uses that evaluator. `inject_host_script_query_snapshot` (`scripts_camera.rs:187-216`) copies only AreaTracker AABBs into the host snapshot — polygon-only areas never appear. Host units have XZ in the snapshot but no polygon test is applied.

## Player-visible
"Unit/team is inside the objective polygon" never becomes true. "Unit/team is entirely outside" fires on frame 1 even when everyone is standing in the zone. Campaign hold-the-area / leave-the-base / perimeter scripts invert or never complete.
acceptance_criteria: Live NAMED/TEAM INSIDE uses C++ pointInTrigger (or Object::isInside flags) on host units vs map polygons. NAMED_OUTSIDE / TEAM_OUTSIDE_AREA_ENTIRELY are false when the unit/team is actually inside. Verified against ScriptConditions.cpp:378-415,634-657 and PolygonTrigger::pointInTrigger.
close_reason: Live NAMED/TEAM INSIDE uses leftover point_in_trigger_int (host XZ = C++ XY). NAMED_OUTSIDE / TEAM_OUTSIDE invert that result so a unit standing in a map polygon is not outside.

title: [CommandXlat] RMB attack is enemy-tint only — neutrals/tech never attacked
description:
## Why

`system_impl.rs:1302-1303` `classify_right_click_target_from_presentation`: `hint.is_enemy_of_local && !hint.is_neutral && !hint.sold && any_attacker()`.

close_reason: Live CommandXlat/ActionManager: RMB attack is weapon-legal (neutrals/tech; dozer DISARM only vs mines). Unmanned husk Enter for any !REJECT_UNMANNED infantry plus arrival recrew. title: [ActionManager] Unmanned husk RMB never Enter — infantry cannot recrew
description:

title: [Countermeasures] Live missiles skip damage at impact instead of decoy-seeking flares
description:
## C++
`Weapon.cpp` `fireWeaponTemplate` (1144-1155): after launch, if the projectile is `KINDOF_SMALL_MISSILE`, the victim `hasCountermeasures()`, and the victim locomotor set is not `LOCOMOTORSET_SUPERSONIC`, call `victimObj->reportMissileForCountermeasures(projectile)`.

`CountermeasuresBehavior::reportMissileForCountermeasures` (`CountermeasuresBehavior.cpp:86-129`): increment incoming; if `available + active > 0` and `GameLogicRandomValueReal(0,1) < m_evasionRate`, walk the missile's `ProjectileUpdateInterface` and `setFramesTillCountermeasureDiversionOccurs(m_missileDecoyFrames)` (retail MissileDecoyDelay **200 ms → 6f**). If no flares are already active and no reaction is armed, set `m_reactionFrame = now + ReactionLaunchLatency`.

`MissileAIUpdate::update` (`MissileAIUpdate.cpp:638-660`): when `m_framesTillDecoyed` expires, set `m_noDamage = TRUE` then `missile->calculateCountermeasureToDivertTo(*victim)` and `aiMoveToObject` the closest flare from the newest volley. The missile peels off and chases the decoy.

## Leftover
`countermeasures_behavior.rs` `report_missile_for_countermeasures` (800-860) and `missile_ai_update.rs` `handle_countermeasure_diversion` (917+) port the delay + closest-flare seeker. Wave 328 empty dual-world registry short-circuits report to `Ok(())` and diversion to a no-op, so leftover never arms `frames_till_decoyed` on the live host.

## Live
`Main/src/game_logic/host_countermeasures.rs` `try_divert_missile` (219-265) is called from `combat.rs` `update_projectiles_with_countermeasures` (1699-1724) **at Direct-damage impact**, not at fire. A 30% roll immediately returns `true` and the host skips `take_damage`. No `SMALL_MISSILE` / `SUPERSONIC` gate. No `setFramesTillCountermeasureDiversionOccurs`. No `calculateCountermeasureToDivertTo`. Host comments: "collapses delay into immediate miss" / "Not full calculateCountermeasureToDivertTo closest-flare seeker".

## Player-visible
Diverted SAMs and Missile Defender shots fly all the way into the jet and vanish for 0 damage instead of peeling off after 200 ms to chase a flare. Aurora sneak (`SET_SUPERSONIC`) still gets the 30% miss. Non-`SMALL_MISSILE` projectiles that happen to Direct-hit an upgraded aircraft also roll the 30% skip. C++ jets under a missile volley show missiles chasing flares; live jets just sometimes don't take the hit.
close_reason: Live missiles report at launch, decoy-seek newest volley after 6f, no_damage on detonate

title: [Countermeasures] Live dumps one volley per evade instead of timed airborne sequence
description:
## C++
`reportMissileForCountermeasures` does **not** consume flares. The first evaded missile only arms `m_reactionFrame`. `update` (`CountermeasuresBehavior.cpp:214-239`) launches volleys only while `isAirborneTarget()` and `m_availableCountermeasures > 0`:
1. When `m_reactionFrame == now`, `launchVolley()` then `m_nextVolleyFrame = now + DelayBetweenVolleys`.
2. When `m_nextVolleyFrame == now`, launch again and reschedule.

Retail America air (Raptor ModuleTag_11): VolleySize **4**, NumberOfVolleys **5**, DelayBetweenVolleys **1000 ms**. One threat starts a 5-volley sequence over ~4 s. Additional evaded missiles keep using the same stock; they do not dump extra volleys. `reloadFrames == 0` means no auto-reload (airfield only).

`launchVolley` (273-331) always fires a full `m_volleySize` of `FlareTemplateName` objects, decrementing available per flare.

## Leftover
`countermeasures_behavior.rs` `update` (504-518) ports the airborne + reaction + `next_volley_frame` sequence and INI-parsed `volley_size` / `number_of_volleys` / `frames_between_volleys`. Empty dual-world `get_object` fails the update, so leftover never launches.

## Live
`try_divert_missile` on **each** successful evasion consumes `min(available, VOLLEY_SIZE=4)` immediately and queues that many `PendingCountermeasureFlareSpawn`s. `DELAY_BETWEEN_VOLLEYS_FRAMES` / `REACTION_LAUNCH_LATENCY_MS` / `NUMBER_OF_VOLLEYS` are honesty constants only — no timer, no subsequent volleys, no airborne gate on launch. Every aircraft is hard-coded to Raptor **4 × 5 = 20** (`FULL_LOAD_COUNTERMEASURES`); Comanche/Aurora "often 3" volleys never apply. One SAM evade dumps 4 flares now and never continues the 1 s cadence.

## Player-visible
A single incoming missile on a Raptor should pop 4 flares, then 4 more every second until 20 are out. Live pops one burst of 4 (if the 30% roll hits) and stops unless more missiles also evade. A swarm can dump the whole rack in one frame of hits. Comanche/Aurora carry a Raptor-sized rack.
close_reason: Timed airborne volleys: reaction then DelayBetweenVolleys 30f, no per-missile dump, Comanche/Aurora 3 volleys

title: [EVA] Base/Ally under-attack and own/ally EVA use faction Team not getRelationship
description:
## C++
`Radar::tryUnderAttackEvent` (`Radar.cpp:1194-1200`) fires EVA only for `STRUCTURE` + `KINDOF_MP_COUNT_FOR_VICTORY`:
- `obj->getControllingPlayer()->isLocalPlayer()` → `EVA_BaseUnderAttack`
- else `ThePlayerList->getLocalPlayer()->getRelationship(obj->getTeam()) == ALLIES` → `EVA_AllyUnderAttack`

`Player::getRelationship(Team*)` is team-override → playerAllies/playerEnemies → NEUTRAL. Superweapon Detected/Launched/Ready and BeaconDetected use the same own / ALLIES / enemy split.

`Eva::processPlayingMessages` (`Eva.cpp:452-525`) then plays one line: highest Eva.ini `Priority`, `Player::getSide()` vs `SideSounds` (`EvaUSA_*` / `EvaChina_*` / `EvaGLA_*`).

## Leftover
`GameClient/src/eva.rs` `process_playing_messages` matches that Priority + SideSounds path. Live host already ticks it (`update_eva_system`); closed hq-t7eko / hq-09e8 / hq-qaknm.

## Live host
`try_under_attack_event` (`world_scripts/eva_camera.rs:263-292`) does **not** use `object_relationship` / `player_relationship` (those already implement getRelationship + map playerAllies):
- `local_owns` = any local player whose **faction** `Team` equals the victim's `Team` (not `owner_player_id` / `is_local_player` on the controlling player)
- `local_ally` = `alliance_team` equal and `>= 0` and faction `Team` differs

Campaign / map sides leave `alliance_team = -1` (only skirmish lobby writes it). `production_eva.rs` own/ally/enemy for Superweapon Detected/Launched/Ready, BeaconDetected, and hero detected uses the same faction `Team` + `alliance_team` test.

## Evidence
C++ `Radar.cpp:1197-1200` `isLocalPlayer` / `getRelationship == ALLIES`.
Live `eva_camera.rs:263-292` faction `Team` + `alliance_team >= 0`.
Live `object_queries.rs:346-410` already has the C++ helper and is unused here.
`production_eva.rs:792-798,831,883-887,927-932`.

## Player-visible
- Same-faction ally CC attacked → "Our base is under attack" (wrong line).
- Campaign / map `playerAllies` CC attacked → no AllyUnderAttack (alliance_team stays -1).
- Campaign ally superweapon → Enemy* EVA instead of Ally*.
- Other same-faction player's superweapon → Own* EVA.

## Split hint
`try_under_attack_event`: `is_local` on `owner_player_id`, else `object_relationship == Allies`. Reuse that for production_eva own/ally/enemy.
close_reason: try_under_attack_event and production EVA own/ally/enemy use owner_player_id + player_relationship (getRelationship), not faction Team
