title: [Partition] getGroundOrStructureHeight empty-gate returns 0 instead of terrain
description:
## C++
`PartitionManager::getGroundOrStructureHeight` (`PartitionManager.cpp:4674-4701`) always samples `TheTerrainLogic->getGroundHeight`, then `iterateObjectsInRange(..., 1.0f, FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D)` with `PartitionFilterAcceptByKindOf(KINDOF_STRUCTURE)` and adds the tallest `getMaxHeightAbovePosition()`. Terrain height is returned even when no structures exist. No object-registry gate.

## Rust
Leftover `PartitionManager::get_ground_or_structure_height` (`object/collide/partition_manager.rs:1601-1646`) Wave-324 empty-gates first:
```
if dual_world_registry_unavailable() { return 0.0; }  // OBJECT_REGISTRY.is_empty()
```
Only then queries terrain + neighbor structures. Live leftover locomotor `LocomotorBehaviorZ::RelativeToGroundAndBuildings` (`locomotor/core_impl/behavior_z.rs:106-116`) calls this leftover PM. Host-only path keeps OBJECT_REGISTRY empty, so the function never reaches `get_ground_height`.

## Evidence
C++ always `terrainHeightHere + tallestHeight`. Rust returns 0.0 before terrain. Distinct from closed hq-hldn (handleBehaviorZ snap was wired to this helper). Wave-324 residual only documents the gate; it does not restore terrain.

## Player-visible
Helicopters/Comanches using Z_RELATIVE_TO_GROUND_AND_BUILDINGS snap to `preferredHeight + 0` (world origin) instead of flying over hills and rooftops. Units clip terrain and never rise over Command Centers / superweapons.
close_reason: Leftover PartitionManager::get_ground_or_structure_height no longer empty-gates 0; always samples terrain + tallest KINDOF_STRUCTURE (C++ 4674-4701).

title: [Partition] PartitionData::getShroudedStatus is ShroudManager stub — no COI mix, fogged-enemy, mines, or PARTIAL_CLEAR
description:
## C++
`PartitionData::getShroudedStatus` (`PartitionManager.cpp:1582-1688`):
- Before first `PartitionManager::update`, `!getUpdatedSinceLastReset()` invalidates and returns INVALID so fog does not persist across reset.
- Counts COI cells: all shrouded → SHROUDED; all shrouded+fogged → FOGGED then:
  - Neutral *mobile* → SHROUDED (moving neutrals never ghost in fog)
  - Enemy non-immobile, never-seen faction buildings, or `KINDOF_MINE` → SHROUDED
  - Seen immobile enemy buildings stay FOGGED (ghost silhouette)
- 0 COIs (off-map) → SHROUDED
- All clear → CLEAR; mixed cells → PARTIAL_CLEAR
- `m_everSeenByPlayer` records first CLEAR/PARTIAL so later fog can show the building ghost

## Rust
hq-cq1j closed by wiring `Object::get_shrouded_status` (`object/vision.rs:107-116`) to AlwaysVisible + `PartitionData` + CLEAR. `PartitionData` (`object/mod.rs:2531-2568`) is still a stub:
```
can_see_object → CLEAR
has_explored_object → FOGGED
else SHROUDED
```
No COI walk, no INVALID-before-update, no everSeen, no mine/neutral-mobile/unseen-building fog rules, no PARTIAL_CLEAR.

## Evidence
C++ `PartitionManager.cpp:1582-1688` vs Rust `object/mod.rs:2538-2568`. Distinct from closed hq-cq1j (Object getter) and hq-ij4 (client PartialClear presentation).

## Player-visible
Enemy units and mines linger as fog ghosts after you leave vision. Neutral civilians/animals appear as fog silhouettes while moving. Unseen enemy buildings show fog ghosts the first time they enter fog. Large buildings that straddle shroud/clear never go PARTIAL_CLEAR.
close_reason: PartitionData::get_shrouded_status walks COI cells, INVALID-before-update, everSeen, mine/neutral-mobile/unseen-building fog, PARTIAL_CLEAR (C++ 1582-1688).

title: [AIPlayer] Host never queues or repairs bridges
description:
## C++
`AIPlayer::update` always calls `updateBridgeRepair` (`AIPlayer.cpp:2296-2384`): once/second, pop dead heads from `m_structuresToRepair`, assign `findDozer` / `queueDozer`, `aiRepair`, complete when `BODY_PRISTINE` and idle, then send the dozer home. `repairStructure` (`:2254-2280`) enqueues damaged structures. `AISkirmishPlayer::checkBridges` (`AISkirmishPlayer.cpp:694-711`) walks the waypoint chain, `findBrokenBridge`, then `repairStructure`.

## Rust
Live crate implements `repair_structure`, `update_bridge_repair`, and `check_bridges`. The live host `AIPlayer::update` (`Main/src/ai.rs:348-349`) calls `resume_interrupted_construction` (reattach dozer to under-construction **buildings**) instead. Host `ai.rs` has no `repair_structure`, `check_bridges`, `structures_to_repair`, or `repair_dozer`.

## Evidence
C++ `update()` → `updateBridgeRepair`. Host `update()` → `resume_interrupted_construction` only. `grep` of `Main/src/ai.rs` finds no `repair_structure` / `check_bridges`.

## Player-visible effect
Broken map bridges stay broken. Skirmish AI never sends a dozer to repair a span blocking a scripted waypoint path, so attack/reinforce routes remain cut.
close_reason: Main/src/ai.rs: update calls check_bridges + update_bridge_repair; repair_structure enqueues damaged spans; dozer assign/queue/home

title: [Campaign] Challenge startNewGame never copies ThePlayer relationships onto the local player
description:
## C++
`GameLogic::startNewGame` (`GameLogic.cpp:1150-1151`) sets `isChallengeCampaign` from `TheCampaignManager->getCurrentCampaign()->m_isChallengeCampaign` in GAME_SINGLE_PLAYER.

After `PlayerList::newMap` (`:2073-2119`), Challenge copies alliances from the map's dummy `ThePlayer` onto the local player: every enemy of ThePlayer becomes a mutual ENEMIES pair with the local general. If ThePlayer is missing, every non-neutral/non-civilian player becomes a mutual enemy (self ALLIES).

Challenge also binds `TheGameInfo = TheChallengeGameInfo` (`:1180-1182`) so slots/colors/start positions come from the Challenge menu.

## Rust
Leftover `Campaign.is_challenge_campaign` is parsed (`ini_campaign.rs:393-400`) and ScoreScreen/load-screen read it. Leftover `start_new_game_now` (`impl_lifecycle.rs:479-571`) only calls `GameInitializer::initialize_game` — no ThePlayer relationship copy, no ChallengeGameInfo as TheGameInfo.

Live host `host_start_new_game_with_player_template` (`ui_commands.rs:846-880`) binds the selected General template then loads the map. No post-newMap ThePlayer relationship pass.

## Evidence
C++: `GameLogic.cpp:1150-1151`, `:1180-1182`, `:2073-2119`.
Rust leftover start: `impl_lifecycle.rs:554-557` initialize_game only.
Live host: `ui_commands.rs:846-880` SessionControlOp::StartNewGameWithPlayerTemplate.
Grep of Main `start_new_game` / leftover lifecycle has no `ThePlayer` relationship copy.

## Player-visible
Generals Challenge maps that authored alliances on dummy ThePlayer (or omitted ThePlayer and expect everyone-is-enemy) leave the local general on map-default relationships. Opponents can start Allied/Neutral, refuse to attack, or never count as enemies for scripts and victory.
close_reason: Challenge copies ThePlayer relationships onto local general after newMap

title: [Campaign] THE_PLAYER aliases fire outside Challenge; CampaignManager isChallengeCampaign unused
description:
## C++
`ScriptEngine::getPlayerFromAsciiString` (`ScriptEngine.cpp:5809-5814`) remaps `THE_PLAYER` to the local player **only** when `TheCampaignManager->getCurrentCampaign()->m_isChallengeCampaign`. Comment: regular single-player maps use a real side named ThePlayer; it is not an alias there.

`getTeamNamed` (`:5935-5939`) remaps `teamThePlayer` to the local default team under the same CampaignManager gate.

`getSkirmishEnemyPlayer` (`:5781-5791`) in Challenge skips the dummy human named ThePlayer when picking the first human enemy.

## Rust
Leftover condition evaluator gates **only** `TEAM_THE_PLAYER` (`eval_basic.rs:8-11`, `:52-57` via `capture_campaign_manager_runtime().is_challenge`).

`THE_PLAYER` is always remapped to current player in leftover `eval_basic.rs:30-33`, action `dispatch.rs:11-14`, and `actions/helpers.rs:248-255`. Action-path `TEAM_THE_PLAYER` (`dispatch.rs:39-52`, `helpers.rs:311-326`) is never gated.

Leftover `get_skirmish_enemy_player` (`dispatch.rs:941-968`) returns the first Human with no ThePlayer dummy skip.

## Evidence
C++: `ScriptEngine.cpp:5781-5814`, `:5935-5939`.
Rust leftover: `eval_basic.rs:30-33` (ungated THE_PLAYER), `dispatch.rs:11-14` and `:39-52` (ungated action aliases), `dispatch.rs:941-968` (no dummy skip).
Campaign flag lives on leftover `Campaign.is_challenge_campaign` (`campaign_manager.rs:80`).

## Player-visible
Regular USA/GLA/China maps that address player `ThePlayer` or team `teamThePlayer` hit the local/current player instead of the authored side. Challenge AI that falls back to "first human" can treat the empty ThePlayer dummy as the enemy instead of the real general.
close_reason: THE_PLAYER/teamThePlayer Challenge-only; skip Challenge ThePlayer dummy enemy

title: [Campaign] startNewGame never SetVictorious(FALSE) so leftover win flag survives into the next mission
description:
## C++
`GameLogic::startNewGame` (`GameLogic.cpp:1254-1256`) always clears the campaign win flag before the map load:

```
if(TheCampaignManager)
    TheCampaignManager->SetVictorious(FALSE);
```

`CampaignManager::SetVictorious` writes `m_victorious` (`CampaignManager.h:120`). ScoreScreen `finishSinglePlayerInit` (`ScoreScreen.cpp:768`) only advances `gotoNextMission` / missionSave / End Campaign when `TheCampaignManager->isVictorious()`.

## Rust
Leftover `CampaignManager::set_victorious` exists (`GameClient/src/gui/campaign_manager.rs:463-468`) and script VICTORY/DEFEAT now call it (`named_trackers.rs:320-328` → GameClient `script_action_handler.rs:1657-1659`).

Leftover `GameLogic::start_new_game` / `start_new_game_now` (`impl_lifecycle.rs:479-571`, `:924-949`) never call `set_victorious(false)`. Live host `host_start_new_game_with_faction` / `host_start_new_game_with_player_template` (`ui_commands.rs:816-880`) also never touch leftover CampaignManager.

## Evidence
C++: `GameLogic.cpp:1254-1256`.
Rust leftover start: `impl_lifecycle.rs` has no `set_victorious`.
Live host start: `ui_commands.rs:816-880` session-control only.
ScoreScreen still reads leftover `is_victorious()` (`score_screen.rs:636-640`).

## Player-visible
Win USA-01, Continue into USA-02. The leftover flag stays true. Opening ScoreScreen without a new DEFEAT script (quit-to-score, timer, or a map that never fires DEFEAT) treats the next mission as already won: auto-saves the following map and can skip the rest of the campaign.
close_reason: leftover+live startNewGame SetVictorious(FALSE) before map load

title: [Garrison] Live enter never setTeam / apparent controller
description:
## C++
`GarrisonContain::onContaining` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:1589-1625`) then `recalcApparentControllingPlayer` (`:1182-1277`): first occupant’s controlling player `getDefaultTeam()` becomes the building’s team; `m_originalTeam` is saved for restore. `getApparentControllingPlayer` (`:1167-1178`) returns the original owner to non-allies when `m_hideGarrisonedStateFromNonallies`. Drawable indicator color uses that apparent player (day/night).

## Rust
Leftover crate `garrison_contain.rs:866-928` / `:1082-1229` implements setTeam + hide + indicator color, but Wave 260 `dual_world_registry_unavailable` no-ops when `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is empty.

## Evidence
C++ `GarrisonContain.cpp:1206-1211`, `:1247-1255`, `:1618`. Leftover crate `:1140-1148`. Live `buildings.rs:1022-1038`.

## Player-visible

title: [Overcharge] onDisabledEdge never strips active EnergyBonus so hacked/EMP reactors keep +power
description:
## C++
`Object::onDisabledEdge` (`Object.cpp:3790-3855`) when `EnergyProduction > 0` builds `powerToAdjust` as base production plus `EnergyBonus` if `PowerPlantUpgrade` is already upgraded **and again** if `OverchargeBehavior::isOverchargeActive()`. It then `Energy::adjustPower(powerToAdjust, !becomingDisabled)`. The overcharge module itself stays active and `update()` keeps applying `DAMAGE_PENALTY`. Complementary to `OverchargeBehavior::onCapture` (already closed as hq-xxb): disable does not turn overcharge off; it only folds the bonus out of / back into the Energy pool.

## Rust
Leftover `object_upgrade.rs:278-357` `on_disabled_edge` ports that fold (walks leftover `OverchargeBehavior` / module interface and `adjust_power`). Live host never calls it.

Live disable (`apply_disabled_hacked` / EMP / paralyzed in `object/install.rs`) only sets status bits and stops orders. `power_provided` (base + overcharge EnergyBonus from `toggle_overcharge_object`) is untouched. `update_player_resources` (`resources_income.rs:46-56`) sums `power_provided` for every constructed+alive owner object with **no** `is_disabled()` filter.

## Evidence
- C++: `findModule("OverchargeBehavior")` + `if (overChargeMod->isOverchargeActive()) powerToAdjust += getEnergyBonus()`.
- Leftover: `BehaviorUtilityModuleKindMut::overcharge_active` then `player_guard.adjust_power(power_to_adjust, !becoming_disabled)`.
- Live: `apply_disabled_hacked` (`install.rs:531-542`) has no power mutation; `update_player_resources` fold has no disable gate.
- Not hq-xxb (capture-while-disabled Energy correction) and not hq-xgf3/hq-5t5k (leftover setDisabledUntil audio/dozer).

## Player-visible
Black Lotus hack, EMP, or other disable on an overcharging nuclear reactor leaves the full grid contribution (retail 10 + 5) in the owner's power. C++ drops both until the disable expires, then restores them. Hacking a China nuke does not brown out the base while overcharge is on.
close_reason: onDisabledEdge keeps overcharge; EnergyBonus folded by disabled-producer scan skip

title: [Overcharge] Save/load drops m_overchargeActive so drain stops and toggle double-applies EnergyBonus
description:
## C++
`OverchargeBehavior::xfer` (`OverchargeBehavior.cpp:275-289`) version 1 persists `m_overchargeActive` after `UpdateModule::xfer`. `Energy::xfer` v2+ deliberately does **not** save production (`Energy.cpp:240-249`: reconstructed when buildings load). `objectEnteringInfluence` only adds `ThingTemplate::getEnergyProduction()`, so `loadPostProcess` (`OverchargeBehavior.cpp:294-304`) re-fires `addPowerBonus` when the saved flag is true.

## Rust
Leftover `overcharge_behavior.rs` Snapshotable xfers `overcharge_active` and `load_post_process` re-adds the bonus — unused on the live host path.

Live host authority is `Object::overcharge_enabled` + `power_provided`. `ObjectSnapshot` / `BuildingSnapshot` (`save_load/snapshot/object.rs`) persist `power_provided` but never `overcharge_enabled`. Restore (`restore.rs:394-398`) copies power only; `overcharge_enabled` stays the `false` default. Player restore also zeros `captured_overcharge_power_delta` with a comment that C++ `loadPostProcess` would re-add the bonus — that replay never runs.

## Evidence
- C++: `xferBool(&m_overchargeActive)` + `if (m_overchargeActive && getControllingPlayer()) addPowerBonus`.
- Leftover: `xfer_bool(&mut self.overcharge_active)` + `load_post_process` → `add_power_bonus`.
- Live: `BuildingSnapshot.power_provided` only; grep of `save_load/` has zero `overcharge_enabled`.
- After a mid-overcharge save: grid still has EnergyBonus (restored `power_provided`), drain stops (`update_overcharge_drain` filters `overcharge_enabled`), control-bar ACTIVE is lost, next toggle thinks the plant is off and `saturating_add`s EnergyBonus again.

## Player-visible
Saving while a China nuke is overcharging, then loading: the reactor keeps the extra power for free (no HP drain), the overcharge button looks off, and clicking it stacks a second EnergyBonus. Toggling off then leaves a leaked +EnergyBonus on the grid forever.
close_reason: persist overcharge_enabled as world tail v12; restore flag without double EnergyBonus

title: [Experience] Residual combat fire awards invented per-hit XP
description:
## C++
`ExperienceTracker` never awards XP for chip damage. `Object::scoreTheKill` (`Object.cpp:2932-2940`) is the only combat grant: if the killer `isAcceptingExperiencePoints()` and the victim is not `UNDER_CONSTRUCTION`, it takes `victim->getExperienceTracker()->getExperienceValue(this)` (`ExperienceTracker.cpp:37-43` — 0 if relationship is `ALLIES`, else `template->getExperienceValue(m_currentLevel)`) and calls `addExperiencePoints(experienceValue)`.

## Rust
Live residual fire in `Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/combat.rs` awards invented per-hit XP on the attacker via `gain_experience((hits as f32) * N)` for Nuke Cannon (`:695-696` ×20), Neutron unman/kill (`:730-732` ×20/×30), Helix minigun (`:758-759` ×6), Comanche/RPG/Missile Defender and ~15 more residual branches (×2…×15). Several projectile-spawn arms count `hits=1` at launch, before impact. `_destroyed_any` is ignored. These branches replace the generic kill path, so they never call `award_experience(..., kill_experience_value())`.

Leftover crate `ExperienceTracker::calculate_damage_experience` (`experience/tracker.rs:432-434`, `damage * 0.1`) and `ExperienceGainManager::award_damage_experience` invent the same non-C++ damage-XP idea.

## Evidence
C++ `ExperienceTracker.cpp` has no damage/hit API. C++ `Object.cpp:2938-2939` is kill-table only. Rust `combat.rs` residual fire writes XP from hit counts. Closed `hq-w87m` fixed the generic kill path to `ExperienceValue`; these leftover residual weapons were not migrated.

## Player-visible
Nuke Cannon, Helix, Comanche, RPG Trooper, Missile Defender, Terrorist, Tomahawk and other residual-fire units promote from chip damage (or even from firing a projectile) instead of from the victim's INI `ExperienceValue`. A Ranger-value kill that should give 20 XP can give 6–20 per hit instead; splash “hits” farm veterancy without kills.
close_reason: Removed invented per-hit gain_experience from residual combat.rs fire (35+ remaining sites). Kill XP stays scoreTheKill/award_score_the_kill_experience.

title: [Experience] Host never setExperienceSink; implicit producer_id sink
description:
## C++
`isAcceptingExperiencePoints` is `isTrainable() || (m_experienceSink != INVALID_ID)` (`ExperienceTracker.cpp:53-56`). Sink is only set explicitly: projectiles (`Weapon.cpp:3021`), neutron missiles (`NeutronMissileUpdate.cpp:219`), Overlord/Helix rider when `ExperienceSinkForRider` (`OverlordContain.cpp:354-355`, default true), and SpecialAbility-spawned objects (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:1641`). `addExperiencePoints` (`:126-135`) forwards `experienceGain * m_experienceScalar` to that sink object if it still exists; otherwise it falls through to self. Untrainable objects with a producer but no sink do not accept XP.

## Rust
Leftover crate tracker implements explicit `set_experience_sink` and sink-forward (`experience/tracker.rs:88-93,244-260`). Leftover residual `ExperienceTrackerResidual` (`host_ai_path_combat_residual_wave105.rs:1198-1208`) matches C++ (trainable || sink; forward `gain * scalar`).

Live host never calls `Object::set_experience_sink` (definition only at `object/update.rs:478-481`). Instead `is_accepting_experience_points` (`:441-447`) also returns true for any untrainable object with `producer_id`. `GameLogic::award_experience` (`world_tick/shock.rs:671-695`) dest = `experience_sink` else (`!trainable` ? `producer_id` : none). Host Object has no `experience_scalar`; forwarded amount is unscaled.

## Evidence
C++ sink call sites are four explicit setters. `rg set_experience_sink` under `Main/` is only the setter. Overlord crate path (`overlord_contain.rs:368-373`) sets rider sink; host contain never does. Implicit `producer_id` has no C++ counterpart.

## Player-visible
Overlord/Helix bunkered units keep kill XP on the rider instead of promoting the tank. Untrainable spawned objects that still have a producer (mines, helpers, some projectiles if producer ≠ launcher) accept and siphon XP to the producer; C++ would drop that XP. Source AdvancedTraining/scalar never multiplies the forwarded amount.
close_reason: is_accepting and award_experience no longer use implicit producer_id. Overlord rider sink already set. note_producer sets projectile sink (Weapon.cpp:3021) on host spawn.

title: [Rebuild] Killing the hole worker mid-rebuild never resumes construction
description:
## C++
`RebuildHoleBehavior::update` (`RebuildHoleBehavior.cpp:171-280`): if `m_workerID` is set but the worker is gone, `newWorkerRespawnProcess(NULL)` starts `m_workerWaitCounter`. When the counter hits 0 a new worker is spawned. If `reconstructing` still exists, C++ calls `ai->aiResumeConstruction(reconstructing, CMD_FROM_AI)` (cpp:241). The scaffold keeps progressing.

## Rust
Live leftover `GameLogic::update_rebuild_holes` (`rebuild_dozer.rs:1498-1603`): worker-gone restarts `rebuild_ready_frame` but **keeps** `rebuild_reconstructing_id` when the building is still alive. Later the same tick hits `if h.rebuild_reconstructing_id.is_some() { continue; }` and never respawns a worker. Crate `RebuildHoleBehavior::spawn_worker_and_construct` does resume via `AiCommandType::ResumeConstruction`, but that path is dual-world gated (`dual_world_registry_unavailable` → Forever sleep) so it is not the live host tick.

## Evidence
C++: `else ai->aiResumeConstruction(reconstructing, CMD_FROM_AI);`
Leftover: `if h.rebuild_reconstructing_id.is_some() { continue; }` after only clearing `rebuild_worker_id`.

## Player-visible effect
Shoot the unselectable GLA hole-worker while the barracks/palace scaffold is up. In ZH a replacement worker appears after WorkerRespawnDelay (20s) and finishes the building. In Rust the scaffold freezes forever; the hole stays masked/unselectable and no new worker ever comes.
close_reason: leftover update_rebuild_holes respawns worker and resumes existing scaffold (rebuild_dozer.rs)

title: [Projectile] Live DumbProjectile flight is a straight line, not a terrain-clearing Bezier
description:
## C++
`DumbProjectileBehavior::calcFlightPath` (`DumbProjectileBehavior.cpp:383-438`) builds a 4-point Bezier: start/end are firer and victim center; inner X/Y sit at `FirstPercentIndent` / `SecondPercentIndent` along the 3D chord; Z is `estimateTerrainExtremesAlongLine` highest intervening terrain (clamped above start/end Z) plus `FirstHeight` / `SecondHeight`. Segment count is `ceil(arcLength / weaponSpeed)`. `update` (`:557-674`) steps that polyline, orients to the tangent when `OrientToFlightPath && !TumbleRandomly`, and detonates at the last point.

## Rust
Leftover `dumb_projectile_behavior.rs` ports the Bezier (`init_flight_path` / `BezierSegment::create_projectile_arc`) but `update` no-ops when `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is empty (`dual_world_registry_unavailable`, Wave 286). Live host never runs that module.

Live `HostProjectileLifecycle::DumbProjectile` (`projectile_lifecycle.rs:22-118`) stores only `max_lifespan_frames`. `CombatSystem::fire_projectile_ex` / `Projectile::update` (`combat.rs:418-443`, `:984-1027`) integrate `position += velocity * dt` on a straight chord (or a simple homing retarget). GameWorld named residuals (`inferno_shell_bezier_point`, `flashbang_shell_bezier_point`, `usa_tank_shell_bezier_point`, …) sample a cubic with `Y += FirstHeight` off the start/end line — they do not call `estimateTerrainExtremesAlongLine` and CombatSystem never uses them.

## Evidence
Closed hq-hg3x accepted the lightweight host entity; it did not close the flight-shape gap. Closed hq-c6up is leftover muzzle-bone / collide, already fixed in the crate. Distinct residual: live flight ignores authored Bezier + intervening terrain.

## Player-visible
Tank/artillery/inferno/nuke shells from the live fire_at path punch through hills in a straight line. Even GameWorld residual arcs do not rise over intervening ridges, so long-range China/GLA artillery clips terrain that retail clears.
close_reason: Live DumbProjectile steps leftover calc_dumb_projectile_bezier_points (terrain-clearing 4-point Bezier, ceil(arc/speed) segments). CombatSystem bind_authored_flight + update replace straight-line integrate.

title: [Projectile] Live GarrisonHitKill never clears occupied buildings
description:
## C++
Both `DumbProjectileBehavior::projectileHandleCollision` (`DumbProjectileBehavior.cpp:458-496`) and `MissileAIUpdate::projectileHandleCollision` (`MissileAIUpdate.cpp:316-352`) implement `GarrisonHitKillCount`. On collide with a garrisonable, non-immune container that has occupants: walk the contain list, `isKindOfMulti(Required, Forbidden)`, `scoreTheKill` + `kill()` up to Count, play `GarrisonHitKillFX` at the *building* center, then `destroyObject` the projectile **without** the normal detonation weapon. DumbProjectile also `recordClearedGarrisonedBuilding`. Retail Ranger flashbang comment at `:474` is this path.

## Rust
Leftover crate ports the walk (`dumb_projectile_behavior.rs:815-899`, `missile_ai_update.rs:655-731`) but both early-return when the dual-world registry is empty. Live host never calls them.

Live flashbang residual (`apply_ranger_residual_at`, `world_combat/streams_and_rpg.rs:385-508`) applies dual-radius SURRENDER splash to *exposed* objects only. `host_ranger.rs:22-23` honesty: "Not full SURRENDER DamageType infantry-surrender AI / garrison clear matrix". `update_flashbang_grenade_projectiles` detonates via that splash. CombatSystem structure intercept (`combat.rs:1214-1317`) deals area/direct HP to the building, not `kill()` on occupants. No `GarrisonHitKillCount` / KindOf / FX / academy clear.

## Evidence
`bd search` has no GarrisonHit / flashbang projectile bead. Contain leftover (garrison fire points, exit) is a different topic. This is the projectile collide-to-clear-building warhead.

## Player-visible
Ranger flashbangs (and any other authored GarrisonHitKill warhead) do not pull infantry out of occupied buildings. Players must smash the structure; retail flashbangs clear N garrisoned units and consume the grenade without a normal explosion.
close_reason: Live apply_garrison_hit_kill walks garrisonable contained_units, kill() up to GarrisonHitKillCount/KindOf, FX at building, destroy projectile without detonation weapon. Wired on structure intercept and target hit.

title: [ControlBar] showPurchaseScience leftover never unhides GeneralsExpPoints.wnd
description:
## C++
`ControlBar::init` (`ControlBar.cpp:1058-1142`) `winCreateLayout("GeneralsExpPoints.wnd")`, hides it, binds `CP_PURCHASE_SCIENCE` to `GenExpParent`, and caches `ButtonRank1Number%d` / `ButtonRank3Number%d` / `ButtonRank8Number%d`.

`showPurchaseScience` (`:2918-2933`) returns if `TheScriptEngine->isGameEnding()`, `populatePurchaseScience`, clears star flash, `winHide(FALSE)` on `CP_PURCHASE_SCIENCE`, and `TheTransitionHandler->setGroup("GenExpFade")`.

`hidePurchaseScience` (`:2935-2958`) `winHide(TRUE)` if visible. `togglePurchaseScience` (`:2960-2966`) is hide-state based.

`evaluateContextUI` (`:1698-1700`) re-calls `showPurchaseScience()` whenever the panel is already up so buttons refresh.

## Rust
`show_purchase_science` (`impl_science.rs:107-111`) populates leftover `science_state` and sets `is_visible = true`. It never loads `GeneralsExpPoints.wnd`, never unhides `GenExpParent`, never applies `GenExpFade`, and does not check game-ending.

`hide_purchase_science` (`:113-115`) only clears `is_visible`. `evaluate_context_ui` does not refresh a visible panel.

Wave138 host residual (`host_generals_exp_residual_wave138.rs`) is an honesty name table (`GeneralsExpPoints.wnd:ButtonExit` only).

## Evidence
Closed `hq-5n2p` was Rank1/3/8 command-set *binding* (leftover `populate_purchase_science` now fills `rank*_buttons`). Closed science auto-buy beads are host purchase, not this overlay. The leftover remaining gap is the WND overlay never appearing.

## Player-visible
Clicking `ButtonGeneral` / toggling purchase science does not open the generals experience overlay. Rank buttons and purchased ALWAYS_COLOR never appear on `GeneralsExpPoints.wnd`.
close_reason: ControlBar leftover loads GeneralsExpPoints.wnd, unhides GenExpParent, applies GenExpFade, and refresh from evaluate_context_ui (impl_science.rs / impl_lifecycle.rs).

title: [ControlBar] showRallyPoint leftover never creates RallyPointMarker drawable
description:
## C++
`ControlBar::showRallyPoint` (`ControlBar.cpp:2669-2720`) is the leftover rally-marker producer. `loc == NULL` destroys `m_rallyPointDrawableID`. Otherwise it `ThingFactory::newDrawable("RallyPointMarker")` (NO_SAVE), `setPosition(loc)`, `setOrientation(TheGlobalData->m_downwindAngle)`, and sets indicator color to local player day/night color.

`switchToContext(CB_CONTEXT_NONE)` (`:2170`) calls `showRallyPoint(NULL)`.

## Rust
Leftover+live ControlBar never implements `show_rally_point`. `portrait_state.rally_point` is only an `Option<[f32;3]>` stamped from presentation (`impl_portrait.rs:380-403`) and never used to spawn a drawable.

Repo-wide search: no `RallyPointMarker` and no `show_rally_point` in Rust.

## Evidence
Closed `hq-zx8k` is 3D waypoint/rally *paths* never draw (W3DDraw). Closed `hq-996dq` is SetRallyPoint pathfind reachability. Neither is this ControlBar.cpp leftover marker drawable.

## Player-visible
Setting a factory/war factory rally point never shows the retail RallyPointMarker flag at the destination. The leftover only remembers a coordinate.
close_reason: ControlBar::show_rally_point creates RallyPointMarker via TheGameClient, sets pos/orientation/indicator color, and switchToContext NONE destroys it (impl_portrait.rs / impl_context.rs).

title: [ControlBar] Special-power shortcut leftover never loads PlayerTemplate WND or command set
description:
## C++
`ControlBar::initSpecialPowershortcutBar` (`ControlBar.cpp:3198-3254`) requires a local active player, `PlayerTemplate::getSpecialPowerShortcutButtonCount() > 0`, and a non-empty `getSpecialPowerShortcutWinName()`. It `winCreateLayout`s that faction WND, binds `ButtonCommand%d` / `ButtonParent%d`, and sets `WIN_STATUS_SHORTCUT_BUTTON`.

`ControlBar::populateSpecialPowerShortcut` (`:3256-3482`) looks up `getSpecialPowerShortcutCommandSet()`, hides empty slots, skips `NEED_UPGRADE` unless `player->hasUpgradeComplete`, skips `NEED_SPECIAL_POWER_SCIENCE` unless `findMostReadyShortcutSpecialPowerOfType` exists and required science is owned (then `copyImagesFrom` / `copyButtonTextFrom` from Rank1/3/8 purchase buttons), skips `SELECT_ALL_UNITS_OF_TYPE` unless an object of that template exists, then `setControlCommand` + `GUIGenShortcutClick`.

## Rust
Leftover+live `init_special_power_shortcut_bar` (`impl_science.rs:491-518`) allocates `MAX_SPECIAL_POWER_SHORTCUTS` hidden slots and never reads `get_special_power_shortcut_win_name` / `button_count` / never loads the faction layout.

`populate_special_power_shortcut` (`:520-589`) looks up the hardcoded name `"SpecialPowerShortcut"` (not `SCIENCE_AMERICA_SHORTCUT` / `SCIENCE_CHINA_SHORTCUT` / `SCIENCE_GLA_SHORTCUT`). `NEED_UPGRADE` only checks `UpgradeCenter::find_upgrade` exists, not `has_upgrade_complete`. Science-upgrade image/text copy and select-all existence gates are skipped.

Host residuals (`host_control_bar_residual_wave133.rs`) are honesty name tables only.

## Evidence
PlayerTemplate INI parse already stores `SpecialPowerShortcutCommandSet` / `WinName` / `ButtonCount` (`ini_player_template.rs:573-584`) and getters exist (`player_template.rs:291-304`). Shortcut leftover never consumes them. `apply_need_special_power_science` (`impl_buttons.rs:314-420`) only runs for command-set populate, not the shortcut bar.

## Player-visible

title: [Bridge] Leftover BridgeBehavior damage/heal/state callbacks never dispatched
description:
## C++
`ActiveBody` walks every behavior module's `getDamage()` and calls:
- `onDamage` (`ActiveBody.cpp:589-595`)
- `onHealing` (`:826-832`)
- `onBodyDamageStateChange` (`:601-607`, `:838-844`)

`BridgeBehavior::onDamage` / `onHealing` (`BridgeBehavior.cpp:409-487`) propagate the same percent of max HP to every tower unless the source is already `KINDOF_BRIDGE_TOWER`.

`BridgeTowerBehavior::onDamage` / `onHealing` (`BridgeTowerBehavior.cpp:68-214`) mirror that percent onto the other three towers and the span.

`BridgeBehavior::onBodyDamageStateChange` (`:587-677`) plays damage/repair sounds, area FX/OCL, `updateBridgeDamageStates`, and radar terrain refresh on rubble transitions.

## Rust
Leftover `ActiveBody::for_each_damage_module_mut` (`active_body.rs:1223-1241`) walks `get_behavior_modules()` → `TemplateModuleBehavior`.

`TemplateModuleBehavior::get_damage` returns `Some(self)` when the DIE/DAMAGE mask is set, but `on_damage` (`object_modules.rs:1243-1258`) only downcasts `AutoHealBehaviorModule`. Every other DAMAGE module, including leftover `BridgeBehavior` / `BridgeTowerBehavior`, is `Ok(())`.

`on_healing` and `on_body_damage_state_change` are trait defaults (`specialized_behavior.rs:166-180`) — no-ops. The leftover implementations (`bridge_behavior.rs:1626-1876`, `bridge_tower_behavior.rs:481-540`) are never reached.

Distinct from closed hq-3xw1 (empty `play_audio_event` body — now implemented) and closed hq-7lca5 (AutoHeal-only wrapper).

## Evidence
`TemplateModuleBehavior` AutoHeal-only downcast vs leftover `DamageModuleInterface` impls that are never selected.

## Player-visible
Shooting a leftover tower does not damage the span or the other towers. Healing/repairing one piece does not heal the rest. Leftover damage/repair sounds, area FX/OCL, and rubble radar refresh never run even though leftover `play_audio_event` now submits audio.
close_reason: Leftover ActiveBody TemplateModuleBehavior downcasts BridgeBehaviorModule/BridgeTowerBehaviorModule for onDamage/onHealing/onBodyDamageStateChange; leftover BridgeBehavior/Tower wrappers implement Damage+Die; empty dual-world gates removed from leftover damage/heal.

title: [Bridge] Leftover BridgeBehavior/BridgeTower onDie never dispatched
description:
## C++
`Object::onDie` (`Object.cpp:4548-4566`) walks every behavior module, takes `getDie()`, and calls `onDie`.

`BridgeBehavior::onDie` (`BridgeBehavior.cpp:822-841`) kills all four towers, then `handleObjectsOnBridgeOnDie` (deck units fall or die), then records `m_deathFrame` so `update` can fire delayed `BridgeDieFX` / `BridgeDieOCL`.

`BridgeTowerBehavior::onDie` (`BridgeTowerBehavior.cpp:227-234`) `kill()`s the owning span (which then kills the other towers).

## Rust
Leftover `call_on_die_hooks` (`object_lifecycle.rs:828-840`) only dispatches modules that `module_die_kind` (`object/mod.rs:1344-1379`) recognizes: `DieModuleWrapper`, `MinefieldBehaviorModule`, `ProductionUpdateCompleteModule`, `SlowDeathBehavior`, or `Box<dyn DieModuleInterface>`.

`BridgeBehaviorModule` and `BridgeTowerBehaviorModule` are not in that enum. Their leftover `DieModuleInterface::on_die` bodies exist (`bridge_behavior.rs:1881-1898`, `bridge_tower_behavior.rs:543-556`) but are never invoked.

Update *is* dispatched (`update_via_behavior!(BridgeBehaviorModule)` at `object/mod.rs:1968`), so delayed death FX would run if `death_frame` were set — it never is.

Live host has no leftover BridgeBehavior (Wave 301/318 empty-gate residuals only). Distinct from closed hq-dqdob (SlowDeath).

## Evidence
`module_die_kind` arms vs leftover factory installing `BridgeBehaviorModule` / `BridgeTowerBehaviorModule` (`contain_module_overrides/update_modules.rs:439-456`).

## Player-visible
Killing a leftover GameLogic bridge leaves its four towers standing and targetable. Units on the deck stay put (no fall / no kill). Delayed collapse FX and OCL never spawn.
close_reason: Leftover call_on_die_hooks/module_die_kind now dispatch BridgeBehaviorModule and BridgeTowerBehaviorModule; wrappers forward DieModuleInterface::on_die (C++ Object::onDie getDie).

title: [Energy] Live sabotage timer hits first same-faction player
description:
## C++
`SabotagePowerPlantCrateCollide::executeCrateBehavior` (`SabotagePowerPlantCrateCollide.cpp:112-120`) takes `other->getControllingPlayer()`, then `player->getEnergy()->setPowerSabotagedTillFrame(frame)` and `onPowerBrownOutChange(TRUE)`. The victim plant's owner is the only grid that goes dark.

## Rust
Leftover crate (`sabotage_power_plant_crate_collide.rs:361-377`) uses `other.get_controlling_player()` the same way. Unused on the live saboteur path.

Live `PendingSpecialAbility::Sabotage` (`support_states.rs:2822-2830`) writes `player.power_sabotaged_till_frame` via `get_player_mut_by_team(target_team)`.

`get_player_mut_by_team` (`object_queries.rs:1208-1213`) returns the first `Player` whose `team` enum matches (USA/China/GLA), not `player_owner_for_host_object`.

## Evidence
C++: `Player *player = other->getControllingPlayer(); player->getEnergy()->setPowerSabotagedTillFrame(frame);`
Rust leftover: `other_lock.get_controlling_player()` then `set_power_sabotaged_till_frame`.
Rust live: `self.get_player_mut_by_team(target_team)` → `players.iter().find_map(|(id, p)| if p.team == team)`.

## Player-visible
USA vs USA (or any two players sharing a faction) : sabotaging P2's reactor blacks out P1's grid (first matching slot) and leaves P2's factories powered.
close_reason: live sabotage timer uses plant owner not first same-faction slot

title: [Energy] Sabotage zeros available but not production used for build speed
description:
## C++
`Energy::getProduction` / `getEnergySupplyRatio` / `hasSufficientPower` (`Energy.cpp:40-76`) all treat `TheGameLogic->getFrame() < m_powerSabotagedTillFrame` as zero production, ratio 0.0, and insufficient power.

`ThingTemplate::calcTimeToBuild` (`ThingTemplate.cpp:1541-1555`) uses `player->getEnergy()->getEnergySupplyRatio()` so GLA power sabotage immediately floors War Factory / dozer construction to MinLowEnergyProductionSpeed (retail 0.5).

`SabotagePowerPlantCrateCollide` also calls `onPowerBrownOutChange(TRUE)` the same frame (`SabotagePowerPlantCrateCollide.cpp:116-120`).

## Rust
Leftover `Energy::get_production` / `PlayerEnergy::production` / `supply_ratio` correctly return 0 while sabotaged (`common/rts/energy.rs:72-81`, `energy_handicap.rs:34-56`). Unused on the live host.

Live `update_player_resources` (`resources_income.rs:75-89`) keeps `power_produced` at the unsabotaged object sum and only sets `power_available = -power_consumed`.

Live `compute_player_power_factors` (`crates_radar_power.rs:869-883`) uses `power_produced / power_consumed` with no sabotage check. If produced >= consumed on paper, factor stays 1.0 for the whole outage.

Presentation freeze does zero produced for the HUD (`presentation_frame/build.rs:158-163`); build speed does not.

## Evidence
C++: `if (TheGameLogic->getFrame() < m_powerSabotagedTillFrame) return 0.0f;`
Rust host: `if player.power_sabotaged_till_frame > 0 { player.power_available = -power_consumed; }` — `power_produced` unchanged.
Rust factors: `(player.power_produced as f32 / player.power_consumed as f32).min(1.0)`.

## Player-visible
GLA Saboteur blacks out the power bar (available negative) but factories and dozers keep building at full speed for the 30s outage whenever the victim still has plants on paper.
close_reason: sabotage zeros power_produced and energy ratio used for build speed

title: [Energy] Host power scan still counts EMP/hacked producers
description:
## C++
`Object::friend_adjustPowerForPlayer` (`Object.cpp:3770-3782`) returns immediately when the object is disabled and `getEnergyProduction() > 0` — "Disabledness only affects Producers, not Consumers."

`Object::onDisabledEdge` (`Object.cpp:3825-3854`) when a producer becomes disabled/enabled walks PowerPlantUpgrade + OverchargeBehavior and `adjustPower(energyProduction + EnergyBonus, !becomingDisabled)`. EMP, hack, unmanned, etc. drop that plant from the grid the same frame.

## Rust
Leftover `Object::adjust_power_for_player` (`object_upgrade.rs:362-390`) ports the disabled-producer skip, and leftover `on_disabled_edge` (`:322-356`) adjusts player energy. Live host never uses that path.

Live `GameLogic::update_player_resources` (`resources_income.rs:46-56`) folds `power_provided` / `power_consumed` for every `is_constructed() && is_alive()` owner object. No `is_disabled()` / EMP / hacked / unmanned filter. `apply_disabled_emp` / `apply_disabled_hacked` only flip status bits (`object/install.rs:531-572`).

## Evidence
C++: `if (isDisabled() && getTemplate()->getEnergyProduction() > 0) return;`
C++: `controller->getEnergy()->adjustPower(powerToAdjust, !becomingDisabled);`
Rust host scan: `.filter(|object| object.is_constructed() && object.is_alive())` then `produced.saturating_add(object.power_provided)`.

## Player-visible
EMP Pulse, Black Lotus Disable Building, or Kell snipe on a Cold Fusion / Nuclear Reactor leaves its +5/+10 (and rods/overcharge bonus) on the owner's grid. Defenses and factories stay powered while the plant is dark.
close_reason: live power scan skips disabled producers (C++ friend_adjustPowerForPlayer)

title: [Science] Leftover first_capable walks sample table, not ScienceStore::getPurchasableSciences
description:
## C++
`ScienceStore::getPurchasableSciences` (`Science.cpp:301-329`) walks every `m_sciences` final override: skip cost==0 (not purchasable), skip already owned, then `playerHasPrereqsForScience` → purchasable else `playerHasRootPrereqsForScience` → potentiallyPurchasable. It does not consult a hardcoded name list. ControlBar / scripts / AI consume those two vectors.

`playerHasPrereqsForScience` (`:257-275`) and `playerHasRootPrereqsForScience` (`:278-296`) read the same store that parsed Science.ini.

## Rust
Live `ScienceStore::get_purchasable_sciences` (`rts/science.rs:693-725`) matches the C++ walk, but the live host never calls it.

Leftover host Alt+G / `PurchaseScience` (`selection.rs:458-487`) calls `first_capable_purchase_science_residual` (`wave109.rs:917-935`), which walks `SCIENCE_STORE_TABLE_WAVE109` (~30 sample rows). The table omits `SCIENCE_CashBounty2` (so CashBounty3 is unreachable), SpectreGunship, EmergencyRepair2/3, Paradrop2/3, LeafletDrop, and every other Science.ini purchasable not in the sample.

Leftover `ini_science::ScienceStore` has no `getPurchasableSciences` / `playerHasPrereqsForScience` / `playerHasRootPrereqsForScience`. Leftover `science_prereqs_met_residual` (`wave109.rs:854-877`) asks the empty live rts store first, then a 2-slot residual row — it never reads leftover `ini_science` prereqs even though host INI populated that store.

Closed hq-nk2eh was the old 5–7 faction array. This leftover remaining still does not call `getPurchasableSciences`.

## Evidence
`Science.cpp:257-329` vs `wave109.rs:459-703,834-935` vs `selection.rs:458-487` vs leftover `ini_science.rs` (no purchasable/prereq APIs) vs live `rts/science.rs:693-725` (unused by host).

## Player-visible
Generals points still auto-buy only from the sample table. CashBounty2 never appears so CashBounty3 cannot chain. Rank 3/5 extras in Science.ini (Spectre, Leaflet, repair/paradrop tiers) stay unobtainable via leftover first-capable even when leftover `ini_science` has their real cost/prereqs.

title: [Science] Host INI Science blocks populate leftover ini_science; live GrantScience/scripts use empty rts store
description:
## C++
One `TheScienceStore`. `INI::parseScienceDefinition` (`Science.cpp:355-358`) calls `ScienceStore::friend_parseScienceDefinition` (`:138-210`), which inserts into `m_sciences`. `GrantScienceUpgrade` (`GrantScienceUpgrade.cpp:70-71`), `ScriptActions` grant/purchase (`ScriptActions.cpp:5910-5925`), and `Player::grantScience` / `attemptToPurchaseScience` (`Player.cpp:2569-2634`) all call `TheScienceStore->getScienceFromInternalName` / `isScienceGrantable` / `getSciencePurchaseCost` / `playerHasPrereqsForScience` on that same store.

`getScienceFromInternalName` (`Science.cpp:67-74`) is NameKey identity: empty → `SCIENCE_INVALID`, else `(ScienceType)TheNameKeyGenerator->nameToKey(name)` even if the science is not yet registered. Callers then fail via `isScienceGrantable` / `isValidScience`.

## Rust
Two stores:

- Leftover `ini_science::ScienceStore` (`Common/src/common/ini/ini_science.rs`). Host `register_science_template` (`ini_template_loader.rs:1565-1586`) and `load_all_ini_templates` (`:598-601`) parse Science.ini from BIG archives into this leftover store only.
- Live `rts::science::ScienceStore` (`Common/src/common/rts/science.rs`). `ScienceSubsystem` (`:1168-1185`) loads `Data/INI/Science.ini` via `load_from_paths`. Host Main never registers/inits `ScienceSubsystem`.

Live GameLogic `GrantScienceUpgrade::resolve_science_type` (`grant_science_upgrade.rs:92-107`), `science_management.rs` grant/purchase (`:393-510`), and script `PlayerGrantScience` all call `rts::get_science_store()`. Live `get_science_from_internal_name` (`science.rs:462-471`) returns `SCIENCE_INVALID` unless the name is in that empty map.

Leftover host purchase (`player.rs:1006-1041`) consults leftover `ini_science` for cost, but leftover `science_ini_prereq_names` (`wave109.rs:834-847`) only reads the live rts store.

## Evidence
`Science.cpp:67-74,138-210,355-358` vs `ini_template_loader.rs:538-601,1565-1586` vs `rts/science.rs:462-471,1168-1185` vs `grant_science_upgrade.rs:92-107` vs `science_management.rs:393-510`. Main has no `ScienceSubsystem` init.

## Player-visible
PaladinTank / Pathfinder `GrantScienceUpgrade` never grants. Campaign `PLAYER_GRANT_SCIENCE` / `PLAYER_PURCHASE_SCIENCE` no-ops. Crate Player purchase sees an empty store. Science.ini is loaded, but into the leftover store nobody in GameLogic reads.
close_reason: register_science_template now ingest_definition into live rts ScienceStore as well as leftover ini_science. GrantScience/scripts/get_purchasable_sciences read the same INI-backed store.

title: [SpecialAbilityUpdate] Leftover steal/disable recharge is click-time or missing
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate::startPreparation` (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:1062-1067`) calls `getMySPM()->markSpecialPowerTriggered(NULL)` only after the unit is in range, unpacked, and facing — that is when the special-power reload starts. StealCashHack `ReloadTime = 2000`ms. DisableVehicleHack `ReloadTime = 0`. A cancelled approach does not start recharge.

## Rust
`DoSpecialPower` leftover (`command_executor/special_power.rs:255-331`) calls `consume_special_power_charge_for` on the click, then `execute_steal_cash_hack` / `execute_disable_vehicle_hack`. Dedicated `CommandType::StealCashHack` / `DisableVehicleHack` (`abilities.rs:642-819`) queue `PendingSpecialAbility` with **no** consume. Neither leftover completion arm calls `start_power_recharge` / `markSpecialPowerTriggered`. Capture and HDB correctly consume in `start_*_preparation`.

## Evidence
C++: recharge in `startPreparation` after unpack.
Rust leftover: consume-on-click (generic special-power path) or never (dedicated command). Completion: steal/disable just `stop_moving`.

## Player-visible effect
Via the command-button special-power path, Lotus's 2s steal cooldown starts when she is clicked on a distant supply center — cancel the walk and the power is already on cooldown. Via the dedicated leftover command, she can steal again immediately with no reload.
close_reason: leftover steal/disable consume at startPreparation (special_power.rs + leftover SA channel)

title: [SpecialAbilityUpdate] Leftover Burton/TNT plant skips unpack
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate::startUnpacking` + `handlePackingProcessing` (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:770-794`, `618-678`). Burton timed/remote C4 and Tank Hunter TNT use `UnpackTime` **5500**ms (`FlipOwnerAfterUnpacking` for Burton). During unpack, `LoseStealthOnTrigger` + `PreTriggerUnstealthTime` **5000**ms calls `StealthUpdate::markAsDetected` when `m_animFrames < preTriggerUnstealthFrames`. Crate path is dual-world gated.

Colonel Burton and Tank Hunters slap C4/TNT on instantly at approach range. Retail kneels for 5.5s (and Burton decloaks ~0.5s before the plant), giving the target time to move or kill the planter.

title: [SpecialAbilityUpdate] Leftover never flees after planting C4/TNT
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate::finishAbility` (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:1733-1818`). If `FleeRangeAfterCompletion` is set and there is a valid target/pos, C++ computes a flee point along `±getUnitDirectionVector2D() * fleeRange` (add if flip-after-pack/unpack, else subtract), steers away from the closest own `KINDOF_MINE` in that radius, applies a zero motive force so AI skips the idle pop, `aiMoveToPosition`, and `ignoreObstacle(target)`. Burton/TNT INI `FleeRangeAfterCompletion = 100`.

## Rust
Leftover plant arms (`support_states.rs:3056-3080`) only `stop_moving` + `set_target(None)`. `BURTON_FLEE_RANGE_AFTER_CHARGE = 100` is honesty-only; no leftover call site applies it. Crate `finish_ability` ports flee but is Wave 296 gated.

## Evidence
C++: `if (m_fleeRangeAfterCompletion && validTarget) { dir.scale(flee); aiMoveToPosition; ignoreObstacle; }`
Rust leftover: `obj.stop_moving(); obj.set_target(None);`

## Player-visible effect
Burton and Tank Hunters stand on the charge they just planted. Retail they immediately run ~100 wu away (and avoid walking back onto a previous mine).
close_reason: leftover flee after plant 100wu flip-after-unpack + own-mine steer

title: [SpecialAbilityUpdate] Leftover Lotus steal/disable skip unpack+prep+pack
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate::update` / `startUnpacking` / `startPreparation` / `startPacking` (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:388-442`, `770-794`, `963-1077`, `717-767`). After `isWithinStartAbilityRange`, C++ faces, unpacks (`UnpackTime`: Lotus steal **6730**ms, disable **2000**ms), then `startPreparation` (`PreparationTime` **6000**/**2000**ms): creates `BinaryDataStream` laser, sets `OBJECT_STATUS_IS_USING_ABILITY`, plays `PrepSoundLoop`, calls `markSpecialPowerTriggered`. On success it packs (`PackTime` **5800**/**1000**ms) with `Voice*Complete`. Lotus `StealthForbiddenConditions` includes `USING_ABILITY`.

No unpack, face, prep, pack, `BinaryDataStream`, or `set_status_using_ability`. Capture and HDB have dedicated channels; steal/disable do not. Host comments: "Not full SpecialAbilityUpdate preparation timers / packing".

## Evidence
C++: unpack → face → prep (laser + `IS_USING_ABILITY` + `markSpecialPowerTriggered`) → trigger → pack.
Rust leftover: `StealCashHack`/`DisableVehicleHack` arms apply the effect the first tick inside range 150 and `stop_moving`.

Black Lotus steals $1000 or disables a vehicle the frame she enters range, stays cloaked (no `USING_ABILITY` break), and never plays the 8–13s unpack/hack/pack animation. Retail is a long visible hack the defender can interrupt.

title: [CommandXlat] Hijack/carbomb/sabotage context leftover unused; live attacks instead
description:
## C++
`evaluateContextCommand` (`CommandXlat.cpp:1856-1918`) before enter/attack: if not force-attack and `canSelectedObjectsDoAction` is true, hijack / convert-to-carbomb / sabotage issue `createEnterMessage` (`MSG_ENTER`). Hints are `MSG_HIJACK_HINT` / `MSG_CONVERT_TO_CARBOMB_HINT` / `MSG_SABOTAGE_HINT`. Attack is later (`:1962`).

## Rust
Leftover `evaluate_context_action` (`command_translator.rs:489-506`) ports the same order via `selection_can_hijack_target` / `selection_can_convert_to_carbomb_target` / `selection_can_sabotage_target` (`dual_world.rs:335-353, 616-628`). Unused on the live OS click path.

Live `classify_right_click_target_from_presentation` (`command_system/system_impl.rs:1152-1196`) does ordinary Enter (capacity/garrison) then `AttackObject` for enemies. No hijack / carbomb / sabotage predicates. Hijacker vs enemy vehicle is therefore an attack unless the control-bar button armed `PendingUnitAbility::Hijack`.

## Evidence
C++ :1856-1918 before :1941 enter and :1962 attack. Leftover `command_translator.rs:489-506`. Live `system_impl.rs:1152-1196` enter-then-attack only; hijack is button-only (`ui_commands.rs:1798-1800`).

## Player-visible
Right-clicking an enemy vehicle with a Hijacker (or a terrorist carbomb / saboteur on a building) issues Attack instead of Enter. Players must arm the ability button first. Retail context-click does it automatically.
close_reason: Live classify_right_click_target_from_presentation now evaluates hijack/carbomb/sabotage before enter/attack (C++ evaluateContextCommand CommandXlat.cpp:1856-1962). Issues CommandType::Hijack/ConvertToCarbomb/Sabotage so live executors run; leftover evaluate_context_action already posted MSG_ENTER in that order.

title: [W3DModelDraw] validateCachedBones never fills pristine bone cache
description:
## C++
`ModelConditionInfo::validateCachedBones` (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:566-689`) is the producer for `m_pristineBones`. It `Create_Render_Obj`s the state model if needed, poses frame 0 (or last if `PRISTINE_BONE_POS_IN_FINAL_FRAME`), identity×scale, then `doSingleBoneName` for every `StandardPublicBone` and the state's `publicBones` (turret/weapon/extra). `validateStuff` (`:545`) calls this before turret/barrel validation. Every bone query (`getProjectileLaunchOffset` `:3275`, `getPristineBonePositionsForConditionState`) re-validates.

## Rust
Leftover `ModelConditionInfo.pristine_bones` (`Module/wthree_d_model_draw.rs:222`) is never filled. Live `validate_runtime_caches` (`types.rs:469-475`) only ORs `PRISTINE_BONES_VALID` if the map is already nonempty; there is no `validateCachedBones` port and no W3D load that inserts bones. The only writers are tests (`tests.rs`) and xfer load of an already-empty map (`module_data.rs:440-450`). `validate_turret_info` / `validate_weapon_barrel_info` early-return when the map is empty (`types.rs:311-312`, `:360-361`).

## Evidence
C++: `robj = Create_Render_Obj(...); doSingleBoneName(...)` into `m_pristineBones`.
Live: `if !self.pristine_bones.is_empty() { valid |= PRISTINE_BONES_VALID }` — never populated.
Leftover: map stays default-empty.

## Player-visible
Turret/weapon/public bone indices stay 0. Launch matrices stay identity, recoil/muzzle bones never resolve, `ParticleSysBone` attach falls back to origin. Distinct from closed recoil/FX beads: those assume barrel/pristine caches exist.
close_reason: Live ModelConditionInfo::validate_cached_bones now produces m_pristineBones like C++ validateCachedBones (W3DModelDraw.cpp:566-689): do_single_bone_name for StandardPublicBones + state publicBones via register_pristine_bone_lookup_hook. GameClient ensure_logic_draw_hooks registers Create_Render_Obj analog (THE_RENDER_BRIDGE hierarchy/HLod bind pose). Turret/barrel validation no longer early-outs on empty map after the valid bit is set.

title: [InGameUI] leftover setGUICommand never enters GUI_COMMAND mouse mode
description:
## C++
`InGameUI::setGUICommand` (`InGameUI.cpp:2865-2918`) is the leftover command-button arming path: skip during replay playback; reject buttons that do not `COMMAND_OPTION_NEED_TARGET`; set `m_mouseMode = MOUSEMODE_GUI_COMMAND`; store `m_pendingGUICommand`; set mouse cursor ARROW; `setRadiusCursor(command->getRadiusCursorType(), specialPower, weaponSlot)` so the targeting circle bleeds out from under the panel. Clearing the command restores `MOUSEMODE_DEFAULT` and `setRadiusCursorNone()`. `createCommandHint` (`:2710-2769`) then uses the GUI_COMMAND branch for valid/invalid cursors.

## Rust
Leftover `InGameUI::set_gui_command` (`leftover.rs:397-399`) only stores `Option<String>` — no playback skip, no NEED_TARGET reject, no `MouseMode::GuiCommand`, no radius cursor. Live control-bar `set_pending_command_with_visual` (`commands.rs:57-65`) stores a `PendingCommand` struct but never calls `set_mouse_mode(MouseMode::GuiCommand)`. `set_mouse_mode` exists (`impl_input.rs:509`, `helpers.rs:1988`) but nothing passes `GuiCommand`. `create_command_hint`'s GUI_COMMAND branch (`impl_input.rs:1203-1229`) is therefore dead on both leftover and live paths.

## Evidence
Grep `MouseMode::GuiCommand` / `set_mouse_mode(`: only definitions and the unused hint match-arm. Distinct from closed hq-d77h / hq-38as / hq-4ce57 (radius texture/size/draw) — this is leftover `setGUICommand` never entering GUI_COMMAND mouse mode so the hint/cursor branch never runs.

## Player-visible
Clicking a need-target command (guard, special power, mine, rally, beacon, …) does not switch into targeting mouse mode. The cursor stays the default world cursor instead of the button's targeting/invalid cursor, and the leftover GUI_COMMAND hint path never applies.
close_reason: C++ InGameUI::setGUICommand (InGameUI.cpp:2865) leftover InGameUI::set_gui_command now sets MouseMode::GuiCommand / Default, skips playback, rejects non-NEED_TARGET; live TheInGameUI::set_pending_command_with_visual arms GUI_COMMAND via arm_gui_command_mouse_mode.

title: [AIGuard] Return and crate leftover issue a parent MoveTo instead of InternalMoveTo
description:
## C++
`AIGuardReturnState` (`AIGuard.h:193`) **is** `AIInternalMoveToState`. `onEnter` (`AIGuard.cpp:602-625`) sets the post as `m_goalPosition`, `adjustDestination`, `setAdjustsDestination(true)`, then `AIInternalMoveToState::onEnter()`. `update` (`:629-640`) re-scans `lookForInnerTarget()` on `m_guardEnemyReturnScanRate` and otherwise runs the move-to loop. The unit stays in `AI_GUARD`.

`AIGuardPickUpCrateState` extends `AIPickUpCrateState` on the **guard** machine (`:744-770`).

## Rust
Live `AIGuardReturnState::classic_on_enter` (`guard.rs:1536`) leftover-issues `ai.ai_move_to_position(..., CommandSourceType::FromAi)`. That is `execute_command(MoveToPosition)` (`ai_commands.rs:129-151`): if the parent is not idle (Guard is never `isIdle`), it `set_temporary_state(MoveTo, 20s)` on the **parent** `AIStateMachine`, leaving Guard. Return `update` then only polls `CLOSE_ENOUGH` and never runs `lookForInnerTarget` while the temp MoveTo is active.

Crate pickup (`guard.rs:1678`) leftover-issues the same parent `ai_move_to_position`.

## Evidence
C++: `class AIGuardReturnState : public AIInternalMoveToState` + `return AIInternalMoveToState::update()`.
Rust: `ai.ai_move_to_position(&self.goal_position, false, CommandSourceType::FromAi)` then parent `set_temporary_state(AIStateType::MoveTo, LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND * 20)`.

## Player-visible
A unit walking back to its Guard post (after a chase, or after the guarded object moved) drops out of Guard for up to 20 seconds, ignores new enemies that enter the guard radius, and can fail to resume Guard if the walk takes longer than the temp state.
close_reason: guard.rs: AIGuardReturnState/AIGuardPickUpCrateState now compose InternalMoveTo/AIPickUpCrateState instead of parent ai_move_to_position

title: [AIGuard] Inner/Outer/Aggressor leftover uses AttackStateMachine instead of AIAttackState
description:
## C++
`AIGuardInnerState::onEnter` (`AIGuard.cpp:397`), `AIGuardOuterState::onEnter` (`:520`), and `AIGuardAttackAggressorState::onEnter` (`:815`) construct a full `AIAttackState` on the parent machine with `&m_exitConditions`:

## Rust

Leftover `ai/ai_states/combat.rs` `AIGuardState` does nest `AIGuardMachine` (same inner shortcut).

title: [Particle] Attached systems use yaw-only parent and drop setPosition translation
description:
## C++
`ParticleSystem::setPosition` (`ParticleSys.cpp:1281-1286`) writes **local Matrix3D translation** and clears `m_isLocalIdentity`. `update` (`:1910-1931`) builds `m_transform = parentXfrm * m_localTransform` (or parent alone) from the drawable/object **full 4x4** (`getTransformMatrix`, `:1863` / `:1886-1890`). `generateParticleInfo` (`:1729-1771`) then `mulVector3`s emission pos/vel through that 4x4. Bone FX and `skipParentXfrm` rely on local translation living in the matrix.

## Rust
Live `set_position` (`particle_system.rs:1483-1491`) only stores a world `Point3`. `local_transform` is a **3x3** (`set_local_transform` `:1523-1526`) with no translation slot. `resolve_attached_parent` (`:1698-1732`) overwrites `position` with the parent world pos and sets `parent_transform` to **yaw-only** `Matrix3` from `orientation.sin_cos()`. `compute_particle_position` (`:2155-2156`) is `position + transform * local_vol`. Any prior `set_position` offset is lost on the next attach tick.

Leftover Main `effects/particle_system.rs` has no attach/parent matrix at all.

## Evidence
C++ `setPosition` → `Set_X/Y/Z_Translation`. Live `set_position` does not touch `local_transform` / `is_local_identity`. Attach resolve uses yaw, not `getTransformMatrix`. Distinct from closed hq-lf92 (attach was previously not resolved at all).

## Player-visible
Bone-offset FX (muzzle flash, repair weld, jet exhaust bones) emit from hull origin. Aircraft/slope-aligned units emit exhaust in yaw-only space so trails ignore pitch/roll.
close_reason: set_position writes local Matrix3D translation (ParticleSys.cpp:1281-1286). update_transform_from_parent concatenates parent 4x4 * local including translation (1910-1931). generate_particle_info mulVector3s pos/vel through that affine (1729-1771). resolve_attached_parent uses drawable/object getTransformMatrix not yaw-only. Tests: set_position_writes_local_translation, attached_parent_applies_set_position_through_full_rotation, skip_parent_xfrm_keeps_local_set_position.

title: [W3DModelDraw] Team/house color never reaches the render object
description:
## C++
`W3DModelDraw` ctor (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:1734-1742`) seeds `m_hexColor` from the object's night/day indicator color. `setModelState` (`:3010`) creates the render object with `Create_Render_Obj(model, scale, m_hexColor)`. `replaceIndicatorColor` (`:3188-3207`) is gated by `OkToChangeModelColor`; a new color ORs `0xFF000000`, then nulls `m_curState` and rebuilds so house-color / ZHC textures rematch. `Drawable::setIndicatorColor` (`Drawable.cpp:4081-4088`) walks every draw module and calls that method.

## Rust

Live GameLogic `W3DModelDraw::new` (`draw.rs:106`) hard-inits `hex_color: 0` and never reads the owner indicator. Live `ObjectDrawInterface` (`draw_module.rs:198-374`) has no `replace_indicator_color`. Live `Drawable::set_indicator_color` (`drawable.rs:1746-1748`) only writes `self.indicator_color`. Submit still stamps `render_object_color = Some(self.hex_color as u32)` (`impl_anim.rs:560`) — always 0. Distinct from closed `hq-wzad` (Recolor_Asset now wired): the ModelDraw caller never feeds a non-zero color.

## Evidence
C++: `Create_Render_Obj(..., m_hexColor)` + `di->replaceIndicatorColor(color)`.
Leftover: rebuild is a debug log.
Live: `hex_color: 0` forever; GameLogic drawable does not dispatch.

## Player-visible
USA/China/GLA units and `OkToChangeModelColor` meshes stay unpainted house-color (default gray/tan skins). Capture, disguise, and night-indicator swaps never recolor the model.
close_reason: Live W3DModelDraw seeds hex_color from Object day/night indicator (C++ ctor W3DModelDraw.cpp:1734-1742), replace_indicator_color ORs 0xFF000000 and nulls cur_state then setModelState (cpp:3188-3207), Drawable::set_indicator_color walks ObjectDrawInterface, submit uses hex_color as Create_Render_Obj color. Leftover Device replace_indicator_color now rebuilds via set_model_state.
