title: [Object] WeaponSet snapshot in Object xfer missing ttName and named flags
description:
## C++
`WeaponSet::xfer` (WeaponSet.cpp:190-249), invoked from Object::xfer v4, writes `xferAsciiString(&ttName)` + `wsFlags.xfer` (named bits) before the slot loop, then `m_totalDamageTypeMask.xfer` (named BitFlags). Load rebinds `findWeaponTemplateSet(wsFlags)`.

## Rust
`weapon/weapon_set.rs` `xfer_state` starts at the slot loop (no ttName, no wsFlags). Damage mask is two raw u32s. Object::xfer compensates with `update_weapon_set` from current flags.

## Evidence
C++: ttName + wsFlags named bits before slots.
Rust xfer_state: slot loop first; `total_damage_type_mask` as two u32s.

## Player-visible effect
C++ saves desync at every armed object's weapon-set snapshot. After load, units can keep the wrong WeaponTemplateSet when multiple sets share flags.

## Split hint
Write ttName + named WeaponSetFlags then slots, then named damage-type mask — same as WeaponSet.cpp.
close_reason: WeaponSet::xfer_state writes ttName + named wsFlags before slots, named damage-type mask after

title: [Object] FiringTracker xfer omits module version chain and wake frame
description:
## C++
`FiringTracker::xfer` (FiringTracker.cpp:340-366) writes version → UpdateModule::xfer (version chain + `m_nextCallFrameAndPhase`) → consecutiveShots, victimID, frameToStartCooldown. It is the ctor helper `ModuleTag_FiringTrackerHelper` inside Object::xfer's module loop.

## Rust
`object_xfer.rs` `EngineSnapshotable for FiringTracker` calls `xfer_cpp_runtime_state` (`helpers/object_helpers.rs:64-75`) which writes only the 3 fields. No version bytes, no next_call_frame_and_phase. A correct impl exists in unused `firing_tracker_behavior.rs`.

## Evidence
C++: UpdateModule xfer + 3 fields.
Rust: consecutive_shots / victim_id / frame_to_start_cooldown only.

## Player-visible effect
C++ saves desync at every armed object's FiringTracker block. Rust-only loads lose the wake frame so continuous-fire cadence resumes on the wrong frame.

## Split hint
Use the firing_tracker_behavior xfer (version + update-module base + 3 fields) for the ctor helper.
close_reason: FiringTracker ctor-helper xfer: version + UpdateModule chain + consecutive/victim/cooldown

title: [Object] Repulsor status clears immediately instead of after 2 seconds
description:
## C++
`Object::setStatus` (`Object.cpp:965-970`) on REPULSOR: `m_repulsorHelper->sleepUntil(now + 2*LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND)`. Helper `update` then clears the bit. No helper (not CAN_BE_REPULSED) leaves the bit set.

## Rust
`object_status.rs:139-148` `wake_for_clear(TheGameLogic::get_frame())` — wake is NOW. `object_update.rs` clears REPULSOR the same/next frame. Also lazily creates a helper on any object, so script-set repulsor is auto-cleared too.

## Evidence
C++: `sleepUntil(TheGameLogic->getFrame() + 2*LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND)`
Rust: `guard.wake_for_clear(wake_frame);` with `wake_frame = get_frame()`.

## Player-visible effect
Damaged-civilian panic repulsion lasts one frame instead of 2s, so crowds do not scatter. Script UNIT repulsor toggles vanish immediately.

## Split hint
Wake at now+2s; do not lazily create a helper for non-repulsable objects.
close_reason: object_status.rs: REPULSOR wakes existing helper at now+2s; does not lazily create a helper for non-repulsable objects

title: [Object] FiringTracker update is never scheduled
description:
## C++
Ctor installs `FiringTracker` on `m_behaviors` as an UpdateModule (`Object.cpp:373-377`). `shotFired` `setWakeFrame`; `update()` force-reloads idle clips (`reloadAllAmmo(TRUE)`), stops looping fire sound, and `coolDown()` spin-up.

## Rust
`install_ctor_helpers` creates an object-owned `FiringTracker` and `shot_fired` calls `set_wake_frame`, but that only wakes other update modules. Nothing calls the owned tracker's `update()`. `CtorHelperBehavior` is name-only. The only `tracker.update()` is `firing_tracker_behavior.rs`, unused by stock INI.

## Evidence
C++: FiringTracker.cpp update idle reload / `removeAudioEvent` / `coolDown()`.
Rust: grep of `firing_tracker.` is shot_fired / last-shot / consecutive / xfer only.

## Player-visible effect
Continuous-fire weapon bonuses never decay after a burst. AutoReloadWhenIdle never reloads. Looping fire sounds never stop until the unit dies.

## Split hint
Drive FiringTracker::update from Object::update or register it as a real sleepy UpdateModule.
close_reason: Object::update drives FiringTracker::update_for_owner (idle reload, loop sound stop, coolDown)

title: [Production] Railed cancel_dock strands HELD dockers
description:
## C++
RailedTransportDockUpdate does not override cancelDock. DockUpdate::cancelDock only frees approach slots / activeDocker. action() already set DISABLED_HELD + UNSELECTABLE and m_dockingObjectID; update() doPullInDocking keeps swallowing the unit until contained. An interrupted approach still finishes the pull.

## Rust
Live railed_transport_dock.rs cancel_dock (602-610) clears docking_object_id when it matches, then calls base cancel_dock. do_pull_in_docking then sees INVALID_ID and returns. The docker stays DISABLED_HELD and UNSELECTABLE forever.

## Evidence
C++ RailedTransportDockUpdate.h declares no cancelDock.
Rust: if self.docking_object_id == obj_id { self.docking_object_id = INVALID_ID; }

## Player-visible effect
Canceling or bumping a unit mid AutoFerry/rail load freezes it unselectable and held in place instead of finishing the swallow.

## Split hint
Remove the cancel_dock override so pull-in continues, matching C++.
close_reason: railed_transport_dock.rs: cancel_dock no longer clears docking_object_id; pull-in finishes the swallow like C++.

title: [Production] Specialized dock INI omits inherited DockUpdate fields
description:
## C++
DockUpdateModuleData::buildFieldParse (DockUpdate.cpp:25-39) adds NumberApproachPositions and AllowsPassthrough. RepairDockUpdateModuleData::buildFieldParse and SupplyCenterDockUpdateModuleData::buildFieldParse first call DockUpdateModuleData::buildFieldParse, then add TimeForFullHeal / GrantTemporaryStealth. Retail WarFactory/RepairPad/SupplyCenter INI therefore parse approach-slot count and passthrough before the specialized keys.

## Rust
Live RepairDockUpdateData::parse_from_ini uses only REPAIR_DOCK_UPDATE_FIELDS = TimeForFullHeal (dock_update.rs:952-955). SupplyCenterDockUpdateData uses only GrantTemporaryStealth (1235-1238). impl_legacy_module_data_via_base does not merge base INI fields. Common ini.rs init_from_ini_with_fields returns UnknownToken on the first unrecognized key and the factory warns then keeps the partial default (0 approach slots, TimeForFullHeal never reached if it follows NumberApproachPositions).

## Evidence
C++: DockUpdateModuleData::buildFieldParse(p); then TimeForFullHeal.
Rust: const REPAIR_DOCK_UPDATE_FIELDS = &[FieldParse { token: "TimeForFullHeal", ... }] only.

## Player-visible effect
Crate RepairDock/SupplyCenter parse 0 approach positions so isClearToApproach fails and no unit can dock, or later TimeForFullHeal/GrantTemporaryStealth is dropped so pads heal instantly / never grant stealth.

## Split hint
Chain DOCK_UPDATE_FIELDS into each specialized table the way C++ MultiIniFieldParse does.
close_reason: dock_update.rs + supply_warehouse_dock.rs: specialized INI tables now include NumberApproachPositions and AllowsPassthrough before TimeForFullHeal/GrantTemporaryStealth/StartingBoxes.

title: [InGameUI] Radius-cursor INI table unused; all types share one texture
description:
## C++
`InGameUI::s_fieldParseTable` (`InGameUI.cpp:820-853`) parses ~29 `*RadiusCursor` keys (`ParticleCannonRadiusCursor`, `NuclearMissileRadiusCursor`, `EmergencyRepairRadiusCursor`, …) into `m_radiusCursors[RADIUSCURSOR_*]` via `RadiusDecalTemplate::parseRadiusDecalTemplate`. `setRadiusCursor` (`1257`) does `m_radiusCursors[cursorType].createRadiusDecal(...)`.

## Rust
`Common/src/common/ini/ini_in_game_ui.rs` `INGAME_UI_FIELD_PARSE_TABLE` has zero `*RadiusCursor` tokens. `impl_update.rs` / `radius_cursor.rs` fill `radius_cursor_templates` with `RadiusDecalTemplate::with_texture("SCCAttackDamageArea")` for every `RadiusCursorType`. Closed hq-d77h made *a* decal draw; it is always the generic attack-damage texture.

## Evidence
C++ table: `\"ParticleCannonRadiusCursor\", … offsetof(..., m_radiusCursors[RADIUSCURSOR_PARTICLECANNON])`
Rust: `vec![RadiusDecalTemplate::with_texture(\"SCCAttackDamageArea\"); RadiusCursorType::COUNT]`

## Player-visible effect
Nuke, particle cannon, repair, guard, and other targeting circles all look like the same attack-damage overlay instead of their authored InGameUI.ini decals.
close_reason: radius_cursor_templates_from_ini fills m_radiusCursors with per-type authored textures (ParticleCannon/Nuke/Repair/Guard/...) instead of one SCCAttackDamageArea (radius_cursor_ini.rs, impl_update.rs).

title: [PlaceEvent] Sneak-attack construction always issues DozerConstruct
description:
## C++
`PlaceEventTranslator.cpp:214-240`: if the builder `ProductionUpdateInterface::getSpecialPowerConstructionCommandButton()` is set (sneak-attack / special-power construct), the click appends `MSG_DO_SPECIAL_POWER_AT_LOCATION` with template ID, world, angle, options, and source object — not a dozer construct.

## Rust
Live host `place_structure_from_ui` (`ui_commands.rs:1293-1317`) always queues `GameCommand::DozerConstruct`. No `getSpecialPowerConstructionCommandButton` / `DoSpecialPowerAtLocation` branch. Crate translator has `active_special_power_construction` but is not the live click path.

C++: `placeMsg = TheMessageStream->appendMessage( GameMessage::MSG_DO_SPECIAL_POWER_AT_LOCATION );`
Host: `command_type: CommandType::DozerConstruct { template_name, location, orientation }`

## Player-visible effect
Gla sneak-attack (and other special-power-constructed buildings) try to send a dozer instead of instantly spawning via the special power, so the ability either fails or builds the wrong way.

title: [CommandXlat] Factory ground-click issues move instead of SetRallyPoint
description:
## C++
`CommandTranslator::evaluateContextCommand` (`CommandXlat.cpp:2180-2199`): if there is a position and no drawable, and `canSelectedObjectsDoAction(ACTIONTYPE_SET_RALLY_POINT, NULL, SELECTION_ALL)`, it posts `MSG_SET_RALLY_POINT` per selected factory (object ID + location) or `MSG_SET_RALLY_POINT_HINT`.

## Rust
Crate `handle_point_click` with `target == None` goes to `resolve_move_command` → `DoMoveTo`. Rally exists only as a pending GUI-button command (`pending.rs` / host `PendingMapCommand::SetRallyPoint`). Live host `mouse.rs` uses that pending arm for the Y/button path; selecting a factory and clicking empty ground does not enter it.

## Evidence
C++: `canSelectedObjectsDoAction( ACTIONTYPE_SET_RALLY_POINT, NULL, SELECTION_ALL, FALSE )` → `MSG_SET_RALLY_POINT`.
Rust host: rally only when `pending_map_command == SetRallyPoint`.

## Player-visible effect
Selecting a war factory / barracks and right/left-clicking the ground tries to move an immobile building (or does nothing) instead of relocating the rally flag.
close_reason: Fixed on both paths: GameClient CommandTranslator handle_point_click emits SetRallyPoint per AutoRallypoint selection when ground-click (no target); Main command_system::determine_context_command returns SetRallyPoint for empty ground + all AutoRallypoint (landed aaabae7a9 / C++ CommandXlat.cpp:2180-2199). Pending-button path remains for Y/control-bar arming.

title: [PlaceEvent] Placement angle is wheel-45deg, not click-drag
description:
## C++
`PlaceEventTranslator` (`PlaceEventTranslator.cpp:52-128, 302-329`) anchors on LMB-down, then `MSG_RAW_MOUSE_POSITION` after 5px drag calls `setPlacementEnd`. `InGameUI::handleBuildPlacements` (`InGameUI.cpp:1395-1418`) converts start/end world points to `v.toAngle()` so click-drag aims the building. Wheel is zoom, not rotate.

## Rust
Live host `mouse.rs:245-248` commits a non-wall building on empty-ground click (no drag-aim). `handle_mouse_wheel` (`mouse.rs:923-933`) if placement is armed applies `delta_y * FRAC_PI_4` (45°/notch) via `rotate_structure_placement` and **returns**, so zoom is stolen. Crate translator has the 5px drag threshold but is not the live click path.

## Evidence
C++: `angle = v.toAngle();` from worldStart/worldEnd.
Host: `let step = delta_y * std::f32::consts::FRAC_PI_4; ... return;` // skips zoom

## Player-visible effect
Players cannot aim a building by dragging; they must use the mouse wheel, which also cannot zoom while placing. Retail drag-aim is missing.
close_reason: Placement angle is click-drag world start/end (v.toAngle). handle_build_placements + host LMB-down anchors / LMB-up confirms. Wheel no longer steals zoom (place_icons.rs, mouse.rs).

title: [CommandXlat] Unreachable ground never shows the invalid-move cursor
description:
## C++
CommandTranslator::evaluateContextCommand final else (CommandXlat.cpp:2222-2278): if the cell is shroud-clear, each selected AI runs isQuickPathAvailable(pos) with cliff-locomotor rescue via isCliffCell. If none can path, hint is MSG_DO_INVALID_HINT (cannot-move cursor). Shrouded/fogged cells skip the check and stay valid.

## Rust
Crate translators/pick.rs selection_has_quick_path_to is hardcoded to return true, so DoInvalidHint is unreachable. Live host mouse.rs cursor table has no unreachable-ground case (selection plus empty terrain always Move).

## Evidence
C++: if (!validQuickPath) { msgType = GameMessage::MSG_DO_INVALID_HINT; }
Rust: pub(super) fn selection_has_quick_path_to(...) -> bool { true }

## Player-visible effect
Hovering or clicking water, cliffs, or isolated islands with land units still shows a legal move cursor; players get no cannot-go-there feedback.
close_reason: selection_has_quick_path_to uses AI is_quick_path_available, cliff locomotor + is_cliff_cell rescue, and skips the check on non-clear shroud so DoInvalidHint is reachable (pick.rs).

title: [Object] goInvulnerable incorrectly blocks all damage
description:
## C++
`Object::goInvulnerable` (`Object.cpp:6225-6233`) only `friend_setUndetectedDefector` + `startDefectionTimer(..., WITHOUT_DEFECTOR_FX)`. `attemptDamage` has no invulnerability check; the unit still takes damage.

## Rust
`object_combat.rs:1302-1304` `if self.is_invulnerable() { return Err(ObjectError::Invulnerable); }`. `is_invulnerable` is the `invulnerable_until_frame` set by `go_invulnerable`.

## Evidence
C++ attemptDamage: body + shockwave + radar only.
Rust: `if self.is_invulnerable() { return Err(ObjectError::Invulnerable); }`

## Player-visible effect
Defecting units and OCL InvulnerableTime spawns cannot be damaged or killed until the timer expires. Retail they take damage normally (they are only undetected).

## Split hint
Remove the attempt_damage invulnerable gate; keep the undetected-defector timer.
close_reason: object_combat.rs: removed attempt_damage invulnerable gate; go_invulnerable only sets undetected-defector + timer

title: [Locomotor] LocomotorSetUpgrade apply no-ops when OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty
description:
## C++
`LocomotorSetUpgrade::upgradeImplementation` (LocomotorSetUpgrade.cpp:28-33): `ai->setLocomotorUpgrade(true)` so `chooseLocomotorSet` can pick SET_NORMAL_UPGRADED (and other upgraded rows).

## Rust
`LocomotorSetUpgrade::apply_upgrade` (`locomotor_set_upgrade.rs:129-132`) returns false if `OBJECT_REGISTRY.is_empty()` (Wave 448). Production host keeps the registry empty, so the upgrade never sets the AI flag. Host bootstrap comments \"Fail-closed residual: Not a full multi-locomotor set / SET_PANIC upgrades\".

## Evidence
```
if dual_world_registry_unavailable() {
    return false;
}
```

## Player-visible effect
Units whose INI uses LocomotorSetUpgrade (upgraded workers, capture-flag, veteran loco rows) keep SET_NORMAL movement after the upgrade completes.

## Split hint
Call set_locomotor_upgrade on the live AI/host binding; delete the empty-registry gate.
close_reason: GameLogic locomotor: C++-matching flags/defaults/INI bridge/dispatcher/motive/Z/thrust/hover/upgrade

title: [Locomotor] Wheels donut timer never expires on move_towards
description:
## C++
`moveTowardsPositionWheels` (Locomotor.cpp:1405-1409): if onPathDistToGoal > DONUT_DISTANCE reset `m_donutTimer = frame + 2.5s`; else if `m_donutTimer < TheGameLogic->getFrame()` set IS_BRAKING. Kills the orbit-around-destination donut after 2.5s inside 40 wu.

## Rust
`move_towards_position_wheels_physics` compares `current_frame >= self.donut_timer`. Live `move_towards` (`move_towards.rs:53`) passes `0` as the frame (\"no frame available in move_towards context\"). Donut timer is initialized to `now+75`, so `0 >= donut_timer` is never true.

## Evidence
```
0, // no frame available in move_towards context
```
Wheels path: `else if current_frame >= self.donut_timer { set_flag(FLAG_IS_BRAKING, true); }`

## Player-visible effect
Wheeled vehicles (Humvee, Technical, trucks) circle the last waypoint forever instead of forcing a brake after 2.5s.

## Split hint
Pass TheGameLogic::get_frame() into wheels; do not invent a 0 default.
close_reason: GameLogic locomotor: C++-matching flags/defaults/INI bridge/dispatcher/motive/Z/thrust/hover/upgrade

title: [Locomotor] Damage-condition speeds apply at Damaged not ReallyDamaged
description:
## C++
`getMaxSpeedForCondition` / `getMaxTurnRate` / `getMaxAcceleration` / `getMaxLift` (Locomotor.cpp:768-844): if `IS_CONDITION_BETTER(condition, TheGlobalData->m_movementPenaltyDamageState)` (default BODY_REALLYDAMAGED) use undamaged values. Damaged units keep full speed; only ReallyDamaged+ use *Damaged. `getMaxTurnRate` also multiplies by TURN_FACTOR=2 when ULTRA_ACCURATE.

## Rust
`locomotor.rs:116-153` match:
- Damaged → *_damaged immediately
- ReallyDamaged → *_damaged * 0.5 (invented)
- Rubble → 0.0 (invented)
No ULTRA_ACCURATE ×2 on turn rate.

## Evidence
```
BodyDamageType::Damaged => self.template.max_speed_damaged,
BodyDamageType::ReallyDamaged => self.template.max_speed_damaged * 0.5,
BodyDamageType::Rubble => 0.0,
```

## Player-visible effect
Yellow-health tanks/infantry crawl at SpeedDamaged (or half of that when critical) instead of full speed until really-damaged. Ultra-accurate jet landings turn at half the C++ cheat rate.

## Split hint
One getter helper matching IS_CONDITION_BETTER + GlobalData movementPenaltyDamageState; add TURN_FACTOR on turn.
close_reason: GameLogic locomotor: C++-matching flags/defaults/INI bridge/dispatcher/motive/Z/thrust/hover/upgrade

title: [Object] setReceivingDifficultyBonus never applies health or weapon bonuses
description:
## C++
`Object::setReceivingDifficultyBonus` (`Object.cpp:2031-2037`) early-returns if unchanged, then `getControllingPlayer()->friend_applyDifficultyBonusesForObject` (Player.cpp:3338-3367): solo health scale with PRESERVE_RATIO and WEAPONBONUSCONDITION_SOLO_HUMAN/AI_{EASY,NORMAL,HARD}.

C++: `getControllingPlayer()->friend_applyDifficultyBonusesForObject(this, m_isReceivingDifficultyBonus);`
Rust: `self.is_receiving_difficulty_bonus = value;`

Solo/campaign difficulty does not scale unit HP or damage. Easy/Hard play the same as Normal for object bonuses.

Apply Player difficulty bonuses inside the setter; also call it from init_object (hq-y3uy).

title: [Object] Capture never awards AutoDeposit InitialCaptureBonus
description:
## C++

## Rust

Call award_initial_capture_bonus from set_or_restore_team after the new owner is set (same place as becomingTeamMember).

title: [Physics] Live host vehicle-building crash deals 100 Explosive not INI weapon
description:
## C++
`onCollide` (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1336-1359): vehicle vs structure fires `m_vehicleCrashesIntoBuildingWeaponTemplate` via `TheWeaponStore->createAndFireTempWeapon` then `destroyObject`. Non-building immobile fires the non-building template (no destroy). Templates default to VehicleCrashesIntoBuildingWeapon / VehicleCrashesIntoNonBuildingWeapon (OCL/FX).

## Rust
GameLogic `on_collision` is a stub (hq-ckpm). The *live* host path `apply_vehicle_crash_into_immobile` (Main world_tick/physics.rs:538-545) does `const CRASH_DAMAGE: f32 = 100.0` as Explosive `take_damage_from_typed`, with comment \"Fail-closed vs full WeaponStore::createAndFireTempWeapon OCL/FX matrix\". INI crash-weapon names on PhysicsBehaviorModuleData are never resolved or fired.

## Evidence
```
const CRASH_DAMAGE: f32 = 100.0;
v.take_damage_from_typed(CRASH_DAMAGE, Some(vehicle_id), DamageType::Explosive);
```

## Player-visible effect
Cars/tanks hitting buildings take a flat 100 explosive instead of the authored crash weapon (explosion FX, OCL debris, guaranteed destroy). Non-building crashes also miss their weapon.

## Split hint
Call WeaponStore createAndFireTempWeapon from the live collide path; delete CRASH_DAMAGE.
close_reason: GameLogic PhysicsBehavior::on_collision now fires VehicleCrashesIntoBuilding/NonBuilding via TheWeaponStore::create_and_fire_temp_weapon then destroyObject (physics_collide.rs). Deleted the stub-only last_collidee path.

title: [Physics] IS_IN_FREEFALL never set so freefall pose never applies
description:
## C++
`setIsInFreeFall(true)` (PhysicsUpdate.h:164) sets FLAG_IS_IN_FREEFALL. `update` (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:774-778): if airborne and IS_IN_FREEFALL → `setDisabled(DISABLED_FREEFALL)` + `MODELCONDITION_FREEFALL`. Cleared on landing.

## Rust
`physics_update.rs` only *clears* FLAG_IS_IN_FREEFALL on landing (904-907). Nothing in GameEngine sets the flag true. The airborne branch that applies DISABLED_FREEFALL / MODELCONDITION_FREEFALL (805-808) is unreachable. `is_on_ground` is `!FLAG_IS_IN_FREEFALL`, so every object reports on-ground.

## Evidence
Grep `set_flag(FLAG_IS_IN_FREEFALL, true)` / `set_is_in_freefall(true)` in GameEngine: no writers. Only clear on landing.

## Player-visible effect
Parachute/ejected/scripted freefall units never get the freefall pose or DISABLED_FREEFALL (they keep acting). `is_on_ground` lies.

## Split hint
Add the C++ setter and call it from the same parachute/eject sites.
close_reason: Added PhysicsBehavior::set_is_in_freefall/get_is_in_freefall (C++ 0x0200 FLAG_IS_IN_FREEFALL). ParachuteContain::on_die now sets it with set_allow_to_fall + applyForce like C++ ParachuteContain.cpp:643-648.

title: [Physics] Braking projectiles still translate in X/Y
close_reason: update_simple braking matches C++ nested if: BRAKING + !PROJECTILE integrates Z only; BRAKING + PROJECTILE integrates nothing.

title: [Object] DozerConstruct command-button does not use BuildAssistant
description:
## C++
No-target `doCommandButton` groups `GUI_COMMAND_UNIT_BUILD` and `GUI_COMMAND_DOZER_CONSTRUCT` into `pu->queueCreateUnit`.
At-position `doCommandButtonAtPosition` (`Object.cpp:5674-5676`) is `TheBuildAssistant->buildObjectNow(...)` which validates, clears debris, and `ai->construct`.

## Rust
`do_command_button` has no DozerConstruct arm (`_ => {}`).
`do_command_button_at_position` (`object_special_power.rs:548-666`) uses FoundationValidator + pathfinder find_path + factory.new_object + set_build_task. Extra early-outs C++ does not have; no BuildAssistant construct / onStructureCreated.

## Evidence
C++: `TheBuildAssistant->buildObjectNow(this, template, pos, 0.0f, getControllingPlayer());`
Rust no-target: DozerConstruct falls through. At-position: `FoundationValidator::new_strict().validate_placement` can return Ok without building.

## Player-visible effect
Scripted dozer-construct buttons do nothing without a position, and with a position they can silently refuse legal C++ sites or skip construction-complete notifications.

## Split hint
No-target: queueCreateUnit. At-position: BuildAssistant::build_object_now.
close_reason: no-target DozerConstruct queues via production; at-position uses BuildAssistant::build_object_now

title: [Object] goInvulnerable treats already-converted frames as milliseconds
description:
## C++
`InvulnerableTime` INI uses `INI::parseDurationUnsignedInt` (msec → frames). `Object::goInvulnerable(UnsignedInt time)` (`Object.cpp:6225-6233`) passes `time` straight to `startDefectionTimer(time)` — already frames.

## Rust
OCL `store.rs` parses InvulnerableTime with `parse_duration_to_frames` into `invulnerable_time`, then `nuggets.rs:584` calls `go_invulnerable(self.invulnerable_time)`.
`object_upgrade.rs:72-85` documents the arg as milliseconds and does `duration_ms * LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND / 1000`.

## Evidence
C++: parseDurationUnsignedInt then `goInvulnerable(m_invulnerableTime)` with no second convert.
Rust: `let frames = duration_ms.saturating_mul(LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND) / 1000;`

## Player-visible effect
Spawned/ejected units that should be invulnerable for seconds (e.g. 90 frames) only get ~3 frames, so they die immediately after spawn.

## Split hint
Take frames in go_invulnerable, matching C++ and the OCL parser.
close_reason: object/disabled.rs: go_invulnerable takes frames and starts the defection timer with no second msec conversion

title: [Drawable] GameLogic tint envelopes never tick or render
description:
## C++
`Drawable::updateDrawable` (`Drawable.cpp:1284-1288`) ticks `m_colorTintEnvelope` and `m_selectionFlashEnvelope` every frame. `getTintColor`/`getSelectionColor` sample those envelopes for W3D lights. EMP (`EMPUpdate.cpp`) calls `colorTint`/`colorFlash` on that same drawable.

## Rust
hq-46l3 closed the missing EMP `color_tint`/`color_flash` *calls*. Those now write `LegacyTintEnvelope` on GameLogic `object/drawable.rs`. That envelope has play/rest/xfer but **no `update()`**, and `Drawable::update` (`:1937-2009`) never advances it. `get_tint_color` (`:1647`) returns a static field, not the envelope. Behaviors (EMP, grant_stealth, contain flash) mutate this drawable.

## Evidence
`LegacyTintEnvelope` (drawable.rs ~285-330): play/rest/xfer only. No update method. `Drawable::update` has no envelope tick / tint-status ladder.

## Player-visible effect
EMP/neutron pulse still grows uncolored (calls happen, nothing fades or tints the mesh). Script colorFlash and contain flash_as_selected on the logic drawable never appear as an additive light envelope.

## Split hint
Either tick LegacyTintEnvelope like C++ and sample it from get_tint_color, or route those callers onto GameClient BasicDrawable envelopes.
close_reason: GameClient envelopes tick in update; get_tint_color samples status envelope; color_tint/color_flash play it (Drawable.cpp updateDrawable).

title: [Drawable] clear_model_condition_flags never reaches W3DModelDraw
description:
## C++
`Drawable::clearModelConditionFlags` (`Drawable.cpp:411`) goes through `clearAndSetModelConditionFlags` which sets `m_isModelDirty`; `getDrawModules` then `replaceModelConditionState`. Every clear reaches the model.

## Rust
Live GameLogic `Drawable::clear_model_condition_flags` (`object/drawable.rs:3343-3346`) and `clear_model_condition_garrisoned` (`:3348-3352`) only do `model_conditions &= !clear; update_conditional_model();` — they do **not** call `propagate_model_condition_state_to_draw_modules` (the single-flag variants at :3131-3142 do). Live callers: `animation_steering_update.rs:167-169` clears LeftToCenter|RightToCenter after a turn; `cave_contain.rs:263` clears GARRISONED.

## Evidence
Propagating: `clear_model_condition_state` → `propagate_model_condition_state_to_draw_modules()`.
Non-propagating: `clear_model_condition_flags` / `clear_model_condition_garrisoned` stop after `update_conditional_model()`.

## Player-visible effect
Vehicles stay in the left/right turn animation after they straighten. Cave/garrisoned models keep the GARRISONED ConditionState (occupied windows/poses) after units leave.

## Split hint
Make the plural/garrisoned clears call the same propagate helper as the single-flag path.
close_reason: GameClient clear_model_condition_flags/garrisoned/state dirty-apply via replace_model_condition_state like C++ clearAndSetModelConditionFlags.

title: [Object] doCommandButton special-power path skips canUse and forced
description:
## C++
`doCommandButton` / `AtObject` / `AtPosition` / `UsingWaypoints` all call `doSpecialPower*(template, options, cmdSource == CMD_FROM_SCRIPT)`. `Object::doSpecialPower` (`Object.cpp:5314-5330`) returns unless `forced` or `TheSpecialPowerStore->canUseSpecialPower`.

## Rust
`object_special_power.rs` button arms call `with_special_power_module_mut_by_name(...).do_special_power*` directly. `can_dispatch_special_power` exists but is unused on the button path. `source` is not mapped to `forced`.

## Evidence
C++: `doSpecialPower(..., cmdSource == CMD_FROM_SCRIPT)` + `if (!forced && !canUseSpecialPower) return;`
Rust: `sp_module.do_special_power(options);` with no store check.

## Player-visible effect
GUI/script button clicks can fire a special power that is still on cooldown or SharedNSync-locked.

## Split hint
Route every button arm through Object::do_special_power* with forced = (source == FromScript).
close_reason: command_buttons.rs: every SP button arm goes through do_special_power* with forced=(source==FromScript)

title: [W3DModelDraw] Supply CARRYING never reaches the drawable flags
description:
## C++
`W3DModelDraw::updateDrawModuleSupplyStatus` (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:3907-3918`) calls `getDrawable()->setModelConditionState(MODELCONDITION_CARRYING)` or `clearModelConditionState`. That dirties the drawable so **all** draw modules `replaceModelConditionState` with the bit included.

## Rust
Live `update_supply_status` (`trait_impl.rs:527-538`) only mutates this module's `last_model_conditions` and calls `replace_model_condition_state` locally, explicitly to avoid drawable-lock recursion. The Drawable/Object condition bitset is never set. The next drawable-level flag replace (damage, night, move) overwrites without CARRYING.

## Evidence
C++: `getDrawable()->setModelConditionState(MODELCONDITION_CARRYING);`
Rust: `conditions.insert(CARRYING); self.last_model_conditions = conditions; self.replace_model_condition_state(&conditions);` — no drawable write.

## Player-visible effect
Supply trucks/workers often fail to switch to the CARRYING model (full bags/crates) after gathering, or snap back to empty the next time any other condition bit changes.

## Split hint
Set/clear the drawable CARRYING bit outside the draw-module lock (deferred dirty flag) instead of a local last_model_conditions hack.
close_reason: Live update_supply_status now latches pending_carrying and merge_carrying_flag re-applies MODELCONDITION_CARRYING on every replace_model_condition_state / update_model_condition_state so later damage/night/move replaces cannot wipe the carrying model. Device update_draw_module_supply_status does the same via last_condition_flags. Files: w3d_model_draw_impl/carrying.rs + trait_impl.rs + impl_anim.rs; Device wthree_d_model_draw.rs.

title: [Drawable] Dead units keep heat-vision second pass
description:
## C++
`Drawable::draw` (`Drawable.cpp:2615-2622`) if not FRENZY: dead objects set `m_secondMaterialPassOpacity = 0` immediately; otherwise the heat-vision pass fades by `MATERIAL_PASS_OPACITY_FADE_SCALAR`.

## Rust
Live `BasicDrawable::update` (`basic_drawable_trait.rs:269-275`) only checks FRENZY then fades. There is no `isEffectivelyDead` zero-out. Dead stealthed/detected units keep a decaying (or frenzy-held) second pass. GameLogic `object/drawable.rs` draw path does have the dead zero; the mapped Drawable.cpp port does not.

## Evidence
C++: `if (getObject() && getObject()->isEffectivelyDead()) m_secondMaterialPassOpacity = 0.0f;`
Rust: `if !self.test_tint_status(TintStatus::FRENZY) { opacity *= 0.8; }` — no dead test.

## Player-visible effect
Corpses of detected/stealthed units keep a heat-vision / extra material glow instead of dropping it the frame they die.

## Split hint
Add the dead-object zero next to the FRENZY guard in `BasicDrawable::update` / `render`.
close_reason: BasicDrawable::update zeros second_material_pass_opacity when bound object is effectively dead (unless FRENZY).

title: [Object] setDisabledUntil drops audio, tint, rider, slaves, and carbomb
description:
## C++
`Object::setDisabledUntil` (`Object.cpp:2050-2187`) is the full disable-enter path: sniper-splatter / building-or-vehicle-disabled audio; `pauseAllSpecialPowers` (except HELD); drawable `TINT_STATUS_DISABLED` (except HELD/SCRIPT/UNMANNED); propagate to contain rider; `orderSlavesDisabledUntil` for SPAWNS_ARE_THE_WEAPONS; UNMANNED non-drone either scores+kills a carbomb or zeros XP and undoes AutoHeal; then `onDisabledEdge` on the first disable.

## Rust
`object_upgrade.rs:64-69` `set_disabled_until` only `set_disabled` + writes `disabled_till_frame`. `set_disabled` only flips the mask and calls `on_disabled_edge`. `clear_disabled` already has the C++ audio/rider/slave/tint path; the *enter* path does not.

## Evidence
C++: ~140 lines of audio, pause, tint, rider, slaves, carbomb/XP.
Rust: `self.set_disabled(disabled_type); self.disabled_till_frame[index] = frame;`

## Player-visible effect
EMP/hack/unmanned never play disable sounds or blue tint. Riders and stinger-site slaves keep fighting. Sniped carbombs do not explode; sniped veterans keep their rank.

## Split hint
Move the C++ enter-path next to the existing clear_disabled implementation in object_upgrade.rs.
close_reason: object/disabled.rs: set_disabled_until plays disable audio, pauses specials, tints, propagates to rider/slaves, handles unmanned carbomb/XP/AutoHeal, then on_disabled_edge

title: [W3DModelDraw] Runtime sub-object overrides wiped on state change
description:
## C++
`doHideShowSubObjs` (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:2323-2357`) applies the ConditionState HideShowVec, then if `m_subObjectVec` is non-empty calls `updateSubObjects()` so runtime overrides win. `showSubObject` pushes into `m_subObjectVec` and is used by UpgradeSubObject and the A10 strike (comment at :2351-2353). `setModelState` does **not** replace `m_subObjectVec` with the new state's list.

## Rust
Live `set_model_state` (`impl_anim.rs:62-66`) does `self.sub_object_vec = state.hide_show_list.clone()`, discarding any prior `show_sub_object` entries. The next fire/move/damage condition flip restores only the authored HideShowVec.

## Evidence
C++: after applying state vec, `if (!m_subObjectVec.empty()) updateSubObjects();`
Rust: `self.sub_object_vec = self.resolve_state(new_state_ref).map(|s| s.hide_show_list.clone())...`

## Player-visible effect
Upgrade-granted sub-objects (extra weapons, A10 payload pieces, show/hide upgrades) vanish the moment the unit changes model condition (moves, fires, takes damage).

## Split hint
Keep `m_subObjectVec` as the override list; apply HideShowVec then re-apply overrides like C++.
close_reason: set_model_state no longer replaces sub_object_vec with the state's HideShowVec. Authored hide_show_list is composed with runtime overrides (compose_hide_show_list) so UpgradeSubObject/A10 show_sub_object entries survive fire/move/damage. Device do_hide_show_sub_objs uses the same compose. Files: hide_show.rs, impl_anim.rs, Device wthree_d_model_draw.rs + runtime.rs.

title: [W3DModelDraw] ProjectileBoneFeedback ignores single hide-show name
description:
## C++
`doHideShowProjectileObjects` (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:3921-3950`): if `m_weaponProjectileHideShowName[slot]` is empty, hide `LaunchBone01..N` by remaining ammo; **else** hide/show that single authored name when `hideCount > 0`. Gated by `ProjectileBoneFeedbackEnabledSlots`.

## Rust
Live `update_projectile_clip_status` (`trait_impl.rs:504-523`) uses the override name as a **prefix** and always formats `NAME01..N` with per-index hide. The single-name override branch does not exist.

## Evidence
C++: `oneEntry.subObjName = m_weaponProjectileHideShowName[slot]; oneEntry.hide = (0 < hideCount);`
Rust: `let override_prefix = state.weapon_projectile_hide_show_bone[slot]; format!("{}{:02}", feedback_prefix, projectile_index+1)`

## Player-visible effect
Units authored with a single ProjectileHideShowName (one magazine/rocket pack mesh) never hide that mesh as ammo depletes; numbered PREFIX01 meshes are toggled instead and usually do not exist.

## Split hint
Keep the numbered launch-bone loop only when the hide-show name is empty.
close_reason: update_projectile_clip_status now matches C++ doHideShowProjectileObjects: numbered LaunchBone01..N only when hide-show name is empty; otherwise a single authored name is hidden when hideCount>0. Files: hide_show.rs, trait_impl.rs, Device runtime.rs.

title: [W3DModelDraw] setAnimationFrame permanently pins the clip
description:
## C++
`W3DModelDraw::setAnimationFrame` (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:3797-3806`) is a one-shot: `Set_Animation(animHandle, frame)` on the render object. The HLOD then continues from that frame under the current AnimMode. Used by DeployStyleAIUpdate to scrub deploy/undeploy poses.

## Rust
Live `set_animation_frame` (`impl_anim.rs:423-428`) stores `animation_override.manual_frame = Some(frame)`. `tick_animation_state` (`:216-218`) re-applies that frame every draw: `if let Some(frame) = self.animation_override.manual_frame { self.current_anim_frame = frame.clamp(...) }`. Nothing clears the override.

## Evidence
C++: one `Set_Animation(handle, frame)` call, no stored latch.
Rust: `manual_frame = Some(frame)` then every tick overwrites `current_anim_frame`.

## Player-visible effect
After a deploy/undeploy or any scripted frame scrub, the unit's animation freezes on that frame forever (walk/idle/fire clips never advance) until a full state rebuild happens to drop the override.

## Split hint
Apply the frame once then clear `manual_frame`, matching C++ one-shot Set_Animation.
close_reason: set_animation_frame is a one-shot apply_animation_frame_once; manual_frame is cleared and tick_animation_state no longer re-pins the frame. Device set_animation_frame writes current_anim_frame only. Files: anim_playback.rs, impl_anim.rs, Device wthree_d_model_draw.rs.

title: [Drawable] Stealth hide never deselects or hides draw modules
description:
## C++
`Drawable::setStealthLook` ends with `updateHiddenStatus()` (`Drawable.cpp:2604`). That function (`:4629-4641`) computes `hidden = m_hidden || m_hiddenByStealth`, calls `TheInGameUI->deselectDrawable(this)` when hidden, and `di->setHidden(hidden)` on every draw module (which hides the render object and its shadow).

## Rust
Mapped live `BasicDrawable::apply_stealth_look` (`basic_core.rs:819-876`) sets `hidden_by_stealth` / second-pass opacity and returns. There is no `update_hidden_status` in the GameClient drawable crate. GameClient `DrawModule` is never told to `set_hidden`. Selection is left as-is. (GameLogic `object/drawable.rs:3312` does call `update_hidden_status`; the mapped Drawable.cpp port does not.)

## Evidence
C++: `m_stealthLook = look; updateHiddenStatus();` → `TheInGameUI->deselectDrawable` + `di->setHidden`.
Rust apply_stealth_look: assigns fields, no deselect, no module `set_hidden`.

## Player-visible effect
Fully stealthed (invisible) units can remain selected with rings/flash, and W3DModelDraw may keep submitting the mesh/shadow because the module `hidden` flag never flips from the GameClient stealth look path.

## Split hint
Port `update_hidden_status` next to `apply_stealth_look` / `set_drawable_hidden` and call it from both.
close_reason: update_hidden_status deselects and DrawModule::set_hidden from apply_stealth_look and set_drawable_hidden.

title: [Object] initObject skips upgrades, battle plans, mines, and weapon set
description:
## C++
`Object::initObject` (`Object.cpp:495-575`) after modules exist: `sendObjectCreated`, `updateUpgradeModules`, apply script difficulty bonus, apply battle-plan bonuses, fill `m_specialPowerBits` from every SpecialPower module, notify ScriptEngine of creation (non-projectile/inert), `m_weaponSet.updateWeaponSet(this)`, and `recordMine()` for MINE/BOOBY_TRAP/DEMOTRAP.

## Rust
`object_lifecycle.rs:209-232` `init_object` only runs CREATE `on_create` and maybe allocates a FiringTracker. No sendObjectCreated, upgrades, difficulty, battle plans, special-power bits, script notify, weapon-set update, or academy mine record.

## Evidence
C++: ~80-line init including `updateUpgradeModules()`, `applyBattlePlanBonusesForObject`, `SET_SPECIALPOWERMASK`, `updateWeaponSet`, `recordMine`.
Rust: create-module loop + optional FiringTracker then `Ok(())`.

## Player-visible effect
New units spawn without veterancy/player upgrades, without Strategy Center battle-plan bonuses, with empty special-power bits (hasSpecialPower false), wrong starting weapon set, and mines do not count in the academy. Scripts that watch unit counts miss the spawn.

## Split hint
Keep init_object as the single post-ctor hook; do not split the C++ sequence.
close_reason: object/init.rs: init_object runs sendObjectCreated, upgrades, difficulty, battle plans, special-power bits, script notify, weapon-set update, recordMine

title: [Object] Disabled edge does not cancel an active dozer task
description:
## C++
`Object::onDisabledEdge` (`Object.cpp:3796-3802`) if becoming disabled and the object has `DozerAIInterface` with a current task, `dozerAI->cancelTask(...)` so another dozer can take the build/repair.

## Rust
`object_upgrade.rs:318-397` `on_disabled_edge` notifies behaviors, radar upgrade, and power. No DozerAI lookup or cancelTask.

## Evidence
C++: `if (becomingDisabled && dozerAI) { if (getCurrentTask() != DOZER_TASK_INVALID) cancelTask(...); }`
Rust on_disabled_edge: no dozer / cancel_task.

## Player-visible effect
An EMP'd or script-disabled dozer keeps its build/repair reservation; the structure stays claimed and no other dozer can finish it.

## Split hint
Cancel via AI dozer interface at the start of on_disabled_edge when becoming_disabled.
close_reason: object/disabled.rs: on_disabled_edge cancels current DozerAI task when becoming disabled

title: [Object] doSpecialPowerAtLocation drops the facing angle
description:
## C++
`Object::doSpecialPowerAtLocation` (`Object.cpp:5354-5368`) forwards `loc` and `angle` to `mod->doSpecialPowerAtLocation(loc, angle, commandOptions)` so aimed powers (particle cannon, etc.) face the click.

## Rust
`object_special_power.rs:1064-1081` `do_special_power_at_location` has no angle argument and always passes `INVALID_ANGLE` into the module.

## Evidence
C++: `mod->doSpecialPowerAtLocation(loc, angle, commandOptions);`
Rust: `sp_module.do_special_power_at_location(location, INVALID_ANGLE, command_options);`

## Player-visible effect
Location special powers spawn facing default/invalid heading instead of the ordered angle.

## Split hint
Add the angle parameter on Object and thread it from do_command_button_at_position.
close_reason: do_special_power_at_location now takes angle and forwards it to the module; button/group pass INVALID_ANGLE like C++

title: HistoricBonusWeapon Nth qualifying hit must dispatch via createAndFireTempWeapon on canonical dealDamageInternal
close_reason: Canonical deal_damage_internal applies C++ Weapon.cpp:1214-1251 HistoricBonusWeapon: Nth close hit in time/radius calls createAndFireTempWeapon and clears historicDamage. Weak, stored name, store lookup, and Common INI properties all resolve the bonus weapon so INI-loaded Inferno/napalm templates dispatch.

title: [Object] getShroudedStatus ignores ALWAYS_VISIBLE and partition data
description:
## C++
`Object::getShroudedStatus` (`Object.cpp:1778-1788`): `KINDOF_ALWAYS_VISIBLE` → `OBJECTSHROUD_CLEAR`; else `m_partitionData->getShroudedStatus(playerIndex)`; if no partition data (garrisoned infantry, etc.) return CLEAR.

## Rust
`object_vision.rs:538-572` queries `ShroudManager::can_see_object` + `visibility_alpha` for PartialClear + `ExploredTerritoryManager`. No AlwaysVisible short-circuit. No PartitionData path. Lock failure defaults to visible (`unwrap_or(true)`), and missing partition does not force CLEAR.

## Evidence
C++: `if (isKindOf(KINDOF_ALWAYS_VISIBLE)) return OBJECTSHROUD_CLEAR;` / `if (m_partitionData) return m_partitionData->getShroudedStatus;` / else CLEAR.
Rust: shroud_manager + explored_territory + alpha; no AlwaysVisible / partition-data branch.

## Player-visible effect
Always-visible objects (beacons, some script objects) can be fogged. Garrisoned soldiers can stay shrouded instead of CLEAR, hiding FX/selection that C++ always shows.

## Split hint
Keep Object getter as AlwaysVisible + PartitionData + CLEAR fallback; leave ShroudManager to PartitionData.
close_reason: object/vision.rs: get_shrouded_status is AlwaysVisible->CLEAR, else PartitionData, else CLEAR

title: [Object] Defect missing voice, timer tick, and owned-mine transfer
description:
## C++
`Object::defect` (`Object.cpp:6111-6219`) after `setTeam`: plays `getVoiceDefect()`, flashes drawable, plays `m_defectorTimerTickSound`, kick-out-on-capture, `defectAllParkedUnits`, then walks the world and `setTeam` on every `KINDOF_MINE` whose producer is this object.

## Rust
`object_update.rs:729-852` does team switch, idle, flash, kick-out, parked-unit defect. No VoiceDefect audio, no defector-timer tick, no mine walk. Also early-returns if `dual_world_registry_unavailable()` (`730-732`), which would skip the whole defect when the registry is empty.

## Evidence
C++: `TheAudio->addAudioEvent(&voiceDefect);` + `m_defectorTimerTickSound` + mine producer loop.
Rust: no `VoiceDefect` / `defector_timer` / `KindOf::Mine` in `defect()`.

## Player-visible effect
Hacked/defected units are silent (no voice, no timer tick). Mines laid by a captured structure stay on the old team and still kill the new owner.

## Split hint
Audio events next to flash_as_selected; mine walk after parked-unit defect.
close_reason: capture.rs: VoiceDefect + defector timer tick + owned-mine setTeam; removed empty-registry early-out

title: [Object] Capture does not award score or sell AI faction buildings
description:
## C++
`Object::onCapture` (`Object.cpp:4509-4542`): `newOwner->getScoreKeeper()->addObjectCaptured(this)`; if `oldOwner!=newOwner && newOwner->isSkirmishAIPlayer() && isFactionStructure()` then `TheBuildAssistant->sellObject(this)`.

## Rust
`object_update.rs:354-358` only logs `"awarding points"` inside a read lock (no score-keeper call). `object_update.rs:431-434` skirmish-AI sell is commented out.

ScoreKeeper `add_object_captured_obj` exists in Common but Object never calls it.

## Evidence
C++: `addObjectCaptured(this)` + `TheBuildAssistant->sellObject(this)`
Rust: `log::debug!("captured - awarding points")` and `// TheBuildAssistant->sellObject(this);`

## Player-visible effect
Captured buildings do not count on the score screen. Skirmish AI that steals a war factory / barracks keeps it instead of selling, so the AI hoards unusable faction buildings.

## Split hint
Score call + BuildAssistant sell in on_capture after ownership has already switched.
close_reason: capture.rs: add_object_captured_obj + BuildAssistant sell for skirmish AI faction structures

title: [Object] Team switch skips becomingTeamMember power and InGameUI timers
description:
## C++
`Object::setOrRestoreTeam` (`Object.cpp:836-902`) on leave: `removeFrom_TeamMemberList` + `oldPlayer->becomingTeamMember(this, false)`. On join: prepend + `newPlayer->becomingTeamMember(this, true)` (which calls `friend_adjustPowerForPlayer`). Then `TheInGameUI->objectChangedTeam(this, oldIndex, newIndex)` so superweapon timers move.

## Rust
`object_lifecycle.rs:638-699` add/remove owned object and battle-plan bonuses, team member list, on_capture, radar refresh, AI attitude, drawable team visuals. No `becomingTeamMember` (symbol does not exist in Rust). No `TheInGameUI::object_changed_team` (the client method exists at `ingame_ui/impl_update.rs:259` but Object never calls it). `adjust_power_for_player` exists on Object but is not invoked from the team switch.

## Evidence
C++: `getControllingPlayer()->becomingTeamMember(this, false/true);` + `TheInGameUI->objectChangedTeam(...)`
Rust set_or_restore_team: no becoming_team_member / object_changed_team / adjust_power_for_player.

## Player-visible effect
Capturing or defecting a power plant does not move its energy onto the new player (brownout stays wrong). Superweapon timers stay on the old player's UI.

## Split hint
Call adjust_power_for_player from set_or_restore_team and forward objectChangedTeam to InGameUI.
close_reason: object_lifecycle.rs: leave-power before team switch, join-power after; TheInGameUI::object_changed_team moves superweapon timers

title: [Object] onDie never detonates an attached booby trap
description:
## C++
`Object::onDie` (`Object.cpp:4551`) first line is `checkAndDetonateBoobyTrap(NULL)` so a booby-trapped building/unit explodes when it dies (planting, capture, or death).

## Rust
`object_lifecycle.rs:887-1008` `on_die` never calls `check_and_detonate_booby_trap`. The helper exists on `object_status.rs` but death does not use it.

## Evidence
C++: `checkAndDetonateBoobyTrap(NULL);// Already dying...`
Rust on_die: die modules, radar event, spawner, partition, team, EVA, idle worker, rebuild-hole comment — no booby-trap call.

## Player-visible effect
Demo-trap / booby-trap upgrades do not explode when the host dies, so the trap never punishes the killer.

## Split hint
Call check_and_detonate_booby_trap(None) at the top of on_die.
close_reason: die_hooks.rs: on_die calls check_and_detonate_booby_trap(None) first, matching Object.cpp:4551

title: [Object] onDie GLA rebuild-hole transfer is a comment stub
description:
## C++
`Object::onDie` (`Object.cpp:4616-4645`) when `OBJECT_STATUS_RECONSTRUCTING`: find producer hole, `RebuildHoleBehaviorInterface::startRebuildProcess(template, id)`, then walk every object and `ai->transferAttack(deadID, holeID)` so attackers retarget the hole.

## Rust
`object_lifecycle.rs:1001-1005` only logs `"handling rebuild hole logic"` with a comment. No hole lookup, no startRebuildProcess, no transferAttack.

Closed hq-h71k / hq-98sg cover hole worker leak and INI defaults, not this Object::onDie transfer.

## Evidence
C++: `rhbi->startRebuildProcess(getTemplate(), getID());` + `ai->transferAttack(getID(), hole->getID());`
Rust: `// This transfers attackers from destroyed building to the hole` and nothing else.

## Player-visible effect
A GLA building lost mid-rebuild does not restart the hole and attackers keep shooting empty space instead of the hole.

## Split hint
Keep the hole-behavior call on Object::on_die; transferAttack can live next to AI update.
close_reason: die_hooks.rs: reconstruct hole start_rebuild_process + transferAttack walk

title: [Object] Fire-weapon command button never locks the slot
description:
## C++
`doCommandButton` FIRE_WEAPON (`Object.cpp:5429-5443`) `setWeaponLock(slot, LOCKED_TEMPORARILY)` then `aiAttackPosition(NULL, maxShots)`.
`doCommandButtonAtObject` FIRE_WEAPON (`5557-5583`) same lock, then attack object or object position.

## Rust
`object_special_power.rs:260-284` and `:413-454` issue AttackPosition/AttackObject with max shots but never call `set_weapon_lock`. The lock helper exists (`object_combat.rs:1098`).

## Evidence
C++: `setWeaponLock(commandButton->getWeaponSlot(), LOCKED_TEMPORARILY);`
Rust fire-weapon arms have no `set_weapon_lock`.

## Player-visible effect
Scripted/command-bar fire-weapon buttons (demo charges, one-shot special guns) fire with the current weapon instead of the button's slot, so the wrong gun shoots or the unit refuses.

## Split hint
Lock temporarily in both no-target and at-object FireWeapon arms before the AI attack.
close_reason: object/command_weapon.rs: FireWeapon no-target, at-object, and at-position arms lock the button slot LockedTemporarily before the AI attack

title: [Object] Switch-weapon command button is a no-op
description:
## C++
`Object::doCommandButton` `GUI_COMMAND_SWITCH_WEAPON` (`Object.cpp:5421-5427`) `setWeaponLock(weaponSlot, LOCKED_PERMANENTLY)` so the unit stays on that gun until switched again.

## Rust
`object_special_power.rs:257-259` `CommandType::SwitchWeapons => { return Ok(()); }`

## Evidence
C++: `setWeaponLock(weaponSlot, LOCKED_PERMANENTLY); return;`
Rust: empty arm that returns Ok.

## Player-visible effect
Scripted or command-bar weapon swaps (dual-gun vehicles, hero weapon modes) never change the active slot.

## Split hint
Call existing `Object::set_weapon_lock` with Permanent from the SwitchWeapons arm.
close_reason: object/command_weapon.rs: SwitchWeapons calls set_weapon_lock(slot, LockedPermanently)

title: [Object] Map-boundary helpers skip radar, partition, and pathfinder
description:
## C++
`Object::friend_prepareForMapBoundaryAdjust` (`Object.cpp:2777-2794`) removes the object from radar and partition, then resets all SightingInfo.
`friend_notifyOfNewMapBoundary` (`2799-2813`) `registerObject`, `TheRadar->addObject`, `pathfinder()->addObjectToPathfindMap`, `handlePartitionCellMaintenance`, then sets/clears OFF_MAP from `TheTerrainLogic->getExtent()`.

## Rust
`object_vision.rs:467-483` prepare only `reset()`s the five SightingInfo blobs. Notify only calls `handle_partition_cell_maintenance` and toggles OFF_MAP via `is_off_map()` (pathfind extent, not playable map extent). No radar remove/add, no partition unregister/register, no pathfinder add.

Closed hq-l8ci made TerrainLogic call these hooks; the Object side is still incomplete.

## Evidence
C++ prepare: `TheRadar->removeObject(this); ThePartitionManager->unRegisterObject(this);`
Rust prepare: five `reset()` calls only.

## Player-visible effect
SWITCH_BORDER / multi-boundary maps leave objects off radar, out of partition queries, and unpathable after the rebuild, even though terrain now notifies them.

## Split hint
object_vision map-boundary pair; keep SightingInfo reset plus the three subsystem rebinds.
close_reason: object/vision.rs: prepare removes radar+partition then resets SightingInfo; notify re-registers partition, radar, pathfinder, playable-extent OFF_MAP, then handle_partition_cell_maintenance

title: [Object] Construction vision is not shrunk to the footprint
description:
## C++
`Object::getShroudClearingRange` (`Object.cpp:5128-5156`) returns `getGeometryInfo().getBoundingCircleRadius()` while `OBJECT_STATUS_UNDER_CONSTRUCTION` so a building only sees itself until complete. Completing construction flips the bit and `setStatus` dirties partition / Rust already calls `handle_partition_cell_maintenance`.

## Rust
`object_vision.rs:11-13` `get_shroud_clearing_range` returns the stored field with no under-construction override. `look()` uses that getter for `do_shroud_reveal`.

## Evidence
C++: `if (getStatusBits().test(OBJECT_STATUS_UNDER_CONSTRUCTION)) shroudClearingRange = getGeometryInfo().getBoundingCircleRadius();`
Rust: `self.shroud_clearing_range`

## Player-visible effect
Foundations and half-built structures reveal the full finished sight radius, lighting fog for the enemy before the building exists.

## Split hint
Override only in the getter used by look/value/threat.
close_reason: object/vision.rs: get_shroud_clearing_range returns bounding-circle radius while UnderConstruction

title: [Object] setShroudClearingRange never refreshes partition look
description:
## C++
`Object::setShroudClearingRange` (`Object.cpp:5159-5191`) writes the field and, unless the object is still at origin (0,0,0), calls `handlePartitionCellMaintenance()` so battle-plan / radar-upgrade range changes re-look immediately.

## Rust
`object_vision.rs:15-17` `set_shroud_clearing_range` only clamps and stores.

## Evidence
C++: `if (pos->x || pos->y || pos->z) handlePartitionCellMaintenance();`
Rust: `self.shroud_clearing_range = range.max(0.0);`

## Player-visible effect
Search-and-destroy battle plan, radar upgrades, and scripted vision-range changes do not expand or shrink fog until the unit happens to move.

## Split hint
Call handle_partition_cell_maintenance from the setter with the C++ origin skip.
close_reason: object/vision.rs: set_shroud_clearing_range calls handle_partition_cell_maintenance unless the object is still at origin

title: [Physics] Empty OBJECT_REGISTRY makes PhysicsBehavior sleep forever
description:
## C++
`PhysicsBehavior::update` always runs in PHASE_PHYSICS (after AI). `calcSleepTime` (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:903-921) sleeps FOREVER only when vel/accel are zero, no YPR, not motive, on ground, no overlap, and UPDATE_EVER_RUN. applyForce wakes the module.

## Rust
`update_simple` (`physics_update.rs:706-710`): if `OBJECT_REGISTRY.is_empty()` return Forever. `apply_force` / `apply_random_rotation` / `set_stunned` similarly no-op. Host-only play (registry empty) never integrates gravity, friction, bounce, or fall damage. Closed hq-vqg5 was the host scheduler; this gate remains on the live PhysicsBehavior module.

## Evidence
```
fn dual_world_registry_unavailable() -> bool {
    crate::object::registry::OBJECT_REGISTRY.is_empty()
}
if dual_world_registry_unavailable() {
    return UpdateSleepTime::Forever;
}
```

## Player-visible effect
On the host-only path, rigid-body physics never ticks: no gravity, no bounce, no fall splat, no motive friction. Combined with kinematic locomotor (hq-142b) units skate without C++ physics.

## Split hint
Delete the Wave-316 empty-registry gate; sleep only via calc_sleep_time.
close_reason: Removed Wave-316 OBJECT_REGISTRY.is_empty() gates from update_simple, apply_force, apply_random_rotation, set_stunned, object_arc, on_object_created. Sleep only via calc_sleep_time.

title: [Object] Single-use command flag is never set or read
description:
## C++
`Object.h:358-359` `markSingleUseCommandUsed()` sets `m_singleUseCommandUsed`; `hasSingleUseCommandBeenUsed()` returns that field. ControlBar (`ControlBarCommandProcessing.cpp:178`) marks the flag after the first click so the button stays disabled.

## Rust
`object_status.rs:515-518` `has_single_use_command_been_used()` tests `ObjectStatusTypes::MissileKillingSelf`. There is no `mark_single_use_command_used`. The real field `single_use_command_used` exists and is xfer'd (`object_xfer.rs:884`) but is never written or read at runtime. GameClient `control_bar/commands.rs:602` uses the broken getter.

## Evidence
C++: `void markSingleUseCommandUsed() { m_singleUseCommandUsed = true; }` / `return m_singleUseCommandUsed;`
Rust: `self.status.test_status(ObjectStatusTypes::MissileKillingSelf)` and grep for `mark_single_use` is empty.

## Player-visible effect
One-shot command-bar abilities (e.g. some hero/superweapon buttons) can be clicked repeatedly; the C++ lock-after-first-use never happens.

## Split hint
Keep the flag on Object; wire setter from ControlBar and read the field, not MissileKillingSelf.
close_reason: object/status_cmds.rs: has_single_use_command_been_used reads single_use_command_used; added mark_single_use_command_used; ControlBar dispatch writes the flag after SINGLE_USE_COMMAND clicks

title: [Object] setGeometryInfo skips partition re-register and drawable react
description:
## C++
`Object::setGeometryInfo` (`Object.cpp:746-760`) assigns geometry, then `ThePartitionManager->unRegisterObject` + `registerObject` so collision size updates, and `m_drawable->reactToGeometryChange()`.
`setGeometryInfoZ` (`764-770`) calls `m_geometryInfo.setMaxHeightAbovePosition(newZ)` and still notifies the drawable (no partition churn).

## Rust
`object_status.rs:367-373` `set_geometry_info` is a field write. `set_geometry_info_z` writes `geometry_info.position.z` (wrong field) and does not notify the drawable.

## Evidence
C++: unregister/register + `reactToGeometryChange()`; Z path uses `setMaxHeightAbovePosition`.
Rust: `self.geometry_info = geom;` / `self.geometry_info.position.z = new_z;`

## Player-visible effect
Expanding/shrinking objects (gates, inflatable decoys, construction height) keep the old collision/selection footprint. Height-only changes move the object in Z instead of stretching the volume, so health boxes and targeting miss.

## Split hint
object_status geometry setters + partition/drawable hooks.
close_reason: object/status_cmds.rs: set_geometry_info unregisters/registers partition and react_to_geometry_change; set_geometry_info_z uses set_max_height_above_position

title: [Object] setSelectable does not notify the drawable
description:
## C++
`Object::setSelectable` (`Object.cpp:2991-2997`) sets `m_isSelectable` and `m_drawable->setSelectable(selectable)` so the client selection outline/cursor matches logic.

## Rust
`object_status.rs:456-458` only writes `self.is_selectable`.

## Evidence
C++: `if (m_drawable) { m_drawable->setSelectable(selectable); }`
Rust: `self.is_selectable = selectable;`

## Player-visible effect
Script/map `objectSelectable` and runtime unselectability change the logic flag but the drawable still accepts clicks/hover as before.

## Split hint
Forward to Drawable::set_selectable next to the field write.
close_reason: object/status_cmds.rs: set_selectable writes the field and forwards Drawable::set_selectable

title: [Object] Script-unsellable reads CAPTURED private bit
description:
## C++
`ObjectScriptStatusBits.h:16` `OBJECT_STATUS_SCRIPT_UNSELLABLE = 0x04` is a *script* status bit. ControlBar hides Sell when `testScriptStatusBit(OBJECT_STATUS_SCRIPT_UNSELLABLE)`. `onCapture` clears that script bit so stolen buildings can be sold.

## Rust
`object_status.rs:521-523` `is_script_unsellable()` tests `self.private_status & 0x04`. Private bit 0x04 is `ObjectPrivateStatusBits::Captured` (`mod.rs:2370`), not script Unsellable. The correct enum `ObjectScriptStatusBit::Unsellable = 0x04` exists and is used by `on_capture` / map properties, but the query looks at the wrong byte.

## Evidence
C++: `testScriptStatusBit(OBJECT_STATUS_SCRIPT_UNSELLABLE)`
Rust: `// C++ OBJECT_STATUS_SCRIPT_UNSELLABLE is a script status bit` then `(self.private_status & 0x04) != 0`

## Player-visible effect
Every captured object reports unsellable (Captured bit). Script/cinematic Unsellable buildings still show Sell. Capture's `clear_script_status(Unsellable)` cannot unstick the sell button.

## Split hint
Query `script_status` / `ObjectScriptStatusBit::Unsellable` only.
close_reason: object/status_cmds.rs: is_script_unsellable queries ObjectScriptStatusBit::Unsellable on script_status, not Captured private bit

title: [W3DModelDraw] Hide/enable never toggles unit shadows
description:
## C++
`W3DModelDraw::setHidden` (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:1799-1818`) calls `m_shadow->enableShadowRender(!hidden)` and `m_terrainDecal->enableShadowRender(!hidden)`, then caps tracks and stops particles. `setShadowsEnabled` (:1856-1860) forwards `enableShadowRender(enable)` to the live shadow object. `allocateShadows` (:1829-1852) / `setModelState` (:3042-3059) create the shadow via `TheW3DShadowManager->addShadow` from the ThingTemplate ShadowType/texture/size. `Drawable::draw` turns shadows off for `STEALTHLOOK_VISIBLE_DETECTED`.

## Rust
Live `w3d_model_draw_impl/trait_impl.rs:101-148`: `set_shadows_enabled` only stores `self.shadow_enabled`. `release_shadows` / `allocate_shadows` are comment stubs (\"When shadow system is implemented\"). `set_hidden` stops particles and caps tracks but never toggles a shadow or terrain-decal render flag. `set_model_state` never creates a template shadow. hq-fmsy closed Display-level blob flush under visible drawables — that path does not read this module flag, so hide/detected-stealth/Options cannot turn those blobs off.

## Evidence
C++: `if (m_shadow) m_shadow->enableShadowRender(!hidden);` / `TheW3DShadowManager->addShadow(...)`.
Rust: `self.shadow_enabled = enable;` and allocate/release bodies are comments only.

## Player-visible effect
Hidden or fully stealthed units still leave contact blobs. Detected heat-vision units keep shadows (C++ turns them off). Options shadow on/off does not allocate/release per-model shadows or authored ShadowTexture sizes.

## Split hint
Wire `shadow_enabled` + hide into the Display blob/decal collector; implement allocate/release against the projected-shadow manager using template ShadowType.
close_reason: set_hidden / set_shadows_enabled now toggle projected-shadow render via TerrainDecalClient.set_shadow_enabled and keep Options shadow_enabled independent of hide. allocate_shadows / release_shadows create/release a template ShadowTexture blob. Device allocate/release uses TheW3DShadowManager add_shadow/remove_shadow and set_hidden enables handle.is_enabled. Files: shadow_bind.rs, trait_impl.rs, Device runtime.rs + wthree_d_model_draw.rs.

title: [WW3D] GPU skin palette truncates to 64 bones; C++ deforms every pivot
description:
## C++
`MeshGeometryClass::get_deformed_vertices` (`meshgeometry.cpp:1965-2007`) transforms each vertex by `htree->Get_Transform(bonelink[vi])` with no bone-count cap. `HTreeClass` allocates `Pivot[NumPivots]` from the W3D header (`htree.cpp:159-162`). Skin draw (`mesh.cpp:746-771` / `dx8renderer.cpp:1811-1816`) uses those CPU-deformed verts with a world-identity matrix.

## Rust
Live GPU upload `pad_bone_palette` (`ww3d-renderer-3d/.../wgpu_material_binds.rs:59-65`) copies `bones.len().min(MAX_BONES)` into `[Mat4; 64]`. Shader `BoneUniform { bones: array<mat4x4<f32>, 64> }` (`skinned.wgsl:27-29`). CPU fallback `compute_deformed_vertices_from_palette` (`mesh.rs:232-237`) uses `palette.get(palette_index).unwrap_or(Mat4::IDENTITY)` — any `bone_idx >= palette.len()` (including idx>=64 after truncate) skins against identity. Comments still mention the identity 64-mat pad (`pipeline_collect.rs:1858-1859`).

## Evidence
`const MAX_BONES: usize = 64; fn pad_bone_palette(bones: &[Mat4]) -> [Mat4; MAX_BONES] { let n = bones.len().min(MAX_BONES); … }`. C++ loop is `for (vi = 0; vi < vertex_count; vi++) { tm = htree->Get_Transform(bonelink[vi]); }`.

## Player-visible effect
Skinned meshes whose HTree has more than 64 pivots (or any vertex whose `W3dVertInfStruct.bone_idx` is >= 64) leave those verts at bind/identity: floating shards, collapsed limbs, or unposed extras on high-bone infantry/hero/vehicle skins.

## Split hint
`bone_palette.rs` (dynamic storage buffer, no 64 cap), `skin_deform.rs` (single-bone HTree path matching C++).
close_reason: Dynamic storage bone palette (bone_palette.rs + skinned.wgsl/projected_shroud_skinned.wgsl); CPU single-bone HTree deform in skin_deform.rs. No 64-cap pad.

title: [WW3D] CAMERA_ALIGNED / CAMERA_ORIENTED meshes never billboard
description:
## C++
`MeshGeometryClass` load (`meshgeometry.cpp:1558-1562` / `meshmdlio.cpp:231-235`) sets `ALIGNED` / `ORIENTED` from `W3D_MESH_FLAG_GEOMETRY_TYPE_CAMERA_ALIGNED` (0x00010000) and `CAMERA_ORIENTED` (0x00060000). `DX8MeshRenderer` (`dx8renderer.cpp:1787-1809`) rebuilds the world matrix each draw: ALIGNED looks along camera Z; ORIENTED looks at camera position. `MeshClass::Cast_Ray` (`mesh.cpp:1143-1151`) applies the same look-at so picks hit the billboarded pose. Bounds become a sphere-cube when either flag is set (`mesh.cpp:1438-1441`).

## Rust
Main defines `W3D_MESH_FLAG_GEOMETRY_TYPE_CAMERA_ALIGNED` (`w3d_mesh.rs:18`) but the only geometry-type consumer is SKIN (`w3d_model.rs:445-446`). Grep of `Main/src/graphics` for CAMERA_ALIGNED / ALIGNED / ORIENTED apply is empty. Live collect/forward submit the authored rigid transform. ww3d-renderer-3d `mesh_system_impl` never sets an ALIGNED flag.

## Evidence
C++: `if (mesh->Peek_Model()->Get_Flag(MeshModelClass::ALIGNED)) { tmp_world.Obj_Look_At(mesh_position, mesh_position + camera_z_vector, 0); }`. Rust live path only tests `attrs & GEOMETRY_TYPE_MASK == GEOMETRY_TYPE_SKIN`.

## Player-visible effect
Camera-facing W3D meshes (sprite cards, some FX/decals, oriented props) stay in model space: they appear edge-on or locked to the unit facing instead of billboarding toward the tactical camera, and ray picks miss the on-screen quad.

## Split hint
`mesh_camera_align.rs` (flag from header), `collect_billboard_xform.rs`, `cast_ray_aligned.rs`.
close_reason: CAMERA_ALIGNED/ORIENTED flags from W3D header (mesh_camera_align.rs); DX8 look-at world rebuild (collect_billboard_xform.rs); Cast_Ray billboard (cast_ray_aligned.rs); sphere-cube bounds.

title: [WW3D] Live Main W3D loader still drops model-attached ParticleEmitter protos
description:
## C++
`W3DDisplay.cpp:700` registers `_ParticleEmitterLoader` on the live asset manager. `ParticleEmitterLoaderClass::Load_W3D` reads `W3D_CHUNK_EMITTER` (0x500) into a prototype; `Create()` builds a `ParticleEmitterClass`. `HLodClass(HLodDef)` (`hlod.cpp:990-1007`) `Create_Render_Obj`s each LOD child and aggregate by name, attaching exhaust/fire/sparks/bone-linked smoke.

## Rust
Library `DefaultLoaders` now pushes `ParticleEmitterLoader` (`prototype_loader.rs:1425`) — that closed `hq-e99h`. Live Main `w3d_loader.rs:612-735` has no `W3D_CHUNK_EMITTER` arm (unknown skip / recursive container walk only). Live `W3dRenderObjectPrototypeKind` (`manager.rs:108-114`) cannot represent an emitter, so HLOD children named after an emitter never instantiate.

## Evidence
Main chunk match ends at HLOD then `_ => Unknown`. Registry `register_source_model` only registers meshes/hlods/hmodels.

## Player-visible effect
Vehicles and buildings lose W3D-authored particle FX (exhaust, chimney smoke, muzzle sparks, fire). Only INI ParticleSys (if any) remains.

## Split hint
`w3d_emitter_loader.rs`, `w3d_proto_registry.rs` (Emitter kind), `hlod_emitter_child.rs`.
close_reason: Main w3d_loader parses W3D_CHUNK_EMITTER (w3d_emitter_loader.rs); registry Emitter kind; HLOD child lookup (hlod_emitter_child.rs).

title: [WW3D] Live Main proto registry still omits Collection/Box/Ring/Sphere/Aggregate/Null
description:
## C++
`WW3DAssetManager` ctor (`assetmgr.cpp:153-162`) registers Collection, Box, DistLOD, Aggregate, Null, Ring, Sphere (plus Mesh/HModel/HLod). `HLodClass` (`hlod.cpp:990`) `Create_Render_Obj`s every named LOD child; hidden `CLASSID_OBBOX` children named BOUNDINGBOX drive animated bounds (`hlod.cpp:3280-3310`) and are skipped at render (`hlod.cpp:2029-2030`).

## Rust
Library `DefaultLoaders` now installs those loaders — that closed `hq-6dzk`. Live Main parser (`w3d_loader.rs:612-735`) never matches `W3D_CHUNK_COLLECTION` / `BOX` / `RING` / `SPHERE` / `AGGREGATE` / `NULL_OBJECT` / `LODMODEL` as prototypes (LODMODEL only recurses for nested meshes). Live registry (`manager.rs:108-114,191-225`) only Mesh/Hlod/Hmodel. No BOUNDINGBOX/OBBOX handling exists in Main.

## Evidence
`W3dRenderObjectPrototypeKind { Mesh, Hlod, Hmodel }`. Unknown chunks: `debug!(Unknown W3D chunk type: 0x{:08X})`. Grep of Main for BOUNDINGBOX/CLASSID_OBBOX is empty.

## Player-visible effect
Grouped collection props, ring/sphere effect meshes (force fields, ion/nuke rings), collision-box vis when enabled, DistLOD swaps, aggregate composites, and animated OBBOX bounds never instantiate from W3D. Distinct from HLOD mesh children (Main does parse those).

## Split hint
`w3d_primitive_protos.rs` (box/ring/sphere/null), `w3d_collection_aggregate.rs`, `hlod_bounding_box.rs`.
close_reason: Main loader parses Collection/Box/Ring/Sphere/Aggregate/Null/DistLOD; registry kinds; Collection/Aggregate/DistLOD Create_Render_Obj recurse.

title: [WW3D] Live Main W3D loader still drops Dazzle/lens-flare proto chunks
description:
## C++
`WW3DAssetManager` ctor (`GeneralsMD/Code/Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WW3D2/assetmgr.cpp:160`) registers `_DazzleLoader`. `HLodClass` from `HLodDef` (`hlod.cpp:990`) does `Create_Render_Obj(def.Lod[ilod].ModelName[imodel])` for every named child, including `W3D_CHUNK_DAZZLE` (0x900) headlights/sun glints/halos (`dazzle.cpp` / `w3d_file.h`).

## Rust
Library `DefaultLoaders` now installs `DazzleLoader` (`ww3d-assets/src/prototype_loader.rs:1422`) — that closed `hq-radq`. The *live* game path is Main `W3DLoader` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/assets/models/w3d_loader.rs:612-735`): match arms are Mesh/Hierarchy/Materials3/Textures/Animation/CompressedAnim/HModel/LODMODEL/HLOD only; 0x900 falls through `_ => Unknown W3D chunk`. Live registry `W3dRenderObjectPrototypeKind` (`Main/src/assets/manager.rs:108-114`) is only Mesh/Hlod/Hmodel, so even a library-parsed dazzle cannot be `Create_Render_Obj`'d as an HLOD child.

## Evidence
Main: `match chunk_type { W3D_CHUNK_MESH | … | W3D_CHUNK_HLOD => … _ => debug!(Unknown W3D chunk type) }`. Registry register loop only enumerates `model.meshes` / `model.hlods` / `model.hmodels`.

## Player-visible effect
No W3D dazzle/halo/lens-flare objects: missing headlights, sun flares, and glare on bright model lights.

## Split hint
`w3d_dazzle_loader.rs`, `w3d_proto_registry.rs` (add Dazzle kind), `hlod_dazzle_child.rs`.
close_reason: Main loader parses W3D_CHUNK_DAZZLE (w3d_dazzle_loader.rs); registry Dazzle kind; HLOD child lookup (hlod_dazzle_child.rs).

title: [Pathfind] Bridge layers are an AABB, not a classified PathfindLayer cell grid
description:
## C++
`PathfindLayer` (`AIPathfind.h:363-412`) is a sub-rectangle of PathfindCells. `classifyLayerMapCell` (`AIPathfind.cpp:3647-3724`) counts how many of the 4 cell corners sit on the bridge polygon:
- 4 → CELL_CLEAR (deck)
- 1–3 → CELL_BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE (edge) unless on end/entry (CLEAR + connectLayer=GROUND)
- 0 → CELL_IMPASSABLE (getCell returns NULL)
`setDestroyed` reclassifies that layer matrix. Ground under a low deck is marked BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE only when `groundHeight + LAYER_Z_CLOSE_ENOUGH_F > bridgeHeight`.

## Rust
`pathfind_complete` `BridgeLayer` is bounds + entry cells, no per-cell matrix. `get_cell_type_at_cell` (`line_passable.rs:623-632`): if coord is inside AABB → Clear, or BridgeImpassable if destroyed; else None. `change_bridge_state` (`snap.rs:770-793`) stamps the **entire ground A*** AABB to BridgeImpassable on destroy (including off-deck cells).

## Evidence
C++ 4-corner `isPointOnBridge` + `isCellOnSide/OnEnd/EntryPoint` vs Rust `b.contains(coord)` then `Some(Clear)` / `Some(BridgeImpassable)`. Destroy path: `for bx in lo.x..=hi.x { set_cell_type(..., BridgeImpassable) }` on the ground grid.

## Player-visible effect
Units treat the whole bridge bounding box as walkable deck (including air beside the span) and, when the bridge dies, the whole box becomes impassable on the **ground** (blocking the riverbank/underpass). Ramps/entry connect cells are only the two attach points. Distinct from hq-6htk (terrain rubble/splat) and hq-c23o (host not calling crate search).
close_reason: BridgeLayer now has a classified per-cell matrix (4/1-3/0 corner rules). get_cell_type_at_cell reads cell_type_at; destroy reclassifies. pathfind_layer_classify.rs + types.rs/line_passable.rs.

title: [Partition] getPropShroudStatusForPlayer is missing — trees/props never fog
description:
## C++
`PartitionManager::getPropShroudStatusForPlayer` (`PartitionManager.cpp:3038-3060`) samples four partition cells around the prop (world pos minus half a cell, then (x,y)/(x+1,y)/(x+1,y+1)/(x,y+1)). Mixed cell shroud → OBJECTSHROUD_PARTIAL_CLEAR; all shrouded → SHROUDED; all clear → CLEAR; else FOGGED. `W3DPropBuffer` and `W3DTreeBuffer` skip/draw/topple using this (props vanish in shroud; fogged trees freeze topple).

## Rust
No `get_prop_shroud_status_for_player` anywhere under GeneralsRust. Live `get_shroud_status_for_player` only returns CellShroudStatus for a single point via the 50wu shroud_manager grid. Tree/prop draw paths have nothing to call.

## Evidence
Repo-wide grep of `get_prop_shroud` / `getPropShroudStatusForPlayer` is empty on the Rust side. C++ W3DPropBuffer.cpp:341 and W3DTreeBuffer.cpp:1843 call ThePartitionManager->getPropShroudStatusForPlayer.

## Player-visible effect
Trees and civilian props stay fully drawn in unexplored shroud and keep animating (topple) while fogged. Distinct from object-ghost FOW (hq-2hqt / shroud_manager lookers) and from W3D ST_SHROUD_TEXTURE (hq-qipd.1).
close_reason: Added get_prop_shroud_status_for_player on collide PartitionManager and live game_logic_impl partition (four-cell sample at loc-halfCell). partition_shroud.rs.

title: [Partition] Shroud looker grid is 50wu, not PartitionCellSize 40
description:
## C++
Shroud/looker/shrouder circles are drawn on the same PartitionCell grid as objects (`m_cellSize` = GameData `PartitionCellSize = 40`). `getShroudStatusForPlayer(player, loc)` maps world→cell with that size. W3D FOW (`BaseHeightMap.cpp:1759`) inits the visual shroud with `m_partitionCellSize`.

## Rust
Live shroud queries go through `system/shroud_manager.rs`, not the 40wu collide partition:
```
const SHROUD_GRID_CELL_SIZE: f32 = 50.0;
```
`ShroudGrid::new` / `world_to_grid` / `do_shroud_reveal` all use 50. `ThePartitionManager::get_shroud_status_for_player` (`object_queries.rs:672-692`) reads this 50wu grid.

## Evidence
`shroud_manager.rs:63` `SHROUD_GRID_CELL_SIZE = 50.0` vs C++ `PartitionManager.cpp:2567` + GameData 40. Helper maps Visible/Explored/Hidden onto CELLSHROUD_CLEAR/FOGGED/SHROUDED from the 50wu cells.

## Player-visible effect
Fog-of-war tiles, reveal/cover circles, and script map-reveal snap to a 50wu lattice. Vision edges and minimap FOW do not line up with retail 40wu cells; a unit that just barely reveals a cell in ZH may leave it shrouded (or vice versa).
close_reason: Partition looker/shroud grid is PARTITION_CELL_SIZE=40wu. get_shroud_status_for_player on collide + live GameLogic partition uses that grid.

title: [Pathfind] PathfindLayerEnum is not C++ 0/1/2–14/LAYER_WALL=15
description:
## C++
`GameType.h:167`: `enum PathfindLayerEnum { LAYER_INVALID=0, LAYER_GROUND=1, LAYER_WALL=15, LAYER_LAST=15 }`. Layers 2–14 are unnamed bridge slots (`m_layers[LAYER_LAST+1]`). `Pathfinder::getCell(layer,x,y)` uses `layer > LAYER_GROUND && layer <= LAYER_LAST` to hit the bridge/wall cell matrix. Object `m_layer` and path nodes store these values.

## Rust
Live A* enum (`pathfind_astar.rs:54-59`) is only `Invalid=0, Ground=1, Top=2`. `get_cell_type_at_cell` takes that enum so layers 3–15 cannot be queried. Parallel `common/types/enums.rs:463-475` invents `Bridge1=3 … Wall=7, Tunnel=8, Water=9, Air=10, Last=11`; `from_u32(15)` returns Invalid. Host leftover (`pathfinding_system.rs`) maps 2 to Air.

## Evidence
C++ `LAYER_WALL = 15` vs crate A* `Top = 2` and common `Wall = 7` / `from_u32(15) → Invalid`. `line_passable.rs:620-632` can only special-case Ground/Invalid vs “everything else as Top/bridge 2”.

## Player-visible effect
Units cannot be on the correct bridge layer (3–14) or China/GLA wall-walk layer (15). Object/path xfer of layer 15 becomes Invalid; infantry never path on wall tops even when wall cells exist. Distinct from hq-c23o (host find_path_ex not calling crate internals) and hq-hvac (wall cell types).

## Split hint
One PathfindLayerEnum matching GameType.h (0,1,2–14,15); delete Top/Air/Tunnel inventions.
close_reason: Live A* PathfindLayerEnum is C++ 0/1/2-14/Wall=15 with from_u32(15)=Wall. path.rs Wall=15. pathfinding_system no longer maps layer 2 to Air.

title: [Partition] Live GameLogic closest-object grid uses 100wu cells, not retail 40
description:
## C++
`PartitionManager::init` (`PartitionManager.cpp:2567-2571`) sets `m_cellSize = TheGlobalData->m_partitionCellSize` (GameData.ini `PartitionCellSize = 40.0`, clamped to >= 1). `worldToCell` floors `(wx - extents.lo) / cellSize`. Closest-object rings (`FASTER_GCO`), COI fills, threat/value, and shroud looker circles all share this 40wu grid.

## Rust
Closed hq-805q only fixed `object/collide/partition_manager.rs` (`PARTITION_CELL_SIZE = 40.0`). The **live** iterator used by `ThePartitionManager::get_objects_in_range` / `get_closest_object*` is `system/game_logic_impl/partition.rs`:
```
cell_size: 100.0,  // PartitionManager::new
position_to_cell: (position.x / self.cell_size).floor()
```
That leftover is what GameLogic owns and what AI/scripts query. collide PM is a parallel store.

## Evidence
C++ `m_cellSize = TheGlobalData->m_partitionCellSize` vs Rust `partition.rs:29` `cell_size: 100.0`. Helper `object_queries.rs:71-74` calls `logic.partition_manager().find_objects_in_radius`.

## Player-visible effect
