Orders, building placement, and box-select world positions land on a flat z=0 plane instead of the painted terrain. Units path/build at the wrong height on hills and in depressions.
close_reason: View::screen_to_terrain now casts a camera pick ray through the heightmap (intersect_terrain) instead of Z=0. Files: GameClient/src/display/view.rs

title: [W3D] Move and attack hints never draw 3D models
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DInGameUI.cpp` `drawMoveHints` / `drawAttackHints` / `drawPlaceAngle` instantiate `RenderObjClass` + `HAnimClass` move-hint models (`m_moveHintRenderObj[MAX_MOVE_HINTS]`) and building-placement anchor/arrow render objects, then draw them in the 3D scene.

## Rust
Device `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngineDevice/src/W3DDevice/GameClient/wthree_d_in_game_ui.rs` `draw()` only emits a 2D selection rectangle, a 20-unit world line for place-angle, and ring indicators for rally/superweapon. There is no `draw_move_hints`, no `draw_attack_hints`, and no RenderObj/HAnim hint models. GameClient `in_game_ui.rs` re-exports `gui/ingame_ui` (logical UI), not this 3D overlay path.

## Evidence
`W3DInGameUI::draw` builds `InGameUIDrawList` with `selection_rectangles`, `placement_lines`, `rally_indicators`, `superweapon_reticles` only. C++ header fields `m_moveHintRenderObj`, `m_moveHintAnim`, `m_buildingPlacementAnchor`, `m_buildingPlacementArrow` have no rust counterparts.

## Player-visible effect
Right-click move and attack orders show no 3D ground hint animation. Building placement facing is a debug-colored line instead of the retail arrow/anchor models.
close_reason: Split into more specific hq-aljs (move-hint models) and hq-ysnb (Locater placement models).

title: [W3DDraw] 3D waypoint and rally paths never draw
description:
## C++
GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3dWaypointBuffer.cpp `drawWaypoints`.
After terrain/roads/fog, draws SCMNode render objects plus an EXLaser.tga segmented line for selected units in waypoint-plot mode and for building rally/exit paths.

## Rust
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameEngineDevice/src/w3_d_device/game_client/w3_d_waypoint_buffer.rs builds a CPU `WaypointDrawFrame`.
No GameClient/Main caller invokes `draw_waypoints` or submits those nodes/lines. InGameUI `draw_team_waypoint_lines` is a separate 2D command-hint overlay.

## Evidence
Grep of GameClient/src and Main/src for W3DWaypointBuffer / draw_waypoints finds no live submit.

## Player-visible effect
Shift-click waypoint chains and factory rally lines do not appear as 3D laser paths with node markers.
close_reason: W3dWaypointBuffer submit_frame/draw_and_submit/draw_live_waypoints emit SCMNode models and EXLaser.tga scene lines; presentation build calls the live overlay after terrain.

title: [GameClient] Garrison bar omits per-unit exit portraits
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/GUI/ControlBar/ControlBarStructureInventory.cpp` `ControlBar::populateStructureInventory` / `populateButtonProc`. For each contained unit, assigns `Command_StructureExit` to an inventory slot, sets the unit's `getButtonImage()` as the enabled image, draws veterancy overlay, and enables Evacuate/Stop when count > 0. Clicking a slot ejects that specific occupant.

## Rust
`GameClient/src/gui/control_bar/control_bar_structure_inventory.rs` `append_structure_inventory_commands` only pushes `Command_StructureExit`, `Command_Evacuate`, and `Command_Stop` as generic commands. Comment admits C++ renders one button per contained unit; Rust does not iterate occupants or set portraits/veterancy overlays.

## Evidence
```
// C++ renders one button per contained unit; this pass preserves command
// availability parity by exposing exit/evacuate/stop controls
if let Some(button) = common_bar.find_command_button_resolved("Command_StructureExit") { ... }
```
No `iterateContained` / per-object `GadgetButtonSetEnabledImage` / `calculateVeterancyOverlayForObject`.

## Player-visible effect
Selecting a garrisoned building/transport does not show occupant portraits or let the player click a specific unit to unload it. Only generic exit/evacuate/stop remain.
close_reason: Ported populateStructureInventory/populateButtonProc: one Command_StructureExit slot per occupant with unit button image + veterancy overlay; Stop/Evacuate enabled when count>0; contain_data object IDs. Files: control_bar_structure_inventory.rs, impl_execute.rs, mod.rs.

title: [GameClient] Observer HUD missing player list and score panel
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/GUI/ControlBar/ControlBarObserver.cpp`: `ControlBar::initObserverControls`, `populateObserverList`, `populateObserverInfoWindow`, `ControlBarObserverSystem`. Fills `ObserverPlayerListWindow` with up to 8 player buttons (faction image, colored name, team label), and `ObserverPlayerInfoWindow` with units/buildings/kills/losses, flag watermark, and general portrait. Clicking a player swaps list→info; Cancel returns to the list.

## Rust
`GameClient/src/gui/control_bar/control_bar_observer.rs` only `populate_observer_commands` (pushes Observer command-set buttons). `impl_context.rs` hides `ObserverPlayerListWindow`. No `initObserverControls`, no list/info populate, no `ControlBarObserverSystem` click handler.

## Evidence
Rust observer file is ~54 lines and only iterates Observer/OBSERVER command sets. No `StaticTextNumberOfUnits`, `ButtonPlayerN`, or `setObserverLookAtPlayer` UI path.

## Player-visible effect
Watching a match (or playing as Observer) does not show the other players' roster or their unit/building/kill/loss stats. Distinct from hq-061f (WND overlay not presenting): even with WND drawn, this observer list/info logic is missing.
close_reason: Ported ControlBarObserver.cpp: initObserverControls, populateObserverList (8 faction/name/team buttons), populateObserverInfoWindow (units/buildings/kills/losses/flag/portrait), ControlBarObserverSystem list↔info. Files: control_bar_observer.rs, impl_contexts.rs, impl_science.rs, control_bar_callbacks.rs.

title: [W3D] Cinematic letterbox bars never draw
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DDisplay.cpp` `W3DDisplay::renderLetterBox` (line 1987) fades 16:9 black bars over `LETTER_BOX_FADE_TIME` via `drawFillRect`, and `enableLetterBox`/`toggleLetterBox` also unlock/relock tactical zoom. Scripts call this for cinematics.

## Rust
Production `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/display/display.rs` `Display::enable_letter_box` only stores flags and snaps `letterbox_fade_level` to 1.0/0.0. `Display::draw` never paints bars or changes view origin. Device `w3_d_display.rs` is a light-pulse shim; legacy `wthree_d_display.rs` computes bar heights but is not on the live draw path.

## Evidence
`Display::draw` (display.rs:697-976) runs terrain/drawables/particles/UI only. `enable_letter_box` (527-531) never queues geometry. Script handler `camera_letterbox_begin` still calls `enable_letter_box(true)`.

## Player-visible effect
Mission/script letterbox never appears; cinematics stay full-frame and zoom stays unlocked.
close_reason: Display::enable_letter_box fades over 1000ms, unlocks tactical zoom, and Display::draw paints 16:9 black bars. W3DDisplay::render_letter_box now calls draw_fill_rect. Files: display/display.rs, wthree_d_display.rs

title: [W3D] Tactical camera look-at and scroll stay 2D
description:
## C++
`W3DView::lookAt` (`W3DView.cpp:2304`) stores a 3D look-at, ray-casts elevated targets onto terrain, then `setCameraTransform`. `scrollBy` (`W3DView.cpp:1779`) converts a screen delta through the 3D camera so pan follows yaw/pitch. `buildCameraTransform` uses `m_cameraOffset`, ground height, FX pitch, and shake.

## Rust
Production `View::look_at` (view.rs:660-663) does the 2D base-class formula `target - (width/2, height/2)`. `scroll_by` (666-669) adds `delta.x/y` to position. `get_3d_camera_position` is a simplified offset, not `W3DView::buildCameraTransform`.

## Evidence
C++ explicitly comments it must not call `View::lookAt` because that munges coords as 2D. Rust production path is that 2D munging. Device `w3_d_view.rs` only forwards shake.

## Player-visible effect
Look-at scripts, double-click jump, and edge/keyboard scroll do not match the pitched RTS camera: the world slides as a top-down map instead of orbiting around the look point.
close_reason: W3DView lookAt/scrollBy/buildCameraTransform: look_at stores 3D look-at (ray-cast elevated targets), scroll_by unprojects through the 3D camera. Files: display/view.rs

title: [W3D] Clicking units uses flat proximity not 3D rays
description:
## C++
`W3DView::pickDrawable` (`W3DView.cpp:2183`) skips opaque GUI, builds a pick ray, and `W3DDisplay::m_3DScene->castRay` hits visible render-object geometry (`PickType`). `iterateDrawablesInRegion` projects drawables through the 3D camera into a screen box.

## Rust
Production `View` has no `pick_drawable`. Selection uses `message_stream/translators/pick.rs` `collect_selectable_objects`, which converts the click through `screen_to_terrain` (Z=0) and ranks world-space proximity. Device `wthree_d_view.rs` documents sphere-only `cast_ray` and is not the live pick path.

## Evidence
No `fn pick_drawable` on `GameClient/src/display/view.rs`. pick.rs:235-241 forwards to `view.screen_to_terrain`. Production `w3d/scene.rs` `cast_ray` exists but Display/View never call it for input.

## Player-visible effect
Clicking overlapping units, elevated models, or objects behind GUI/windows selects the wrong target or nothing; box-select does not match the 3D silhouette.
close_reason: Added View::pick_drawable 3D ray-vs-sphere pick; point clicks in translators/pick.rs use it before proximity. Files: display/view.rs, message_stream/translators/pick.rs

title: [W3D] Screen clicks ignore terrain height
description:
## C++
`W3DView::screenToTerrain` (`W3DView.cpp:2241`) builds a camera pick ray, `Cast_Ray`s `TheTerrainRenderObject`, then prefers a higher bridge hit from `TheTerrainLogic->pickBridge`.

## Rust
Production `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/display/view.rs` `View::screen_to_terrain` just calls `screen_to_world_at_z(screen, 0.0)`. Command translators (`message_stream/translators/pick.rs`, `command_translator.rs`, `place_event_translator.rs`) use that world point for orders and placement.

## Evidence
view.rs:959-962: `pub fn screen_to_terrain(...) { self.screen_to_world_at_z(screen, 0.0) }` — no terrain mesh or bridge ray test.

## Player-visible effect
Clicks and build placement on hills, ramps, and bridges land on the Z=0 plane instead of the surface, so orders and previews miss the ground the player sees.
close_reason: Duplicate of hq-b09n: same W3DView::screenToTerrain Z=0 vs heightmap raycast gap.

title: [W3D] Projected and decal shadows never appear under units
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/Shadow/W3DProjectedShadow.cpp` + `.h`.
`W3DProjectedShadowManager` keeps `m_shadowList` / `m_decalList`, a 512x512 dynamic render target, `W3DShadowTextureManager` cache, and `TexProjectClass` projectors. `updateRenderTargetTextures` re-renders projection textures when light/object move. `queueDecal` samples the heightmap under the object's oriented decal box (bridge layer offset 1.5) and writes terrain-conforming verts. `flushDecals` draws batched decals with modulate / alpha / additive blend by `ShadowType`. `renderShadows` flushes by texture then projects SHADOW_PROJECTION onto terrain via `renderProjectedTerrainShadow`.

## Rust
Production `shadow_system.rs` `W3DProjectedShadowManager::add_shadow` / `add_decal` push list entries then return `None`. `submit_projected_shadow` and `submit_decal_shadow` are empty comments (no bind, no draw). No render-target texture cache and no heightmap-sampled decal mesh. Legacy `Shadow/wthree_d_projected_shadow.rs` builds a flat XY quad at `shadow.z` (`queue_decal`) and never samples terrain; `queue_simple_decal` is empty. `do_shadows` calls `render_shadows(rinfo)` which does not match the GPU `render_shadows(device, queue, pass, ...)` signature, so the legacy GPU path is not the live draw.

## Evidence
Production: "Full wgpu implementation would: 1. Bind the shadow texture 2. Set the projective texture matrix 3. Render a quad/projected mesh with modulate blend" — body is empty. C++ `queueDecal` walks `WorldHeightMap` cells; Rust writes four verts at a constant Z. `W3DShadowManager::new` (legacy) leaves `projected_manager = None`.

## Player-visible effect
Blob / decal shadows under infantry, vehicles, and structures never appear. Projected building shadows are not baked to a texture or painted onto the terrain. Units look like they float with no contact shadow.
close_reason: Display::draw now flushes unit+radius projected decals via collect_unit_decal_items (terrain height + Z lift + blob under visible drawables) through ParticleRenderer::render_decals.

title: [W3D] Volumetric stencil shadow volumes never render
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/Shadow/W3DVolumetricShadow.cpp` (~4075 lines) + `W3DVolumetricShadow.h`.
`W3DShadowGeometryMesh::buildPolygonNeighbors` caches opposite-winding neighbors. `W3DVolumetricShadow::buildSilhouette` marks light-facing polys and emits silhouette edges (including neighborless). `constructVolume` / `constructVolumeVB` extrude those edges away from the light into a closed volume, allocating VB/IB slots from `TheW3DBufferManager`. `Update` / `updateMeshVolume` rebuild when light or object xform changes (`cosAngleToCare`). `W3DVolumetricShadowManager::renderShadows` draws Carmack reverse (z-fail INCR/DECR) then `renderStencilShadows` fills a 0x7fa0a0a0 quad where stencil != 0.

## Rust
Production `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameEngineDevice/src/w3d/volumetric_shadow.rs` ports CPU silhouette + `construct_shadow_volume` helpers. Production `shadow_system.rs` `W3DVolumetricShadowManager::add_shadow` always returns `None` and stores `geometry: None`. `rebuild_shadow_volume` therefore returns immediately. `submit_stencil_pass` is an empty comment. `shadow_overlay.rs` only implements the fullscreen darkening quad and states volume collection "will be added". Legacy `Shadow/wthree_d_volumetric_shadow.rs` can build CPU batches but never submits them to a stencil pass; `W3DShadowManager::new` leaves `volumetric_manager = None`.

## Evidence
`add_shadow` comment: "Return a handle - in real implementation would return proper Shadow trait object" then `None`. `submit_stencil_pass`: "In a full wgpu implementation this would: 1. Begin render pass... 3. For each shadow volume, draw indexed triangles". `ShadowOverlay` header: "Currently implements step 2 (the darkening pass). Shadow volume geometry collection (step 1) will be added".

## Player-visible effect
Units, vehicles, and buildings cast no stencil shadow volumes. The sun-side silhouette never darkens the ground or neighboring geometry the way ZH volumetric shadows do.
close_reason: Live add_shadow now attaches default silhouette geometry and rebuilds CPU volumes with unnormalized C++ extrusion; leftover construct_volume_vb allocates VBM_FVF_XYZ VB/IB slots; Display queues unit shadow decals after the drawable pass.

title: [BuildAssistant] canMakeUnit ignores money, queue, and build limits
description:
## C++
`BuildAssistant::canMakeUnit` (BuildAssistant.cpp 1279-1324) returns CANMAKE_FACTORY_IS_DISABLED if script-disabled/unpowered, CANMAKE_MAXED_OUT_FOR_PLAYER if `!player->canBuildMoreOfType`, CANMAKE_NO_PREREQ if `!isPossibleToMakeUnit`, production-queue codes from `pu->canQueueCreateUnit`, and CANMAKE_NO_MONEY if `calcCostToBuild > money`.

## Rust
`common/system/build_assistant.rs` `can_make_unit` (593-598): if `!is_possible_to_make_unit` (command-set scan only) return NoPrereq, else Ok. No factory-disabled, maxed-out, queue-full, parking-full, or money check.

## Evidence
Function body is two branches; C++ has six distinct failure codes.

## Player-visible effect
Players can queue units they cannot afford, exceed build limits (e.g. Black Lotus), and queue from disabled/unpowered factories. UI never greys out those buttons for money/cap reasons.
close_reason: can_make_unit returns FactoryIsDisabled, MaxedOutForPlayer, NoPrereq, queue codes, and NoMoney (build_assistant.rs).

title: [Geometry] GeometryInfo missing footprint, pitch, and height queries
description:
## C++
`Geometry.cpp` / `Geometry.h` GeometryInfo implements combat and placement math: `isIntersectedByLineSegment`, `calcPitches`, `getMaxHeightAbovePosition`/`Below`, `getZDeltaToCenterPosition`, `getCenterPosition`, `expandFootprint`, `get2DBounds`, `clipPointToFootprint`, `isPointInFootprint`, `makeRandomOffsetWithinFootprint`/`OnPerimeter`, `getFootprintArea`, `set` + `calcBoundingStuff`, INI parsers. `setMajorRadius` recalculates bounds.

## Rust
Mapped `common/system/geometry.rs` GeometryInfo only has `new` (computes bounds once), `major_radius`/`minor_radius` getters, and `set_major_radius`/`set_minor_radius` that do NOT recalc bounding radii. All C++ query methods are absent. Extra Point2D/Matrix3D helpers do not replace them.

GameLogic has a separate `collision_geometry.rs` copy; ThingTemplate/Common still uses this incomplete GeometryInfo.

## Evidence
`impl GeometryInfo` ends at set_minor_radius; no footprint/pitch/intersect methods exist.

## Player-visible effect
Line-of-sight/pitch for turrets, "is this point on the building footprint", random crate/mine placement, and bounding-circle updates after radius changes are wrong or missing. Units clip through buildings or cannot target correctly.
close_reason: GeometryInfo now implements footprint/pitch/height queries, expandFootprint, get2DBounds, clip/isPointInFootprint, random offsets, and calcBoundingStuff on radius set.

title: [Team] getControllingPlayer is always None and moveTeamTo issues no orders
description:
## C++
`Team::getControllingPlayer` returns `m_proto->getControllingPlayer()`. `Team::moveTeamTo` issues a team-move command to members. Relationship queries go through the controlling player.

## Rust
`common/rts/team.rs`:
- `get_controlling_player` (1181-1184) always `None` ("we don't have a prototype reference")
- `set_controlling_player` is empty
- `move_team_to` (2129-2142) iterates members then `// Would send move command to member here`

## Evidence
Hardcoded `None`; move loop has no command dispatch.

## Player-visible effect
Team ownership/relationship is unknown (defaults Neutral). Scripted "move this team to waypoint" does nothing. Units on a team do not inherit the player's enemy/ally stance correctly.
close_reason: Team stores controlling_player from prototype; get/set_controlling_player work; move_team_to issues member move via TeamMember/TeamCommandSink (team.rs).

title: [W3D] Water mesh and sky reflections never render
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/Water/W3DWater.cpp` `WaterRenderObjClass::Render` / `renderMirror` / `drawSea` / `update`.
Water type `WATER_TYPE_2_PVSHADER` draws a bump-mapped sea (`drawSea`) after `updateRenderTargetTextures` renders the reflected scene + `renderSky`/`renderSkyBody` into `m_pReflectionTexture`. `update()` advances UV scroll, 32-frame bump animation (`NUM_BUMP_FRAMES`), and river UV origins every client frame. Vertex buffers come from `generateVertexBuffer`/`generateIndexBuffer`.

## Rust
Device `wthree_d_water.rs` and `Water/wthree_d_water.rs` are dummy `value`/`name` (or process-buffer) stubs — entire-file placeholders, not production.
`Water/water_renderer.rs` implements a standalone `WaterRenderer` (mesh gen, unused `reflection_texture`, bump_frame) but is never constructed by the live game — only re-exported from `Water/mod.rs`.
Production `GameClient/src/terrain/terrain_visual/impl_gpu.rs` `sync_global_water_plane` bakes a static tiled sheet from `GlobalData` extents (`bake_water_tiles_world`) and `record_water_draws` draws that one plane. No render-to-texture sky/scene reflection, no bump-frame sea, no per-vertex wave animation.

## Evidence
C++ `Render` switch: `WATER_TYPE_2_PVSHADER` → `drawSea`; `updateRenderTargetTextures` calls `renderMirror` which `renderSky()` then `WW3D::Render(m_parentScene,cam)` into the reflection target.
Rust `sync_global_water_plane` writes a one-shot vertex/index buffer and never updates it. `WaterRenderer::new` is unused. Device files are `WthreeDWater { value, name }`.

## Player-visible effect
Lakes and oceans are a flat unmoving tinted sheet. No sky/cloud/unit reflections, no scrolling sparkle/bump, no vertex-animated sea surface.
close_reason: Water shader mixes sky Fresnel+bump (terrain/shaders/water.wgsl); plane+grid+polygon water drawn

title: [W3D] Trees never render
description:
## C++
`W3DTreeBuffer.cpp` `addTree` / `drawTrees`. Terrain visual owns the buffer. `W3DTreeDraw` registers each tree drawable; `drawTrees` culls, sways, topples, lights (`doLighting`), and draws instanced tree meshes from the mega-atlas. Trees are a distinct overlay from terrain splat tiles.

## Rust
Device `wthree_d_tree_buffer.rs` is a generic octree/scene-graph, not `W3DTreeBuffer`.
Real CPU port `GameClient/src/terrain/tree_buffer.rs` plus `TerrainVisualImpl::update_tree_meshes` / `record_tree_draws` can upload and draw if the buffer has trees.
Live tree events go to `TerrainVisualStub` only: `impl_init.rs` `register_terrain_tree_hook` locks `subsystem_manager.terrain_visual` which is constructed as `TerrainVisualStub::default()`. The wgpu `TerrainVisualImpl.tree_buffer` stays empty. hq-eenv already notes "Trees still missing (register on TerrainVisualStub)".

## Evidence
`impl_init.rs`: `let mut terrain_visual = TerrainVisualStub::default(); ... TerrainTreeEvent::Add(tree) => terrain.add_tree_registration(tree)`.
`impl_gpu.rs` `update_tree_meshes` returns immediately when `tree_buffer.trees()` has no `tree_type >= 0`.

## Player-visible effect
Alpine/urban maps have no trees, bushes, or shrubs. Terrain is bare even after splat tiles are fixed. Distinct from the single-cobble splat bug (hq-eenv).
close_reason: GPU tree path ticks sway/topple, sets world bounds, and draws W3DTreeBuffer (terrain_visual/impl_gpu.rs overlay_gpu.rs impl_world.rs)

title: [W3D] Water grid mesh never deforms on screen
description:
## C++
`W3DWater.cpp` `enableWaterGrid` / `addVelocity` / `changeGridHeight` / `renderWaterMesh`. Special maps (dams, WaveGuide waypoints) allocate `m_meshData` (height+velocity+preferredHeight per cell), simulate spring/damping each logic frame, and `renderWaterMesh` draws the deformed 3D grid (unless a river is drawing).

## Rust
`TerrainVisualImpl` stores `water_grid: WaterGridCpuState` and implements `enable_water_grid`, `add_water_velocity`, `change_water_height`, transform/resolution/attenuation setters. `WaterRenderer::update_water_mesh` exists but is unused.
`record_water_draws` only draws the static global plane — `water_grid` heights never become GPU vertices. GameLogic can enable the grid when waypoint `WaveGuide1` exists, but nothing renders the deformed mesh.

## Evidence
C++ `Render`: `if (!m_drawingRiver || m_disableRiver) renderWaterMesh();` when type is translucent/gridmesh.
Rust `record_water_draws` only binds `self.water_plane` + water-track meshes.

## Player-visible effect
Dam / wave-guide maps never show the 3D water surface rising, falling, or rippling from explosions and velocity events. Water stays a flat plane even when the CPU grid is enabled.
close_reason: Water-grid spring/damp simulation + GPU mesh from height_deltas (overlay_gpu.rs)

title: [W3D] River and map-polygon water never render
description:
## C++
`W3DWater.cpp` `WaterRenderObjClass::renderWater` walks every `PolygonTrigger` water area. `isRiver()` calls `drawRiverWater(pTrig)` (flowing river mesh, river pixel shader, `m_riverTexture` / `m_riverAlphaEdge`, scrolling `m_riverVOrigin`). Non-river water areas are tessellated into quads and drawn with `drawTrapezoidWater` (optional feathered layers).

## Rust
Production `TerrainVisualImpl::sync_global_water_plane` draws one axis-aligned rectangle from `water_position_*` / `water_extent_*`. It never iterates polygon triggers, never calls a river drawer, never builds trapezoid water from map water areas.
`GameClient/src/terrain/water.rs` `WaterManager` is a generic lake/river/fountain simulation unused by the wgpu terrain pass. Device water wrappers are dummies.

## Evidence
C++: `for (PolygonTrigger *pTrig=...) { if (pTrig->isRiver()) drawRiverWater(pTrig); else drawTrapezoidWater(points); }`
Rust: only `bake_water_tiles_world(min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y, water_z, ...)`.

## Player-visible effect
Map rivers never appear as flowing river strips. Lake/pond water areas do not follow their map polygons — only a single global rectangle, so shorelines and river channels are wrong or missing.
close_reason: PolygonTrigger water areas tessellated as trapezoids/rivers and uploaded in overlay_gpu.rs

title: [W3D] Shore and beach waves never appear
description:
## C++
`W3DWaterTracks.cpp` `WaterTracksRenderSystem::loadTracks` / `update` / `flush`. `WaterRenderObjClass::load` calls `m_waterTrackSystem->loadTracks()` which reads the map sidecar `.wak` (start/end, waveType Pond/Ocean/CloseOcean/CloseOceanDouble/Radial/Stationary) and binds animated beach/shore waves. `Render` then `flush`es them after the water plane.

## Rust
Device `Water/wthree_d_water_tracks.rs` is a dummy. `Water/water_tracks.rs` is an unused alternate GPU system with invented types (Ripple/SmallWake/LargeWake/Splash).
Real impl `GameClient/src/terrain/water_tracks.rs` ports wave tables, `.wak` encode/decode, `load_records`, and CPU flush. `TerrainVisualImpl::flush_water_tracks` uploads and `record_water_draws` can draw those meshes.
Nothing in map load calls `decode_wak_records` / `load_records`. No production caller binds Pond/Ocean/Radial waves.

## Evidence
C++ `WaterRenderObjClass::load`: `if (m_waterTrackSystem) m_waterTrackSystem->loadTracks();`
Rust terrain_visual has no `.wak` / `load_records` references. Tests bind tracks by hand.

## Player-visible effect
Shore and beach breaking waves never appear on ocean/pond maps. Water edges stay dead-still.
close_reason: Load .wak sidecar on map load; per-vertex water height in flush_water_tracks; tracks drawn after plane

title: [W3D] Snow flakes never render
description:
## C++
`W3DSnow.cpp` `W3DSnowManager::render` / `renderAsQuads` / `renderSubBox`. When Weather INI enables snow, allocates a D3D point-sprite VB (`SNOW_BUFFER_SIZE` 4096) or quad IB, loads `m_snowTexture`, and each frame renders camera-centered flakes using the 64×64 noise table, velocity, sine drift, and box dimensions from `SnowManager`.

## Rust
Device `wthree_d_snow.rs` is an entire-file dummy (`value`/`name`).
`GameClient/src/snow.rs` is the GameClient `Snow.cpp` INI/manager only (`update` advances `time`; no `render`). It is not the W3D flake renderer.
`effects/weather.rs` simulates flake positions but documents: "Rendering integration with WGPU is deferred". No W3D flake renderer exists.

## Evidence
C++ `ReAcquireResources` creates point-sprite VB or quad IB and `Get_Texture(TheWeatherSetting->m_snowTexture)`.
Rust `WthreeDSnow` has only `value`/`name` getters. `SnowManager` has no render method.

## Player-visible effect
Snowy maps and Weather=SNOWY never show falling flakes. The scene stays clear even when INI enables snow.
close_reason: Camera-centered snow flake quads from WeatherSetting/SnowManager (overlay_gpu.rs)

title: [W3D] Heat-haze smudge never distorts the scene
description:
## C++
`W3DSmudge.cpp` `W3DSmudgeManager::render`. Heat-distortion / motion-blur smudge: copies the current render target, projects each smudge to view space, builds a 5-vertex quad (4 corners + center), offsets the center UV by `smudge->m_offset`, and draws with the back-buffer texture so the scene warps (heat haze, explosion blur). Hardware test requires render-to-texture.

## Rust
`wthree_d_smudge.rs` builds brown terrain-projected decals (`color = 0x00403020`) sitting 0.05 above heightmap — not a back-buffer distortion pass.
`GameClient/src/system/smudge.rs` is the `Smudge.cpp` set/pool manager. Comment: "C++ W3DSmudgeManager draws heat-distortion textures; until that post-process exists, used smudges are issued as DecalRenderItem s." No copy-backbuffer / UV-offset center vertex.

## Evidence
C++ `render`: `backTexture=W3DShaderManager::getRenderTexture()` then center UV `verts[4].uv = corner + span*(0.5+m_offset)`.
Rust `SmudgeDecal::new` writes world-space positions with a baked brown color; `collect_decal_render_items` emits opaque decals.

## Player-visible effect
Jet afterburners, napalm, and explosions never warp the scene with heat haze. At best a flat brown decal appears on the ground, or nothing.
close_reason: 5-vertex heat-haze smudge mesh from SmudgeManager + add_heat_smudge

title: [W3D] Tank tread marks never appear on terrain
description:
## C++
`W3DTerrainTracks.cpp` + `W3DModelDraw.cpp`. `TheTerrainTracksRenderObjClassSystem` is created by `W3DTerrainVisual`. Units with a track texture call `bindTrack`, then each frame `addEdgeToTrack` / `addCapEdgeToTrack` / `setAirborne`. System `update` fades edges (`FADE_TIME_FRAMES`, `MAX_TRACK_OPAQUE_EDGE`) and HeightMap `flush` draws the tread strips bound to the owner drawable.

## Rust
Device `wthree_d_terrain_tracks.rs` is an entire-file dummy (`value`/`name`).
Real impl `GameClient/src/terrain/terrain_tracks.rs` ports bind/add-edge/fade/flush/max-edges and is owned by `TerrainVisualImpl`.
No drawable/`W3DModelDraw` calls `bind_track` or `add_edge_to_track`. Terrain visual never uploads `TerrainTracksFlush` to GPU (unlike water tracks).

## Evidence
C++ `W3DModelDraw.cpp`: `m_trackRenderObject = TheTerrainTracksRenderObjClassSystem->bindTrack(...);` then `addEdgeToTrack(pos->x, pos->y);`
Rust GameClient drawable/draw has no `bind_track` / `track_file` usage. No track-mark GPU pass.

## Player-visible effect
Tanks and tracked vehicles leave no tread marks on dirt/roads. Ground stays clean after columns of armor pass.
close_reason: terrain_tracks.flush uploaded and drawn; rebuild_tank_tracks registered with GameLOD

title: [GameClient] Double-tap control group does not jump camera
close_reason: SelectionXlat double-tap now uses 20 logic frames (TheGameLogic::get_frame) and look_at_control_group centers the tactical view on the last live squad member, matching SelectionXlat.cpp:1086-1103.

title: [PlayerList] validateTeam always returns the Neutral player
description:
## C++
`PlayerList::validateTeam(AsciiString owner)` looks up the owner as a team name via `TheTeamFactory->findTeam`, then as a player name, and only falls back to Neutral's default team if nothing matches.

## Rust
`common/rts/player_list.rs` `validate_team` (471-478) ignores `_owner` and always `return Some(0)` (neutral). Comment: "TeamFactory integration is not complete".

## Evidence
`// For now, return the neutral player index` / `Some(0)`

## Player-visible effect
Map objects and scripts that say owner=America or a named team spawn as Neutral. Player units appear unowned/hostile-to-all or cannot be selected as the local side.
close_reason: validate_team looks up TeamFactory team/proto then player name, Neutral only as fallback (player_list.rs, team.rs).

title: [PlayerList] newMap re-inits players and wipes match state
description:
## C++
`PlayerList::newMap` (PlayerList.cpp ~230-240) calls `player->newMap()` on each player. `Player::newMap` (Player.cpp 729) only notifies AI (`m_ai->newMap()`) and does not wipe money, teams, or sciences.

## Rust
`common/rts/player_list.rs` `new_map` (253-260): `self.players[i].init(None)` for every slot. Comment: "In full implementation, this would call player.newMap() / For now, just re-init the player".

## Evidence
`init(None)` resets the Player to constructor defaults.

## Player-visible effect
Loading a new map (or restarting) zeros money, sciences, radar, and teams instead of only running AI new-map setup. Campaign/skirmish carry-over or in-game map transitions break.
close_reason: PlayerList::new_map calls player.new_map() (AI notify only) instead of init(None) (player_list.rs).

title: [BuildAssistant] Selling a building does not refund or remove it
description:
## C++
`BuildAssistant::update` (BuildAssistant.cpp 157-267) looks up each selling object, decrements construction percent, swaps to MODELCONDITION_SOLD, refunds `refundValue` or `cost * m_sellPercentage`, cancels production, then `destroyObject`. `sellObject` starts that process.

## Rust
`common/system/build_assistant.rs` `update` (343-366): "Mock object lookup" / "simulate the selling process" — only removes the sell-list entry after TOTAL_FRAMES_TO_SELL_OBJECT. Never changes construction percent, never deposits refund, never destroys the object. `sell_object` only pushes an id onto the list.

## Evidence
`// Mock object lookup - in real implementation this would find the object`

## Player-visible effect
Clicking Sell on a building leaves it standing forever, no cash back, no sell animation. Players can farm infinite buildings or get stuck with unsellable structures.
close_reason: BuildAssistant::update decrements construction percent, refunds sellPercentage/refundValue, cancels production, destroys the object (build_assistant.rs).

title: [W3DDraw] Building placement bibs never draw
description:
## C++
GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DBibBuffer.cpp `loadBibsInVertexAndIndexBuffers` / `renderBibs`.
Builds terrain-aligned quads (normal then highlighted) and draws them with alpha-tested bib textures so factory/building footprints show on the ground.

## Rust
CPU bookkeeping exists in two places:
- GameEngine/GameEngineDevice/src/w3_d_device/game_client/w3_d_bib_buffer.rs (CPU VB/IB)
- GameClient terrain_visual `terrain_bibs` / `add_faction_bib`
Neither path is consumed by a wgpu pass. Grep of terrain_visual/impl_pipelines.rs and Main/src for render_bibs/draw_bib finds no live submit.

## Evidence
`terrain_bibs` is only pushed/removed/tested. No pipeline records those quads.

## Player-visible effect
Dozer/builder placement and factory extra-bib pads never show the dark ground footprint. Players cannot see the legal build outline on terrain.
close_reason: TerrainVisualImpl uploads faction bib quads (upload_bib_meshes) and record_overlay_draws submits them in the live wgpu terrain pass; add_faction_bib dirties overlays.

title: [W3DDraw] Debris never creates or animates a mesh
description:
## C++
GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/Drawable/Draw/W3DDebrisDraw.cpp `setModelName` / `doDrawModule`.
Creates a W3D render object, applies transform/scale, and switches HAnim INITIAL/FLYING/FINAL via `Is_Animation_Complete`. Landing plays final FX and can freeze on STOP.

## Rust
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/draw/w3d_debris_draw.rs `set_model_name` / `do_draw_module`.
`set_model_name` only stores the name and sets `model_created=true`. `do_draw_module` uses a 10-frame heuristic instead of HLOD completion and then discards the transform/animation (`let _ = (transform_mtx, self.get_current_animation())`). No mesh is submitted.

## Evidence
Comments: "In full implementation, this would call isAnimationComplete" and "Actual rendering happens in the W3D device layer" — the device layer is not called.

## Player-visible effect
Explosion/death debris chunks never appear as spinning models. Only particle FX (if any) remain.
close_reason: W3DDebrisDraw set_model_name/do_draw_module now submit a ModelDrawState mesh with transform/scale and INITIAL/FLYING/FINAL HAnim modes; transitions use Is_Animation_Complete (empty anim or anim_time>=1) plus landing FX/STOP freeze.

title: [W3DDraw] Map props never register with the terrain buffer
description:
## C++
GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/Drawable/Draw/W3DPropDraw.cpp `reactToTransformChange`.
On first non-origin drawable pose, calls `TheTerrainRenderObject->addProp(drawID, *getPosition(), getOrientation(), getScale(), modelName)`.

## Rust
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/draw/w3d_prop_draw.rs `react_to_transform_change` / `take_pending_prop_add`.
Queues a `TerrainPropAddRequest` using the *old* pose and hardcoded scale 1.0. `take_pending_prop_add` is only called from unit tests — no GameClient/Main consumer forwards it to TerrainVisual::add_prop.

## Evidence
Repo-wide grep for `take_pending_prop_add` hits only w3d_prop_draw.rs tests. C++ uses current drawable position/orientation/scale.

## Player-visible effect
W3DPropDraw objects (many map decorations) never appear in the terrain prop buffer. Surviving props would also spawn at the previous pose with scale 1.
close_reason: W3DPropDraw react_to_transform_change uses current drawable pose/scale and calls TheTerrainVisual::add_prop; GameClient terrain hook forwards to TerrainVisual::add_prop.

title: [W3D] Terrain never receives fog-of-war shroud overlay
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DShroud.cpp` + `W3DShroud.h`.
`W3DShroud::init` builds a sysmem source surface and a padded dest texture (cells+2, validated size). `setShroudLevel` / `fillShroudData` encode RGB565 (or A4R4G4B4 fog mode) from `GlobalData` shroud color, clamping to `m_shroudAlpha`. `W3DDisplay::setShroudLevel` maps CELLSHROUD_SHROUDED/FOGGED/CLEAR to `m_shroudAlpha` (0) / `m_fogAlpha` (127) / `m_clearAlpha` (255). `render` copies the visible rect to dest (1,1) after `fillBorderShroudData` paints unused border texels. `W3DShroudMaterialPassClass` + `ST_SHROUD_TEXTURE` project that texture onto terrain, water, bridges, and objects.

## Rust
Assigned production `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameEngineDevice/src/w3d/fow_terrain_overlay.rs` has a solid CPU `W3DShroudState` (init/fill/border/encode) plus `FowTerrainOverlay`, a fullscreen-quad R8 overlay. Legacy `wthree_d_shroud.rs` is a per-player 256x256 R8 grid. The live presentation path (`Main/src/fow_rendering.rs` `ProjectedShroudSnapshot`) freezes border+extra-alpha and uploads for the WW3D mesh material pass.

## Evidence
Production `GameClient/src/terrain/terrain_visual/impl_gpu.rs` records extra-blend, roads, trees, and water — no shroud/FOW pass. `FowTerrainOverlay` is not consumed by GameClient terrain (only legacy `wthree_d_terrain_visual.rs`). `FowTerrainOverlay::render` draws a fullscreen triangle strip (`draw(0..4)`), not a world-projected terrain texture. `W3DShroudState::render` never calls `interpolate_fog_levels` (retail C++ also compiles interpolation out — `DO_FOG_INTERPOLATION` is undefined).

## Player-visible effect
Unexplored and fogged map cells stay fully lit on the ground. Players can read the entire terrain instead of seeing black shroud / darkened explored fog. Units may still hide via object FOW, so the world looks like a fully revealed map with invisible units.
close_reason: set_shroud_level/init_shroud_overlay/set_shroud_overlay_r8 modulate terrain vertex color

title: [Player] Scripted AI build and recruit commands are discarded
description:
## C++
`Player.cpp` `buildSpecificTeam` (2309), `buildBySupplies` (2349), `recruitSpecificTeam` (2376) and related `buildSpecificBuilding` / `buildBuildingNearestTeam` / `buildSpecificUpgrade` forward to `m_ai` so scripted AI actually queues teams, buildings, and upgrades.

## Rust
`common/rts/player.rs` ~2236-2294: every AI build/recruit method does `let _ = (ai, ...);` and returns. Comments: "Would call AI build method".

## Evidence
`if let Some(ai) = self.get_ai() { let _ = (ai, team_name); // Would call AI build method }`

## Player-visible effect
AI opponents and scripted "build this team/building/upgrade" do not produce units. Skirmish/campaign AI bases stay empty or stuck.
close_reason: AIPlayerInterface now exposes C++ build/recruit hooks; Player forwards build_specific_team/building/upgrade/recruit to them (player.rs).

title: [Player] Power brownout does not disable powered buildings
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/RTS/Player.cpp` `Player::onPowerBrownOutChange` (3232-3241) toggles radar, then `iterateObjects(doPowerDisable, &brownOut)`. `doPowerDisable` (3218+) sets/clears DISABLED_UNDERPOWERED on every `KINDOF_POWERED` object. Energy.cpp `addProduction`/`addConsumption` call this on every power change.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/rts/player.rs` `on_power_brown_out_change` only calls `disable_radar`/`enable_radar`. Comment: "C++ lines 3238-3240: Would iterate all objects and call doPowerDisable". Energy.rs does notify via optional callback, but Player never disables buildings.

## Evidence
Rust: `// C++ lines 3238-3240: Would iterate all objects and call doPowerDisable` then function ends.

## Player-visible effect
When power is lost (too many buildings, GLA sabotage), Patriot/base defenses/powered structures keep firing instead of going dark. Radar still toggles.
close_reason: on_power_brown_out_change iterates owned objects via PlayerObjectWorld and sets DISABLED_UNDERPOWERED on KINDOF_POWERED buildings (player.rs).

title: [Player] Transfer assets only moves cash, not units or buildings
description:
## C++
`Player::transferAssetsFromThat` (Player.cpp ~1666-1701) transfers money AND iterates the source player's objects onto this player's default team (used by capture-all / alliance-defeat / script transfers).

## Rust
`common/rts/player.rs` `transfer_assets_from` (2010-2022) withdraws/deposits money only. Comment: "In full implementation, would also transfer all objects to this player's default team".

## Evidence
Money moves; object iteration is missing.

## Player-visible effect
When a player is defeated and assets transfer, or a script hands over a base, units/buildings stay with the old owner (or vanish with the player) while only cash changes hands.
close_reason: transfer_assets_from moves non-beacon objects onto this player's default team then transfers cash (player.rs).

title: [Player] Map-script garrison, sell-all, idle, and enable-object commands are no-ops
description:
## C++
`Player.cpp` implements real world iteration:
- `garrisonAllUnits` (2147) finds structures and garrisons nearby infantry
- `ungarrisonAllUnits` (2200) evacuates all structures
- `setUnitsShouldIdleOrResume` (2234) idles or resumes all units
- `sellEverythingUnderTheSun` (2288) `iterateObjects(sellBuildings, NULL)`
- `setObjectsEnabled` (2074) enables/disables objects matching a template

These are used by campaign/skirmish scripts.

## Rust
`common/rts/player.rs` 2024-2058:
- `garrison_all_units` / `ungarrison_all_units`: "Simplified: just mark intent" empty bodies
- `set_units_should_idle_or_resume`: "Simplified: no-op"
- `sell_everything`: only clears `build_list`, does not sell buildings
- `set_objects_enabled`: "Simplified: no-op"

## Evidence
Comments literally say "Would iterate" / "Simplified: no-op".

## Player-visible effect
Map scripts that garrison everyone, evacuate, idle units, sell the base, or disable a template (e.g. campaign events) do nothing. Player keeps units/buildings as-is.
close_reason: garrison/ungarrison/idle/sell_everything/set_objects_enabled iterate real object IDs through PlayerObjectWorld + team member lists (player.rs).

title: [W3DDraw] Police cars have no flashing ground light
description:
## C++
GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/Drawable/Draw/W3DPoliceCarDraw.cpp `createDynamicLight` / `doDrawModule`.
Creates a W3DDynamicLight from the 3D scene, then every draw pulses red/blue ambient+diffuse and places the light 8 units above the car (`Set_Far_Attenuation_Range(3,20)`). Destructor fades the light over 5 frames.

## Rust
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/draw/w3d_police_car_draw.rs `do_draw_module`.
Only advances `cur_frame` and writes `animation_time`. No dynamic light is allocated or colored.

## Evidence
C++ lines 97-130 set red/green/blue from frame windows and call `m_light->Set_Diffuse/Set_Ambient/Set_Position`. Rust has no `m_light` field.

## Player-visible effect
USA/China police cars (and any W3DPoliceCarDraw unit) never cast the flashing red/blue searchlight on the ground at night.
close_reason: W3DPoliceCarDraw allocates a persistent scene point light, pulses C++ red/blue frame windows, places it 8 units above the car with far atten 3-20, and fades over 5 frames on delete. Terrain lighting merges these lights.

title: [W3DDraw] Truck wheels ignore suspension height offsets
description:
## C++
GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/Drawable/Draw/W3DTruckDraw.cpp `doDrawModule`.
Uses `getDrawable()->getWheelInfo()` (`TWheelInfo`) to `Adjust_Z_Translation` each tire bone (`m_frontLeftHeightOffset` etc.) and to drive cab/trailer desired angle from `m_wheelAngle`. Wheels bounce independently over terrain.

## Rust
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/draw/w3d_truck_draw.rs `append_bone_overrides`.
Rotates tire/cab/trailer bones from physics speed/turning only. No `wheel_info` / height-offset lookup. Cab angle is `turning * cab_rotation_factor` without the C++ path-angle clamp.

## Evidence
Grep of w3d_truck_draw.rs for wheel_info/HeightOffset: no matches. C++ lines 473-501 apply per-wheel Z offsets.

## Player-visible effect
Trucks, supply trucks, and other W3DTruckDraw vehicles have wheels that spin but stay glued to the chassis. No independent suspension bounce on bumps.
close_reason: W3DTruckDraw applies TWheelInfo height offsets via Adjust_Z-equivalent bone translation, uses wheel_angle for steer/cab/trailer, and clamps cab angle to the path goal like C++.

title: [W3DDraw] Tank treads never scroll
description:
## C++
GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/Drawable/Draw/W3DTankDraw.cpp `updateTreadObjects` / `updateTreadPositions` / `doDrawModule`.
Discovers TREADS* mesh sub-objects with LinearOffsetTextureMapper, then UV-scrolls left/right/middle treads from locomotor speed and pivot turning. Same TREADS* discovery exists in W3DTankTruckDraw.cpp.

## Rust
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/draw/w3d_tank_draw.rs `update_tread_objects` / `publish_tread_uv_overrides`.
`update_tread_objects` always clears the list and never discovers sub-objects. `publish_tread_uv_overrides` is empty. W3DTankTruckDraw.rs has the same empty discovery. Animation math exists but never runs because `treads` stays empty.

## Evidence
Comment: "Until the render object bridge exposes those sub-objects, keep the list empty rather than animating fake treads."

## Player-visible effect
Moving tanks and Scorpion-style tank-trucks have frozen tread textures. Pivot-in-place does not counter-scroll left/right treads.
close_reason: W3DTankDraw/W3DTankTruckDraw discover TREADS* HLOD children with LinearOffset mapper and publish MeshUvOverrideState U offsets from locomotor pivot/drive scroll.

title: [W3DDraw] Scripted camera fades never overlay the screen
description:
## C++
GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DStatusCircle.cpp `Render`.
After the optional team-dot, reads `TheScriptEngine->getFade()` / `getFadeValue()` and draws a fullscreen quad with ADD / REVSUBTRACT / 4x SATURATE / MULTIPLY blend. This is how CAMERA_FADE_ADD/SUBTRACT/SATURATE/MULTIPLY become visible.

## Rust
ScriptEngine stores fade type/value (GameLogic scripting). No GameClient/Main render path draws W3DStatusCircle or an equivalent fullscreen fade overlay. `show_team_dot` exists as a flag only.

## Evidence
Grep of GameClient/Main for get_fade / TFade / FADE_ADD overlay draw finds only script action names, no render.

## Player-visible effect
Mission/cinematic CAMERA_FADE_* scripts change no pixels. White-ins, black-outs, saturate flashes, and multiply fades do not appear. `-showTeamDot` also draws nothing.
close_reason: W3DStatusCircle fade overlay reads ScriptEngine get_fade/get_fade_value, publishes CameraFadeOverlay, and PresentationFrame.camera_fade freezes ADD/SUBTRACT/SATURATE/MULTIPLY for the render path.

title: [GameLogic] Special-power subclasses never fire from Object dispatch
description:
## C++
`OCLSpecialPower`, `CashHackSpecialPower`, `SpyVisionSpecialPower`, `DefectorSpecialPower`, `DemoralizeSpecialPower`, `FireWeaponPower`, `BaikonurLaunchPower`, `CleanupAreaPower`, `CashBountyPower`, and `SpecialAbility` inherit `SpecialPowerModule` and override `doSpecialPower*`. Object/ControlBar call the virtual, so each subclass runs after the base recharge/EVA/view-object path.

## Rust
Live factories in `contain_module_overrides` instantiate the `object/special_powers/*` types (and mapped `special_power_module/{baikonur,cleanup,fire_weapon}` types). Object dispatch (`object_special_power.rs` `with_special_power_module_mut_by_name` / `special_power_interface_cast.rs` `module_special_power_kind`) only downcasts `object::special_power_module::SpecialPowerModule`. `OclSpecialPower` implements `Module` + `BehaviorModuleInterface` with no `get_special_power()` and no `SpecialPowerModuleInterface`. Same for the other mapped subclass files.

## Evidence
`module_special_power_kind` returns Some only for `SpecialPowerModule`; else None. OCL `do_special_power_at_location` also never calls the base recharge/EVA/view-object path even if invoked directly.

## Player-visible effect
Clicking OCL powers (A10, paradrop, carpet bomb, scud, etc.), cash hack, spy vision, defector, demoralize, fire-weapon powers, Baikonur, cleanup area, cash bounty, and special abilities does nothing: no spawn, no money steal, no reveal, no cooldown, no EVA.
close_reason: Object special-power dispatch downcasts all subclass modules; each implements SpecialPowerModuleInterface and calls base recharge/EVA then subclass fire. Files: special_power_interface_cast.rs special_powers/*

title: [GameLogic] Partition cells are 100wu instead of retail 40wu
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/PartitionManager.cpp` `PartitionManager::init` sets `m_cellSize = TheGlobalData->m_partitionCellSize` (GameData.ini `PartitionCellSize = 40.0`). Cell grid, shroud/look rings, collision broadphase, findPositionAround, threat/value maps, and LOS cell walks all use that size.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/collide/partition_manager.rs` hardcodes `const PARTITION_CELL_SIZE: f32 = 100.0` and comments it as matching C++. Other residual files already record the retail value as 40.

## Evidence
Retail INI: `PartitionCellSize = 40.0`. Rust: `const PARTITION_CELL_SIZE: f32 = 100.0`. C++ default in GlobalData is 0 then loaded from INI; never a 100 constant.

## Player-visible effect
Shroud/fog cells are 2.5× too large, proximity/collision queries and “find a clear spot” (OCL passable adjust, crate drops, exits) use the wrong grid, and AI threat/value peaks sit on the wrong cell centers.
close_reason: PARTITION_CELL_SIZE is 40.0 matching GameData.ini PartitionCellSize. File: GameLogic/src/object/collide/partition_manager.rs

title: [GameLogic] Elite units reject multi-level veterancy crates
description:
## C++
`ExperienceTracker::canGainExpForLevel` (ExperienceTracker.cpp:114-121) clamps `newLevel` to `LEVEL_LAST` then returns `newLevel > m_currentLevel`. An Elite unit asked for +2 levels can still gain the remaining level to Heroic. Veterancy crates call this before granting XP.

## Rust
`experience/tracker.rs` `can_gain_exp_for_level` does `new_level <= max_level` without clamping. Elite (2) + 2 = 4, which is > Heroic (3), so it returns false. The unit test even asserts `!can_gain_exp_for_level(4)` from Regular and does not test the clamp-to-last-level case. `veterancy_crate_collide.rs` bails when this returns false.

## Evidence
C++: `if (newLevel > LEVEL_LAST) newLevel = LEVEL_LAST; return (newLevel > m_currentLevel);`
Rust: `let new_level = current + levels_to_gain; new_level <= max_level`

## Player-visible effect
Elite units ignore +2 veterancy crates (and any other +N grant that overshoots Heroic) instead of promoting to Heroic.
close_reason: can_gain_exp_for_level clamps new_level to Heroic then tests new_level > current. File: GameLogic/src/experience/tracker.rs

title: [WW3D] Default proto loaders omit Collection/Box/Ring/Sphere/Aggregate/DistLOD/Null
description:
## C++
`WW3DAssetManager::WW3DAssetManager` (`assetmgr.cpp:148-164`) installs Mesh (unless USE_WWSHADE), HModel, Collection, Box, HLod, DistLOD, Aggregate, Null, Dazzle, Ring, Sphere, plus `SHD_REG_LOADER`. W3DDisplay also re-registers Aggregate and ParticleEmitter. These create render objects from `W3D_CHUNK_COLLECTION` (0x420), `W3D_CHUNK_BOX/SPHERE/RING` (0x740+), DistLOD, Null, Aggregate.

## Rust
`DefaultLoaders::install_into` (`prototype_loader.rs:1421-1427`) only pushes MeshLoader, HModelLoader, HTreeLoader, HAnimLoader. Live Main parser handles Mesh/HLOD/HModel/Anim but not Collection/Box/Ring/Sphere/Aggregate/DistLOD/Null. Device `parse_collection_chunk` (`model_loader.rs:2045-2076`) reads the header then skips transforms: `Collection '…' has N transforms — parsed header, data skipped (not yet populated into model)`.

## Evidence
C++ registers 10+ loaders. Rust test `test_default_loaders_installation` asserts `loaders.len() == 4`. Collection skip warn is explicit.

## Player-visible effect
Grouped collection props, ring/sphere effect meshes (force fields, ion/nuke rings), collision-box vis when enabled, DistLOD swaps, and aggregate composites never instantiate from W3D. Distinct from HLOD (Main does parse HLOD) and from hq-2k22 shard transforms.
close_reason: DefaultLoaders now installs Collection/Box/HLod/DistLOD/Aggregate/Null/Dazzle/Ring/Sphere (C++ assetmgr.cpp:148-162). Loaders parse W3D chunks into live prototypes; parse_w3d_file registers them. Files: proto_loaders.rs, prototype_loader.rs, loaders/mod.rs

title: [WW3D] Model-attached particle emitters never instantiate
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DDisplay.cpp:699-701` registers `_ParticleEmitterLoader` on the live `W3DAssetManager`. `ParticleEmitterLoaderClass::Load_W3D` (`part_ldr.cpp:1828+`) reads `W3D_CHUNK_EMITTER` (0x500) into a `ParticleEmitterPrototypeClass`; `Create()` builds a `ParticleEmitterClass` that HLOD children attach as exhaust, fire, sparks, and bone-linked smoke.

## Rust
Live Main parser `GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/assets/models/w3d_loader.rs:556-567` treats 0x500 as an unknown chunk (recursive container walk only). Device loader `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameEngineDevice/src/w3d/model_loader.rs:615-616` and `skip_emitter_chunk` (`:2084-2108`) explicitly skip: `Emitter '…' parsed header, particle system data skipped`. WWVegas `DefaultLoaders` (`prototype_loader.rs:1411-1418`) never installs a ParticleEmitter loader. WW3DDisplay-equivalent never calls `Register_Prototype_Loader(&_ParticleEmitterLoader)`.

## Evidence
Device: `W3DChunkType::Emitter => { self.skip_emitter_chunk(...) }` plus warn `particle system data skipped`. Main match has Mesh/Hierarchy/Animation/HModel/LODMODEL/HLOD only.

## Player-visible effect
Vehicles and buildings lose W3D-authored particle FX (exhaust, chimney smoke, muzzle sparks, fire). Only INI ParticleSys (if any) remains.
close_reason: ParticleEmitterLoader registered (C++ W3DDisplay.cpp:700 + part_ldr.cpp Load_W3D). Create() builds ParticleEmitterInstance so HLOD children attach. Files: proto_loaders.rs, prototypes.rs, prototype_loader.rs

title: [WW3D] Static sort lists stay off so transparent W3D draws out of order
description:
## C++
`W3DDisplay` init (`W3DDisplay.cpp:714`) calls `WW3D::Enable_Static_Sort_Lists(true)`. Alpha-tested trees, additive FX, and other sort-level meshes queue into static sort lists and flush in order (`ww3d.h:244-249`, `static_sort_list.cpp`). Default `AreStaticSortListsEnabled` is then true for the whole session.

## Rust
`WW3DState` (`ww3d-core/src/ww3d.rs:107-109`) defaults `static_sort_lists_enabled: false`. `WgpuMainRenderer` also starts `static_sort_enabled` false (`wgpu_main_renderer.rs:791`). No live Main/Device boot path calls `WW3D::set_static_sort_lists_enabled(true)` (no matches under GameEngine or Main). `StaticSortManager::add_to_static_sort_list` (`static_sort.rs:109`) no-ops when the flag is false, so meshes with `sort_level != NONE` draw immediately instead of sorted.

## Evidence
C++: `WW3D::Enable_Static_Sort_Lists(true)`. Rust default false; `if !ww3d_core::WW3D::are_static_sort_lists_enabled() { return; }`.

## Player-visible effect
Transparent/additive W3D objects (foliage alpha, glass, additive glows, sorted FX) draw in submission order and z-fight or appear behind/through solid meshes. Not a DX→wgpu difference.
close_reason: WW3D static_sort_lists_enabled now defaults true to match post-W3DDisplay C++ session; WgpuCoreBridge starts enabled. Files: ww3d-core/src/ww3d.rs, wgpu_main_renderer.rs

title: [WW3D] Prelit lightmap material chunks never loaded
description:
## C++
`WW3D::PrelitMode` defaults to `PRELIT_MODE_LIGHTMAP_MULTI_PASS` (`ww3d.cpp:127`). `W3DDisplay.cpp:712` sets it again. `MeshModelClass` load (`meshmdlio.cpp:261-275`) switches on `WW3D::Get_Prelit_Mode()` and reads `W3D_CHUNK_PRELIT_LIGHTMAP_MULTI_PASS` (0x25) / multi-texture (0x26) / vertex (0x24) wrappers so baked lightmap extra passes become extra material passes.

## Rust
Live Main `w3d_loader.rs` / `w3d_loader_parse.rs` have no `W3D_CHUNK_PRELIT_*` (0x23-0x26) arms. WWVegas chunk enums exist (`ww3d-core/src/chunks.rs:18-20`) but the live mesh parse path does not select a prelit wrapper from a global PrelitMode. There is no `Set_Prelit_Mode` / `Get_Prelit_Mode` on the live WW3D façade used at boot.

## Evidence
C++ meshmdlio: `case WW3D::PRELIT_MODE_LIGHTMAP_MULTI_PASS: if (Attributes & W3D_MESH_FLAG_PRELIT_LIGHTMAP_MULTI_PASS) PrelitChunkID = W3D_CHUNK_PRELIT_LIGHTMAP_MULTI_PASS`. Rust Main grep for PRELIT / 0x00000025 in assets/models is empty.

## Player-visible effect
Static meshes authored with baked lightmaps (buildings, props) lose the extra lightmap pass and look dynamically lit or flat. Distinct from hq-eenv (terrain splat) and hq-2k22 (shard transforms).

title: [WW3D] Dazzle and lens-flare prototypes never load
description:
## C++
`WW3DAssetManager` constructor (`assetmgr.cpp:160`) registers `_DazzleLoader`. `W3D_CHUNK_DAZZLE` (0x900) plus name/typename (`w3d_file.h:445-447`) create `DazzleRenderObjClass` instances (headlights, sun glints, halo/flare around bright lights). Types come from dazzle.ini.

## Rust
`DefaultLoaders` (`WW3D2/crates/ww3d-assets/src/prototype_loader.rs:1389-1427`) only installs Mesh/HModel/HTree/HAnim. Live Main `w3d_loader.rs` has no `W3D_CHUNK_DAZZLE` arm; 0x900 falls through as unknown. Device `model_loader.rs` also has no Dazzle variant (unknown skip). A dazzle crate exists (`ww3d-assets/src/dazzle.rs`, `ww3d-effects/.../dazzle_system.rs`) but is not registered on the live asset manager / Create_Render_Obj path.

## Evidence
C++: `Register_Prototype_Loader(&_DazzleLoader)`. Rust default install test asserts `loaders.len() == 4`. Main chunk match ends at HLOD then `_ => unknown`.

## Player-visible effect
No W3D dazzle/halo/lens-flare objects: missing headlights, sun flares, and glare on bright model lights.
close_reason: DazzleLoader registered; Load_W3D reads W3D_CHUNK_DAZZLE_NAME/TYPENAME and Create() instantiates DazzleInstance (dazzle.cpp:1657-1691). Files: proto_loaders.rs, prototypes.rs

title: [GameClient] Language.ini fonts unused; UI ignores resolution scale
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/GlobalLanguage.cpp` `GlobalLanguage::init` loads `Data/<lang>/Language.ini`, registers LocalFontFile resources, and `adjustFontSize` scales point size by `TheGlobalData->m_xResolution/800` clamped to [1,2] using `m_resolutionFontSizeAdjustment` (default 0.7). Field table includes UnicodeFontName, MilitaryCaptionSpeed/Delay, every UI FontDesc (Message, Tooltip, Superweapon countdown, DrawableCaption, DefaultWindow, Credits*, etc.).

## Rust
Mapped `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/global_language.rs` is a disconnected stub: only three hardcoded Arial credits fonts; `adjust_font_size` returns the input size unchanged. Credits (`credits.rs`) and HeaderTemplate (`header_template.rs`) read this stub, not Common's `ini_language.rs` parser.

## Evidence
GameClient stub:
```
pub fn adjust_font_size(&self, size: i32) -> i32 { size }
credits_title_font: FontDesc::new("Arial", 18, false)
```
C++:
```
adjustFactor = 1.0f + (adjustFactor-1.0f) * m_resolutionFontSizeAdjustment;
Int pointSize = REAL_TO_INT_FLOOR(theFontSize*adjustFactor);
```

## Player-visible effect
Credits, header templates, and any GameClient UI that uses `get_global_language_data()` stay at default Arial sizes; widescreen/high-res font scaling from Language.ini never applies. Military-caption / tooltip / countdown fonts from Language.ini are ignored on this path.
close_reason: GameClient GlobalLanguageData loads Data/<lang>/Language.ini, copies FontDesc fields from Common, and adjust_font_size scales by xResolution/800 clamped [1,2] using ResolutionFontAdjustment 0.7. InGameUI font overrides apply the scaled size.

title: [GameClient] Superweapon/ability radius overlay never draws
description:
## C++
`InGameUI::setRadiusCursor` (`InGameUI.cpp` ~1172-1269) looks up `m_radiusCursors[cursorType]`, computes radius from SpecialPowerTemplate/WeaponSlot, then `createRadiusDecal(pos, radius, controller, m_curRadiusCursor)` and `handleRadiusCursor()` each frame so the targeting circle follows the mouse.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/gui/ingame_ui/radius_cursor.rs` only writes `RadiusCursor` state (type/active/position/radius). It never calls `RadiusDecalTemplate::create_radius_decal` even though `radius_decal.rs` implements decals. `create_command_hint` sets a dummy radius of 1.0 and `set_radius_cursor_active_with_type` does not spawn a decal.

## Evidence
```
self.radius_cursor.cursor_type = cursor_type;
self.radius_cursor.active = true;
self.radius_cursor.position = position;
self.radius_cursor.radius = radius;
```
No create_radius_decal / projected shadow.

## Player-visible effect
Guard-area, artillery, special-power, and other radius-cursor commands show no ground circle; players cannot see the affected area while targeting.
close_reason: InGameUI::set_radius_cursor creates a RadiusDecal via RadiusDecalTemplate::create_radius_decal (default SCCAttackDamageArea texture). handle_radius_cursor follows the mouse each frame and GUI-command hints spawn the overlay (radius_cursor.rs, impl_update.rs, impl_input.rs).

title: [GameClient] Units stay silent on move/attack/select commands
description:
## C++
`pickAndPlayUnitVoiceResponse` in `GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/MessageStream/CommandXlat.cpp` (~271-731) walks the selected drawable list and plays per-unit VoiceSelect / VoiceMove / VoiceCrush / VoiceEnter / VoiceBuildResponse / VoiceSupply / VoiceUnload / VoiceRepair / VoiceCombatDrop / VoiceSalvage / VoiceMoveUpgraded (GLA worker shoes) etc. via `TheAudio`. Called from command issue paths.

## Rust
`GameClient/src/message_stream/command_xlat.rs` is a compatibility shim. `translators/command_translator.rs` evaluates context commands but has no `pick_and_play_unit_voice_response` and no per-unit voice lookup. Repo-wide GameClient search finds no port of this function.

## Evidence
C++ function is ~460 lines of message-type switch + audio. Rust CommandTranslator has mouse/selection state and hint/command emission only.

## Player-visible effect
Selected units never acknowledge orders. Move, attack, enter, repair, salvage, construct, and control-group select produce no unit voice lines.
close_reason: CommandTranslator now calls pick_and_play_unit_voice_response on issued move/attack/select/enter/repair/salvage/build/guard/special-power commands. Plays per-unit Voice* via TheAudio from selected objects (command_translator.rs, voice.rs, selection_xlat.rs, place_event_translator.rs).

title: [Video] Briefing movies play with no Bink soundtrack
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/VideoDevice/Bink/BinkVideoPlayer.cpp`
`BinkVideoPlayer::createStream` maps `TheAudio->getVolume(AudioAffect_Speech)` through `BinkSetVolume`.
`BinkVideoPlayer::initializeBinkWithMiles` / `notifyVideoPlayerOfNewProvider` bind Bink's audio track to Miles DirectSound (`BinkSoundUseDirectSound`). Campaign intro/briefing `.bik` files therefore play with speech-slider volume.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngineDevice/src/VideoDevice/Bink/bink_video_player.rs` `notify_video_player_of_new_provider` only registers/unregisters the video provider and explicitly does not couple audio.
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/bink.rs` `has_bink_audio_bitstream_parser()` is hard-coded `false`; `BinkVideoStream::set_volume` stores the speech-slider mapping but never decodes or mixes Bink audio tracks (`audio_track_count` is parsed and ignored).

## Evidence
C++: `BinkSetVolume(stream->m_handle, 0, volume)` and `BinkSoundUseDirectSound(driver)`.
Rust: `has_bink_audio_bitstream_parser() -> false`; comment "No audio bitstream parser exists … Miles coupling / BinkSetVolume playback cannot run."

## Player-visible effect
Training/campaign intro movies and victory/score movies play silent. Briefing voice that lives in the `.bik` soundtrack is missing; only separate EVA/speech events (if any) can be heard.
close_reason: BinkDecoder decodes audio packets and play_bink_pcm_through_miles mixes them at speech-slider volume; has_bink_audio_bitstream_parser is true.

title: [GameLogic] Mob nexus never holds, heals, or exits mobs
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Contain/MobNexusContain.cpp` `isValidContainerFor` (ally + slot count + parachute unwrap), `onContaining` (DISABLED_HELD + extra slots + MODELCONDITION_LOADED), `onRemoving` (exit bone, velocity, scatter, allow-to-fall), `onObjectCreated` (InitialPayload spawn), `update` (HealthRegen%PerSec heal), `tryToEvacuate`, xfer of `m_extraSlotsInUse`.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/contain/mob_nexus_contain.rs` is an OpenContain wrapper. Module data is parsed (Slots, InitialPayload, HealthRegen%PerSec, exit flags) but never used except `get_usage` slot_capacity. `update`/`onContaining`/`is_valid_container_for` all delegate to OpenContain. No extraSlotsInUse, no payload spawn, no heal, no scatter/velocity exit.

## Evidence
`impl MobNexusContain` only has `new` + save/load. `fn update` is `self.base.update()`. `is_valid_container_for` is `self.base.is_valid_container_for`.

## Player-visible effect
Angry Mob / rebel nexus units do not spawn their initial crowd, do not track multi-slot occupancy, do not heal the mob, and do not apply exit scatter/velocity. GLA mob gameplay is broken.
close_reason: MobNexusContain now holds allies with extra slots + LOADED/HELD, heals HealthRegen%PerSec, exits via bone/velocity/scatter/allow-to-fall, InitialPayload spawn, tryToEvacuate, parachute unwrap. Files: mob_nexus_contain.rs

title: [GameLogic] Nearby human units never retaliate when friends are attacked
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Body/ActiveBody.cpp` `ActiveBody::attemptDamage` (lines 664-701) plus `shouldRetaliateAgainstAggressor` / `shouldRetaliate`. After damage, if the victim is human-controlled and logical retaliation is on, idle allied mobiles in `m_retaliateFriendsRadius` get `aiGuardRetaliate` against a ground enemy damager (not aircraft, not drones, not stealthed-undetected).

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/body/active_body.rs` `attempt_damage` applies HP, kill-pilot, garrison slay, subdual, lastDamageInfo, damage modules, and FX. There is no `should_retaliate`, no partition iterate, no `aiGuardRetaliate`. `YELLOW_DAMAGE_PERCENT` is the only leftover constant and is unused.

## Evidence
No matches for `retaliat`, `should_retaliate`, or `guard_retaliate` in active_body.rs. C++ block after `doDamageFX` is missing.

## Player-visible effect
When a human unit is shot, nearby idle friends stand still instead of turning to attack the aggressor. Human retaliation feel is gone.
close_reason: Human logical-retaliation path iterates allies in retaliate_friends_radius and issues ai_guard_retaliate after should_retaliate / can-attack filters (no aircraft, drones, stealthed-undetected). File: active_body.rs

title: [GameLogic] Transports reject parachute-wrapped infantry
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Contain/TransportContain.cpp` `isValidContainerFor` (lines 143-159): if the rider is a special zero-slot container (parachute), replace the check target with the first contained infantry so a plane can accept a paratrooper.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/contain/transport_contain.rs` `is_valid_container_for` detects zero-slot containers but then still uses the original object:
```
// Get first object inside the zero-slot container
// For now, just use the original object since we can't easily
// get a reference to the contained object
obj
```
The parachute itself has `transport_slot_count == 0`, so the later `if transport_slot_count == 0 { return false; }` rejects it.

## Evidence
Comment at transport_contain.rs:427-430 plus the slot-count reject at 458-460.

## Player-visible effect
Paratroopers cannot be loaded into transport planes (or any transport that should accept the infantry inside the chute). Paradrop delivery and chute-to-plane boarding fail.
close_reason: TransportContain::is_valid_container_for unwraps special zero-slot (parachute) riders to the first contained infantry, matching C++ isValidContainerFor. Files: transport_contain.rs, contain/mod.rs

title: [GameLogic] Parachute drops never open, land, or kill riders
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Contain/ParachuteContain.cpp` `ParachuteContain::update` / `onContaining` / `onRemoving` / `onDie` / `onCollide` / `xfer`. After `paraOpenDist` the chute opens (model condition + audio + landing AI), sways via bone offsets, kills empty chutes, kills water/impassable landings, applies free-fall damage if the chute dies airborne, and dumps the rider on ground collide. Xfer persists pitch/roll/open/landing override/bones.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/contain/parachute_contain.rs` only stores `OpenContain` + `object_id`. `update()` delegates to OpenContain. `deploy_parachutes()` is `Ok(())`. No open-distance, no FREEfall/PARACHUTING flags, no audio, no water kill, no onCollide ground dump, no xfer of chute state.

## Evidence
```
pub fn deploy_parachutes(&mut self) -> GameResult<()> {
    // Implementation would handle parachute deployment
    Ok(())
}
fn update(...) { self.base.update() }
```
Struct has no `opened`, `pitch`, `start_z`, or landing override fields. 371-line wrapper vs 767-line C++ implementation.

## Player-visible effect
Paratroopers never deploy a chute, never sway, never land, and never die from water/impassable/free-fall. Airborne drops are broken.
close_reason: ParachuteContain now matches C++: paraOpenDist open (model/audio/landing AI), sway, empty-chute kill, water/impassable rider death, airborne free-fall damage, ground collide dump, xfer of pitch/roll/open/landing/bones. Files: parachute_contain.rs
